This inexactness criterion can be assessed by each client independently based on its unique condition, thereby reducing the local computational cost and mitigating the undesirable straggle effect. The convergence of the resulting inexact ADMM is proved under the assumption of strongly convex loss functions. Additionally, we present a self-adaptive scheme that dynamically adjusts each client's penalty parameter, enhancing algorithm robustness by mitigating the need for empirical penalty parameter choices for each client. Extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets are conducted. As validated by some numerical tests, our proposed algorithm can reduce the clients' local computational load significantly and also accelerate the learning process compared to the vanilla FedADMM. The source code is available at https://github.com/DCN-FAU-AvH/FedADMM-InSa.

papers.title: Stein Boltzmann Sampling: A Variational Approach for Global Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a flow-based method for global optimization of continuous Sobolev functions, called Stein Boltzmann Sampling (SBS). SBS initializes uniformly a number of particles representing candidate solutions, then uses the Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD) algorithm to sequentially and deterministically move those particles in order to approximate a target distribution whose mass is concentrated around promising areas of the domain of the optimized function. The target is chosen to be a properly parametrized Boltzmann distribution. For the purpose of global optimization, we adapt the generic SVGD theoretical framework allowing to address more general target distributions over a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$, and we prove SBS's asymptotic convergence. In addition to the main SBS algorithm, we present two variants: the SBS-PF that includes a particle filtering strategy, and the SBS-HYBRID one that uses SBS or SBS-PF as a continuation after other particle- or distribution-based optimization methods. A detailed comparison with state-of-the-art methods on benchmark functions demonstrates that SBS and its variants are highly competitive, while the combination of the two variants provides the best trade-off between accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: A sharper bound of the Hotelling-Solomons inequality
papers.abstract: The original Hotelling-Solomons inequality states that an upper bound of the absolute difference between the mean and median, standardized by the standard deviation, is 1. However, in this paper, we introduce a new bound that depends on the sample size, which is strictly smaller than 1.

papers.title: Approximate and Weighted Data Reconstruction Attack in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed learning paradigm that enables multiple clients to collaborate on building a machine learning model without sharing their private data. Although FL is considered privacy-preserved by design, recent data reconstruction attacks demonstrate that an attacker can recover clients' training data based on the parameters shared in FL. However, most existing methods fail to attack the most widely used horizontal Federated Averaging (FedAvg) scenario, where clients share model parameters after multiple local training steps. To tackle this issue, we propose an interpolation-based approximation method, which makes attacking FedAvg scenarios feasible by generating the intermediate model updates of the clients' local training processes. Then, we design a layer-wise weighted loss function to improve the data quality of reconstruction. We assign different weights to model updates in different layers concerning the neural network structure, with the weights tuned by Bayesian optimization. Finally, experimental results validate the superiority of our proposed approximate and weighted attack (AWA) method over the other state-of-the-art methods, as demonstrated by the substantial improvement in different evaluation metrics for image data reconstructions. The source code is available at https://github.com/DCN-FAU-AvH/FL-AWA-attack.

papers.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.

papers.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $Φ^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $Φ^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this article, it is proved that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function must lie on the critical line, known as the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: On properties of the generalized Davenport Expansion
papers.abstract: We study the continuity properties of a generalized Davenport Fourier expansion we recently discovered, by imposing conditions on the coefficients. We also put our expansion into perspective from the position of Appell sequences.

papers.title: Triangular prism equations and categorification
papers.abstract: We obtain the triangular prism equations by evaluating a labelled prism in two ways, as a sum of products of two or of three tetrahedral coefficients. For a spherical fusion category an explicit change of variables identifies these equations with the pentagon equations. Prisms with repeated edge labels yield local subsystems, simplified using tetrahedral rotations and the Fuchs-Runkel-Schweigert parity theorem. Additional prism equations couple these subsystems. Two further obstructions, the zero- and one-spectrum criteria, follow directly from the pentagon equations and apply over every field without a pivotal structure. We prove that F210 admits no fusion categorification in characteristic zero and no pivotal fusion categorification in positive characteristic, and that F660 admits no fusion categorification over any field. Together with a bounded census and known unitary obstructions, these results classify, up to Grothendieck equivalence, the non-pointed unitary simple integral fusion categories of rank at most 8 and Frobenius-Perron dimension at most 20000 for which the Frobenius-Perron dimension of each simple object divides that of the category.

papers.title: Resolvent convergence under heterogeneous second-moment profiles and quadratic-form control
papers.abstract: Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ have independent real columns with finite second moments, not necessarily centered or identically distributed. For $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$, we compare \[ G^z=\left(\frac1nXX^\top-zI_p\right)^{-1} \] with a deterministic matrix $\tilde G^z$ defined by the second-moment profile $(Σ_i)_{i\in[n]}$, where $Σ_i=\mathbb E[x_ix_i^\top]$. For deterministic matrices \(A\), we prove finite-dimensional \(L^q\) bounds for $\tr(A(G^z-\tilde G^z))$ in terms of moments of centered quadratic forms, without assuming independence among the coordinates of a column. Operator-test bounds impose no trace-growth or aspect-ratio restriction and display explicitly the effect of the sizes and repetitions of the second-moment matrices $(Σ_i)_{i\in[n]}$. Under $\sqrt p\sup_{i\in[n]}|Σ_i|_{\hs}=O(n)$, the Hilbert-Schmidt bounds involve approximation of the profile by commuting positive-semidefinite matrices, with explicit dependence on the approximation error and the dimension of their span. We also obtain corresponding bounds for \(\tr(A G^z B G^z)\), with deterministic \(A,B\). All bounds are locally uniform in $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$.

papers.title: Classification of the d-representation-finite symmetric k-algebras of finite representation type
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric Nakayama algebras and of all $d$-representation-finite trivial extensions of path algebras of quivers, over an arbitrary field. As a consequence we get a classification, up to Morita equivalence, of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric algebras of finite representation type over an algebraically closed field.

papers.title: A Divisor Function Inequality
papers.abstract: This short note provides a sharper upper bound of a well known inequality for the sum of divisors function. This is a problem in pure mathematics related to the distribution of prime numbers. Furthermore, the technique is completely elementary.

papers.title: On Fourier frames
papers.abstract: We solve the problem of Duffin and Schaeffer (1952) of characterizing those sequences of real frequencies which generate Fourier frames. Equivalently, we characterize the sampling sequences for the Paley-Wiener space. The key step is to connect the problem with de Branges' theory of Hilbert spaces of entire functions. We show that our description of sampling sequences permits us to obtain a classical inequality of H. Landau as a consequence of Pavlov's description of Riesz bases of complex exponentials and the John-Nirenberg theorem. Finally, we discuss how to transform our description into a working condition by relating it to an approximation problem for subharmonic functions. By this approach, we determine the critical growth rate of a nondecreasing function $ψ$ such that the sequence $\{\lamdda_k\}){k\in \Bbb Z}$ defined by $λ_k + ψ(λ_k)=k$ is a sampling.

papers.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
papers.abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

papers.title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_φ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $φ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques. Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
papers.abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

papers.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

papers.title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
papers.abstract: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

papers.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
papers.abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal étale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
papers.abstract: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

papers.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
papers.abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

papers.title: Rigid Theories
papers.abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

papers.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
papers.abstract: Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+yα)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture. We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.

papers.title: Triply conservative schemes for degenerate convection-dispersion equations
papers.abstract: It is well known that for numerically solving hyperbolic conservation laws, even a convergent numerical scheme still may not always converge to a weak solution. The remedy is the famous Lax-Wendroff theorem. In a recent work on degenerate convection-diffusion equations, an analogous phenomenon was identified and doubly conservative schemes were introduced. In this paper, we address the same issue for solving the following nonlinear degenerate dispersive or convection-dispersion equations: \begin{equation*} u_t+f(u)_x+A(u)_{xxx}=0. \end{equation*} The resulting equation is regarded as degenerate if $A'(u)$ is allowed to vanish. An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. In contrast to classical KdV solitons possessing exponentially decaying tails, $K(m,n)$ equations can admit compactly supported solitary waves, known as compactons, whose regularity can deteriorate at the boundary of their support. We first give an example in which both a classical conservative and doubly conservative scheme converges to a limit that fails to satisfy the ultra-weak formulation. To address this issue, we introduce the notion of a triply conservative (TriC) scheme and prove a Lax-Wendroff type theorem for consistent TriC schemes. Under suitable assumptions, a convergent sequence generated by a consistent TriC scheme will converge to an ultra-weak solution. Several existing high-order schemes are shown to have a TriC structure. We further introduce a new high-order TriC finite volume scheme based on a connection between triple cell averages and quadratic B-splines. The theory and the scheme are also suited for two-dimensional anisotropic problems and non-uniform meshes. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions confirm the high-order accuracy on smooth solutions and illustrate the behavior of the schemes for compactons and traveling fronts.

papers.title: Counterexample to Flow-Transfer Conjectures
papers.abstract: An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp. $M$-tension) taking values in $B$. For subsets $B=-B\subseteq M$ with $M$ an abelian group, Šámal conjectured that a graph admits an $(M,B)$-flow if and only if it admits an $FT_M$ map to the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)$. DeVos conjectured that, whenever there is a graph homomorphism $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)\to\operatorname{Cay}(M',B')$, every graph admitting an $(M,B)$-flow also admits an $(M',B')$-flow. We prove that these conjectures are equivalent and give a counterexample using the Petersen graph.

papers.title: Floating Body Asymptotics via Fractal Strings
papers.abstract: Schütt and Werner associated an almost polygonal planar convex body with a decreasing convex sequence and obtained two-sided estimates for the area removed by its floating body. We reinterpret the gaps of the defining sequence as the lengths of a normalized fractal string. Our main result shows that the area deficit, that is, the difference between the area of the set and its floating body, is comparable to an integral transform of the inner tubular volume of this string. As a consequence, if the string has Minkowski dimension $D$, then the principal power exponent of the area deficit is $1-D/3$. We also derive refinements for regularly varying tube functions, establish a realization criterion extending the almost polygonal case of the theorem of Schütt and Werner, and discuss several examples. As an application, we obtain corresponding asymptotic rates for the expectations and variances of the missed area and the number of vertices of random polygons, including new intermediate behaviors between the classical polygonal and smooth cases.

papers.title: Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher
papers.abstract: A discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network, a classical state-space fact: a fixed linear memory of the running integral and the last error, read out by three trainable weights that map one-to-one to the PID gains. Networks with bounded hidden states, such as LSTMs of any width, only approximate it. Trained only on a one-step physical cost (the expected cost of one transition from a fixed state distribution), with no demonstrations, teacher controller, or known gains, the network solves a strongly convex least-squares problem, so gradient descent converges from any initialization to the unique one-step optimal PID gains; the limit network is that PID, with the same action on every error sequence. Partitioned regression then shows what extra capacity buys. Orthogonal residual features keep these gains and improve on the PID if and only if they correlate with the part of the optimal action outside the PID span. On a nonlinear second-order example the gap is 5.88% of the optimal PID cost, and 4.00% against PID with a bias; no controller can improve on PID by more on this objective. A residual started at a tuned PID begins exactly at that PID; at the one-step optimal PID, a fixed-feature residual's first gradient step lowers the cost if and only if its features can improve on the PID. Experiments confirm the realization, recovery, and gap results to numerical precision. On held-out plants of three families, under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, a residual warm-started at a heavily tuned PID and trained with it lowers the long-horizon cost by 3.5%, 3.5%, and 1.9%, with family-wise 95% bounds excluding zero, also under distribution shift; a post hoc comparison with the PID tuned alone suggests that most of it comes from the recurrent part in two families. The primary endpoint, a gain of at least 5% from a generic PID start, is not met in any family.

papers.title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
papers.abstract: This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for Itô diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem. More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehatμ_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iδ_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$. In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2λ_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2λ_d}$, where $λ_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.

papers.title: MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime
papers.abstract: We study MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to remain positive for a long time when $|θ|>1$, where $θ$ denotes the coupling parameter. We show that, for a fixed starting point, the finite-dimensional distributions of the conditioned process converge and identify the limiting process as a Doob $h$-transform with explicit function $h$. We also obtain precise asymptotics for the corresponding persistence probabilities. The limiting process exhibits qualitatively different behaviour depending on $θ$ and on the support of the innovation distribution. We also determine stationary distributions of the limiting conditioned processes for all $θ\ne 1$.

papers.title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $Π_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.

papers.title: Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang. On the other hand, we provide an example of a smooth projective toric DM stack where this intrinsic window is never a grade restriction window despite the many possible choices. As an application, we demonstrate that reordering and/or taking a subset of an HKKN stratification sometimes changes the grade restriction window and sometimes does not.

papers.title: Formal completions and decompositions of matrix factorization categories of Fano mirrors
papers.abstract: We study the derived categories of matrix factorizations for certain toric Landau--Ginzburg models that are mirror dual to del Pezzo surfaces and Fano threefolds. Some of these models have non-isolated singularities: their critical loci may contain curves and surfaces, possibly with intersecting irreducible components. We handle these cases by studying the potential in the formal neighborhood of each irreducible component of the critical locus. Away from $\operatorname{Sing}(\operatorname{CritLoc}(W)_{\mathrm{red}})$, we construct global formal coordinates and determine the local normal form of the singularity. Near the singular or intersection strata, we analyze how the pieces of the whole connected formal neighborhood are related by localization. This gives explicit decompositions of the derived categories of matrix factorizations after idempotent completion. For the five rank-one pairs $(B_d,V_{4d+2})$, we also compare projective compactifications. The isolated sectors and central-component counts agree for $d=2,3,4,5$ and differ for $d=1$. Equivalence of the distinguished compactified contributions for the remaining matched pairs requires compatible global gluing data or compactified Homological Mirror Symmetry.

papers.title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
papers.abstract: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincaré duality algebras.

papers.title: On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Broué--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.

papers.title: Zero detection via Cox random measures
papers.abstract: Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's ξ function.

papers.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $μ$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $μ$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $μ$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.

papers.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
papers.abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(σ)$ to $L^q(ω)$ for the operator $H_σg(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,dσ$, where $σ$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $ω$ is a $σ$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $κ_{p,q}$ in $C_*\leκ_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $ω$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Osękowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
papers.abstract: We investigate the blow-up behavior of solutions to the semilinear wave equation $$ \partial_t^2 u - \partial_x^2 u = |u|^{p-1}u \ln^a(u^2+2), \quad (x,t)\in \mathbb{R} \times [0,T), $$ with $p > 1$ and $a<0$. While the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. The main obstruction is that known constructions of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. Focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a Lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. This yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. To our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.

papers.title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art neural network verifiers evaluate linear relaxations over axis-aligned bounding boxes. However, verification domains in cyber-physical systems are rarely boxes. Reachability specifications, obstacle-avoidance constraints, and neural Lyapunov certificates typically yield oblique or non-convex polyhedral regions, over which box-based bounds become extremely loose. This paper proposes Fit-LRP (Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes), a framework the implements exact optimization of affine bounds over non-convex domains (represented by unions of polytopes) by solving a sequence of small, low-dimensional linear programs. Our approach seamlessly enhances the final optimization step of LiRPA and $α,\! β$-CROWN branch-and-bound (BaB) algorithms. In BaB verification, approximating oblique constraints with axis-aligned splits causes severe combinatorial blowup and risks non-termination. By optimizing the final affine bound of a nonlinear function over the exact polyhedral state-space constraints our method eliminates box-induced over-approximations, enabling earlier search-tree pruning. On ARCH-COMP and neural Lyapunov benchmarks, Fit-LRP reduces branching on the hardest region by $47\times$, cuts worst-case verification time by $15\times$, and with region-wise partitioning, verifies on a single CPU $6.1\times$ faster than $α,\! β$-CROWN on a GPU.

papers.title: On the algebraic Mackey deformation
papers.abstract: This paper provides a conceptual understanding of the Mackey bijection from the admissible dual of a real reductive group $G$ into the admissible dual of its Cartan motion group $G_0$, by studying the primitive spectrum of a Hecke algebra over $\mathbb{C}[t]$ arising from the contraction of $G$ to $G_0$. If $K$ denotes a maximal compact subgroup of $G$, our approach leads to the following two results: the admissible Mackey bijection is a piecewise homeomorphism, each piece being defined by the length of the lowest $K$-types; the Hecke algebras of $G$ and $G_0$ have, up to $K$-types not exceeding a certain length, the same periodic cyclic homology.

papers.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
papers.abstract: We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite. In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators. We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

papers.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
papers.abstract: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $μ$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $PΓ_N$ generated by a semigroup $Γ_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $PΓ_N$ and that the chain graphs of $PΓ_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $Γ_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(Γ)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(Γ_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.

papers.title: Path Components of Almost Doubly Commuting Fredholm Tuples
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that the Fredholm index classifies the norm-path components of almost doubly commuting Fredholm n-tuples on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space. Using Kasparov's technical theorem, we join each tuple to an essentially normal one by a straight-line Fredholm path and applying the Douglas-Curto theorem.

papers.title: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
papers.abstract: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was previously established by SAT searches of the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound. The lower bound combines derivatives, quadratic products, complementary minors, and extraction modulo a Boolean ideal. Independent finite checks accompany the arguments. $\mathrm{MC}(M_3)=6$ is fully formalized in Lean 4. The kernel-checked proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. Working in dimension $n \ge 2$ throughout the paper, we prove that for symmetric uniformly elliptic operators with bounded measurable coefficients, every bounded open set satisfying the mean value inequality for all integrable subsolutions defined on that set (what we call ``strong mean value sets'') agrees almost everywhere with the canonical set from Caffarelli's construction which has the same center and volume. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ``mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume as this weak mean value ball has a hole of positive measure.

papers.title: K3 surfaces and BHK Mirror symmetry: A counterexample
papers.abstract: For K3 surfaces of BHK type, there are two versions of mirror symmetry that might be applied, namely BHK mirror symmetry and LPK3 mirror symmetry of Dolgachev, which involved choosing a polarizing lattice. It has been conjectured that for a pair of BHK mirror K3 surfaces, one can choose a polarizing lattice as the invariant lattice of some nonsymplectic diagonal symmetry. We provide a counterexample, showing that LPK3 mirror symmetry cannot be realized by polarizing surfaces by the invariant lattice of a diagonal symmetry. However, in our example the polarizing lattice can be realized as the invariant lattice of a permutation symmetry.

papers.title: Analysis of TraceFEM for the Surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard Model
papers.abstract: We analyze a trace finite element method (TraceFEM) for a surface fluid with a stabilization term that filters out Killing vector fields, and use it to discretize the surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard problem in space only. Assuming no geometric error, we show that the discrete inf-sup condition that our method requires is equivalent to the usual condition found in the literature and known to hold for trace Taylor-Hood pairs of arbitrary order in intrinsic dimension two. Inspired by a continuous dependence estimate at the PDE level, we derive error estimates for our scheme in the energy norms, which in turn lead to estimates in $L^2$-norms and, for two-dimensional surfaces, $L^\infty$-norm for the phase variable. To that end, we introduce a $p$-dependent scaling for the normal derivative volume stabilization, and use it to prove new approximation and inverse estimates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-based setting ($p \in [1,\infty]$ for approximation and $p \in [2,\infty]$ for inverse estimates). Finally, we corroborate the analysis with numerical experiments.

papers.title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We develop two hybrid data-driven Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) Reduced-Order Models (ROMs) for the non-stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes Equations (NSEs) with random viscosity. The proposed framework combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) ROMs, spatial filtering, data-driven closure modeling, and the Stochastic Collocation Method (SCM). A key feature is the approximation of the realization-dependent closure term by the closure associated with the expected viscosity. Consequently, a single data-driven closure model constructed from the full-order solution corresponding to the expected viscosity can be reused across all realizations, thereby avoiding the expensive construction of realization-specific closure models. This leads to the Data-Driven Correction UQ ROM (DDC-UQ-ROM) and its physically constrained variant, the Constrained DDC-UQ-ROM (CDDC-UQ-ROM), in which physical constraints are imposed on the data-driven correction model. The proposed methods are evaluated for a two-dimensional (2D) flow past a circular cylinder problem with a 5D random viscosity field, considering mean Reynolds numbers $Re=100$ and $Re=500$, different correlation lengths, and both in-sample and out-of-sample parameter settings. Numerical results show that the DDC-UQ-ROM generally improves upon the standard Galerkin ROM (G-ROM), while the CDDC-UQ-ROM exhibits the most accurate and robust approximation of the benchmark energy evolution across the cases considered. The robustness and accuracy of the CDDC-UQ-ROM are further assessed through statistical error analyses of the first- and second-order energy moments, reduced-training-data experiments, and an indicative comparison of wall-clock computational costs with the full-order UQ calculations.

papers.title: Finiteness properties of Bestvina-Brady kernels for graph products with torsion
papers.abstract: We study Bestvina-Brady kernels associated to graph products whose vertex groups are either infinite cyclic or finite. Using a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ cubical complex constructed by Ruane and Witzel, on which the graph product with defining graph $Γ$ acts, together with an equivariant Morse function, we establish sufficient conditions for homological finiteness properties in terms of the topology of the flag complex $Γ^\blacktriangle$, the subcomplex $Γ^\blacktriangle_\infty$ spanned by the infinite vertices, and the ascending and descending links of certain vertices. We also prove a partial converse, showing that, under additional vanishing hypotheses on homology in the next degree, non-vanishing homology of these complexes obstructs higher finiteness properties of the Bestvina-Brady kernel. The main new features are the presence of finite stabilizers and the resulting additional link conditions, which are expressed in terms of the flag complex of $Γ$. When the finite vertex groups are abelian, we characterize when the kernel has finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, describe the normalizers of its finite subgroups as Bestvina-Brady kernels of smaller graph products, and obtain a criterion for the kernel to be of Bredon type $\underline{\mathrm{FP}}_n$.

papers.title: Pointwise Convergence and Approximation of Matrix-Transform Means of Vilenkin--Fourier Series
papers.abstract: We study convergence, divergence, and approximation of matrix-transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series. For bounded groups, we prove convergence along ${M_n}$ at Vilenkin--Lebesgue points without additional diagonal conditions. For arbitrary bounded or unbounded groups, every regular matrix-transform method admits divergence on any prescribed null set along any increasing sequence. We also obtain $L_p(G_m)$ approximation estimates in terms of the modulus of continuity.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.

papers.title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
papers.abstract: We develop a pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot-Poisson-Nernst-Planck system describing ionic transport in a charged, saturated, and deformable porous medium. The mechanical equations are reformulated in terms of a non-symmetric pseudostress and the solid displacement, while mixed formulations are retained for the Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations. The nonlinear electrostatic and advective couplings are treated in a Banach space setting. The formulation provides direct approximations of the pseudostress, fluxes, and concentration gradients, and permits algebraic reconstruction of the displacement gradient and Cauchy stress. Under block-stability and small-data assumptions, we establish continuous and discrete well-posedness, with poroelastic stability bounds uniform with respect to the first Lame parameter. A conforming Raviart-Thomas discretization, completed by discontinuous polynomials, yields a priori error estimates and convergence rates. For the coupled scheme in two dimensions, we construct a residual-based a posteriori error estimator and establish its reliability under an additional smallness condition on the prescribed data. Local efficiency is proved for polynomial boundary data, with boundary-data oscillation included for general traces. We also describe the estimator modifications for nonhomogeneous displacement and normal-flux data under corresponding stability and solvability hypotheses. Numerical experiments examine convergence of the mixed and reconstructed fields, robustness in the nearly incompressible regime, adaptive refinement, and ionic polarization in a charged porous medium.

papers.title: Almost sure behaviour of empirical measures for intermittent maps whose return time distribution is 1-regularly varying
papers.abstract: In this article we study sets of limit points $\mathcal{L}$ for the sequence of empirical measures of intermittent maps with several equally sticky neutral fixed points. Such intermittent maps come with a parameter $α> 0$ which determines the "stickiness" of the neutral fixed points. When $α\neq 1$, it is known that two different behaviours can occur: either $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely the singleton $\{μ\}$ where $μ$ is an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure; or $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely given by the entire simplex $π\mathcal{S}$ of invariant measures supported at the neutral fixed points. We study the case that $α= 1$ and show that neither of these two behaviours occur and that $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely equal to a star-shaped subset of the simplex $π\mathcal{S}$. Moreover, we show that when slowly varying functions are introduced one can obtain a large range of different behaviours, including both the possible outcomes when $α\neq 1$. Our results apply to a large class of intermittent interval maps as well as parabolic rational maps of the Riemann sphere.

papers.title: Riordan Arrays as Structured Operators for Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Riordan arrays have traditionally been studied as infinite lower-triangular matrices that encode generating-function transformations and combinatorial relationships. This note proposes a complementary direction: using Riordan arrays as structured operators in artificial intelligence and data analysis. For a data sequence with generating function $A(z)$, a Riordan array $(g(z),f(z))$ produces the transformation \[ A(z)\longmapsto g(z)A(f(z)). \] This yields a parameterized family of causal linear operators that combine convolution, substitution, and multiscale mixing. The resulting structure may support parameter-efficient neural-network layers, variable-length sequence models, interpretable recurrent systems, invertible architectures, and models for hierarchical or recursively generated data. We explain what the infinite-dimensional viewpoint does and does not provide, outline several possible architectures, identify theoretical and numerical challenges, and propose an initial experimental program. The aim is not to claim that Riordan arrays are appropriate for all data, but to identify settings in which their algebraic structure supplies a useful inductive bias.

papers.title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.

papers.title: Wasserstein Stability of the Nerve Map
papers.abstract: Given a locally finite open cover of a paracompact space, a subordinate partition of unity defines a map into the geometric realization of the nerve. When the cover is good, the nerve theorem asserts that this map is a homotopy equivalence. In applied topology, one specializes this construction to covers of metric data by open balls centered at finitely many landmarks. The corresponding nerve map represents the data inside the Čech complex, enabling one to pull cohomological or spectral invariants back to the data. Since point cloud data often comes equipped with weights encoding domain-specific importance, we introduce a weighted version of the nerve map and study its stability under perturbations of the landmarks and weights using metrics from optimal transport. Our main result is a Lipschitz stability theorem for the weighted nerve map under a uniform nondegeneracy assumption. We state the bound in terms of a scale-dependent optimal transport distance, and give an example where our estimate is attained. Since this distance is dominated by a multiple of the $1$-Wasserstein distance, Wasserstein stability follows as a corollary. We also give geometric conditions ensuring nondegeneracy, obtain explicit estimates of the Lipschitz constant for closed Riemannian manifolds, and sketch applications to Laplacian eigenvector cascading and Eilenberg--MacLane coordinates.

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: We study how stability and the independence property of the norm formula $\varphi(x,y)=\lVert x+y\rVert$ on a real Banach space relate to the same properties in its complete theory. We construct separable Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ and a separable elementary extension $W$ of $X$. The norm formula is stable on $X$ and has the independence property on $W$, and therefore in $\operatorname{Th}(X)$. It is unstable on $Y$ and has no independence property in any model of $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$. Together with $\ell_2$ and $X\oplus_2Y$, these spaces realize all five possible combinations of stability, instability without the independence property, and the independence property on a space with the presence or absence of the independence property in its complete theory. All five spaces are uniformly convex and $\sqrt3$-isomorphic to Hilbert space. Their norms satisfy the common midpoint estimate $\lVert x\rVert,\lVert y\rVert\leq1 \Longrightarrow \lVert(x+y)/2\rVert^2\leq1-(1/12)\lVert x-y\rVert^2$, and $W$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. The proof for $Y$ uses coordinate truncation and a polynomial bound on threshold patterns for vectors of bounded support. These bounds give finite fat-shattering dimension at each positive scale, from which the complete-theory conclusion follows.

papers.title: Proximal random reshuffling with inexact gradients for nonconvex composite optimization
papers.abstract: We design and justify a proximal inexact random reshuffling method for minimizing sums of the finite average of functions with Lipschitz continuous gradients and lower semicontinuous regularizers that may be nonconvex. Each epoch visits every component once, using inexact gradients with a prescribed tolerance, and ends with a single proximal step. Our analysis is pathwise: it holds for every sequence of permutations and does not depend on how the reshuffling is performed. We show that when the stepsizes and error tolerances satisfy suitable summability conditions, the objective values converge and every accumulation point is stationary. Furthermore, under the Polyak--Łojasiewicz--Kurdyka condition at a single accumulation point and sufficient decrease of stepsizes, the entire sequence has finite length and converges to that point. For polynomial stepsizes and power-type desingularizing functions, we derive convergence rates for objective values and iterates. Finally, faster objective-value rates are derived when the limit is a local minimizer.

papers.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

papers.title: Some families of birational cubic and Verra fourfolds
papers.abstract: We study the birational relationship between cubic fourfolds and Verra fourfolds, which are double covers of the product of two projective planes. We show that in?nitely many divisors in the moduli space of cubic fourfolds containing a plane parametrize cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. Our approach relies on the geometry of quadric surface bundles and their associated K3 surfaces, together with the study of Brauer classes. We also investigate two particularly interesting families, providing explicit geometric descriptions and equations for the associated varieties. In one case, the cubic fourfolds have two planes and the two projections from these planes directly show the existence of birational isomorphisms with Verra fourfolds.

papers.title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
papers.abstract: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

papers.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Kollár. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume. The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Kollár's gluing techniques.

papers.title: Your Hypergradient is Skewed: Antithetic Neumann Estimation for Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization is a core tool in practical machine learning workflows, including hyperparameter tuning, data reweighting, robust learning, reinforcement learning, and imbalanced classification. Hypergradient computation requires the inverse of the inner Hessian, typically estimated via a truncated Neumann series. While existing analyses focus on bias and variance, we show that the product structure of the Neumann series introduces a third source of error: skewness. We identify that, unlike ordinary gradients, whose asymmetry is suppressed by mini-batch averaging, the Neumann estimator amplifies skewness across factors, with the third-moment error growing, under weak contraction, with truncation depth, inner condition number, and per-factor noise asymmetry. This arises in many practical settings such as corrupted labels, outliers, heterogeneous or class-imbalanced datasets. To address this, we introduce the Antithetic Neumann Estimator (ANE), which pairs each Hessian sample with a mirrored counterpart around a reference Hessian and averages the resulting inverse-Hessian estimates. With an exact reference, the antithetic product retains only even-order noise, eliminating all odd-order perturbation terms; with an approximate reference, the residual odd-order contribution is bounded linearly in the reference error. ANE requires only a modification of the Hessian vector step and combines with existing stochastic or variance-reduced bilevel methods. We instantiate ANE-SGD and ANE-VR, the latter adding recursive variance reduction. Across robust regression, data cleaning, offline reinforcement learning, and imbalanced classification, ANE-based methods improve on stochastic and variance-reduced baselines on every task (20 seeds each), lowering loss by 4 to 25% relative to the best baseline; the largest gains, on robust regression, are a 25% lower test loss and a 54% higher test r-squared.

papers.title: Sharp Lower Bounds for Parallel Log-Concave Sampling
papers.abstract: How many rounds of parallel queries are needed to sample from a smooth, strongly log-concave distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$? For every fixed condition number $κ\in (1, \infty)$, we prove that any sampler making polynomially many queries per round requires $Ω_κ(\log d)$ rounds to achieve constant total variation error in the worst case. The lower bound holds even if queries return derivatives of all orders. Together with the first-order parallel Picard algorithm of \cite{zhou2025parallel}, this establishes a depth complexity of $Θ_κ(\log d)$ for parallel log-concave sampling with $\operatorname{poly}(d)$ width. We then study centered Gaussian targets to understand how much width is needed at a given depth. From \cite{chewi2023query,zhou2026complexitygaussiansampling}, it is known that either one round of width $d$ or $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtκ \log d)$ rounds of constant width suffice for first-order Gaussian sampling. At fixed $κ$ we characterize the depth-width tradeoff interpolating between these regimes: when using $ \lceil c \log d\rceil$ rounds, if $0 < c < c_\star(κ)$ then the optimal width at constant TV error is $\widetildeΘ(d^{1-c/c_\star(κ)})$, while if $c \geq c_\star(κ)$ then it is $Θ_κ(1)$. Here, $c_\star(κ)$ is an explicit constant with $c_\star(κ) \sim \sqrtκ / 8$ as $κ\to \infty$.

papers.title: Conflict-Free Cuts: Exploring the Boundaries of Tractability
papers.abstract: A conflict-free cut of a host graph $G$ is an edge cut containing no conflicting pair of edges. The conflicts are specified by a conflict graph $\widehat G$ whose vertex set is $E(G)$. The conflict-free cut problem asks if the given instance $(G, \widehat G)$ has a conflict-free cut. When restricted to planar $G$ and 1-regular $\widehat G$, the problem is polynomial time solvable when $G$ has maximum degree 4, but NP-complete already at maximum degree 5. We study the complexity of conflict-free cut problem under restrictions on the degrees of $G$, the components of $\widehat G$, and the locality of the conflicts. A conflict is local if its two edges share an endpoint in $G$. We prove the following results. * For $Δ(\widehat G)\le1$, a directed-cycle formulation gives a polynomial-time algorithm when $|E(G)|\le2|V(G)|$, hence for maximum degree four. The problem is NP-complete on $5$-regular hosts with exactly $1$-regular conflicts. * For $Δ(\widehat G)\le1$, we give a constructive FPT algorithm in $s_4(G)=\sum_v\max\{0,d_G(v)-4\}$, single-exponential for planar hosts. For arbitrary conflicts, we give an XP algorithm in $η=\max\{0,|E(\widehat G)|-|V(G)|\}$. * On $4$-regular hosts, local exactly $2$-regular conflicts with components $C_3,C_4$ give NP-completeness. For local conflicts at maximum degree four, pair or triangle components separately permit polynomial algorithms, but mixing them gives NP-completeness. We classify cases where $\widehat G$ is a union of cliques. * An $a$-COC is a vertex set whose deletion leaves components of order at most $a$. For local conflicts, the problem is FPT in the minimum $2$-COC size, but NP-complete with a supplied $3$-COC of size six. Without locality, hardness holds with a supplied $2$-COC of size six. Both hardness results use exactly $1$-regular conflicts.

papers.title: Normality in generalized Rudin spaces
papers.abstract: In \cite{Kojman2026}, Kojman generalized Mary Ellen Rudin's construction of a ZFC Dowker space to larger cardinals and gave a pcf-theoretic condition ensuring that the resulting spaces are collectionwise normal. A subsequent manuscript by Eisworth, Kojman, Lambie-Hanson, and Marun \cite{EKLM2026} develops the theory further and leaves open whether these generalized Rudin spaces can fail to be normal. We answer this question by proving that, for cardinals $μ<δ$ with $\operatorname{cf}(δ)=\aleph_0$, the generalized Rudin space $X(μ,δ)$ is normal if and only if $\operatorname{pp}(ν)<δ$ for every cardinal $ν\in(μ,δ)$ with $\operatorname{cf}(ν)=\aleph_0$. Given this characterization, known consistency results provide consistent examples of nonnormal generalized Rudin spaces.

papers.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
papers.abstract: In pre-deployment testing of AI systems such as AI agents, a developer can often deal with known failure modes (e.g., leaking API keys, deleting important databases, or installing a malicious package) by implementing fixes or making contingency plans for when the same issue might occur again. What is more challenging are the unknown unknowns: the unseen failure modes that haven't surfaced during testing. The decision to stop testing and deploy therefore faces an inherent tradeoff: continue testing to observe more behaviors, at the cost of time and resources, or stop testing and deploy, at the risk of failure modes remaining undiscovered. How then does the developer decide when they have tested enough? To answer this, we develop an algorithm that certifies when the probability of observing an unseen failure mode is sufficiently small. The algorithm constructs an anytime-valid upper confidence sequence on this quantity, so the developer can repeatedly test a system, inspect the bound, and decide to stop when it falls below a chosen threshold without invalidating the statistical guarantee. Our problem can be interpreted as a sequential variant of the missing-mass estimation problem which gave rise to the classic Good-Turing estimator (Good, 1953). On SWE-Chat, a dataset of real-world coding agent traces (Baumann et al., 2026), we implement our procedure and show that it achieves tighter upper bounds than a simple multiple-testing corrected Good-Turing baseline, and even dominates a fixed-horizon (non-multiple-testing-corrected) Good-Turing upper confidence bound, which is not anytime valid. Additionally, to better match realistic evaluation pipelines, we extend our method to handle sampling from a different task distribution and imperfect automated failure labeling.

papers.title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
