The main result of this article provides methods for constructing nearly computable numbers with additional properties. The main result is proved by an infinite injury priority argument. Using these methods, we construct nearly computable numbers with several different additional properties: - a nearly computable number that is not divergence bounded computable, - for any left-computable number $α$ that is neither in the least nor in the highest Solovay degree, a left-computable, nearly computable number that is Solovay incomparable with $α$, - a nearly computable number $γ$ that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers but has the property that for any two left-computable numbers $α$ and $β$ wih $γ=α-β$ both $α$ and $β$ are Martin-Löf random. We also look at two classes of nearly computable numbers: the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ of differences of real numbers that are nearly computable and left-computable, and the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$ of nearly computable numbers that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers. Both classes form real closed fields, in fact, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is closed under computable functions with open domain that are Lipschitz continuous or differentiable. Finally, we show that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is a proper subset of $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$.

papers.title: Higher order schemes for the numerical solution of integro-differential equation-based age-of-infection models with time-dependent contact rates
papers.abstract: Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging. Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. The resulting numerical schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulations of IDE-based epidemic models with general sojourn time distributions and changing contact patterns.

papers.title: Growth function of the cactus groups
papers.abstract: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous First-order Differential Operator Representations of $E_6$ and Graded Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We realize the restricted dual Verma modules of arbitrary highest weight for the complex simple Lie algebra of type $E_6$ by inhomogeneous first-order differential operators in $36$ variables. The construction is obtained by applying Xu's functor (2016) to the full conformal oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{o}(10)$. We construct polynomial bases for all six fundamental $E_6$-modules and obtain a finite spanning set for every finite-dimensional irreducible $E_6$-module $V(λ)$. The degree in $16$ selected variables gives $V(λ)$ a grading over the symmetric algebra of the opposite abelian nilradical. We compute its Hilbert series and graded Betti numbers, and verify the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks conjecture for this family. The minimal graded free resolution of $V(λ)$ is pure precisely when $λ$ is a nonnegative multiple of the Weyl vector of $E_6$. Among nonzero dominant integral $λ$'s, the minimum total Betti number is $435204$, attained exactly at two minuscule weights $ω_1$ and $ω_6$.

papers.title: Small cells in great-circle arrangements
papers.abstract: We study the areas of the cells determined by an arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ of $n$ distinct great circles on the unit sphere, with no three concurrent. Let $m(\mathcal{A})$ and $M(\mathcal{A})$ denote the smallest and largest cell areas, respectively. Our first result is the bound \[ m(\mathcal{A})\le \frac{C_*+O(n^{-3/4})}{n^2}, \qquad C_*=7.0666071493\ldots , \] where the implied constant is absolute. This improves the coefficient $π^2$ obtained from classical polygonal perimeter estimates. We also prove that $M(\mathcal{A})/m(\mathcal{A})>13$ for all sufficiently large $n$, improving the bound $7.43$ of L.~Fejes Tóth. The main tool is a perimeter inequality for planar polygons which takes account of their exterior angles. We combine this with a positive semidefinite kernel on the sphere and use gnomonic projection to obtain bounds for spherical cells.

papers.title: The Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
papers.abstract: We prove the Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $Λ_1\left(Ω\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 λ_1^{\mathrm D}\left(Ω\right)$, where $λ_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{ν,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_ν$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.

papers.title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
papers.abstract: Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. Reynolds-number-dependent initial conditions are constructed with a boundary layer of Prandtl thickness that converge in the energy norm to an analytic, stationary Euler flow, while the associated Prandtl system develops a finite-time singularity. Highly resolved simulations show boundary-layer detachment and departures from Prandtl scaling, yet provide numerical evidence that the Navier--Stokes solutions continue to converge to the Euler flow over the simulated time interval. In particular, the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and the time-averaged energy dissipation both scale approximately as $Re^{-1/2}$, consistently with established convergence criteria. Although the detached vortices become more numerous and intense as the Reynolds number increases, their characteristic size and occupied area appear to decrease. These observations suggest how boundary-layer detachment and the breakdown of the Prandtl description can coexist with convergence to a smooth Euler flow.

papers.title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
papers.abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincaré map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

papers.title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
papers.abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

papers.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
papers.abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

papers.title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
papers.abstract: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.

papers.title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,dμ=0 \] for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis. We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if \[ \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,dμ= O(r^d) \] for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.

papers.title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constants
papers.abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge2$ that is not a power of two there are constants $c_n>0$ and $B_n>2$ such that $s(C_n^r)\ge c_nB_n^r$ for all $r\ge1$. For powers of two, Harborth's formula gives growth rate exactly $2$. For the remaining even exponents, the previous lower bounds were of order $r2^r$. When $n=2m$ with $m\ge3$ odd, we prove the transfer inequality \[ A_n(H\oplus C_n^5)\ \ge\ 12\,A_n(H\oplus C_n)+8\,A_n(H\oplus C_m), \] where $A_n(G)$ is the maximal length of a sequence over $G$ without an $n$-term zero-sum subsequence and $H$ is any finite abelian group whose exponent divides $n$. The transfer extends a configuration of Elsholtz to twenty full cyclic fibers. Combined with a nine-point binary construction for $2m$-term zero-sums over $C_m^r$, it gives bases at least $2.0341$ that tend to $2.0394\ldots$; combined with a finite-field construction, it gives $s(C_6^r)\ge c\cdot 2.0491^r$. For exponents divisible by $4$ that are not powers of two, we obtain a base above two from a weighted random construction on the eighteen-point configuration of Wang and Zeng.

papers.title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
papers.abstract: We prove that the collection of all cluster boundaries of near-critical site percolation (with a fixed parameter) on the triangular lattice has a unique scaling limit in the loop-ensemble space, as the mesh size tends to 0. This answers a problem proposed by Camia, Fontes and Newman (2006). Using this, we also prove that near-critical percolation exploration path in a disk converges in distribution to a continuous path as the mesh size goes to 0. The main idea of our proof is to construct the cut-off loop ensembles under the near-critical coupling, based on the enhanced networks and the quad-crossing scaling limits of near-critical percolation constructed by Garban, Pete and Schramm (2018); the proof also relies on the study of the geometry of cluster chains. Some properties of the limiting loop ensemble, including rotation invariance, scale covariance and finite chaining, are established. Moreover, a few applications of our scaling-limit result and proof strategy are discussed.

papers.title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
papers.abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

papers.title: The Calderón Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $ρ\in C^1(\overlineΩ)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-Δ+P^2ρ-ω^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-Δ+P^2ρ$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.

papers.title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
papers.abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(Δ=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+Δ)\) is nef and big, then \((X,Δ)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata. We construct such a curve from a free Campana curve by attaching to it free rational curves which intersect positively with divisors that span the cone of effective divisors, and smooth the resulting comb.

papers.title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
papers.abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/Γ$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

papers.title: Volume asymptotics for a family of hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
papers.abstract: For the family $\{\mathcal{M}_{g,k}\}_{g\geqslant k\geqslant 0}$ of orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary and cusps introduced by R.~Frigerio, B.~Martelli, and C.~Petronio, the volume of the manifolds depends only on the non-negative integer parameters $g$ and $k$; thus the volume function $Vol(g,k)$ is well defined. The main result of the paper is an asymptotic description of this function: it is approximated by a linear function of $g$ and $k$ whose coefficients are explicitly expressed in terms of the volumes of the regular ideal tetrahedron and the regular ideal octahedron; moreover, the volume does not exceed the linear approximation by a difference of order $O(1/g)$. As consequences, three theorems comparing volumes are obtained: monotonicity under coordinatewise increase of the parameters, estimates for the passage from parameter $g$ to $g+1$, and monotonicity along lines of constant complexity $g+k$. For small values of the parameters, approximate values of the volumes are computed and collected in a table used in verifying the cases $g<8$.

papers.title: Moving Cut Loci and Gaussian Fluctuations of Intrinsic Huber Means on Compact Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: Moving cut loci can change the limiting covariance of sample Huber means even when the cut locus of the population mean has probability zero. On a closed connected Riemannian manifold, we prove that the averaged logarithm field is $C^1$ near a point $m$ whenever the sampling law has a continuous density near its cut locus. The result holds for every continuous weight depending only on the observation, and the covariant derivative includes an explicit integral over the regular cut locus. When $m$ is a Huber mean for a fixed positive threshold, assume that the distance to $m$ has no atom at that threshold. The Hessian of the population risk then equals the expected pointwise Hessian minus a positive semidefinite cut locus correction. If $m$ is unique and this Hessian is positive definite, every measurable selection of global minimizers for i.i.d. samples satisfies a tangent-space central limit theorem. The cut loci of points in a ball of radius $δ$ sweep out a region of volume $O(δ)$, uniformly in the centre. These results establish the volume and integrability conditions previously assumed in a central limit theorem for intrinsic Fréchet means. At each fixed centre, the volume measure on this region, divided by $δ$, converges weakly to an explicit measure on the regular cut locus. The Huber correction vanishes exactly when the region swept out about $m$ has probability $o(δ)$.

papers.title: Isomorphic embeddings of $L_q(0,1)$ into Lorentz--Schatten ideals
papers.abstract: Let \(0<p,q<\infty\). We prove \[ L_q(0,1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal C_{p,q} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q=2. \] As a consequence, we obtain, for all \(0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2<\infty\), \[ L_{p_1,q_1}(0,1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal C_{p_2,q_2} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p_1=q_1=2. \]

papers.title: Robust High-Order BUG Integrators without Basis Augmentation
papers.abstract: We develop robust high-order basis-update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation without basis augmentation or rank truncation. The basis and core updates use the same approximate increment. We establish a two-sided relaxed-exactness estimate that controls the error in the low-rank approximation by the increment error. Under the stated assumptions on the vector field and its normal component, sufficiently accurate increments yield local and global error bounds whose constants and step-size restrictions are independent of small singular values. Using explicit Runge--Kutta increments, we obtain robust orders two, three, and four for the explicit midpoint method, Heun's third-order method, and Merson's fourth-order method, respectively. Every internal stage and final approximation has rank at most the prescribed rank $r$. We also prove that these orders are retained under arbitrary basis augmentation followed by best rank-$r$ SVD truncation at the internal stages and the endpoint, without a separate assumption on the truncation error. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence orders and show comparable performance with and without augmentation.

papers.title: Self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
papers.abstract: We prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $C^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ Hölder regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. This class includes the Camassa--Holm and Degasperis--Procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. In the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized Hunter--Saxton (gHS) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. Consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. To handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the gHS family. The key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. We identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. This leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp Hölder regularity. The theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.

papers.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
papers.abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the coefficients in these expansions, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$.

papers.title: A Chord-Arc Estimate for Graphical Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove an interior chord-arc estimate for graphical hypersurfaces without an a priori gradient bound, which is not restricted to balls on the scale of their curvature. As a main application we derive an in-radius lower bound depending on the curvature which then also implies Heinz-type estimates for minimal graphs and uniform area bounds for graphical hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we prove that every finite $p$-group of nilpotency class at most $(p+5)/2$ satisfies the Quadratic Conjecture. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $(p+5)/2$.

papers.title: On Star Monotone Operators: Theory and Applications
papers.abstract: Introduced by Solodov and Svaiter \cite{SS}, star monotone operators have repeatedly appeared as a sufficient condition ensuring global convergence of first-order algorithms, without requiring full monotonicity. Yet, despite this recurring role, a systematic study of the class itself has been missing from the literature. This paper fills that gap with the first comprehensive treatment of star monotone operators, a class that strictly encompasses monotone and pseudomonotone operators with nonempty zero sets, together with operators that are strongly quasimonotone along rays and satisfy a radial nondegeneracy condition. We develop basic calculus rules, existence and uniqueness results for zeros, global metric subregularity, and precise structural relationships with classical monotonicity notions. We further demonstrate the versatility of star monotonicity through a Clarke subdifferential characterization of nonsmooth star quasiconvexity, applications to Minty and Stampacchia variational inequalities, linear convergence guarantees for subgradient-type methods, and separable operators related to the Debreu--Koopmans problem.

papers.title: Connection-twisted modules and logarithmic twisted modules of vertex algebras
papers.abstract: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for $\mathbb{C}$-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let $G$ be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra $V$ by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of $\nabla$-twisted $V$-modules and the category of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, where $\nabla$ is a regular singular $\mathfrak{g}$-connection and $g\in G$ is its monodromy. For symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras, we explicitly compute the commutation relations and the action of the Virasoro algebra on connection-twisted modules, recovering the formulas obtained by Feigin and Lentner \cite{FL24,FL25}.

papers.title: Subgradient and Stochastic Finite-Difference Methods for Constrained Strongly Quasiconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a projected subgradient method for solving quasiconvex minimization problems. By employing the Clarke subdifferential, we prove that the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm converges to a solution of the minimization problem when the objective function is locally Lipschitz continuous and strongly quasiconvex in the sense of Polyak, under the same assumptions required for convex functions with the convex subdifferential. Moreover, we derive explicit convergence rate estimates for both the iterates and objective function values. In particular, compared with the corresponding results for nonsmooth, locally Lipschitz, strongly convex optimization, our analysis replaces strong convexity with strong quasiconvexity while preserving the order of the convergence rate, thereby extending the guarantees to a class of possibly nonconvex objective functions. In addition, we investigate a stochastic finite-difference scheme for minimizing a strongly quasiconvex function subject to inequality constraints defined by strongly quasiconvex functions, and establish a convergence rate of order $O(k^{-1/4})$, consistent with known complexity bounds for stochastic zeroth-order methods.

papers.title: A Monotone Meshfree-Particle Method for Mean Field Games on Scattered Point Clouds
papers.abstract: We develop a monotone meshfree--particle method for mean field games (MFGs). We discretize the backward Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation on a fixed scattered cloud, transport the forward Fokker--Planck law with reflected and killed particles, and close the fictitious-play loop by interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation. Monotonicity is imposed row by row on two-dimensional clouds. Each row combines a positive generalized finite difference Laplacian with a nonnegative decomposition of the drift along rays to surrounding visible neighbors, with mirror images at reflecting walls, and every fixed-policy matrix is an M-matrix for arbitrary cell-Péclet number. We prove a discrete comparison principle and, on polygons with re-entrant corners included, that one HJB solve at a prescribed density converges to the viscosity solution off the boundary vertices, for convex Hamiltonians of at most quadratic growth under a structure condition. On a two-room floor plan with re-entrant door jambs, the computed HJB solutions converge to exact ones. A source-free exact MFG tests the fully coupled computation. At matched degrees of freedom on a grid domain, the meshfree HJB solve has a larger $L^2$ error and a smaller $L^\infty$ error than a five-point finite-difference solve, and is about twice as expensive including the stencil construction. On a non-convex evacuation game, the interior nodes of nine clouds receive monotone rows, apart from a few next to the boundary vertices that copy a neighbor.

papers.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
papers.abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterised by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.

papers.title: Domination in token graphs of graphs with domination number two
papers.abstract: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two $k$-subsets adjacent if and only if their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper we study the domination number of $F_k(G)$ for graphs $G$ whose domination number $γ(G)$ is at least two, with a primary focus on the case $γ(G)=2$. For $k=2$, we give an upper bound for $γ(F_2(G))$ in terms of a dominating pair of $G$, and show that this bound is sharp for every double star $S_{a,b}$ with $2\le a\le b$; moreover, we determine the exact value for every double star, namely $γ(F_2(S_{a,b}))=2a+b-1$ for $1\le a\le b$. We also prove that $γ(F_2(G))\ge\lceil n/2\rceil$ for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $γ(G)\geq2$, with equality for the graphs with the maximum number of edges among those with $γ(G)\geq2$. Then, we focus on complete bipartite graphs; we give upper bounds for $γ(F_2(K_{r,t}))$ that match the exact values independently established in recent work, together with a short proof that $γ(F_2(K_{2,n-2}))=n-2$. For $k\ge3$ we show that $γ(F_k(K_{2,n-2}))$ equals, up to lower-order terms, the Turán number $T(n-2,k,k-1)$, and we determine $γ(F_3(K_{2,n-2}))$ exactly, obtaining $T(n-2,3,2) +n-4=n^2/4+O(n)$; for $k=4$, determining the leading constant is related to the still-open Turán conjecture for 3-uniform hypergraphs. Finally, for $n\geq 12$ even, we prove that $γ\left(F_3(K_{n/2,n/2})\right) =\frac{7}{48}n^2+O(n)$.

papers.title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
papers.abstract: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis. Furthermore, by considering fixed dilations, we investigate the associated dimensional generating functions and derive rational forms for the generating functions of the lattice points in the $m$-th dilates of the polytopes.

papers.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
papers.abstract: We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $Φ$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_τΨ<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_τ(Φ,Ψ)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,τ}(Φ,Ψ)$, and the associated exact sequence. The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $Ψ$ is the Carlitz module, $N_Φ=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.

papers.title: On the Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality in Pseudo-Euclidean Space
papers.abstract: In a pseudo-Euclidean space, the Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz inequality generalization is derived and studied. Complex vector space is considered as well. Generalizations of angles and dihedral angles in these spaces are studied.

papers.title: On the moduli of distinct covering systems
papers.abstract: In 2022, Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba proved that the least common multiple of the moduli in any distinct covering system with odd moduli is divisible by $9$ or $15$. We strengthen this necessary condition to divisibility by $45$ and prove that the minimum modulus of an odd distinct covering system is at most $9$. For arbitrary distinct moduli, we lower the upper bound of Balister et al.\ on the minimum modulus from $616000$ to $14000$. For distinct squarefree moduli, we lower the upper bound of $118$ obtained by Cummings, Filaseta, and Trifonov in 2025 to $7$. Our proofs combine the distortion method with a joint comparison based on directional convexity. The comparison uses independent random exponents to bound expectations of convex functions of sums of indicators of residue classes, while retaining the restrictions on the allowed moduli. A sharper bound for the conditional density on each fibre further improves the estimates for the subsequent stages of the distortion process.

papers.title: Solvability of $L^2$-Neumann Problems for Fractional Laplace Equations on Bounded Lipschitz Domains
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq2$, $s\in(0,1)$, and $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. In this paper, we study the solvability of the fractional Neumann problem \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{aligned} (-Δ)^su&=0 & & \text{in}\ \ Ω,\\ \mathcal{N}_s u&=g & & \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ, \end{aligned}\right. \end{equation*} with $\mathcal{N}_s$ denoting the nonlocal normal derivative in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$ and $g:=a_sq$, where $a_s(z):=(1-s)\frac{δ(z)^{-s}}{1+δ(z)^{n+s}}$ with $δ(z):=\mathrm{dist\,}(z,\partialΩ)$ for any $z\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$, and $q\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,a_s\,dz)$ satisfies $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ}a_sq\,dz=0$. For the weak solution $u$, we obtain the non-tangential maximal function estimate \begin{equation*} \left\|\left(δ^{1-s}|\nabla u|\right)^*\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}, \end{equation*} where, for any function $f$ on $Ω$, $f^\ast$ denotes the non-tangential maximal function of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$. This result extends the classical $L^2$ solvability theory for the Neumann problem of Laplace equations on bounded Lipschitz domains to the setting of fractional Neumann problems, and also provides a Neumann counterpart to the $L^2$-solvability result for fractional Dirichlet problems established by Colombo, Fernández-Real and Ros-Oton \cite{CFR26}. In addition, we prove the fractional Sobolev estimate $\|u\|_{H^{3s/2}(Ω)}\leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}$ and the weighted gradient estimate \begin{equation*} \left(\int_Ωδ^{2-3s}|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)^{\frac12} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}. \end{equation*}

papers.title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
papers.abstract: Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls. For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

papers.title: Secular Dynamics and the LFL for $β$ Corner Process
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Gaussian $β$ corner process, whose edge particles are known to converge to the Tracy-Widom $β$ law. We study the almost sure behaviour of the extrema of the whole trajectory of the edge particles and establish a law of fractional logarithm (LFL) for the corner process for every fixed $β>0$, extending the previous known results in the case $β=1,2$. Our proof relies on the upward Gamma and downward Dirichlet secular equations, which can be regarded as two discrete dynamics to form the corner processes. The secular dynamics are used in both the correlation estimate and the decorrelation estimate, which are known as two key steps of proving LFL in \cite{BCEHK-LFL} for the Wigner minor process. Especially, in the decorrelation part, they are used as discrete analogues of the continuous Dyson Brownian motion.

papers.title: Well-Posedness for the Cauchy Problem with Free Boundary in Half-Space Arising from Combustion Problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the local-in-time well-posedness of an obstacle problem arising from a combustion model. The equation under consideration is a linear inhomogeneous heat equation on the moving domain $(s(t),\infty)$, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet and inhomogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Our main result establishes the existence and uniqueness of a positive classical solution. Although several results are known for the homogeneous heat equation, much less is known about the inhomogeneous case. We show that the boundary function $s(t)$ is $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuous in time when the forcing term has a singularity of order $O(1/\sqrt{t})$ as $t \to 0$. We also prove that if both the initial data and the forcing term are smooth, then $s$ has higher regularity than $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuity.

papers.title: Relative-energy stabilization of an irreversible port-Hamiltonian tubular reactor
papers.abstract: This paper develops a relative-energy control approach for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular reactor around a spatially nonuniform stationary profile. The starting point is a thermodynamic duality between the entropy-based availability used in earlier reactor control and the relative Hamiltonian induced by the irreversible port-Hamiltonian representation. Under physically interpretable stability conditions---positive heat capacity, positive compressibility and positive compositional susceptibility---the Hamiltonian density is shown to be strictly convex, while the corresponding entropy representation is strictly concave. The resulting relative Hamiltonian decomposes into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing contributions and yields an exact relative-energy balance in which irreversible dissipation is separated from profile-dependent terms. This structure leads to a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback that injects thermal damping without cancelling the nonlinear PDE dynamics. A continuous coercivity condition gives a local a-priori decay estimate for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions, while a composite energy functional provides an exponential estimate for the linearized closed-loop initial-boundary value problem. Structure-preserving PFEM simulations are used to verify the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.

papers.title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
papers.abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $τ\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $τ\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Rayleigh--Taylor instability and Hadamard ill-posedness for the rotating free-boundary Euler equations in three dimensions
papers.abstract: The free-boundary incompressible Euler equations linearized at a rigidly rotating equilibrium on the flat product of the unit disk and a circle are Hadamard ill-posed in Sobolev spaces of order at least two. The equilibrium violates the Taylor sign condition, under which local well-posedness is known. Eulerian linearization retaining free-surface advection reduces the spectral problem to a modified Bessel equation; Rouché's theorem yields an unstable root whose real part grows as the square root of the axial frequency. Eigenmode Sobolev norms grow as the corresponding power of that frequency. Rescaling gives data tending to zero whose solutions are unbounded at any prescribed positive time. At zero axial frequency the analysis recovers Ebin's rotating-disk rate (Communications in Partial Differential Equations 12 (1987), 1175--1201). The product lift gives nonlinear ill-posedness on the invariant class of axially independent data.

papers.title: Sharp weighted bounds for reverse fractional integral operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the one-weight reverse fractional integral operators \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^q(w^q)}\geq C_w\|f\|_{L^p(w^p)} \] holds for all nonnegative measurable functions $f$, with $\frac ns<p<1$ and $\frac1q=\frac1p-\frac sn$, if and only if $w^{p/(1-p)}\in A_{\frac{p(s-n)}{n(1-p)}}$. Furthermore, we show the lower bound \[ C_w\gtrsim_{n,s,p}[w]_{p,q}^{\min\left\{\frac{p(n-s)}{n(1-p)},\frac{p(n-s)}{sp-n}\right\}}, \] and the exponent is sharp. We also investigate when the reverse weak-type estimate \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-s},\infty}(w^{\frac{n}{n-s}})}\geq \frac{n}{s}\,v_n^{(n-s)/n}[w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}]^{(n-s)/n}_{A_1}\|f\|_{L^1(w)} \] holds if and only if $w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}\in A_1$.

papers.title: Abelian covers and the index of the centre in a group
papers.abstract: Let $h(n)$ be the largest number of abelian subgroups needed to cover a group in which every set of more than $n$ elements contains two distinct elements that commute, and let $ζ(n)$ be the largest index of the centre under the same constraint. Erdős asked for the growth of $h$, Neumann proved that both quantities are finite, and Pyber bounded both $ζ$ and $h$ exponentially. We determine $h(n)$ for every positive integer $n$ and prove that $h(n)=1+\sqrt{ζ(n)}$ whenever the constraint admits a nonabelian group. The covers are built directly from the commutator geometry of a scalar quotient, and the comparison with $ζ$ is made afterwards. Beyond finitely many small cases, both maxima are attained by the same groups, those isoclinic to an extraspecial $2$-group of order $2^{1+2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}$, confirming Pyber's prediction for the central index in this range.

papers.title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
papers.abstract: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_Δ$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $Δ$. We then show this is equivalent to $X_w$ being cut out of the complete flag variety by particular inclusion conditions on the pieces of the flag. We prove these complexes are vertex decomposable, and are Cohen-Macaulay precisely when $X_w$ is smooth. We then give a closed formula for the Poincaré polynomial of $X_w$. For unions $X_W$, pattern avoidance is necessary but no longer sufficient, and we prove a necessary and sufficient condition we call prunable that describes how the individual complexes associated to each $w\in W$ may be glued in the union. Quotients of $R_n$ by squarefree monomial ideals appear naturally in the Adams-Reiner conjecture on resolutions of Stanley-Reisner rings over certain parameter rings. We prove their conjecture for a family of simplicial complexes that includes the doubly-pruned complexes.

papers.title: Strict Monotonicity of the First Positive Steklov Eigenvalue on Eccentric Spherical Shells in Every Dimension
papers.abstract: For $d\ge2$, consider the region between two nested spheres of fixed radii, with the inner sphere translated a distance $\varepsilon$ from the outer center. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Steklov problem, with the spectral boundary condition imposed on both spheres, decreases strictly with $\varepsilon$ throughout the noncontact interval. This settles the planar monotonicity conjecture formulated by Nigam and establishes its higher-dimensional counterparts. In dimension two we use a double-center holomorphic expansion and a pair of positive compact coefficient operators. For every $d\ge3$, solid Gegenbauer harmonics yield analogous axisymmetric and transverse operators, with a positive rank-one monopole correction. Weighted angular-mode comparison for $d\ge3$ and a direct matrix comparison for $d=2$ identify the first positive eigenvalue as the unique level-one crossing of an associated spectral radius. The first eigenspace has dimension $d$ in the concentric case and dimension one for every nonconcentric configuration. Convergence and reconstruction estimates justify the coefficient reductions at the two boundaries.

papers.title: Frank-Wolfe Theorems for Mixed Integer Quadratic Optimization
papers.abstract: The Frank-Wolfe theorem states that a quadratic function bounded from below on a polyhedron attains its infimum. We study when this remains true in the presence of integer variables, for sets defined by quadratic inequalities. Our main result is a complete classification for sets defined by convex quadratic inequalities with rational coefficients and a rational affine hull, a condition that holds for all full- dimensional sets. One integer variable never destroys attainment: if every rational quadratic objective that is bounded from below attains its infimum over the set, even after adding rational linear constraints, the same holds with one integer variable. In dimension at most 2, integer variables never destroy attainment. In dimension at least 3 and with two or more integer variables, attainment holds for every such objective if and only if the set has bounded curvature, that is, it is bounded except along directions in which all constraints are linear. Without convexity, these results remain valid, except that bounded curvature is no longer necessary. Moreover, integer variables can destroy attainment only if there are at least two of them and at least one continuous variable. The result for one integer variable follows from a lifting theorem, which also extends known results for cubic objectives and convex polynomial constraints. Finally, for convex constraints and rational data, attainment holds when the objective is bounded from above, convex, or quasi-convex over a full-dimensional convex set containing the feasible region.

papers.title: Positivity in symplectic groups and electrical networks
papers.abstract: We study the relation between electrical positivity introduced by Lam and Pylyavskyy $[9]$ and total positivity of symplectic matrices arising from circular planar electrical networks. A particularly convenient framework for our purpose is provided by a construction of an embedding of electrical network into the positive Lagrangian Grassmannian, see Section $1.1$. Employing this technique, we demonstrate that mentioned below two types of positivity do not coincide, see Theorem $2.2$. In Section $3$ we also derive explicit rational formulas recovering the parameters of the factorization from our symplectic matrix entries and minors, and prove uniqueness under explicit nonvanishing conditions.

papers.title: A symmetry on Young tableaux with walls and holes
papers.abstract: The Pons--Batle conjecture on tree-child networks was regarded as a specific and challenging problem in the phylogenetics community. We found an unexpected weighted symmetry for a class of three-row Young tableaux with walls and holes. This weighted symmetry implies the Fuchs--Yu identity, which together with the bijection of Chang, Fuchs, Liu, Wallner, and Yu leads to a simple proof of the Pons--Batle conjecture. We construct an involutive proof of this symmetry via introducing decorated binary networks as an intermediate structure. We also provide an elementary proof of this weighted symmetry using recurrence relations.

papers.title: RPX: Certifying Agent-Generated MILP Reformulations at Scale
papers.abstract: We present RPX, an independent certificate checker for AI-generated reformulations of mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). RPX verifies that every feasible solution of either the original or the reformulated model can be converted into a feasible solution of the other with no worse objective value. This guarantees equal optimal values and enables solution recovery in the original variables. The checker derives the required checks directly from both models and verifies the certificate using exact arithmetic and reusable reconstruction rules. RPX certifies an agent-generated reformulation for each of the 240 instances in MIPLIB 2017 Benchmark v2. The source models contain up to 27.3 million matrix nonzeros. The median time to decode and check a certificate is 0.312 s, with a 95th percentile of 10.1 s.

papers.title: On piecewise-regular and quasirational functions
papers.abstract: We fully characterize piecewise-regular functions on nonsingular real algebraic varieties in terms of continuous quasirational functions. We also obtain extension theorem for piecewise-regular functions defined on closed semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n.$

papers.title: Multiple-relaxation-time vectorial lattice Boltzmann schemes for incompressible flow: second-order consistency and parameter selection
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze multiple-relaxation-time vectorial lattice Boltzmann schemes for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two and three space dimensions. The same moment-space relaxation matrix is applied to all physical components, with independent rates for the flux, stress, and energy moments. A Maxwell expansion organized by moment parity establishes formal second-order consistency of the unforced interior schemes under diffusive scaling, assuming a smooth near-equilibrium Maxwell branch. The viscosity depends only on the flux rate; for the two-dimensional scheme, we identify the first contributions of the stress and energy rates to the second-order macroscopic truncation error. We further construct a positive definite symmetrizer for the collision Jacobian at rest and derive an exact weighted-norm identity for the nonlinear kinetic residual under local collision. At fixed viscosity, a finite Fourier search selects the free rates by combining transverse-mode accuracy with short-wavelength damping. The resulting rates are compared with those calibrated against flow errors on a coarse grid. Numerical experiments exhibit second-order convergence and illustrate how the free rates affect spectral properties and finite-time flow errors.

papers.title: Sidorenko inequalities and symmetry-forcing for graph orientations
papers.abstract: We study directed graphs whose homomorphism densities never increase or never decrease when the host edge directions are randomized. We call these properties oriented Sidorenko (OS) and oriented anti-Sidorenko (OAS), respectively. A directed graph is symmetry-forcing if equality between its original and randomized densities forces quasi-random edge directions. We characterize connected OS directed graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs and show that they are symmetry-forcing exactly when their underlying graphs contain a cycle. We also prove that a connected graph is step forcing exactly when it is step Sidorenko and contains a cycle, giving a negative answer to a question of Doležal et al. Both forcing results follow from a characterization of strict convexity: the homomorphism density functional of a graph is strictly convex on nonnegative kernels exactly when the graph is weakly norming and contains a cycle. On the OAS side, we construct an infinite symmetry-forcing family and a nonbipartite example. We also classify OS and OAS orientations of stars, paths, and cycles.

papers.title: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
papers.abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly.

papers.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Kuramoto model on the sphere
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for a generalization of the classical Kuramoto model on spheres of arbitrary dimension. For $n$ particles that are initialized independently from a probability measure with an $L^p$ density, $p>1$, and a nonzero mean vector, we obtain an explicit high-probability bound for the supremum over all times of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical and mean-field distributions. In sufficiently high dimension, this bound has the same order as the standard empirical sampling rate on the sphere and is therefore optimal. The proof combines a finite-time propagation of chaos estimate, a quantitative synchronization result for the mean-field model, and a late-time stability estimate of the system.

papers.title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent for the integrated density of states
papers.abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent $1/(2ω)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local Hölder exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-Hölder regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.

papers.title: The Merino-Welsh conjecture for sparse and dense graphs
papers.abstract: The Merino-Welsh conjecture states that the Tutte polynomial $T_G(x,y)$ of a loopless and bridgeless graph $G$ satisfies the inequality $\max\{T_G(2,0),T_G(0,2)\}\geq T_G(1,1).$ It is known to hold for several graph classes, among them sufficiently sparse and sufficiently dense graphs. In this paper, we improve the previously known sufficient density conditions and show that the multiplicative version of the conjecture also holds for sufficiently sparse and sufficiently dense graphs. In particular, we show that for a connected graph $G$ with $m$ edges and $n$ vertices, the Merino-Welsh conjecture holds if either $m\leq1.64(n-1)$ and $G$ is loopless or $m\geq2.55(n-1)$ and $G$ is bridgeless, and the multiplicative conjecture holds if $G$ is loopless and bridgeless with $m\leq1.21(n-1)$ or $m\geq5.62(n-1)$.

papers.title: Weight-Adjusted Entropy-Stable BR2 and CDG Viscous Discretizations with Wall Boundary Conditions for Compressible Flows on Curvilinear Grids
papers.abstract: Entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin schemes are known for their robustness. These schemes satisfy a semi-discrete entropy inequality, mimicking the entropy inequality of the continuous governing equations. Entropy-stable viscous discretizations with entropy-stable wall boundary conditions have been used in the literature, using a scheme similar to BR1. On the other hand, viscous discretizations with compact stencil, such as BR2 and CDG schemes, are more efficient for computation and for forming the Jacobian. Moreover, it is known that the weight-adjusted formulations have better efficiency with regard to the computational and storage costs. To that end, we derive the weight-adjusted entropy-stable BR2 and CDG schemes with modifications for the numerical flux at the boundary to account for the entropy-stable boundary conditions.

papers.title: Thin Edges in Braces
papers.abstract: A connected graph with at least two vertices is matching covered if each of its edges is contained in a perfect matching. A bipartite matching covered graph is a brace if no nontrivial cut meets every perfect matching in exactly one edge.An edge $e$ of a brace $G$ is thin if $G-e$ is matching covered and its retract is a brace. Every brace can be reduced to $K_2$ or $C_4$ by successively deleting thin edges and taking retracts. Indeed, Carvalho, Lucchesi and Murty proved that every brace of order at least six has at least two thin edges. They conjectured that there exists a positive constant $c$ such that every brace of order $n\ge6$ has at least $cn$ thin edges. In this paper, we prove that every simple brace of order $n\ge6$ has at least $\left\lceil\frac{n+2}{6}\right\rceil$ thin edges and that every brace of order $n$, withparallel edges allowed, has at least $\frac{n}{13}$ thin edges. This proves the conjecture. Moreover, we prove that every cubic brace of order $n$ has at least $\left\lceil\frac{n+1}{5}\right\rceil$ thin edges for $n\ge6$ and that the coefficient $\frac15$ is best possible.

papers.title: Hotelling's $T^2$ and the generalized domain of attraction of the normal law
papers.abstract: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be independent copies of a full random vector in $\mathbb R^p$, where $p$ is fixed. We prove that Hotelling's $T^2$-statistic at a prescribed location converges to $χ_p^2$ if and only if the underlying distribution belongs to the generalized domain of attraction of the normal law and has that location as its mean. Our proof of necessity combines moment bounds with matrix comparisons for self-normalized sums. It yields a sharp moment inequality for the squared norm of the uncentered self-normalized sum. Convergence of the first two moments of this squared norm to the chi-square values implies generalized normal attraction and identifies the mean. The necessity part of the multivariate Student normal-limit theorem follows as a corollary. Its sufficiency is the established result of Sepanski and of Vu, Maller and Klass.

papers.title: Cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras
papers.abstract: We study cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras, namely the dimension vectors of cluster-indecomposable modules. We give a direct proof of Mizuno's higher analogue of Gabriel's theorem, and show that cluster-roots are precisely the non-negative integer vectors whose Coxeter orbits contain the dimension vector of an indecomposable projective module. Moreover, we give an explicit description of all cluster-roots of the $(n-1)$-Auslander algebras of type $A$. For $n=2$, we use periodic integer sequences to give a method for constructing counterexamples to Mizuno's positivity conjecture within this family, which reduces to determining whether finitely many quadratic equations admit non-negative integer solutions.

papers.title: On the uniform algebras generated by powers of the coordinates and smooth functions on compact subsets of $\Bbb C^N$
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\Bbb C^N$ be compact and let $f=(f_1,\dots,f_N)$ be a smooth map on a neighbourhood of $K$. We give sufficient conditions for the algebra generated by $z_1^{m_1},\dots,z_N^{m_N}$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$ (or by all monomials of degree $n$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$) to be dense in $C(K)$. We appropriately extend the techniques developed in our previous works [3,4,6] and [8] for algebras of functions on the complex plane to tackle the problem in the several-variable setting. More precisely, the argument separates a purely algebraic reduction, in which the rotated graphs are glued one coordinate at a time, from the study of the single graph of $f$. For the latter we give an exact computation of the Levi form of $|w-f|^{2p}$, which yields a Hermitian matrix criterion on the polynomial hull of the graph; a criterion by peak functions that removes the invertibility hypothesis from a theorem of Preskenis; a division theorem for $f_j=\bar k_jh_j$ with degenerate holomorphic factors $h_j$; and a treatment of the singular set $\{\det(\partial f_i/\partial\bar z_j)=0\}$, which in several variables is not finite. The angle $π/m_j$ in the reduction is shown to be sharp.

papers.title: A regular free action on the integral plane and a problem on left braces
papers.abstract: We construct a free subgroup of countably infinite rank in $\ZZ^2\rtimes\SL_2(\ZZ)$ that acts regularly on $\ZZ^2$. At each stage we adjoin an affine transformation taking the origin to the least point of a prescribed orbit. Disjoint domains for reduced words ensure that the stabilizer of the origin remains trivial. The orbit map gives a left brace with additive group $\ZZ^2$ and multiplicative group free of countably infinite rank. This group contains a nonabelian free subgroup and is therefore nonsolvable, answering both parts of Problem 20.126 of the Kourovka Notebook.

papers.title: The optimization landscape of robust high-dimensional mean estimation: stability, moment adaptation, and mirror descent reweighting
papers.abstract: We study efficient robust estimation of a high-dimensional mean under strong contamination when the clean distribution has only $p\ge2$ moments, bounded by $ν_p$. We give a unified proof of stability for every $p\ge2$ with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction $\varepsilon_{n,k}=k/n$ of the mass, where the trimming parameter $k$ slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature $\frac{1-\varepsilon_{n,k}}{\varepsilon_{n,k}}$, relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for $\varepsilon_{n,k}<\frac13$ that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of $(p,ν_p)$. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Remarks on the BKM criterion for both classical and variable Euler systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish new results on BKM-type criteria for the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ as well as the Euler equations with space-time variable coefficients in a bounded domain. Our first result shows that if a finite-energy solution to the Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ blows up at a time $T_\ast$, and $T_\ast$ is the first such time, then $\limsup_{t\to T_\ast^-}(T_\ast -t)^{1+2k/5}\|D^kω(t)\|_{L^\infty} = \infty$ for every $k \geq 1$, thereby excluding the endpoint rate allowed by previously established lower bounds. The proof assumes the endpoint rate as an upper bound near the blowup time and uses a result by Chae and Wolf to obtain a contradiction. The second result gives a BKM-type criterion for solutions to the incompressible Euler equations with variable coefficients in the minimal regularity class $H^r$, where $r \in (2.5,3)$.

papers.title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
papers.abstract: We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$. Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous. We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(Ω)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.

papers.title: Relative divisors and intersections of noncommutative rational localizations
papers.abstract: The simple constituents of monic pencils determine singularity support in a free skew field. For a pencil inverse algebra that is a free ideal ring, the multiplicities of the nonbase constituents compute the scalar-regular part of Cohn's matrix divisor theory. For independent generic invertible matrices of size at least two, every entry of a nonidentity free-group word is an atom with one relative singularity component. In rank two, opposite pivots give the exact identifications among these components. Intersections of word-entry localizations are then given by intersections of their label sets. An irreducible pencil of dimension six represents a commutator entry. For an algebra finitely generated over the free polynomial algebra at a common regular scalar point, the residual closure is a finite pencil inverse algebra determined by the generators' common domain. Every nonzero inverse-adjoining defect is infinite-dimensional. We compute how free-group quotients change intersections and give additive formulas for general quotient and tensor intersections. We prove Berenstein--Retakh's polygon conjecture using $n-2$ charts for $n\geq4$. For an unpunctured Möbius strip with $n\geq2$ boundary marks, the upper-algebra equality follows from $n+1$ charts. For the once-marked strip, the allowed algebra is strictly smaller than its residual hull, which equals the full chart.

papers.title: Stability of Hilbert--Samuel functions with linear bounds in homological degree
papers.abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I$ be generated by a filter regular sequence. Set $A=R/I$, $s=\dim A>0$, and $D= \operatorname{hdeg}(A)$. If $A$ is equicharacteristic, we prove that perturbations of order $(2s+1)D$ preserve the Hilbert--Samuel function in every dimension. In arbitrary characteristic, we obtain the order $[s+(s+1)(k!)^{k-1}]D^k$, where $k$ is the maximum of $1$ and the dimensions of the lower deficiency modules of $\widehat A$. Both bounds depend only on the final quotient. The proof constructs monic annihilating equations for the deficiency modules and uses them to choose a parameter $d$-sequence with an explicit relation to a reduction of the maximal ideal. In the equicharacteristic case, a dimension filtration and characteristic polynomials over regular subrings give equations of degree at most the arithmetic degree, with coefficients in the required powers of the reduction.

papers.title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion
papers.abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotics and stability for a two-power affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality
papers.abstract: We study the affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality under the constraint $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}(f^{q-\varepsilon}+f^{q+\varepsilon}) dx=1$ for $f\ge0$, where $q=\frac{2n}{n+α}$, $n\ge2$, $0<α<n$, and $0<\varepsilon<q-1$. We determine the second-order expansion of its sharp constant and the scale selected by all normalized radial extremals as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. For sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon$, we prove stability estimates with power $2$ in $L^{q-\varepsilon}\cap L^{q+\varepsilon}$ for the Euclidean and affine energies. The power $2$ is sharp, and the sharp stability constants admit $O(\varepsilon^2)$ upper bounds as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. The proof combines identities for the two power integrals with Euclidean spectral estimates, affine compactness and a nonlinear directional expansion. No uniqueness or additional regularity of the radial extremals is assumed.

papers.title: Sharp partition function bound for the attractive logarithmic gas
papers.abstract: For the attractive logarithmic potential, we prove that the partition function is bounded uniformly in the number of particles on every compact inverse-temperature interval $[0,\be_0]$ with $\be_0<B$, where $B\in(0,2\d]$ is the sharp constant in the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. The proof separates a smooth bulk, which inherits the entropy inequality, from a short-range singular interaction. The singular contribution is controlled on the event that each box of a fixed grid contains few particles. The complementary overcrowding event has exponentially small probability, which compensates a crude linear-in-$N$ bound on the log partition function. The resulting estimate supplies the partition bound that can be used recycled in a few different results. A separate Lean formalization verifies the conditional partition-bound theorem under the log-HLS assumption.

papers.title: Exact Values and Bounds for Four Color Quadratic Polynomial van der Waerden Numbers
papers.abstract: For a nonzero polynomial $P(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $P(0)=0$, let $W(P(x);4)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every four coloring of $[N]$ contains distinct integers $u,v$ of the same color with $v-u=P(d)$ for some integer $d$. The best known general upper bounds for polynomial van der Waerden numbers are primitive recursive but remain enormous compared with the few known exact values.
