We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, dσ)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $η_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $η_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.

papers.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
papers.abstract: We prove bounds for scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds with nonnegative sectional curvature. In every dimension $n\ge3$, when the asymptotic volume ratio is close to one, we obtain upper and lower estimates with the sharp first-order coefficient and a quadratic remainder. The leading terms involve the asymptotic and local volume deficits, respectively. Rotationally symmetric examples show that both first-order coefficients are optimal and that a quadratic remainder is necessary in the upper bound. For dimensions three, four, and five we give estimates for any positive asymptotic volume ratio. When the center is a pole, we give an estimate in dimension three under nonnegative Ricci curvature and in every dimension $n\ge4$ under nonnegative sectional curvature. This estimate is sharp when the asymptotic volume ratio is at most $2^{-(n-1)}$.

papers.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
papers.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.

papers.title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
papers.abstract: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.

papers.title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 1: The Case \(n+\log n\)
papers.abstract: We prove that $(α(n+\log n))_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for Lebesgue almost every real $α$. This solves a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 2, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021].

papers.title: Spectral stability for strong ideal-gas shock layers
papers.abstract: We give a purely analytical proof of one-dimensional spectral stability of sufficiently strong shock layers for the full ideal-gas Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity and heat conduction. Earlier work reduced this question to a limiting problem and gave strong numerical evidence of stability through Evans function computation, but no proof. We prove stability for every adiabatic index $1<γ<3$ and for an explicit range of ratios of heat conduction to viscosity that contains all common gases.

papers.title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
papers.abstract: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.

papers.title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $Ξ$-function
papers.abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $Ξ$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.

papers.title: 48 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
papers.abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in\mathbb Q$.

papers.title: Dual-Inertial Bregman Methods with Energy-Based Safeguarding
papers.abstract: We study dual-inertial (DI) Bregman proximal methods for convex optimization via an exact representation of the signed energy drift between dual-coordinate and primal affine interpolation. For unrestarted DI, bounded one-sided directional curvature gives a last-iterate objective-gap rate $\mathcal{O}((1+\log N)/N^2)$ after $N$ iterations, which improves to $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2})$ under weighted summability. The energy balance also provides a computable acceptance test, which we use in two safeguards. The restart safeguard attains a global $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate after $T$ proximal calls, including rejected trials. Under local quadratic growth and kernel regularity, it restarts only finitely often and eventually converges linearly. The non-restarting safeguard preserves the quadratic weight recurrence via dual substeps. Every fallback terminates without triangle scaling, yielding a $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2})$ rate in outer iterations and an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate in calls, which improves to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ when the cumulative fallback cost is $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Experiments on relative-entropy regression and nonnegative least squares illustrate the results.

papers.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
papers.abstract:
We approximate the Darcy solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$, where $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$, by operator networks built only from heat-semigroup evaluations $e^{-tL_0}$ of a single fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The key obstacle is the variable-coefficient coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$. We show that it is produced by the heat product defect $[P_t(bu)-P_tb\,P_tu]/(2t)$, which converges quantitatively to $
abla b\cdot
abla u$. Inserted into a Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, this yields an explicit scheme of depth $O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q))$ whose $\dot H^1$ error is at most $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the coefficient class and $L^2$ data, with all parameters explicit. Each block is controlled in continuum operator norm, without Galerkin truncation. On the torus, band-limited inputs admit an exact pseudo-spectral realization on a grid of $O(1/(\varepsilon a_{\min}))$ points per direction, up to logarithmic and class-dependent factors. The argument extends by carre du champ calculus to strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$, with dimension-independent constants after spectral-gap normalization. On the torus we also obtain a $C^2$-type coefficient class and a refinement to Wiener classes of regularity $1+θ$, with product-defect rate $t^{θ/2}$. The factor $1/(2t)$ makes the proved scheme ill-conditioned at small $\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Big Finitistic Dimensions of Formal Power Series Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we completely investigate what the big finitistic projective dimension (resp., big finitistic flat dimension) pair, which abbreviates FPD pair (resp., FFD pair), of a commutative ring and of its formal power series ring can be. When the ring is Noetherian, both invariants increase by one. In general, for every \(n\ge0\) and every \(d\) with \(n+1\le d\le\infty\), the FFD pair \((n,d)\) can be realized; the FPD pairs \((n,d)\) can be realized when \(n\ge1\), also for \((0,1)\) and \((0,\infty)\). However, the FPD pair \((0,2)\) is impossible. For perfect coefficients, we prove that the existence of a commutative perfect ring \(R\) with \(\FPD(R[[x]])=3\) is equivalent to the continuum hypothesis. Under the continuum hypothesis, every finite integer \(n\ge2\) admits a commutative local perfect ring \(R\) with \(\FFD(R[[x]])=1\) and \(\FPD(R[[x]])=n+2\). And for each such \(n\), the existence of a perfect coefficient ring with projective value \(n+2\) does not imply the continuum hypothesis.

papers.title: Dynamic Programming for A Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
papers.abstract: We consider an infinite-horizon discounted dynamic programming (DP) problem for a countable-innovation belief-state model. The model is a surrogate for a linear-Gaussian dual control problem involving an unknown parameter vector and Gaussian observation noise. The surrogate preserves the first two moments of the Gaussian innovation and the resulting posterior second-moment structure. We allow unbounded belief and control spaces and nonnegative stage costs with quadratic growth in the posterior mean and covariance. Using a posterior-moment weight, we show that the Bellman operator is a contraction in a weighted sup-norm space. We characterize the optimal cost as the unique solution of the Bellman equation in this space, establish the existence of optimal stationary policies. We further prove weighted sup-norm convergence of value iteration, policy iteration, and optimistic policy iteration under vanishing approximation errors. The convergence results under vanishing approximation errors rely on general weighted sup-norm contraction properties and are applicable beyond the particular dual control problem considered here.

papers.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
papers.abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

papers.title: $2$-Large Sets and Nil-Bohr Recurrence: A Disproof of the $2$-Large Is Large Conjecture
papers.abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $r$-large if every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every $2$-large set is a set of nil-Bohr recurrence, i.e., it meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. Furthermore, we show that a piecewise syndetic set is $2$-large if and only if it is nil-Bohr recurrent. From this, we show that a small modification of a set constructed by the first author is $2$-large but not $3$-large, thereby disproving the $2$-large is large conjecture of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also deduce that the family of $2$-large sets is not partition regular, thereby answering another question of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Small area learning
papers.abstract: Small area estimation (SAE) traditionally borrows strength across domains through a prespecified working model. We introduce small area learning (SAL), a novel learner-agnostic framework that formulates SAE as a multi-target semi-supervised learning problem and treats outcome prediction as a nuisance task. Areas may differ through unrestricted covariate shift and structured conditional shift, with information shared through common and area-specific components. We develop estimators with and without cross-fitting, accommodating low-complexity and flexible learners and unifying synthetic, model-based, and semi-supervised estimators. For area means, we establish a unified asymptotic theory for these estimator families, characterizing conditions for consistency, asymptotic normality and providing variance estimators and confidence intervals without prescribing a particular learning algorithm. We extend the theory to settings with only aggregated population covariates and characterize the resulting aggregation bias. SAL reveals clearly a bias-variance trade-off: partial residual correction in classical estimators can reduce mean squared error, whereas full correction yields estimators robust to the misspecification of working models, potentially at higher variance. Simulations yield RMSE reductions of 34%-49% relative to direct estimation, with the best configuration varying across settings. The numerical studies also illustrate how shrinkage can produce overly optimistic confidence intervals at the expense of strong modeling assumptions.

papers.title: A Circular Cantor Construction Without Dimension Drop for Harmonic Measure
papers.abstract: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for harmonic measure in the domain $\mathbb C\setminus K$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. Our construction with corrections to the first order gives the range $0<s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.

papers.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
papers.abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with $|x_3|$ of size at most $M$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$, using a smooth weight $Φ(x_3/M)$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and hence to geodesics in the hyperbolic plane. Under this correspondence, $x_3$ is small exactly when the geodesic passes close to the point $i$. We count these geodesics by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $θ=7/64$ is the Kim-Sarnak exponent. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$, with $D_0$ a fundamental discriminant, the geodesics are closed. We obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+θ}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$. The main inputs are the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao for cycle integrals, the cubic moment bounds of Young and of Andersen-Wu, and a Hecke relation which reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$ we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+θ+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, which is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High; Fable 5.2 in the final stage), an AI model developed by Anthropic.

papers.title: Coefficient arithmetic and Mellin moments of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction
papers.abstract: We study the signs of logarithmic coefficients associated with the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. An explicit criterion involving a finite product determines whether all coefficients in an arithmetic progression are negative or both signs occur with positive natural density. On the sets $n=5^a m$, $5\nmid m$, negative coefficients occur with positive relative density $δ_a^-$ at every fixed $a$. If $m_a$ is the least such $m$, we prove that both $5^{-a}\log\log(1/δ_a^-)$ and $5^{-a}\log\log m_a$ tend to $5\logφ/(12e^γ)$, where $φ=(1+\sqrt5)/2$ and $γ$ is Euler's constant. These are leading double-logarithmic asymptotics, obtained from classical results on additive and multiplicative functions. Coefficient formulas also give irrationality and nonvanishing, determine the poles and residues of generating functions for normalized Mellin moments, and imply that these generating functions are not D-finite. We conclude with applications to integrals involving zeta, Dirichlet $L$, and cusp-form $L$-functions.

papers.title: The packing spectrum: interpolation between Hausdorff and packing dimensions
papers.abstract: We introduce a packing spectrum that interpolates between Hausdorff and packing dimensions through a family of metric outer measures. The construction assigns an independent scale label to each member of a countable covering and restricts local packing radii to a window determined by that label. The resulting spectrum is countably stable, satisfies the usual Hölder image bound, and is nondecreasing and locally Lipschitz below the packing endpoint, where a jump may occur. We establish Hausdorff product bounds involving the packing spectrum and upper intermediate dimensions, refining the classical Hausdorff--packing bounds. For nonempty analytic sets, we prove a converse characterization by compact product tests and a variational principle in terms of the local mass decay of compactly supported probability measures below the packing endpoint. Finally, we completely classify the possible spectra in each ambient dimension. Every admissible profile is realized by a compact binary digit set. For each realization, a single complementary digit set attains the product bounds at every parameter, and the uniform digit measure simultaneously attains the corresponding variational suprema.

papers.title: BDF2-type integrator for Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation in micromagnetics: IMEX time-stepping and full effective field
papers.abstract: We extend the BDF2-type finite-element integrator proposed in [M. Aldé, M. Feischl, D. Praetorius; BDF2-type integrator for Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation in micromagnetics: unconditional weak convergence to weak solutions. (Math. Comp., 2026, doi:10.1090/mcom/4210)] to the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation with lower-order effective-field contributions and current-induced non-conservative torques arising in micromagnetic applications. To incorporate these additional terms while retaining a linear solve at each time step, we employ an implicit-explicit (IMEX) time splitting. Our main theorem proves unconditional weak convergence of the fully discrete approximations towards weak solutions of the LLG equation. The analysis removes the mild but artificial CFL-type restrictions required at the first and final time steps in [Aldé M., Feischl M., Praetorius D.; Math. Comp., 2026]. Furthermore, in the presence of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), the convergence is likewise unconditional and does not require the CFL-type restriction imposed in [G. Hrkac, C.-M. Pfeiler, D. Praetorius, M. Ruggeri, A. Segatti, and B. Stiftner. Convergent tangent plane integrators for the simulation of chiral magnetic skyrmion dynamics. (Adv. Comput. Math., 2019. doi: 10.1007/s10444-019-09667-z)]. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Almost-splitting of spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds
papers.abstract: We establish an almost-splitting theorem for spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds in the spirit of the celebrated Riemannian result due to Cheeger and Colding. More concretely, we show that if a globally hyperbolic spacetime with timelike sectional curvature bounded below by a nonpositive constant close to zero contains a long maximizing timelike segment, then causal diamonds along that segment are close in the Lorentzian Gromov--Hausdorff sense of Minguzzi--Suhr to those in a product metric spacetime. Our result can be interpreted as a quantitative analogue of the Lorentzian splitting theorem for spacetimes with nonnegative timelike sectional curvature by Beem--Ehrlich--Markvorsen--Galloway. In contrast to the Riemannian setting, the timelike sectional curvature bound cannot be replaced by Ricci-flatness, as the small mass limit of the Schwarzschild exterior geometry shows.

papers.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
papers.abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.

papers.title: Gamma-Convergence of Weak-Type Nonlocal Functionals
papers.abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$ be a bounded open interval when $N=1$ or a bounded Lipschitz domain when $N\ge2$. For $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $λ\in(0,\infty)$, consider the weak-type nonlocal functional \begin{align*} F_{λ,p,γ}(u;Ω):=λ^p \underset{\scriptscriptstyle |u(x)-u(y)|>λ|x-y|^{1+γ/p}} {\int_Ω\int_Ω}|x-y|^{γ-N}\,dy\,dx \end{align*} with $u:Ω\to\mathbb{R}$ measurable. We prove that, as $λ\to\infty$ for $γ\in(0,\infty)$ or as $λ\to0^+$ for $γ\in(-\infty,-1]$, $F_{λ,p,γ}(\cdot;Ω)$ converges, in the sense of $Γ$-convergence in $L^p(Ω)$, to \begin{align*} Ψ_{p,γ}^Ω(u) :=\begin{cases} C_{N,p,γ}^{\rm cell}\displaystyle\int_Ω|\nabla u|^p\,dx, &p\in(1,\infty)\ \hbox{and}\ u\in W^{1,p}(Ω),\\ C_{N,1,γ}^{\rm cell}|Du|(Ω), &p=1\ \hbox{and}\ u\in BV(Ω),\\ \infty,&\hbox{otherwise}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where the positive constants $C_{N,p,γ}^{\mathrm{cell}}$ are independent of $Ω$. We also establish the $Γ$-convergence of $F_{λ,p,γ}(\cdot;\mathbb R^N)$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^N)$ for all $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, with the limit functional having an additional term when $(N,p,γ)=(1,1,-1)$. These results affirmatively answer [Open Problem~9.3, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 2023] of Brezis and also the other problem by Brezis et al. in [Section~7C, Anal. PDE 2024].

papers.title: Upper deviations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy: the fifth-order law and the onset of constrained Parisi measures
papers.abstract: Let $Z_N$ be the partition function of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $β>1$. Replica theory (Kondor near the critical temperature, Parisi and Rizzo at all temperatures) predicts that the probability that $N^{-1}\log Z_N$ exceeds its typical value by $δ$ decays like $\exp(-Naδ^{6/5})$ with an explicit $a$; Aronow and Lopatto recently proved bounds of this order. The exponent is the Legendre transform of the Parisi problem constrained to carry an atom $θ$ at zero. We show that the constrained minimum exceeds the equilibrium free energy by $c_βθ^5(1+o(1))$, where $c_β=\frac{9}{640}β^3ρ_β(0)^{-3}$ and $ρ_β(0)>0$ is the density at zero of the Parisi measure. With the fractional-moment formula this gives the exponent $\frac56(6c_β)^{-1/5}δ^{6/5}(1+o(1))$ as $N\to\infty$ and then $δ\to0$. The constrained minimizer has a marginal first positive contact, to leading order at $3θ/(2ρ_β(0))$ with an atom $θ/2$. This plateau calculus applies to every mixture with $ξ'''(0)=0$ whose Parisi measure accumulates at zero; a small field $h$ opens a gap of order $|h|^{2/3}$, and an atom of the Parisi measure at zero, present in every pure $p$-spin model with $p\ge3$, makes the rate leave zero linearly. Near criticality the constant tends to Kondor's value $9/5120$ and the marginal regime ends at a de Almeida-Thouless threshold. For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every $β>1$, a finite-step curvature inequality from an unrefereed preprint shows that every constrained minimizer either has an interval of positive contacts, all marginal, or has exactly two atoms, and that the marginal regime ends at a unique de Almeida-Thouless threshold $θ_c(β)$. The laws at every $β>1$ use that the Parisi measure accumulates at zero, a theorem of Lopatto also proved in earlier work of the author.

papers.title: K-unstable Toric Varieties and Secondary Polytopes
papers.abstract: For a K-unstable toric variety, Székelyhidi's optimal test-function $Θ_{P}$ is a mysterious concave function over the moment polytope $P$, which gives the maximal destabilizer for K-stability, and encodes the limiting behavior of the divergent Calabi flow. As balanced norms quantize cscK metrics, we show that $Θ_{P}$ can be quantized by the maximal destabilizers for Chow-stability, which are given by the shortest GKZ vectors, i.e., the least norm point on the secondary polytope associated to the set $P\cap k^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. The proof is via the $Γ$-convergence method. Properties and algorithms for general sGKZ vectors are given. It may provide a new method to detect the K-instability of Delzant polytopes.

papers.title: Shimura Reciprocity for Real Quadratic Fields
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is to give conditional explicit formulas for the Galois action on real multiplication values of the Shintani--Faddeev modular cocycle. We assume the order 1 abelian Stark conjecture for real quadratic fields. We conclude this note by presenting our own conjecture about the Galois action. Numerical evidence for this conjecture is provided by the algorithm described in \hyperref[sec4]{Section 4} and the attached code.

papers.title: Timelike surfaces of constant mean and constant Gaussian curvature in anti-de Sitter 3-space via loop groups
papers.abstract: The loop group description of surfaces whose Gauss map is Lorentz harmonic is known for timelike surfaces of constant mean curvature in the flat Lorentzian 3-space, and for surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in the 3-sphere. We carry out the corresponding construction for timelike surfaces in anti-de Sitter 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3_1\cong SL(2,\mathbb{R})$: those of constant mean curvature, whose Gauss map is harmonic for the conformal structure of the first fundamental form, and those of constant Gaussian curvature $K>-1$, $K\neq0$, whose Gauss map is then an immersion and is harmonic for the second fundamental form. For both classes we prove the harmonicity characterization, recover the surfaces from extended frames by Sym-Bobenko-type formulas, and solve the geometric Cauchy problem by the generalized DPW method, with potentials written explicitly in terms of the data and no normalization of the Gauss map. We then show that the two constructions differ only by a normalization: after the substitution $λ=ζ^2$ and a constant gauge, a constant mean curvature extended frame $\hat F$ is an extended frame of its Gauss map, and the maps $\hat F|_{λ=e^{4θ}}\exp(θe_3)\hat F|_{λ=1}^{-1}$ and $e_3\hat F|_{λ=e^{4θ}}e_3\exp(θe_3)\hat F|_{λ=1}^{-1}$, with $e_3=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, are timelike surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature $1/\sinh^2θ$ and $-1/\cosh^2θ$ wherever the constant mean curvature surface is not flat. The first is the classical parallel surface, the second its polar surface. Explicit families, with extended frames and surfaces in closed form, illustrate the constructions.

papers.title: An Asymptotically Tight Bound on the Number of Distinct Squares in Circular Words
papers.abstract: A square is a word $xx$ with $x$ nonempty. We study the maximum number of distinct squares occurring in the rotations of a word of length $n$. Amit and Gawrychowski (SPIRE 2017) obtained an upper bound of $3.14n$. Charalampopoulos et al. (CPM 2026) improved the upper bound to $\lceil9n/5\rceil$ and gave a binary construction with at least $3n/2-O(\sqrt n)$ distinct squares for infinitely many $n$. They conjectured an upper bound of $3n/2$. Li and Song subsequently reported an improved upper bound of $5n/3$. We prove that a circular word of length $n$ containing $σ$ distinct letters has at most $\lfloor3(n-σ)/2\rfloor$ distinct squares. This settles the conjecture and establishes that the leading coefficient $3/2$ is optimal even for binary words. Our proof groups squares by their Lyndon roots and, for primitive words, uses a weighted count of circuits in the Rauzy graphs of the bi-infinite repetition of the word.

papers.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of Speed Monotonicity for the Biased Random Walk on a Galton-Watson Tree Beyond the Known Range
papers.abstract: The speed $v(λ)$ of the $λ$-biased random walk on a supercritical Galton--Watson tree without leaves is conjectured to be nonincreasing on $[0,m)$, where $m$ is the mean offspring. For non-constant offspring, monotonicity is known only for small bias: $λ\le 1/1160$, $λ\le 1/2$, and, when every vertex has at least $m_1\ge 2$ children, $λ\le m_1/(1+\sqrt{1-1/m_1})$. For offspring uniform on $\{2,3\}$ ($m=2.5$) the last bound is $2/(1+\sqrt{1/2})\approx1.1716$. We prove, with computer assistance, that $v$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1.755]$ for this law. The proof has three parts. Aïdékon's speed formula gives $v=(R-λ)/(R+λ)$ for an explicit functional $R$, so $v$ decreases exactly when $R/λ$ does; we compare $R/λ$ at two biases directly, which avoids differentiating the conductance. A pathwise Lipschitz bound on the conductance in $λ$ turns that comparison into an inequality between expectations of explicit functions. A monotone sandwich of discretised laws gives two-sided bounds on the conductance law, and each $λ$-cell is checked in exact rational arithmetic over bounded floating-point error, with five cells re-checked in interval arithmetic; all reduction lemmas and an exact-integer certificate across $[1.17,1.755]$ are also formally verified in Lean 4. The method stops where the crude Lipschitz bound becomes too weak; sharper control of the derivative of the conductance is what the full range needs. Code and certificates are public.

papers.title: Precise Convergence Speed of Clipped SGD
papers.abstract: We present a tightened convergence analysis of clipped gradient descent on $(L_0, L_1)$-smooth functions, with quantitative constants. Building on the ideas of Koloskova et al (2023), we refactor several case disjunctions to reveal the central role of a control of the bias derived from fundamental properties of $\ell_2$-projection, simplifying proofs. We also extend the domain of validity from $η\leq 1 / (9 β)$ to $η< 1 /β$ where $β= L_0 + c L_1$ for clipping constant $c$, which matches the more traditional analysis of smooth functions. We strengthen the convergence criterion from $\left( \min_{t < T} \mathbb{E}[\lVert \nabla f(x_t) \rVert_2] \right)$ to $\left( \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t < T} \mathbb{E}[\lVert \nabla f(x_t) \rVert_2] \right)$ with matching speed, and lower the final achievable floor from $\mathcal{O}(\min(σ^2/c, σ))$ to the more precise $6 \min(σ^2 /c, 3 σ)$.

papers.title: Noncommutative Maximal Ergodic Theorems for Modulated $(C,α)$-Averages with Operator-Valued Weights
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study modulated $(C,α)$-ergodic averages with operator-valued weights and their subsequential versions in the setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras. Our framework combines $(C,α)$-type modulation with operator-valued weights and extends both scalar-weighted and operator-valued weighted ergodic theories. We establish mean ergodic theorems and maximal inequalities for these averages on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We then study bilateral almost uniform and almost uniform convergence in noncommutative Orlicz spaces, including convergence along subsequences of density one when $α\geq 1$. A key ingredient in our approach is the introduction of the $p$-convexity condition on the underlying Orlicz function. This condition allows us to transfer appropriate maximal estimates from noncommutative $L_p$-spaces to establish bilateral uniform equicontinuity in measure at zero on the corresponding noncommutative $p$-convex Orlicz spaces. Together with the noncommutative Banach principle, this yields the desired pointwise convergence results. As an additional consequence of our $p$-convexity argument, we extend Rota theorem to a larger class of noncommutative Orlicz spaces associated with the $p$-convex Orlicz functions considered in this article.

papers.title: Conformal Killing--Yano Ricci solitons: Basic structure and first examples
papers.abstract: We introduce a conformal Killing-Yano Ricci soliton, coupling conformal Ricci soliton geometry to conformal Killing-Yano 2-forms via the divergence of the form. In four-dimensional Lorentzian signature, the principal conformal structure is not preserved under non-trivial conformal deformation, so the associated form on local Kerr-NUT-(A)dS backgrounds is not closed. For Einstein backgrounds in any dimension and signature, integrability forces the form to be Killing for the background and conformal Killing for the necessarily Einstein soliton metric, with the conformal factor satisfying eigenvalue and Obata-type Hessian equations; the coupling fixes the Einstein constant. Vanishing coupling reduces the data to Killing data on the fiber; otherwise the soliton metric is Ricci-flat. Locally the background is a warped product. In the compact Riemannian case, the manifold is the round sphere. Explicit static spherically symmetric and BTZ constructions are given, with applications to exact geometries in general relativity.

papers.title: On normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
papers.abstract: We study real-analytic planar maps, that admit a real-analytic first integral with a non-degenerate extremum, in a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We prove that, if the map preserves an analytic area form, it is real-analytically and symplectically conjugate to a twist map, both in the resonant and in the non-resonant case. Using an example, we show that without the area-preservation assumption the conclusion fails. We then prove that a second, continuous, first integral is either a function of the first one or forces the map to be periodic, in which case the map is analytically (and, when area-preserving, symplectically) conjugate to its linear part. We illustrate our results, we study the McMillan map, and a planar map obtained from the Adler--Yamilov Yang--Baxter map.

papers.title: Infinitesimmaly homogeneous manifolds with symplectic and almost contact structure groups
papers.abstract: We study infinitesimally homogeneous affine manifolds with prescribed structure groups. First, for the real symplectic group $\operatorname{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, we prove that the corresponding infinitesimally homogeneous structures are precisely flat torsion-free symplectic affine structures. Second, for \(\operatorname{U}(n)\times\{1\}\), whose \(G\)-structures are equivalent to almost contact metric data, we classify the torsion-free characteristic tensors and obtain the general torsional case by invariant deformation. The admissible torsion and inner-torsion parameters are governed by a single algebraic relation, and the horizontal distribution is contact precisely when a certain combination of these parameters does not vanish. We also describe the compatible connections and relate the torsion-free branches to trans-Sasakian geometry.

papers.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
papers.abstract: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.

papers.title: An energy-stable and accuracy-preserving finite volume scheme for wall-distance computations
papers.abstract: The distance to the nearest wall provides a length scale in models of wall-bounded turbulence. Computing this distance accurately on highly stretched meshes is challenging because small near-wall cells restrict explicit pseudo-time steps and geometric singularities can induce spurious oscillations. To address these challenges, this paper presents a semi-implicit finite-volume scheme based on a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) for solving the pseudo-time Eikonal equation on unstructured meshes. An upwind weighted least-squares reconstruction supplies the gradients used to evaluate the cell-averaged Eikonal residuals. The artificial-viscosity term is discretized using a two-point face flux whose coefficient vanishes as the regularized residuals in both adjacent cells tend to zero. The SAV update advances the semi-discrete system in pseudo-time by evaluating the residuals and viscosity coefficients explicitly and coupling the wall-distance averages and auxiliary variables implicitly. The analysis establishes unconditional energy stability under homogeneous Dirichlet conditions, permitting a grid-independent global pseudo-time step. The system's M-matrix structure guarantees nonnegative cell averages of the physical wall distance under a separate step restriction, while residual regularization and artificial viscosity preserve the formal order of spatial accuracy. Numerical tests confirm second-order spatial convergence for the quarter-cylinder case and demonstrate robust wall-distance computation on highly stretched meshes typical of Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes simulations. The SAV formulation is independent of the reconstruction scheme, providing a basis for extensions to higher-order finite-volume methods and other nonconservative scalar equations.

papers.title: On $t$-sumfree sequences
papers.abstract: In this paper we explore the world of $t$-sumfree sequences, primarily for $t=2$ and $t=3$. Starting with $t$ increasing positive integers, build an infinite sequence by choosing as the next entry the least positive integer that is not the sum of $t$ distinct previous values. The main open problem concerns the question of the conjectured ultimate periodicity of these sequences. We formulate a sufficient condition to prove that a conjectured preperiod and period are correct. We also prove periodicity for a considerable subclass of 2-sumfree and of 3-sumfree sequences. Finally, we present the results of extensive computations on 3-sumfree sequences.

papers.title: Learning to Solve Stochastic Controls with Unknown Drifts and Running Rewards: Theory, Algorithms and Convergence
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time and possibly high-dimensional stochastic control problems where drift coefficients and running reward functions are unknown. Due to these missing model primitives, we take the exploratory, reinforcement learning (RL) framework of Wang, Zariphopoulou, and Zhou(2020) with relaxed controls and entropy regularization. The objective is to develop theoretically grounded, efficient and scalable RL algorithms to learn both the optimal value functions (which also solve the exploratory HJB equation) and optimal exploratory feedback control policies. When the diffusion coefficients do not contain control, we employ probabilistic representations of both the optimal value function and its gradient based on an auxiliary state process depending only on the diffusion part of the original dynamics. With a delicate analysis on some properly defined mappings and their fixed points, this leads to the introduction of our policy iteration algorithms and their convergence. We demonstrate the performance of our algorithms through various numerical examples. Finally, we study a special control-dependent diffusion case where probability representation of the Hessian is called for.

papers.title: Subset-Sum Density Realization in Locally Finite Abelian Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a countable locally finite abelian group, and let \[ G_1\leq G_2\leq\cdots, \qquad \bigcup_{i\geq1}G_i=G, \] be any filtration of $G$ by finite subgroups. For $A\subseteq G$, let $\mathcal P(A)$ denote the set of all finite subset sums of elements of $A$, and let $2G:=\{2g:g\in G\}$. We prove that $|2G|=\infty$ if and only if for every filtration and every interval $[α,β]\subseteq[0,1]$, there exists $A\subseteq G$ such that the set of limit points of \[ \left( \frac{|\mathcal P(A)\cap G_i|}{|G_i|} \right)_{i\geq1} \] is exactly $[α,β]$. We also prove a positive-density result that does not require $|2G|=\infty$: if $G$ is infinite and $\mathcal P(A)$ has positive upper density along the given filtration, then there is an infinite set $B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$ such that $B+B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$. Combining this with the realization theorem, we show that, when $|2G|=\infty$, every interval $[α,β]$ with $0\leqα\leqβ\leq1$ and $β>0$ can be realized by a set $A$ with this additional property.

papers.title: Poisson problem with Hardy operator on lattice graph $ \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the application to semilinear equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the analytic properties of the Hardy-type operator $-Δ+ μH_0$ on the $d$-dimensional integer lattice graph $\mathbb{Z}^d$, where $μ\geq -1$ and $H_0$ is a critical Hardy potential at infinity--arising naturally from discrete Hardy inequalities. We derive sharp fixed-pole Green kernel estimates on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and obtain a necessary and sufficient weighted summability condition characterizing the solvability of the nonnegative Poisson problem associated with this operator. Building upon this classification, we provide a complete characterization of the nonexistence of positive solutions to the semilinear elliptic inequality $$ -Δu + μH_0 u \geq W u^p \quad \text{in } \mathbb{Z}^d, $$ where $p > 0$, $d \geq 3$, $μ\geq -1$, and $H_0, W \in C(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ are strictly positive potentials satisfying the asymptotic behaviors $H_0(x) \sim |x|^{-2}$ and $W(x) \sim |x|^θ$ as $|x| \to \infty$, with $θ\in \mathbb{R}$.

papers.title: Minimum central circles: an effective characterization of the global asymptotic constant
papers.abstract: Let $R^\ast(n)$ be the minimum radius of a central circle externally tangent to nonoverlapping circles of radii $1,\ldots,n$. We prove that $R^\ast(n)=C_\ast n^2+o(n^2)$ and give finite linear programs that enclose $C_\ast$ with prescribed error. An exact angular comparison reduces the problem to marked points on a line with separation at least the geometric mean of each pair of marks. Concatenation with bounded joining cost and reassignment to the prescribed normalized radii prove existence of the limit. Balanced finite-word programs give a bracket of width $(1/k+1/r)/π$, before directed arithmetic error, using $k$ types and words of length $r$. We also obtain explicit geometric bounds. For the upper bound, we recover finite and countable reflected-block constructions by actual permutations, retaining all pair constraints. A coupled terminal-subset argument gives an explicit lower bound strictly above $1/8$. Together these give $C_{\rm term}+η_{\rm width}\le C_\ast\le U_4$. The lower endpoint comes from the terminal-subset argument, and the upper endpoint from the four-block construction; neither is asserted sharp. The finite-word scheme establishes computability; efficient high-precision evaluation and the structure of global optimizers remain open.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on the Number of Small Cuts
papers.abstract: A $k$-cut of an undirected graph is a minimal edge set whose removal leaves at least $k$ connected components, and its cost is the sum of its edge costs. Write $λ_k$ for the minimum cost of a $k$-cut. For fixed $k\ge2$ and $α\ge1$, we show that in any $n$-vertex graph with $n\ge k$ and nonnegative edge costs, the number of $k$-cuts of cost strictly below $αλ_k$ is $O(n^{\lceilαk\rceil-1})$. This implies an $O(n^{\lfloorαk\rfloor})$ bound for $k$-cuts of cost at most $αλ_k$, sharpening the $O(n^{αk})$ bound of Gupta, Harris, Lee and Li. For $k=2$, our strict bound resolves a conjecture of Henzinger and Williamson and an open question of Karger. The exponent $\lceilαk\rceil-1$ is optimal for $k$-cuts for every $k\ge2$ and $α>1$.

papers.title: Filtrations on D-modules and multiplicities of roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we relate multiplicities of Bernstein--Sato-type polynomials with respect to a function f to several singularity invariants. First, we introduce certain ``mod'' b-functions and show that they characterize the weight filtration on the localization of a simple algebraic holonomic D-module along f, and we provide an algorithm to compute them. Second, we show that they can be approximated by the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions (i.e., the b-functions with respect to powers of f). Furthermore, we give a sharp upper bound for the Hodge level of elements given by a certain sum of such multiplicities. Next, we give an effective asymptotic solution to the Gelfand problem by determining an explicit threshold after which every integer shift of a root of b_f(s) is a pole of the Archimedean zeta function of f. We also show that the order of these poles is equal to the nilpotency index of the logarithmic monodromy operator, which we further express as the limit of the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions. We define several filtrations, relating them to the weight and Hodge filtrations, based upon which we leave some open questions that we address in the affirmative in the case when f has a homogeneous isolated singularity, or it is a hyperplane arrangement, or a semi-invariant on a spherical variety. We give several immediate applications to our results, including a solution to a question of Torrelli on whether 1/f lies in the intersection complex of the hypersurface of f if and only if -1 is a simple root of b_f(s).

papers.title: Cluster Geometry of Universal Schubert Polynomials I: Geometric Bases and Cluster Monomials
papers.abstract: We study Fulton's universal Schubert polynomials through the cluster structure on the upper unitriangular group and representations of type $A$. The convex hull of the initial tropical vectors of standard-elementary monomials is unimodularly equivalent to a product of simplices, and right-regular multisegments index three integral geometric bases of the standard-elementary module. A recursive prefix-record condition characterizes those universal Schubert polynomials that are homogeneous under diagonal conjugation, coincide with the corresponding generic and dual canonical basis elements, and are extended cluster monomials. On this locus, cover forests give squarefree factorizations into cluster variables. Outside it, the initial Laurent expansion has a coefficient $-1$.

papers.title: Tilting realizations of derived-equivalent matrix centralizer algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a centralizer matrix algebra over an arbitrary field. We prove that a centralizer matrix algebra $B$ is derived equivalent to $A$ if and only if $B\simeq{\rm End}_A(T)^{\rm op}$ for some tilting $A$-module $T$ of projective dimension at most one. We classify the basic tilting $A$-modules and identify their poset with a product of right weak orders on symmetric groups. For a fixed primary block, mutations exchange adjacent entries of the gap word. The isomorphism classes of the resulting opposite endomorphism algebras are parametrized by left cosets of the stabilizer of this word. The quotient of its labeled mutation graph by the stabilizer action is a Schreier multigraph. We also characterize when the right weak-order orientation descends to the nonloop edges of this quotient.

papers.title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of Röckner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $Φ_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $γ_t = \int_0^t Φ_r Φ_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $Φ_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $Φ$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}Φ$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same Hölder triangle of moment exponents.

papers.title: Non-equivalence of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants
papers.abstract: Suppose $p > 7$ is a prime number, and $F$ is a nonarchimedean local field of residual characteristic $p$ satisfying $F \neq \mathbb{Q}_p$. Generalizing results of Ghate--Le--Sheth, Le--Singh, and Huang, we show that any split, connected, reductive group $G$ over $F$ which is not a torus admits a smooth, irreducible, non-admissible mod $p$ representation. We use this to show that the functor of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants does not induce an equivalence between the category of smooth mod $p$ $G$-representations generated by their pro-$p$-Iwahori invariant vectors and modules over the pro-$p$-Iwahori--Hecke algebra, contrary to what happens for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

papers.title: If the moduli space of metrics is Borel, then it is completely metrizable
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metrizable space. We prove that the space of compatible metrics on $X$ is Borel in the space of continuous pseudometrics, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence, if and only if $X$ is $σ$-compact. These conditions are equivalent to complete metrizability of the space of compatible metrics; the same characterization holds for each component. For ultrametrizable $X$ and $R\subseteq[0,\infty)$ containing $0$ and arbitrarily small positive elements, we prove analogous results for compatible $R$-valued ultrametrics and their $R$-components, {with neighborhoods defined by agreement at every point pair where either ultrametric exceeds a positive $ε\in R$}. For the nonempty subspaces of complete compatible metrics and complete compatible $R$-valued ultrametrics, Borelness and complete metrizability are equivalent to compactness of $X$. The proofs use continuous families of metrics parametrized by trees or subsets of compact completions.

papers.title: Internal Reasoning and Consistency in Reflective Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic allowing direct expression of any general-recursive computation. Every RGA term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation, with a proof certificate at each universal quantifier. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, that such a system is powerful enough to carry out its own metamathematics. A fuel-indexed decider of RGA's grounded semantics and checkers for RGA's proofs are compiled primitive-recursive RGA terms. RGA proves internally that its decider never affirms 0 = 1, and that every well-formed term it affirms has an RGA proof accepted by a transparent test. RGA proves that, for each valid RGA proof, its conclusion is true. RGA proves that each grounded-true well-formed term is provable. RGA proves that no proof in either of two decided classes of RGA proofs derives 0 = 1. RGA's truth predicate also serves as a medium for proof by reflection, of the kind that adds nothing to the system. RGA derives disquotation for quantifier-free formulas as rules in every context, at a free variable, and proves, as one sentence, that whenever its normalizer for polynomials in one variable gives two terms the same normal form, the equation between them is true at every value of the variable. Each such polynomial identity then follows from that sentence by closed evaluation and disquotation, with no reflection rule. A companion paper proves Gödel's incompleteness theorems for RGA and its extensions.

papers.title: Disconnected graphs and extremal bounds for realizable distance orders
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph together with a total order $\prec$ on its edges. We say that $\prec$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^d$ if there is a placement of the vertices of $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the Euclidean lengths of the edges induce exactly the order $\prec$. Almendra-Hernández and Martínez-Sandoval proved that every total order on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$. We show that the same is not true for the disjoint union of two complete graphs: for every $n\geq 3$ there is a total order on the edges of $K_n\sqcup K_n$ that is not realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$, but is in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. Thus, the realizability of an order on a disconnected graph is not determined by its restrictions to the connected components. We also study the extremal problem of maximizing the number of edges of an $n$-vertex graph all of whose edge-orders are realizable in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and show that for every fixed $d$ this maximum is $dn+o(n)$, with explicit bounds on the error term. On the real line we sharpen these bounds and show that a disjoint union of two cycles is realizable in $\mathbb{R}$ unless both cycles are triangles.

papers.title: Support $τ$-tilting posets and Hochschild reconstruction for matrix centralizer algebras
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a field and $A$ the endomorphism algebra of a finite direct sum of cyclic modules over a finite-dimensional commutative local principal ideal $R$-algebra. An explicit central quotient identifies the support $τ$-tilting poset of $A$ with the weak order on a symmetric group. The center of $A$, together with degree-zero Hochschild homology as a module over the center, recovers the truncated local algebra and the multiset of successive length gaps. Applied to centralizer matrix algebras, these results show that the support $τ$-tilting poset determines exactly the multiset of distinct-exponent counts of the primary blocks, whereas the center--Hochschild pair recovers their local algebras and gap multisets. Combined with the known classification, this characterizes derived equivalence by isomorphism of these algebra--module pairs. We also establish Morita reconstruction results in the string and gentle classes.

papers.title: Density of list- and correspondence-critical graphs
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is list $k$-critical if $G$ is not $(k-1)$-list-colorable, but every proper subgraph of $G$ is $(k-1)$-list-colorable. In this paper, we study the function $f_{\ell}(n,k)$ denoting the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex list $k$-critical graph, as well as the function $g_{\ell}(k) = \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac 2n f_{\ell}(n,k) - k + 1$. We show that for all $k \geq 4$, every list $k$-critical graph on $n \geq k+2$ vertices has more than $(k-1+\frac 1{28})\frac n2$ edges, which implies that $g_{\ell}(k) \geq \frac{1}{28}$ for all $k \geq 4$. This is the first result showing that $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty} g_{\ell}(k) > 0$. We also show that $g_{\ell}(k) \geq \frac{1}{24}$ for all $k\geq 352$. As a corollary to our result, we obtain the following improvement to Brooks' theorem: For all $d \geq 3$, if $G$ has no $K_{d+1}$ subgraph and has maximum average degree at most $d+\frac 1{28}$, then $G$ is $d$-list-colorable. All of our results hold in the setting of correspondence coloring (DP-coloring) as well. As a corollary of our correspondence coloring result, we also show that for each $d \geq 3$, a minimal unsatisfiable anti-functional binary constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) with variable domains of size $d$ has a primal graph whose unique nontrivial component either contains $K_{d+1}$ or has average degree at least $d+\frac 1{28}$.

papers.title: Small-data $L^2$ theory for the intermediate NLS and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of nonlinear Schrödinger equations (NLS) in a unified way. This class includes two important examples: the intermediate NLS (INLS) and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS (CM-DNLS). Our main results are twofold. First, we prove small-data global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ for a broad class of equations. This includes both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for arbitrary choices of its parameters. Second, we prove small-data scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ under an additional assumption. This result covers both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for specific choices of its parameters. Both the formulation of the problem, including the notion of solution, and the proofs rely crucially on a linear theory for Schrödinger equations with rough time-dependent potentials. This theory is also of independent interest, since we allow potentials so rough that the standard Duhamel formulation may not make sense. Our approach is perturbative and is built on the bilinear Strichartz estimate proved by Ozawa and Tsutsumi in 1998. In particular, our argument does not rely on integrability.

papers.title: Remarks on some quasi-linear fourth order parabolic equations arising in mathematical physics
papers.abstract: This note proves existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to a broad class of fourth-order quasi-linear parabolic equations in the class of Wiener spaces. It improves upon previous results in the literature, devoted to some special cases falling within the general framework developed here, in which uniqueness held true in a smaller class than the space where existence was proven. Gain of analyticity, as well as generalisations to higher-order equations and to propagation of higher regularities, are also discussed.

papers.title: The D'Alembert-Lagrange Principle and Lagrange Equations
papers.abstract: In this expository-research article we present a rigorous geometric framework for analytical mechanics in the extended phase space, accommodating general constraints that may be non-linear in velocities. We prove that the space of virtual displacements and ideal constraint reactions depend strictly on the intrinsic geometry of the constraint manifold and are entirely invariant under the choice of analytical constraint equations. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equations of the second kind are derived through the covector covariance of the variational derivative operator under the embedding mapping of the configuration manifold.

papers.title: A CIR-Type Diffusion Driven by Hermite Processes: Well-Posedness, Positivity and Malliavin Analysis
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic differential equation \[ dX_t=a\bigl(b(t)-X_t\bigr)\,dt+\bigl(σ_0+σ_1\sqrt{φ_\eps(X_t)}\bigr)\,dZ_t^{(q,H)}, \qquad X_0=x_0, \] where $Z^{(q,H)}$ is a Hermite process of order $q\geq1$ and Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$, $b$ is a periodic target, $σ_0>0$, and $φ_\eps$ is a smooth positive function equal to $x+\eps$ on $[0,\infty)$. The equation is understood pathwise, in the sense of Young. We prove that it has a unique solution. We give lower bounds on the probability that the solution stays positive on $[0,T]$, for every $σ_1\geq0$: after a Lamperti-type change of variables, which makes the noise additive, a last-passage argument shows that the probability of reaching $0$ before $T$ is at most of order $\exp(-c\,Λ(m_0)^{2/q}/T^{2H/q})$, where $m_0$ is the smaller of the initial level and the minimum of the target and $Λ$ is the natural scale of the diffusion coefficient. For $q\le2$ and $σ_1=0$ we show that the solution reaches negative values with positive probability, so that no almost-sure positivity holds in that case. Finally, the solution at each time belongs to $\D^{1,\infty}$, with an explicit representation of its Malliavin derivative, and its law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. The proofs of these two results are self-contained and rely on the additive form of the equation. Numerical experiments based on a wavelet-type simulation of Hermite processes illustrate the results.

papers.title: Incompressible surfaces, hierarchies and unknot recognition
papers.abstract: We present a new algorithm to determine whether a compact orientable surface properly embedded in a compact orientable 3-manifold is incompressible. As a special case, this provides a new algorithm to detect the unknot. The central technique is the use of hierarchies. Unlike previous algorithms, no challenging invariants need to be computed and no lengthy search procedures are required. This algorithm leads to a new proof that determining whether a compact orientable 3-manifold has incompressible boundary is in NP.

papers.title: Repeated differentiation of deterministic polynomials with asymptotically radial root distributions
papers.abstract: Recent works of Galligo, Najnudel, and Vu (2025) and Najnudel and Vu (2026) study repeated differentiation for polynomials of the form $P(z)=p(z^m)$, where $p$ is a deterministic polynomial of degree $n$ with real, non-negative roots, in the regime where $m$ and $n$ are large. If $m\gg \log(n)$ and the root distribution of $P$ converges to a compactly supported, radial probability measure $μ_0$, these works show that for $0\le t<1$, the root distribution of the $\lfloor nmt\rfloor$-th derivative of $P$ converges to a compactly supported probability measure $μ_t$ given by an explicit formula for its radial quantile function. We give a substantially simplified proof of this result and also extend the result from repeated differentiation to repeated applications of the differential operator $z^a(d/dz)^b$. Our proof is based on new, sharp estimates on the roots of polynomial with real, non-negative roots in terms of the coefficients of the polynomial. We also compute the limiting root distribution in the case when $m$ is fixed and $n$ tends to infinity. Then letting $m$ tend to infinity we obtain the same limit as before. Along the way, we prove a generalization of the free multiplicative law of large numbers that is of independent interest.

papers.title: Characteristic classes on a noncommutative background: a new approach
papers.abstract: We introduce analogues of partial derivatives with respect to the generators of the enveloping algebras $U(gl(N))$ and their $q$-deformations, the so-called modified reflection equation algebras. Using these quantum partial derivatives, we introduce the corresponding differential algebras, define the quantum de Rham operator, and exhibit the Leibniz rule for its action. Our Leibniz rule differs from its classical analogue and stems from the construction of a quantum double. In the case of the algebra $U(gl(N))$, we present another form of the Leibniz rule that is more convenient for prolonging the differential calculus to certain extensions of this algebra. We then use analogues of the Cayley--Hamilton identity for the generating matrices of $U(gl(N))$ and of reflection equation algebras to construct projective modules over these algebras. For these projective modules, we introduce Grassmannian connections and define the corresponding Chern classes.

papers.title: Swapping and Switching for Markov Processes: Symmetrisation and Fast-Exchange Limits
papers.abstract: In parallel tempering, exchanging the positions of the replicas (swapping) and exchanging the assignment of dynamics to the replicas (switching) are often used interchangeably. We study the two descriptions as stochastic processes, for Markov species (the dynamics that are exchanged) and bounded measurable exchange rates. To guarantee the Markovianity of each process under the exchanges, switching records both the positions and the label that tracks which species each replica carries; swapping records only the positions. Driving both with one exchange clock places them on a common probability space and lets us write swapping as switching with the label forgotten. This relation holds pathwise at every time and, once decomposed over the label, yields an exact identity between their transition kernels. This characterisation lets us relate, in a precise way, where the two processes agree and where they differ. We describe mainly the relation between their decay rates at finite exchange rate, and between their distributions and observables at finite and infinite exchange rate. The relation between the Markovianity of the two is particularly interesting. At finite rate, switching needs the label to be Markov, while swapping is Markov on its own. In the infinite-rate limit this reverses: swapping becomes non-tight, while switching becomes Markov on the physical coordinates alone. We illustrate all these relations on a solvable benchmark of two Brownian motions with drift under a constant exchange rate. The rich behaviour already visible in this simple case, and developed throughout the paper, suggests that the swapping mechanism is of interest in its own right, beyond the balance conditions needed in parallel tempering.

papers.title: Filon Methods for Highly Oscillatory Controlled Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Fast and accurate classical simulation of quantum systems is a central challenge in the design and control of quantum computers, but the highly oscillatory dynamics of these systems severely limit the efficiency of standard numerical methods. To address this, we adapt Filon quadrature for oscillatory integrals into two numerical methods, called Filon and Controlled Filon, for solving linear systems of ODEs with highly oscillatory solutions. We tailor both methods for efficient implementation in controlled quantum systems, and the Controlled Filon method additionally accounts for the oscillatory structure of the control pulses. We show by numerical experiments that these methods significantly reduce the computational cost of accurately simulating systems of superconducting transmon qubits by decreasing the number of timesteps needed to reach a given level of precision, with only a modest increase in the cost per timestep. For a realistic simulation of the dynamics of a CNOT gate, the Controlled Filon method is the most efficient method tested at every target accuracy, outperforming the best Hermite method by up to 6x and the Hermite method of the same order by up to 500x.

papers.title: Learning-enabled Acceleration of Scenario-based Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Scenario-based model predictive control (SBMPC) is a variant of model predictive control (MPC) that explicitly accounts for uncertainty by optimizing control actions over multiple predicted scenarios. However, its computational complexity increases rapidly with the number of scenarios and prediction horizon, limiting its applicability to real-time planning and control. This paper presents a learning-accelerated Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) algorithm for efficiently solving SBMPC problems by leveraging parallel computing and Moreau envelope learning, while maintaining high solution accuracy. We reformulate the SBMPC problems into consensus forms that can be decomposed via ADMM, separating the scenario-dependent dynamics from non-anticipativity constraints and enabling parallel updates across scenarios and time steps. Building on this decomposition, we utilize a learning-to-optimize scheme that leverages Moreau envelope learning of the cost function to accelerate the primal update in ADMM, thereby reducing computation time. The proposed framework is evaluated on a microgrid energy management problem subject to load and renewable generation uncertainties. Comparisons with IPOPT and MadNLP, two popular and modern nonlinear programming solvers, demonstrate substantial computational speedups while maintaining reliable closed-loop control performance.

papers.title: Lie Meets Network Dynamics: Exact Macroscopic Reductions (Finite Systems)
papers.abstract: We establish a unified theory for exact dimensional reductions in network dynamical systems using Lie-Scheffers theory. For network dynamical systems with mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, we prove that networks of $n$ nodes with local dimension $d$ can be exactly reduced from $nd$ dimensions to a fixed macroscopic system of dimension $md$, where $m$ is the number of fundamental solutions required by the nodal dynamics. Crucially, the superposition rule resulting from the Lie-algebraic structure allows the mean-field coupling to be expressed explicitly in terms of the macroscopic variables, yielding a closed self-consistent system independent of the network size $n$. This reduction collapses the high-dimensional network flow onto (typically) low dimensional invariant manifolds parameterized by $γ=d(n-m)$ independent constants of motion. We illustrate the theory on systems with mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure: ensembles of Riccati equations (recovering known reductions for the Kuramoto model and Theta neuron model), recently studied quasi-linear ODEs, as well as a new class of generalized Bernoulli equations; we explicitly derive the macroscopic flows and conserved quantities for each case. Thus, our theory rigorously explains known reductions and provides a systematic method to discover new ones.

papers.title: Fixed-grid symmetry defects and order recovery for explicit Laplace--rotation integrators in Bose--Einstein dynamics
papers.abstract: A factorization exact for the continuous Laplace--rotation flow need not preserve time symmetry when implemented stage by stage on a Fourier grid. We analyze two explicit exact integrators (EEIs) for rotating Bose--Einstein condensates. For the seven-factor EEI, a constant-state Fourier coefficient proves that its fixed-grid logarithm has a nonzero quadratic defect on every centered even grid for any nonzero rotation vector. For a distinct five-operator EEI, a nonconstant-mode certificate proves the same obstruction on nonsingular coefficient branches whenever at least two rotation components are nonzero. In real-coefficient compact splitting, merging adjacent linear stages with fractions $c_j$ multiplies either defect by the strictly positive factor $κ=\sum_jc_j^2$; nominal high order therefore cannot be guaranteed uniformly at fixed grid. For the seven-factor implementation, the accumulated-response formula predicts $κ_4/κ_6\approx0.7606$ for nominal fourth- and sixth-order compact schemes (CS4/CS6). Scalar dipolar and spin-1 tests of that implementation verify the predicted amplitude ratio and reveal a crossover toward first-order compact behavior under time refinement. Pairing a forward linear half-step with its method adjoint around the exact nonlinear flow restores symmetry of the complete step; classical compositions then recover fourth and sixth order at fixed grid. The analysis provides explicit structural diagnostics and a direct structure-preserving repair.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularities of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow with Quantitatively Precise Dynamics
papers.abstract: For each integer $K\geq2$ when $n\geq4$, and for $K=2,3,4$ when $n=3$, we construct an almost-calibrated Lagrangian mean curvature flow $L_K(t)$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, starting from initial data arbitrarily close to being special Lagrangian, which develops a finite-time Type II singularity at time $T$ with the explicit curvature blow up rate \[ \sup_{L_{K}(t)} |\mathbf{A}_{L_{K}(t)}| \sim (T-t)^{-K/2} \qquad \text{as } t\nearrow T . \] The tangent flow at the singularity is a transverse pair of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian cones, while the Type II blow-up limit is a smooth cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularization. This gives a quantitative construction of Type II blow-up for a fully nonlinear parabolic PDE arising from cohomogeneity-one Lagrangian mean curvature flow. Our construction is based on a modulation analysis around a shrinking family of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularizations, using the perturbative spectral theory developed in the companion paper.

papers.title: Homotopies in Batalin-Vilkovisky Formalism
papers.abstract: We review the notion of homotopy of quantum master actions in geometric Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. Then we construct new examples of such homotopies, coming from renormalization group flow and non-infinitesimal changes of gauge fixing. Finally, we use the field redefinitions given by these homotopies to construct spans of quantum master actions with isomorphic effective actions.

papers.title: Conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times
papers.abstract: The gravitational field of a distant, isolated system is manifested by the conformally invariant Weyl tensor. Thus the conformal structure far from the system encodes the system's gravitational mass. It also encodes the causal structure, thereby linking it to the mass. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, this link led to a novel positive mass theorem of Page, Surya, and the second author \cite{PSW} which did not rely on any traditional energy condition. Here we ask whether that theorem has a rigidity case. Specifically, we consider all null geodesics in an asymptotically AdS spacetime that depart from the Penrose conformal infinity, travel through spacetime, and return to conformal infinity. If all such geodesics from a given point refocus at an antipodal point at infinity, is the spacetime conformal to anti-de Sitter space? It is easy to answer the question if the asymptotically AdS spacetime either (i) obeys the null energy condition in 3 or 4 spacetime dimensions, or (ii) is static (in any dimension), and we give simple proofs in those cases. We then answer the question in the case of globally stationary, asymptotically AdS spacetimes, by applying the theory of magnetic geodesics on the Riemannian manifold-with-boundary obtained by quotienting by the stationary Killing vector field. The question has an analogue for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which we also discuss.

papers.title: Zero-Threshold Discrepancies for Multiple Correlation Sequences
papers.abstract: We study the zero-threshold lifting problem for polynomial multiple correlation sequences with respect to the measure-theoretic pro-nilfactor. The structure theory for polynomial multiple averages implies that, at every positive threshold, positivity on the pro-nilfactor lifts to positivity in the original system, except on a set of zero upper Banach density. We demonstrate that this lifting property does not hold at the zero threshold. Specifically, we construct an ergodic system and two sets of positive measure for which the pro-nilfactor correlation is positive along a set of times with positive upper density, while the corresponding exact correlation vanishes on this set.
