This provides a negative answer to a question posed by Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, Le, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson. %\cite{GKLMMRR}. Additionally, we prove a corresponding rigidity property. For any ergodic system, any essentially distinct family of integer polynomials vanishing at the origin, and any tuple of non-negative bounded functions, the zero-threshold discrepancy set is not piecewise syndetic.

papers.title: The general Brannan coefficient conjecture II: Meijer-function approximations
papers.abstract: The coefficients $A_n(α,β,ω)$ in the Maclaurin expansion $(1+ωz)^α(1-z)^{-β}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} A_n(α,β,ω)z^n$ are considered for $|ω|=1$ and $α,β\in(0,1]$. D. A. Brannan conjectured in a 1973 paper that $|A_n(α,β,ω)|\le A_n(α,β,1)$ for every positive odd integer $n$. The present author recently established the conjecture outside a small neighbourhood of $ω=-1$. The remaining range is treated here by combining compound Laplace integral representations with two types of local approximation: a Meijer $G$ function approximation for $n|\arg(-ω)|$ bounded, and a modified Watson approximation for the complementary range. The resulting lower bounds reduce the problem to numerical positivity checks for explicit functions on compact parameter sets. These computations verify the inequality for all $α,β\in(0,1]$ and all odd integers $n\ge5$, and hence, together with Brannan's result for $n=3$, complete the proof of his conjecture.

papers.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
papers.abstract: The paper is concerned with $α$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $α$-stable SDE.

papers.title: Mehler Formula for Wronskians of Hermite Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that the bilinear generating function for Wronskians of Hermite polynomials can be expressed as the classical Mehler kernel multiplied by a polynomial, thereby extending the result of Pupasov-Maksimov [Ann. Physics 363 (2015), 122-135, arXiv:1502.01778] for exceptional Hermite polynomials. We establish several properties of the polynomials appearing in this extended version of the Mehler formula and present four conjectures about them.

papers.title: Refined asymptotic estimates, Morse index and nondegeneracy of solutions to a biharmonic problem with large exponents in dimension four
papers.abstract: We are concerned with the semilinear biharmonic problem under Dirichlet boundary conditions \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} Δ^2 u=(u^+)^{p} &{\text{in}~Ω},\\[0.5mm] u \not\equiv 0 &{\text{in}~Ω},\\[0.5mm] u=\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial ν} = 0 &{\text{on}~\partial Ω}, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain, $u^+ = \max\{u,0\}$, $ν$ denotes the outward unit normal and $p>1$ is sufficiently large. The basic concentration behavior of solutions satisfying the uniform energy bound is known. In this work, we first obtain refined asymptotic estimates for the peak heights, concentration scales and rescaled profiles of multi-spike solutions. Based on these estimates, we further analyze the generalized linearized eigenvalue problem and derive sharp bounds for the Morse and augmented Morse indices. Consequently, if the limiting $k$-spike configuration ${\mathbf{x}}_\infty$ is a nondegenerate critical point of Kirchhoff--Routh function $Ψ_k$, then \[ m(u_p)=k+n_+\big(D^2Ψ_k({\mathbf{x}}_\infty)\big) \] and $u_p$ is nondegenerate for all sufficiently large $p$ along the selected concentration subsequence. The absence of the maximum principle for the Dirichlet biharmonic operator on general domains poses main difficulties in both refined asymptotic analysis and the study of the generalized linearized eigenvalue problem. To address these difficulties, we employ Green's representation together with refined blow-up and spectral analysis.

papers.title: When can a neural operator replace a coarse solve? Architectural principles for two-level preconditioning
papers.abstract: Neural operators are increasingly used as accelerators inside classical numerical methods, but it is rarely clear which architectural ingredients matter for which application. We answer this question for one important use case: the coarse-space correction inside a two-level preconditioner for discretised linear partial differential equations. We systematically vary four DeepONet-like architectures along two design axes: input discretisation (sampling versus integration against a basis) and source-term linearity. In doing this, we show that the favourable corner of this 2x2 design is occupied by a single architecture, the Neural Green's Operator (NGO), and that moving away from it produces predictable failure modes: highly non-normal preconditioned systems, breakdown of preconditioned conjugate gradients on self-adjoint problems, and stagnation on non-self-adjoint ones. Used as a coarse-space correction, the NGO matches the iteration count of an exact coarse solve on 2D diffusion and advection-diffusion problems. The principle generalises: integrating inputs against the basis used for the output is what allows a neural operator to serve as a Galerkin-type coarse-space correction.

papers.title: Evaluation of External Magnetic Flux Density in Piezo-Flexomagnetic Nanobeams Using a Hybrid 1D-2D Finite Element Framework
papers.abstract: Most theoretical models of piezo-flexomagnetic nanostructures forcibly impose magnetic isolation at the structure-air interface, neglecting the external magnetic domain entirely. This mathematical compromise limits the model's capability to account for stray-field behavior in non-contact applications. To overcome this gap, our study proposes a fully coupled hybrid finite element formulation combining a 1D Timoshenko beam model with a 2D magneto-static problem, encompassing both the beam body and the surrounding air domain. By continuously mapping 1D structural kinematics into the 2D space to define the mechanically induced magnetic flux, and subsequently integrating the resulting 2D scalar potential back into 1D static generalized magnetic loads, this framework enhances the capability of the simple 1D beam model. The results present the distribution of an external magnetic flux in piezo-flexomagnetic structures and identify the material parameters driving this. Ultimately, the proposed computational method extends the boundary of a 1D beam model to an infinite-domain multiphysics environment.

papers.title: Efficient TV regularization of large-scale linear inverse problems via the SCD semismooth* Newton method with applications in tomography
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the efficient numerical minimization of Tikhonov functionals resulting from total-variation (TV) regularization of linear inverse problems. Since the TV penalty is non-smooth, this is typically done either via smooth approximations, which are inexact, or using non-smooth optimization techniques, which can often be numerically expensive, in particular for large-scale problems. Here, we present a numerically efficient minimization approach based on the recently proposed semismooth* Newton method, which employs a novel concept of graphical derivatives and exhibits locally superlinear convergence. The proposed approach is specifically tailored to TV regularization, suitable for large-scale inverse problems, and supported by strong mathematical convergence guarantees. Furthermore, we demonstrate its performance on two (large-scale) tomographic imaging problems and compare our results to those obtained via other state-of-the-art TV regularization approaches. Finally, an open-source Matlab implementation of the proposed method is made available online at https://github.com/HGfrerer/TVReg-2D-Semismoothstar-Newton.

papers.title: Diagonal parity and loop toggling for symmetric matrices over $\mathbb F_2$
papers.abstract: For a symmetric matrix $M$ over $\mathbb F_2$, it is known that its diagonal vector belongs to its column space. We prove the parity refinement that every solution of $Mx=\operatorname{diag}(M)$ satisfies $\operatorname{diag}(M)^Tx\equiv\operatorname{rank}(M)\pmod 2$. This extends the parity theorem for odd dominating sets to graph matrices with arbitrary binary diagonal labels. A self-contained rank-one update formula gives the changes caused by a single loop toggle and yields $\operatorname{nul} A(\overline G)=\operatorname{nul}(A(G)+I)+[\operatorname{rank}(A(G)+I)\text{ is odd}]$. For rooted trees, we augment Filmus's three classes of realizable boundary data with an explicit multiplicity recursion. The resulting formula computes the nullity of $A(T)+D_\varepsilon$ in a single traversal and gives a nonsingularity criterion. For complete rooted trees with eventually periodic labels indexed by height above the leaves, we obtain eventual periodicity of the boundary states and nullity formulas affine in powers of the branching degree on each eventual residue class. Constant labels give explicit closed forms.

papers.title: Flotation Rigidity for Convex Polytopes
papers.abstract: We prove that the oriented liquid-level function determines a full-dimensional convex polytope $P\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and its relative density $δ\in(0,1)\setminus\{\tfrac12\}$. Uniqueness also follows from buoyancy surfaces at distinct densities accumulating at a non-half interior value. For polygons, fixed-density buoyancy data determine the normalized difference body, yielding uniqueness among centrally symmetric polygons at every density.

papers.title: Strategically Robust Linear Quadratic Dynamic Games
papers.abstract: We study linear quadratic dynamic games where players are uncertain about each other's control policies or goals and consequently seek to be strategically robust. Building on recent work on strategically robust and risk-averse game theory, we first formalize the problem of strategically robust linear quadratic dynamic games. We show that these can be rewritten as simple transformations of linear quadratic games in which each player chooses a controller in a fictitious game in which they are faced with an adversary who is penalized for deviating from the other players' policies. This formulation naturally induces a novel notion of dynamic equilibrium, which we call a strategically robust dynamic equilibrium. We establish existence and uniqueness (in the subgame-perfect sense) of such equilibria and show that the equilibrium policies are Markovian, linear, and can be efficiently computed via coupled backward Riccati equations. Through numerical simulations, including experiments in a network game, we illustrate the benefits of strategic robustness in designing robust and resilient decentralized control schemes. Our experiments also expose a "free-lunch" phenomenon in games in which robustness does not incur a corresponding loss in performance but can yield improvements in players' utilities and social welfare.

papers.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: II. Wetting and Brownian watermelon
papers.abstract: The $q$-state Potts model is an archetypical model for various types of phase transitions. We consider it on the square grid and focus on the regime where it undergoes a discontinuous transition, that is $q>4$. At the transition point $T_c(q)$, there are exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures (pure phases): $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). This work establishes for the first time the wetting phenomenon in a precise geometric form and in the entire regime of discontinuity $q>4$: at $T_c(q)$, between two ordered phases a disordered layer emerges and, in the diffusive scaling, its boundaries converge to a pair of Brownian motions conditioned not to intersect. This is starkly different from the subcritical ($T<T_c(q)$) behaviour. At $T_c(q)$, previous results (Bricmont--Lebowitz '87, Messager--Miracle-Sole--Ruiz--Shlosman '91) were limited to the construction and properties of the surface tension for large enough $q$. In a companion work, arXiv:2502.04129, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-disorder Dobrushin conditions. That work also develops a ``renewal picture'' à la Ornstein-Zernike for a suitable percolation model, which plays a central part in our study of the Potts interfaces. The latter is the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and is related to the Potts model via a chain of couplings going through the six-vertex model. In the current work, we extend the analysis to a pair of interacting order-disorder interfaces forming the separation between the two ordered phases, and couple them to a pair of well-behaved random walks conditioned not to intersect. The construction of the coupling is based on rigorously deriving entropic repulsion between the two interfaces. We also prove convergence of interfaces in the FK-percolation model at $p_c(q)$ when $q>4$.

papers.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
papers.abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

papers.title: On ergodicity of the SAGA-LD algorithm
papers.abstract: The so-called SAGA-LD algorithm is used for efficient sampling from high-dimensional distributions in machine learning. Its intricate dynamics resists standard approaches of Markov chain theory. We prove, using a model-specific method, that SAGA-LD converges to a limiting distribution and a law of large numbers holds.

papers.title: On Spherically Symmetric Sprays
papers.abstract: This paper studies spherically symmetric sprays, i.e., sprays that are invariant under orthogonal transformations. We first establish a canonical form for such sprays, showing that their geodesic coefficients can be expressed as \(G^i = |y|α(r,s) y^i + |y|^2β(r,s) x^i\), where \(r = |x|^2\) and \(s = \langle x,y\rangle/|y|\). For projectively flat spherically symmetric sprays -- which are directly related to Hilbert's fourth problem on characterizing metrics whose geodesics are straight lines -- we derive a complete classification of those with isotropic curvature, and in particular, we obtain the explicit form of those with zero curvature. Furthermore, we characterize sprays of weakly isotropic curvature in this class by a system of partial differential equations. These results may provide a unified framework for understanding symmetry and curvature in spray geometry and may offer new insights into the metrizability problem in Finsler geometry.

papers.title: Deterministic sketching for Krylov subspace methods
papers.abstract: Randomized sketching is currently introduced into every area of numerical linear algebra. In Krylov subspace methods, it allows runtime savings at the cost of small accuracy reductions. This work offers a different view on sketching in Krylov subspace methods by analyzing what subspace embeddings are obtained by arbitrary sketching matrices. The analysis gives rise to a deterministic sketching approach leveraging row subset selection techniques that yield subspace embeddings holding with probability 1. We propose deterministically sketched Krylov subspace methods for matrix functions, linear systems, and eigenvalue problems that show a similar performance to their randomly sketched counterparts.

papers.title: A Sequential Cubic Programming Method with Second-Order Complexity Guarantees for Equality Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a new method for equality constrained optimization problems based on a sequential cubic programming framework. Each iteration utilizes a step decomposition based on the Jacobian of the constraints into a normal and a tangential component, the latter of which is found by solving a subproblem involving cubic regularization. The method incorporates second-order correction steps as necessary to ensure global convergence to second-order stationary points as well as local quadratic convergence. In addition, we show that the algorithm is the first to obtain worst case complexity guarantees on the order of $\mathcal{O}(ε_g^{-3/2})$ for the gradient of the Lagrangian, $\mathcal{O}(ε_H^{-3})$ in terms of second-order stationarity, and $\mathcal{O}(ε_c^{-1})$ in terms of the constraint violation. These are the best known complexity guarantees of any method for this class of problems.

papers.title: Implication semilattice of 990 quadratic quasigroup equational laws
papers.abstract: In his quest to exhibit a non-distributive lattice, Ernst Schröder considered 135 years ago a list of 990 equational laws on quasigroups, a non-associative generalization of groups. The laws of interest are analogues of associativity, such as $(x // y) * z = (y // x) \backslash\backslash z$, built from the multiplication $*$ and right/left conjugate-division operations, with the same three distinct variables on both sides. I determine all 114 equivalence classes of their conjunctions, and all implications between them. This includes as a small corner the non-distributive lattice identified by Schröder. Apart from 31 classes that are related to inverse properties (and weaker than total symmetry), and 3 that describe groups and their parastrophes, the remaining 80 are subject to the Four Quasigroups Theorem and quasigroups satisfying them are isotopes of Abelian groups. More than half of these describe (affine) modules over interesting rings.

papers.title: Induced quadratic structures of operated algebras with applications to multi-Novikov algebras
papers.abstract: We formulate binary-quadratic induced structures for unary--binary operads by taking the arity-three part of the kernel of the substitution map for chosen induced binary operations. Our purpose is to identify all universal relations in this quadratic class; we make no claim that they generate the full kernel in every arity. For commutative associative algebras equipped with families of derivations, we determine these quadratic relations explicitly. In the noncommuting-derivation case they give the noncommuting multi-Novikov operad; imposing commutation of the derivations yields exactly the additional relations of the multi-Novikov operad. The one-derivation specialization recovers the usual Novikov operad. The calculations are self-contained at arity three and display how operator identities control induced binary-quadratic structures.

papers.title: Asymmetry of a class of Mellin transforms
papers.abstract: We consider a class of Mellin transforms $μ_η$ associated with a class of functions $η$, defined for every complex $s$ in the critical strip. We establish sufficient conditions on $η$ under which $μ_η(s)$ and $μ_η(1-s)$ cannot both vanish outside the critical line for sufficiently large imaginary parts of $s$. An application is given to the case in which $η$ is the fractional part function, for which the zeros of $μ_η$ coincide with the zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Arithmetic Bias in the Distribution of Mersenne Prime Exponents and the Divisor Structure of $p-1$
papers.abstract: Wagstaff's classical heuristic describes how the probability that $2^p-1$ is prime depends on the size of the prime exponent $p$. We investigate whether the divisor structure of $p-1$ is associated with additional variation among exponents of comparable size. We summarize this structure by $S(p)=\logτ(p-1)/\log\log p$, where $τ$ is the divisor function, and compare regions of higher and lower $S$ within six exponent intervals. In a Wagstaff-balanced design covering all $5{,}761{,}450$ prime exponents $13\le p<10^8$, $32$ of the $47$ known Mersenne-prime exponents lie in the higher-$S$ regions, with a conditional two-sided reference value of $0.01154$ under the weighted-subset null. These comparisons are exploratory: the statistic and conditional analyses were selected post hoc, and the present data do not establish an association beyond the contribution of powers of two to the divisor count. We then construct a modular-response benchmark $H(p)$ from an exactly characterized cyclotomic order family. The benchmark averages a declared response over residue configurations satisfying the selected product-one constraints. Its variation across the full population is summarized by $H(p)\approxθτ(p-1)$, with $θ$ determined without using Mersenne-prime labels. Under a restricted effective-channel continuation hypothesis, relative variation in this score redistributes Wagstaff weight while preserving its total mass on the finite calibration population. The resulting rule allocates $32.28$ and $14.72$ cases to the higher- and lower-$S$ regions, respectively. Extrapolating the same rule to $10^8\le p<10^9$ assigns $73.88\%$ of model weight to the higher-$S$ region.

papers.title: The generalized Lefschetz number and loop braid groups
papers.abstract: We study the interplay between braid group theory and topological dynamics in three dimensions. While classical braid theory has been extensively applied to surface homeomorphisms to analyze fixed and periodic points, an analogous framework in three-dimensional manifolds has been lacking. In this work, we use loop braid groups, a three-dimensional generalization of classical braid groups, to investigate homeomorphisms of the $3$-ball that leave invariant a trivial link of finitely many circles. In our main theorem we relate matrix representations of loop braid groups, which are related to the Burau representation, to the abelianized generalized Lefschetz number. This result provides information on the existence of fixed points of such homeomorphisms and on their linking numbers with the invariant link. As an application, we obtain a lower bound for the number of periodic points of a given period. Our theorem establishes a three-dimensional analogue of a classical result for braids in the disk, and connects loop braid groups with Nielsen fixed point theory and topological dynamics in dimension three.

papers.title: Reconstructing a giant component of a point set in $\mathbb{R}$
papers.abstract: Let $V \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a finite set with $|V| = n $ and suppose we are given each pairwise distance independently with probability $p$. We show that if $p = (1+ε)/n$, for some fixed $ε>0$, then we can reconstruct a subset of size $Ω_ε(n)$, up to translation and reflection, with high probability. This confirms a conjecture posed by Girão, Illingworth, Michel, Powierski, and Scott. We also study a deterministic variant proposed by Benjamini and Tzalik. We show that if we are given $m$ distinct pairwise distances of a point set $V \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $|V|=n$, then we can reconstruct a subset of size $Ω(m/ (n \log n)) $, up to translation and reflection. Moreover, we show that this is optimal, which also disproves a conjecture posed by Benjamini and Tzalik.

papers.title: On a class of hypersurfaces of a product of two space forms
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of class $\mathcal{A}$, previously defined for hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbb{S}^n$ and $\mathbb{H}^n$ denote the sphere and hyperbolic space, respectively, to hypersurfaces of a product $\mathbb{Q}_{c_1}^{k} \times \mathbb{Q}_{c_2}^{n-k+1}$, $2\leq k\leq n-1$, of two space forms with arbitrary constant curvatures $c_1$ and $c_2$. When $c_1$ and $c_2$ are not both equal to $0$, such a hypersurface is in class $\mathcal{A}$ if and only if it has a flat normal bundle when regarded as a submanifold of the underlying flat ambient space. We provide an explicit local construction of all hypersurfaces in class $\mathcal{A}$ that do not split in any open subset in terms of parallel families of hypersurfaces of the factors, and show how it simplifies for the hypersurfaces within this class that have a constant product angle function. We also show that hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature in class $\mathcal{A}$ are given in terms of parallel families of isoparametric hypersurfaces in each factor and a solution of a second order ODE. Finally, we classify hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature in class~$\mathcal{A}$ that have a constant product angle function.

papers.title: $γ$-weakly $θ$-up-concavity: A Unified Framework for Non-Convex Optimization Beyond DR-Submodular and OSS Functions
papers.abstract: Many objectives in machine learning and combinatorial optimization are non-concave. We introduce $γ$-weak $θ$-up-concavity, a first-order condition for nonnegative monotone functions in which a scaling function $θ$ lets the curvature change with the size of the solution. The resulting class strictly contains monotone DR-submodular functions and One-Sided Smooth (OSS) functions. It also contains functions whose marginal gains first increase and then decrease, and functions that vanish faster than any power of the norm at the origin. We construct a surrogate gradient from gradients along the segment from the origin to the current point and prove an upper-linearization inequality with a point-dependent approximation coefficient. Restricting actions to the closed convex hull of the coordinate-wise maximal feasible points makes this coefficient uniformly positive, with a value determined by the curvature parameters and the geometry of the feasible set. Standard reductions to linear optimization then give offline approximation algorithms and online algorithms with regret guarantees. The coefficient matches the optimal one for DR-submodular maximization and improves the best known coefficients for OSS maximization over matroid constraints whenever the OSS parameter is positive.

papers.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
papers.abstract: The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms $f_0, f_1 : A \to B$. Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings $Cyl_q(B)$, which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring $Cyl(B)$. For $q=1$ this recovers Keller's original construction. The sets $SHom_q(A,B)$ of DG ring homomorphisms $A \to Cyl_q(B)$ form the simplicial Hom set $SHom(A,B)$. Our main result is that when $A$ is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set $SHom(A,B)$ is a Kan complex. We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid $SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B)$, including invariance under quasi-isomorphism $B' \to B$.

papers.title: Functional Stochastic Localization
papers.abstract: Eldan's stochastic localization is a probabilistic construction that has proved instrumental to modern breakthroughs in high-dimensional geometry and the design of sampling algorithms. Motivated by sampling under non-Euclidean geometries and the mirror descent algorithm in optimization, we develop a functional generalization of Eldan's process that replaces Gaussian regularization with regularization by any positive integer multiple of a log-Laplace transform. We further give a mixing time bound on the Markov chain induced by our localization process, which holds if our target distribution satisfies a functional Poincaré inequality. Finally, we apply our framework to differentially private convex optimization in $\ell_p$ norms for $p \in [1, 2)$, where we improve state-of-the-art query complexities in a zeroth-order model.

papers.title: ReLU Networks for Model Predictive Control: Network Complexity and Performance Guarantees
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed a resurgence in using ReLU neural networks (NNs) to represent model predictive control (MPC) policies. However, determining the sufficient network complexity to ensure closed-loop guarantees remains a fundamental open problem. This involves a critical precision-complexity trade-off: undersized networks may fail to capture the MPC policy, while oversized ones may outweigh the benefits of ReLU network approximation. In this work, we project the MPC actions onto a tightened constraint set to satisfy the hard constraints, and establish a state-dependent Lipschitz continuity property for the optimal MPC cost function, which enables sharp convergence analysis of the closed-loop system. For the first time, we derive explicit bounds on ReLU network width and depth for approximating MPC policies with closed-loop guarantees. To reduce network complexity for the convergence to user-specified target sets, we propose a non-uniform error framework with a state-aware scaling function to adaptively adjust both the input and output of the ReLU network. Our contributions provide a foundational step toward certifiable ReLU NN-based MPC.

papers.title: A construction of smooth varieties admitting small contractions
papers.abstract: Given a smooth variety together with two smooth subvarieties, we construct, via two successive blowups, smooth varieties admitting small contractions. This generalizes Kawamata's example of small contraction in dimension 4. We also construct the flip of the contraction explicitly. As an application, from products of two del Pezzo surfaces we obtain smooth weak Fano fourfolds that admit small contractions with Picard number up to 10.

papers.title: Bi-Lipschitz invariance of Newton polygons along gradient canyons
papers.abstract: We study bi-Lipschitz right-equivalence of holomorphic function germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ via polar arcs and gradient canyons. For a polar arc $γ$ we consider the Newton polygon of $f_x(X+γ(Y),Y)$ and define its augmentation by adjoining the point $(0,\operatorname{ord} f(γ(y),y)-1)$. We prove that the resulting augmented Newton polygon is constant along each gradient canyon of degree $>1$ and is invariant under bi-Lipschitz right-equivalence. Moreover, its compact edges decompose into a topological part and a Lipschitz part: the latter encodes, through simple intercept relations, the second-level Henry-Parusiński type invariants. As applications, we obtain two numerical bi-Lipschitz invariants attached to a canyon: its polar multiplicity and, via the Koike-Kuo-Păunescu curvature formula, the total asymptotic Gaussian curvature concentrated in it.

papers.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
papers.abstract: Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces. The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.

papers.title: On identity Seidel switches
papers.abstract: An identity Seidel switch of a graph is a vertex subset whose Seidel switch produces an isomorphic graph. We distinguish the elementary abelian group of switching operations from the family of identity switches of a fixed graph, which need not be a group. We obtain an edge-count condition for identity switches and deduce that every vertex-identity switch has degree half the number of remaining vertices. In particular, no graph of order at least two has every vertex as an identity switch. For a two-vertex switching set inducing an edge, we characterize the switches admitting an isomorphism that preserves the endpoint pair, in terms of automorphisms of the remaining induced subgraph. We establish modification results under this additional hypothesis and give explicit constructions of identity switches. Counterexamples show why edge-count conditions and unrestricted modification assertions do not suffice.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Dictionary for Partitioned Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish a dictionary between the behavior of a general map $f: X \to X$ which is defined by using a decomposition into disjoint subsets $X = A \cup B$ and the thermodynamic formalism. The approach is set theoretical, topological and ergodic. We define a key topology and consider its Borel $σ$-algebra in order to study the thermodynamic formalism for the general setting, proving that recurrence implies periodicity, the topological entropy is zero, we can decompose the invariant measures into a general sum of ergodic ones and we establish a dictionary between the cycles and the equilibrium states of continuous potentials. All this is done for the general setting, with applications for the Syracuse maps and the Collatz map in particular. Finally, we give several applications beyond the arithmetic realm: algebraic maps, counting closed geodesics by Margulis' formula, infinite chessboard and stochastic lattices.

papers.title: On the well-posedness of two-dimensional Hele-Shaw flow with an elastic interface
papers.abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional Hele-Shaw free-boundary problem with a nonlinear elastic interface, for both one-phase and two-phase scenarios. Using the paradifferential formulation, we demonstrate that the problem is locally well-posed in $H^s$ for $s\geq 2$ for arbitrary initial data. Furthermore, for the one-phase case and the stable two-phase case $(ρ^+ \leq ρ^-)$, we establish global well-posedness for small initial data in $H^s$ when $s> \frac{3}{2}$.

papers.title: Heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes on closed subsets $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a Borel subset $Σ$ of $F$. We assume that $F\setminus Σ$ is a $κ$-fat set and is dense in $F$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $F$, that the Assouad dimension of $F$ is strictly less than $d$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. The jump kernels under consideration take the form $J(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-α}{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, where $α\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal B}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $Σ$ of $F$. A fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $F\setminus Σ$. Examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $α$-stable processes in some unbounded $C^{1,\rm Dini}$ sets, processes in Lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal Neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.

papers.title: On $R$-equivalence of Automorphism Groups of Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional associative $k$-algebra with identity. The primary aim of this paper is to study the rationality properties of the group of all $k$-algebra automorphisms of $A$, as an affine algebraic group over an arbitrary field $k$. We investigate mainly the $R$-equivalence property of the identity component of $\mathrm{Aut}_{k}(A)$ over a perfect field $k$.

papers.title: On $π_1$-injectivity of self-maps in low dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that all self-maps of non-zero degree of $3$-manifolds not covered by $S^3$ and of Thurston geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums not diffeomorphic to $N\#(\#_{p\geq0}S^2\times S^2)\#(\#_{q\geq0}\mathbb C P^2)$, where $N$ is an $S^2\times\mathbb X^2$ or $S^3\times\mathbb R$ manifold, are $π_1$-injective. We thus determine when these maps induce $π_1$-isomorphisms. The results in dimension three were previously established by Shicheng Wang. We give a uniform group theoretic proof in all cases based only on the residual finiteness of the fundamental groups for the $π_1$-injectivity and then only on numerical invariants for the $π_1$-isomorphisms.

papers.title: Polychromatic Localized Waves with Complex Frequencies in Nonlinear Maxwell Equations with Material Dispersion
papers.abstract: We study the existence of polychromatic solutions of cubically nonlinear Maxwell equations in the whole space and with dispersive media, i.e., with a time delayed polarization. Due to the complex nature of the dielectric function, the frequencies are complex, resulting in a decay in time. The geometry is that of a waveguide in $x$ with the propagation direction being $y$ and the solutions are localized in $x$ and have a transverse magnetic polarization. These are often referred to as breathers. They are given as a Fourier series in $y$ and $t$ with the leading frequency $ω$ being an eigenvalue of a corresponding operator pencil on $\mathbb{R}$ (in the $x$ variable). Each term in the series corresponds to a different temporal decay rate or a different frequency. The series is constructed iteratively via a sequence of linear ordinary differential equations. Our general result provides the existence under some assumptions on the spectrum and on estimates of the resolvent of the corresponding linear operator. We also produce an example of a waveguide given by the interface of two spatially homogeneous physically relevant media for which these assumptions are satisfied. For such an interface setting the constructed solutions correspond to nonlinear polychromatic surface plasmons.

papers.title: Topological 5d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ Gauge Theories: Mirror Symmetry and Langlands Duality of $A_\infty$-categories of Floer Homologies
papers.abstract: We explain why on certain five-manifolds, topological 5d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ gauge theory of Haydys-Witten twist with gauge group $G$, is dual to that of Geyer-Mülsch twist with gauge group $^LG$, where $G$ is a real, compact Lie group with Langlands dual $^LG$. In turn, via their 2d and 3d gauged A/B-twisted Landau-Ginzburg model interpretations, we can show that (i) a Fukaya-Seidel-type $A_\infty$-1-category of an HW$_4$-instanton Floer homology of three-manifolds and (ii) a Fueter-type $A_\infty$-2-category of an HW$_3$-instanton Floer homology of two-manifolds, are dual to (i) an Orlov-type $A_\infty$-1-category of a novel holomorphic $^LG_{\mathbb{H}}$-flat Floer homology of three-manifolds and (ii) a Rozansky-Witten-type $A_\infty$-2-category of a novel holomorphic $^LG_{\mathbb{O}}$-flat Floer homology of two-manifolds, respectively. We also derive their Atiyah-Floer-type correspondences to symplectic categories. Our work, which demonstrates a mirror symmetry and Langlands duality of (higher) $A_\infty$-categories of Floer homologies, therefore furnishes purely physical proofs and gauge-theoretic generalizations of the mathematical conjectures by Bousseau [1] and Doan-Rezchikov [2], and more.

papers.title: Logarithmic double phase embeddings with variable exponents: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the necessary and sufficient conditions in the domain for Sobolev-type embedding of the space $W^{1,Φ(\cdot,\cdot)}(Ω)$ where $Φ(x,t):=t^{p(x)}+ a(x) t^{q(x)}\log^{r(x)}(e+t)$ with $1\leq p(x)\leq q(x).$ We have established subcritical embedding in bounded John domains under some regularity assumptions on exponents $p,$ $q,$ $r$, and $a$. Conversely, we have proved that if the embedding holds in any domain $Ω$ in $\mathbb{R}^n,$ then $Ω$ must satisfy the log-measure density condition.

papers.title: On Spectral Clustering in Algebraic Multigrid Methods
papers.abstract: We introduce a new direct multilevel method for solving general nonsingular complex square linear systems admitting a suitable block partition, using a regular smoother and an arbitrary but equal number of pre- and post-smoothings. Through careful analysis of the error propagation operator, we cluster the spectrum of this operator. This allows us to write a direct K-cycle version of the method.

papers.title: Zeroes and Extrema of Functions via Random Measures
papers.abstract: We present methods that provide all zeroes and extrema of a function that do not require differentiation. Using point process theory, we are able to describe the locations of zeroes or maxima, their number, as well as their distribution over a given window of observation. The algorithms in order to accomplish the theoretical development are also provided, and they are exemplified using many illustrative examples, for real and complex functions.

papers.title: Effective existence of primitive k-normal elements via affine spaces
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ be the finite field with $q^n$ elements. An element $α\in \mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ is $k$-normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$ if $α$ and its conjugates span an $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of dimension $n-k$. It is known that, for $q$ larger than a constant $c(n)$, a primitive $k$-normal element exists if and only if there exists a $k$-normal element free of binomials, but $c(n)$ is not explicit. We count the $k$-normal elements in affine subspaces of the form $β+\ker L_h$ and show that, when $h$ is an irreducible factor of the $\mathbb{F}_q$-order of $β$, all but at most one of them are $k$-normal. We also show that, when $β$ is free of binomials, these affine subspaces have degree $n$, so that character sum estimates over affine spaces apply to them. Combining these facts with a sieve, we make the equivalence above effective, with explicit lower bounds on $q$. As an application, we compute these bounds for $5\le n\le 8$ and give a complete characterization of the existence of primitive $k$-normal elements in $\mathbb{F}_{q^6}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

papers.title: A Dynamical Néron--Ogg--Shafarevich Criterion via Orbital Arboreal Representations
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field and $\varphi : \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$ a rational endomorphism of degree $d \geq 2$ over $K$. In the tame case ($p \nmid d$), we show that strict good reduction is equivalent to the existence of a nonempty Zariski open subset $U_k \subset \mathbb{P}^1_k \setminus \mathrm{PC}(\widetilde{\varphi})$ over which the canonical residual morphism is finite étale of degree $d$. The criterion separates two complementary local invariants of a normalized integral lift: $\mathrm{Res}(F,G)$ controls residual degree drop, while the fiber discriminants $\mathrm{Disc}(F_{n,x})$ control étaleness of the residual fibers once full residual degree is ensured. Consequently, for every finite $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$ with $\bar{x} \in U_k$, the extensions $K(X_n(x))/K$ are unramified for all $n \geq 1$. We introduce the orbital preimage tree $T_{O^+(x)} = \varinjlim_n X_\infty(\varphi^n(x))$, the colimit in $G_K$-sets along the forward orbit, and the orbital arboreal Galois image $\mathcal{G}_{O^+(x)} = \mathrm{Im}(G_K \to \mathrm{Aut}(T_{O^+(x)}))$. On the forward-invariant safe locus $U_k^{\mathrm{safe}} = \bigcap_{m \geq 0} \widetilde{\varphi}^{-m}(U_k)$, strict good reduction is captured by the bijectivity of the orbital reduction map $X_n(x_m) \to \widetilde{X}_n(\bar{x}_m)$. This canonical orbit-invariant framework connects with arboreal Galois representations (Boston-Jones, Jones, and others) and yields pointwise and orbit-level reformulations. Explicit examples over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ illustrate the criterion.

papers.title: Solid realization of motives with modulus
papers.abstract: We construct a covariant realization functor $\mathrm{Solid}^m(-)$ from the category of motives with modulus to the derived category of solid modules in the sense of Clausen-Scholze. For a smooth modulus pair $(X,D)$, the dual of $\mathrm{Solid}^m(X,D)$ recovers the Kelly-Miyazaki Hodge realization of $(X,D)$. Let $X$ be a smooth proper variety over a field, let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor whose support has simple normal crossings, and let $U\subset X$ be an open subscheme. We compute $\mathrm{Solid}^m(\mathrm{Cone}(\underline{M}(U,D|_U)\to\underline{M}(X,D)))$ explicitly in terms of the formal completion along $X\setminus U$ of a model of $X$ of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: PAC Reasoning: Controlling the Performance Loss for Efficient Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved remarkable progress in complex problem-solving tasks. Despite this success, LRMs typically suffer from high computational costs during deployment, highlighting a need for efficient inference. A practical direction is to switch the LRM between thinking and non-thinking modes dynamically. However, such approaches often introduce additional reasoning errors and lack statistical guarantees for the performance loss, which are critical for high-stakes applications. In this work, we propose Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) Reasoning that controls the performance loss under the user-specified tolerance. Specifically, we construct an upper confidence bound on the performance loss and determine a threshold for switching to the non-thinking model. Theoretically, using the threshold to switch between the thinking and non-thinking modes ensures bounded performance loss in a distribution-free manner. Our experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that the proposed method can save computational budgets and control the user-specified performance loss.

papers.title: Continuous cochains on Furstenberg boundaries and injectivity of the comparison map
papers.abstract: Monod proved that any continuous cohomology class of a semisimple Lie group $G$ can be represented by a measurable cocycle on the associated Furstenberg boundary, which we upgraded to an alternating cocycle. In the current paper we improve that result by showing that we can actually take a representing cocycle which is continuous on an explicit subset of generic tuples. We give an analogous result in the case of bounded cohomology. Finally, we exploit this characterization to prove the injectivity of the comparison map in degree $3$ for $\mathrm{Isom}^\circ(\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{C}}^n)$, when $n \geq 2$, and in degree $4$ for $\mathrm{Isom}^\circ(\mathbb{H}^n_{\mathbb{R}})$, when $n \geq 2$.

papers.title: Non-fibered strongly quasipositive links and tightness
papers.abstract: It is well known that for fibered links in $\mathbb{S}^3$ being strongly quasipositive and supporting a tight contact structure are equivalent notions (arXiv:math/0509499). In this note we analyze the relation between these two properties for non fibered links. A non fibered link (together with an incompressible Seifert surface) induces a natural partial open book (arXiv:2509.09615). We prove that strongly quasipositive links induce tight contact structures. We also show that, in contrast to the fibered case, the converse is not true, giving examples of links that are not strongly quasipositive but support tight contact structures.

papers.title: When is the canonical conductor minimal?
papers.abstract: For a one dimensional analytically unramified Cohen-Macaulay local ring $R$, the blowup algebra of the canonical ideal is a module finite birational extension. The conductor of this extension always contains the conductor of $R$. We study the case when there is equality. This is the case where $R$ is far from being almost Gorenstein. We characterise such rings among Arf domains and numerical semigroup rings. As an application, we compute the cohomology annihilator ideal of an explicit family of rings and show it to be equal to the conductor ideal.

papers.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo integration over $\mathbb{R}^s$ with boundary-damping importance sampling
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new importance sampling (IS) method tailored to quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) integration over $\mathbb{R}^s$. IS introduces a multiplicative weight that compensates for sampling from a proposal distribution rather than the target distribution. An unsuitable proposal, however, can yield an integrand that exhibits severe boundary growth and suffers from the curse of dimensionality, thus degrading QMC performance. Our approach is to design a weight function with the desired regularity and then construct a transport map realizing it as an IS proposal, thereby obtaining a transformed integrand amenable to QMC integration. We provide a rigorous analysis based on Fourier coefficients and apply it to lattice rule integration. Under suitable conditions, the proposed estimator achieves a fast convergence rate independent of the dimension $s$, making it suitable for high-dimensional problems.

papers.title: Algebraic magnetism, formally verified and extended: a survey
papers.abstract: We formalize in the Lean proof assistant the three papers on algebraic magnetism published in Semigroup Forum: "Algebraic magnetism", "Algebraic magnetism invariants of self-actions of diagonalizable monoid schemes" and "Algebraic magnetism: $X$-products of attractors via $\mathbb{F}_1$-geometry". We also prove further results and comment on the relation with other work in the literature. The description of this formalization and of these results forms in itself a survey of the theory, from the perspective opened by the formalization. The first main mathematical contribution consists of a Bialynicki-Birula decomposition for faces and of proofs of the existence of strongly fixed-point-reflecting atlases, of the finiteness of pure magnets and of the vanishing of the higher monoid cohomology of $\mathrm{A}(M)$ with quasi-coherent coefficients, three conjectures of "Algebraic magnetism". The case of algebraic stacks, where the analogue of the existence of fixed-point-reflecting atlases fails, is treated in joint work with Sylvain Brochard, in which the finiteness of pure magnets was first proved privately, by a comparable method. The second main contribution, for split reductive groups, is a description of the pure magnets and of the join-irreducible ones: besides the classical roots, they are the join-irreducible pure magnets equal to $(1-w)M$ for some $w$ in the Weyl group, which encode the components of attractors; a prime $p$ is a torsion prime of the group, in the sense of Steinberg, if and only if some join-irreducible Weyl magnet $(1-w)M$ has $w$ of $p$-power order.

papers.title: Webification of symmetry classes of plane partitions
papers.abstract: Webs are graphical objects that give a tangible, combinatorial way to compute and classify tensor invariants. Recently, Gaetz, Pechenik, Pfannerer, Striker, and Swanson found a rotation-invariant web basis for $\mathrm{SL}_4$, as well as its quantum deformation $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$, and a bijection between move equivalence classes of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$-webs and fluctuating tableaux such that web rotation corresponds to tableau promotion. They also found a bijection between the set of plane partitions in an $a\times b\times c$ box and a benzene move equivalence class of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$-webs by determining the corresponding oscillating tableau. In this paper, we similarly find the oscillating tableaux corresponding to plane partitions in certain symmetry classes. We furthermore give a combinatorial map, defined on the span of the invariants of webs arising from certain symmetry classes, from $U_q(\sl_4)$ invariants to $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_r)$ invariants for $r=2,3$.

papers.title: Bounds for spectral projectors on the three-dimensional torus
papers.abstract: We study $L^2$ to $L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with $L^p$ norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain. For the three-dimensional torus we prove new cases of a previous conjecture of the first two authors concerning the size of these norms; we also refine certain prior results to remove $ε$-losses in all dimensions. We use methods from number theory: the geometry of numbers, the circle method and exponential sum bounds due to Guo. We complement these techniques with height splitting and a bilinear argument to prove sharp results. We exposit on the various techniques used and their limitations.

papers.title: Time asymptotics, time regularity and separation rates for Navier-Stokes flows in supercritical solution classes
papers.abstract: This paper extends the weak solution theory for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations of Barker, Seregin and Sverak from a critical setting to a supercritical setting making sure to include a useful a priori energy bound as well as a statement about stability under weak-star convergence. Two applications of the a priori bound are then explored. The first provides a spatially local, short-time asymptotic expansion in the time variable starting at $t=0$ which, as a corollary, provides an upper bound on how fast hypothetical non-unique solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations can separate locally. The second establishes higher-order time regularity at a singular time and at spatial points positioned away from the singularity. This quantifies the degree to which the non-local nature of the pressure allows a far flung singularity to disrupt the time regularity at a regular point.

papers.title: Quivers with Polynomial Identities
papers.abstract: We provide a topological characterization of quivers whose path algebra satisfies a polynomial identity. This class includes the oriented cycle and acyclic quivers and, in the latter case, we describe the associated T-ideal. We introduce a generalization of Arnold's A-graded algebras, which we call locally A-graded algebras, and prove that they are also PI. We give an example of a quiver algebra satisfying a polynomial identity, even if the path algebra of the quiver does not.

papers.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
papers.abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.

papers.title: A PINNs approach for the computation of eigenvalues in elliptic problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for computing eigenvalues of elliptic problems using Deep Learning techniques. A key feature of our approach is that it is independent of the space dimension and can compute arbitrary eigenvalues without requiring the prior computation of lower ones. Moreover, the method can be easily adapted to handle nonlinear eigenvalue problems.

papers.title: Minimal W-algebras of $\mathfrak{so}_N$ at level minus one
papers.abstract: For $N \in\mathbb Z_{\geq 7}$ we show that the simple minimal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra of $\mathfrak{so}_N$ at level minus one is isomorphic to the even subalgebra of the tensor product of the simple affine vertex superalgebra of $\mathfrak{osp}_{1|2}$ at level $\frac{N-6}{2}$ with $N-4$ free fermions. In particular when $N$ is even this minimal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra is strongly rational as conjectured by Arakawa-Moreau.

papers.title: Existence of minimizing $n$-harmonic maps in homotopy classes by critical exponents
papers.abstract: We investigate the existence of energy minimizing $n$-harmonic maps from an $n$-dimensional sphere to a compact manifold inside a prescribed homotopy class. Our results are of two kinds. First, inspired by the work by T. Rivière (1998) on minimizing 3-harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ with given Hopf degree and by the work of R. Hardt and T. Rivière (2008) on critical and optimal Sobolev exponents for rational homotopy classes, we exhibit a general principle that guarantees the existence of infinitely many homotopy classes with a minimizing map inside. We apply this principle, each time proving the optimality of the relevant Sobolev exponents, to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{4n-1}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2n}$, where the relevant homotopical quantity is the Hopf invariant, and to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ to $\mathbb{CP}^{n}$, where homotopy classes are generated by the circle bundle on the projective space. These results hold for first-order as well as for fractional Sobolev mappings. Second, elaborating on the recent preprint of Wang G. and Zhang M. (2026), we derive sharp lower energy bounds for mappings with given Hopf invariant. We apply these bounds to deduce a sufficient energetic condition for the existence of minimizing maps in a given homotopy class. Finally, we exploit this condition, by explicit construction of mappings satisfying it, to prove the existence of energy minimizers from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ of Hopf degree $d \in \{\pm2,\pm3,\dotsc,\pm6\}$ and from $\mathbb{S}^{7}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{4}$ of Hopf degree $\pm1$.

papers.title: A Brezis-Nirenberg Type Problem for a Mixed Local-Nonlocal Operator on the Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: This paper studies nonlinear elliptic equations involving the operator $-Δ_{\mathbb{B}^N} + (-Δ_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s-λ$ on the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{B}^N$, where $0 < s < 1$ and $λ<\frac{(N-1)^2}{4}$. We prove that the best Sobolev constant of this mixed local-nonlocal operator equals the Euclidean Sobolev constant $S$ and is never attained, whereas the corresponding purely local constant may lie strictly below $S$. As a consequence, the purely critical problem has no ground state and no nontrivial solution of small $L^{2^*}$ norm. For the subcritical problem, and for the critical problem with a subcritical perturbation $μ|u|^{p-1}u$, we obtain nonnegative radial solutions by variational methods, depending on $p$ and $μ$. Along the way, we prove the continuous embedding $H^1(\mathbb{B}^N)\hookrightarrow H^s(\mathbb{B}^N)$ and the equivalence of the spectral and the pointwise definitions of $(-Δ_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s$.

papers.title: Classification of Certain Rational Isoparametric Functions on Damek-Ricci Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify isoparametric functions on Damek-Ricci spaces which can be written in terms of the standard coordinates $(v,z,t)$ on the half-space model as a polynomial function divided by $t$. Regular level sets of the functions in our classification encompass almost all previously known examples of isoparametric hypersufaces in Damek-Ricci space and also yield new ones. For the new examples, the focal varieties are determined and the mean curvatures of the regular level sets are expressed as a function of the distance from the focal variety. We also study the exceptional case of tubes about $\mathbb R\mathbf H^k$ in $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$, which are isoparametric, but cannot be obtained as the level sets of any function in our classification. We show that these tubes are level sets of a polynomial function divided by $t^2$, and that analogous functions on Damek-Ricci spaces can be isoparametric only in the case of $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$.

papers.title: Analysis of non-linear fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets
papers.abstract: This article addresses three problems: (1) the construction of a general nonlinear fractal interpolation function on post-critically finite (PCF) self-similar sets; (2) the study of the energy and normal derivatives of uniform nonlinear fractal functions; and (3) the estimation of the box-counting dimensions of the proposed fractal functions on the Sierpiński gasket and the von Koch curve. We present a general framework for constructing attractors and fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets using Edelstein contractions. Further, we derive upper and lower bounds for the box-counting dimensions of the graphs of nonlinear interpolants. Finally, we provide several graphical and numerical examples to illustrate the construction and estimate the dimensions for different data sets.

papers.title: High-Order Hermite Optimization: Fast and Exact Gradient Computation in Open-Loop Quantum Optimal Control using a Discrete Adjoint Approach
papers.abstract: This work introduces the High-Order Hermite Optimization (HOHO) method, an open-loop discrete adjoint method for quantum optimal control. Our method is the first of its kind to efficiently compute exact (discrete) gradients when using continuous, parameterized control pulses while solving the forward equations (e.g. Schrodinger's equation or the Linblad master equation) with an arbitrarily high-order Hermite Runge-Kutta method. The HOHO method is implemented in QuantumGateDesign$.$jl (https://github.com/leespen1/QuantumGateDesign.jl), an open-source software package for the Julia programming language, which we use to perform numerical experiments comparing the method to Juqbox$.$jl (https://github.com/LLNL/Juqbox.jl). For realistic model problems we observe speedups up to 775x.

papers.title: Fedder-type criterion for quasi-$F^e$-splitting and quasi-$F$-regularity
papers.abstract: We study quasi-$F^e$-split and quasi-$F$-regular singularities, which generalize Yobuko's quasi-$F$-splitting. We establish Fedder type criteria that characterize these properties for hypersurfaces. These criteria offer explicit tools for computation and verification. As an application, we construct a counterexample to the inversion of adjunction for quasi-$F$-regularity and compute the quasi-$F$-split threshold of the cone over the ordinary cusp.

papers.title: Computing Projective Implicit Representations from Poset Towers
papers.abstract: A family of simplicial complexes connected by simplicial maps and indexed by a finite poset $P$ is called a poset tower. Poset towers subsume multi-parameter filtrations, zigzag filtrations, and one-parameter simplicial towers, while allowing arbitrary finite posets and simplicial maps. The homology of a poset tower is a $P$-persistence module. To compute it globally over $P$, we consider the chain complex segment of $P$-persistence modules $C_{\ell-1}\xleftarrow{\partial_{\ell}}C_\ell \xleftarrow{\partial_{\ell+1}}C_{\ell+1}$ induced by the simplices of the tower. Unlike in one-critical multi-filtrations, the chain modules $C_\ell$ need not be projective and may have a complicated structure. We address the problem of replacing this segment by projective modules and $P$-graded matrices while preserving homology. The resulting projective implicit representation (PiRep) plays the role of the graded boundary-matrix representation in the classical persistence algorithm: it converts simplicial data into algebraic input on which persistent homology can be computed globally over $P$. In particular, a PiRep can be used as input to algorithms for computing minimal presentations of persistent homology. We give an efficient algorithm to compute a PiRep from a poset tower. It constructs degreewise minimal presentations and asymptotically minimal second terms of projective resolutions of the chain modules $C_\ell$, lifts the boundary maps $\partial_\ell$ to these resolutions, and assembles the resulting data into a PiRep using an additional correction term. The method is tailored to chain complexes induced by poset towers and computes the required algebraic data combinatorially, exploiting their special structure and avoiding general-purpose algebraic reduction. In the context of poset towers, it is fully general and can serve as a foundation for efficient algorithms on specific posets.

papers.title: Projective Variety Recovery from Unknown Linear Projections
papers.abstract: We study how a smooth irreducible variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$, $m\geq n+2$, can be recovered from the equations of its images under two generic projections from unknown centers. This extends earlier results on curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ to any dimension. Since $X$ is the normalization of each image, one image determines $X$ modulo the projective group when $X$ is linearly normal; what two images add is the configuration, that is the pair of projections. For complete intersections we prove unconditionally that the set of configurations compatible with the two images and their Hilbert polynomial is finite, of size at most $|\mathrm{Lin}(X)|$, the projective automorphism group of $X$. The argument is effective and the bound is attained. We then introduce an equation generalizing Kruppa's equation, relating the duals of the images to a fundamental matrix, encoding the pair of projections modulo the projective group. We give a necessary condition for its solution variety to be finite, a bound on its isolated points, and a sufficient condition under which the true fundamental matrix is rigid: no quadric may contain a generic line $L$ together with the locus of points of $X$ whose tangent space meets $L$. Rigidity is unconditional for curves; in higher dimension it holds under a first-order liftability hypothesis, which we certify for a del Pezzo quartic surface in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Global finiteness of that solution variety remains open, necessarily so, as it contains solutions realized by no variety; for $\dim X<\mathrm{codim}\,X-1$ the obstruction amounts to knowing the fundamental matrix itself. Once the projections are known, $X$ is recovered from the two cones over the images: in codimension two their intersection is $X$ plus a component of degree $d(d-1)$; in higher codimension $X$ is its unique component of maximal dimension.

papers.title: Homogenization theory of random walks in degenerate random environment
papers.abstract: Recent progress on the understanding of the Random Conductance Model is reviewed. A particular emphasis is on homogenization results such as functional central limit theorems, local limit theorems and heat kernel estimates for almost every realization of the environment, established for random walks among stationary ergodic conductances that are possibly unbounded but satisfy certain moment conditions.

papers.title: Local Linear Convergence of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Semidefinite Programming under Strict Complementarity
papers.abstract: We investigate the local linear convergence properties of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) when applied to Semidefinite Programming (SDP). A longstanding belief suggests that ADMM is only capable of solving SDPs to moderate accuracy, primarily due to its sublinear worst-case complexity and empirical observations of slow convergence. We challenge this notion by introducing a new sufficient condition for local linear convergence: as long as the converged primal-dual optimal solutions satisfy strict complementarity, ADMM attains local linear convergence, independent of nondegeneracy conditions. Our proof is based on a direct local linearization of the ADMM operator and a refined error bound for the projection onto the positive semidefinite cone, improving previous bounds and revealing the anisotropic nature of projection residuals. Extensive numerical experiments confirm the significance of our theoretical results, demonstrating that ADMM achieves local linear convergence and computes high-accuracy solutions in a variety of SDP instances, including those cases where nondegeneracy fails. Furthermore, we identify where ADMM struggles, linking these difficulties with near violations of strict complementarity-a phenomenon that parallels recent findings in linear programming.

papers.title: Optimal linear filtering of partially observed polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to filtering, smoothing, and prediction of polynomial processes that are partially observed. These problems are known to allow for an explicit solution in the simpler case of linear Gaussian state space models. The key insight underlying the present piece of research is that in linear filtering applications polynomial processes and their discrete-time counterpart are indistinguishable from Gaussian processes sharing their first two moments. We describe the construction of these Gaussian equivalents of polynomial processes and explicitly compute optimal linear filters, predictors and smoothers for polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time. The consideration of Gaussian equivalents also opens the door to parameter estimation and linear-quadratic optimal control in the context of polynomial processes.

papers.title: Time-optimal problem in the space of probability measures
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the value function in the time-optimal problem for a continuity equation in the space of probability measures. We derive the dynamic programming principle for this problem. Using this principle, we prove that the Kruzhkov transform of the value function is a unique discontinuous viscosity solution to the corresponding Dirichlet problem for the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the value function in a perturbed problem to the value function in the unperturbed problem.

papers.title: Unavoidable subgraphs in Ramsey graphs
papers.abstract: We study subgraphs that appear in large Ramsey graphs for a given graph $F$. The recent girth Ramsey theorem of the first two authors asserts that there are Ramsey graphs such that all small subgraphs lie in `forests of copies of $F$' amalgamated on vertices and edges. We derive a few further consequences from this structural result and investigate to what extent such forests of copies must be present in Ramsey graphs. As an application, we improve a recent result on generalised Sidon sets with Ramsey-type properties.

papers.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: I. Order-Disorder Interface convergence
papers.abstract: We study a $q$-state Potts model on the square grid when $q>4$ at the point $T_c(q)$ of its (discontinous) transition. This model exhibits exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures: $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). The current work deals with the Dobrushin order--disorder boundary conditions on a finite $N\times N$ box. Our main result is that this interface is a well-defined object, has $\sqrt{N}$ fluctuations, and converges to a Brownian bridge under diffusive scaling. The same holds also for the corresponding FK-percolation model for all $q>4$. Our proofs rely on a coupling between FK-percolation, the six-vertex model, and the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and on a detailed study of the latter. The coupling relates the interface in FK-percolation to a long subcritical cluster in the ATRC model. For this cluster we develop a ``renewal picture'' à la Ornstein-Zernike. This is based on fine mixing properties of the ATRC model that we establish using the link to the six-vertex model and its height function. Along the way, we derive various properties of the Ashkin-Teller model, such as Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics for its two-point function. In a companion work, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-order Dobrushin conditions. We show emergence of a free layer of width $\sqrt{N}$ between the two ordered phases (wetting) and establish convergence of its boundaries to two Brownian bridges conditioned not to intersect.

papers.title: Applications of reduced and coreduced modules III: Derived torsion and completion over polynomial extensions
papers.abstract: We study when degree-zero identities for reduced and coreduced modules extend to ambient derived torsion and completion. For a non-idempotent ideal $I$ in an explicit polynomial ring, we construct a module $M$ that is simultaneously $I$-reduced and $I$-coreduced and satisfies $Γ_I(M)=Λ_I(M)=0$ but $H_I^2(M)\ne0$. The module is a union of finite reduced and coreduced submodules whose positive derived torsion vanishes. The supporting ideal has unrestricted torsion dimension two, whereas the dimension on each bounded-nilpotence quotient category is one. The calculations use compatible cone resolutions for $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$, where $J^2=J$. These give paired Ext--Tor formulas for coefficients annihilated by a fixed power of $t$. For arbitrary coefficients, an explicit mapping-fiber model realizes the standard derived-composition comparison sequence and identifies the obstruction to extending the bounded formula. Coordinate calculations for countably idempotent-generated ideals supply the computational foundation, and a valuation-domain example gives nonzero first derived completion on a cyclic reduced and coreduced coefficient.

papers.title: Drift Parameter Estimation for an Ergodic Extension of the Double Heston Model
papers.abstract: The double Heston model is a widely used stochastic volatility model in financial mathematics, particularly for option pricing, risk management, and volatility surface calibration. This paper investigates the joint estimation of the drift parameters for an ergodic extension of the double Heston model. We first establish stochastic properties of the underlying process, including the existence of a stationary distribution and ergodicity. We then study maximum likelihood and conditional least squares estimators based on continuous-time observations. For both estimation procedures, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality under suitable ergodicity conditions.

papers.title: Well-posedness of kinetic McKean-Vlasov equations
papers.abstract: We consider the McKean-Vlasov equation $dX_t = b(t, X_t, [X_t])dt + σ(t, X_t, [X_t])dW_t$ where $[X_t]$ is the law of $X_t$. We specifically consider the kinetic case, where the equation is degenerate because the dimension of the Brownian motion $W$ is strictly smaller than that of the solution $X$, as commonly required in classical models of collisional kinetic theory. Assuming Hölder continuous coefficients and a weak Hörmander condition, we prove the well-posedness of the equation. This result advances the existing literature by filling a crucial gap: it addresses the previously unexplored case where the diffusion coefficient $σ$ depends on the law $[X_t]$. Notably, our proof employs a simplified and direct argument eliminating the need for PDEs involving derivatives with respect to the measure argument. A critical ingredient is the sub-Riemannian metric structure induced by the corresponding Fokker-Planck operator.

papers.title: Categorical Diffusion of Weighted Lattices
papers.abstract: Quantale-enriched categories unify ordered, metric, relational, and tropical structures that arise across networked systems. To study consensus and relaxation over such structures, we develop a theory of diffusion for cellular sheaves of quantale-enriched categories over graphs, governed by an order-theoretic Laplace operator that we call the Lawvere Laplacian. Over an arbitrary unital quantale, we define the weighted global sections of a cellular sheaf as the quantale-enriched category of natural transformations from a weight diagram into the sheaf, which over a commutative base is a weighted limit, and characterize them as the vertex data that agree up to edge tolerances across every edge. For an adjoint bisheaf, we prove that the weighted global sections coincide with the suffix points of the Lawvere Laplacian, which are the equilibria of its harmonic flow. Under a chain-continuity hypothesis, the harmonic flow converges to the greatest weighted global section below the initial cochain. Instances of the theory include shortest-path iteration over the Lawvere quantale, reconciliation of local cost estimates, quantale and clock synchronization, and coupled max-plus discrete event systems.

papers.title: The Rectifiable Rectangular Peg Problem
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of an inscribed rectangle with any prescribed aspect ratio for a large class of continuous Jordan curves that includes all rectifiable curves and Stromquist's locally monotone curves. Our proof is based on microlocal sheaf theory and is inspired by the recent work of Greene and Lobb.

papers.title: Boolean combinations of graphs
papers.abstract: Boolean combinations allow combining given combinatorial objects to obtain new, potentially more complicated, objects. In this paper, we initiate a systematic study of this idea applied to graphs. In order to understand expressive power and limitations of boolean combinations in this context, we investigate how they affect different combinatorial and structural properties of graphs, in particular $χ$-boundedness, as well as characterize the structure of boolean combinations of graphs from various classes.

papers.title: Interface Energy and Phase Transformations: A Comparative Analysis of Cahn-Hilliard and CALPHAD-based Models in Ternary Substitutional Alloys
papers.abstract: Diffusional phase transformations in alloys are modeled either by phase-field methods of Cahn-Hilliard type, in which a double-well free energy and a gradient term impose an interface energy, or by reactive diffusion models, in which the driving forces follow from the CALPHAD methodology, the convex hull of the molar free energy, and the interface carries no energy. Their numerical schemes are tied to their free energies: phase-field schemes break down when the interface energy is set to zero, and reactive diffusion codes rely on finite differences. We derive, from the thermodynamic extremal principle, a single finite element scheme that covers both limits: the stationarity of the Rayleighian functional (free energy rate plus one half of the dissipation, with mass conservation imposed by multipliers) with respect to the rates, fluxes and multipliers at a frozen state. Fluxes and chemical affinities are primary unknowns, so no derivative of the affinity is required. The time-discrete scheme is the corresponding incremental minimization; it conserves mass exactly and satisfies a discrete energy-dissipation inequality for every convex molar free energy, including the convex hull without regularization.
