We make explicit that this last case is a degenerate parabolic problem of Stefan type, whose degeneracy can be removed, without altering the free energy, only by a moving mesh; since our aim is the coupling to continuum mechanics and damage on a fixed mesh, we operate at the boundary of degeneracy and show that mass conservation, the energy balance and the second law remain intact there. Thermodynamic consistency is proved for multi-component systems, a scheme relating Onsager and diffusion coefficients is proposed, and the role of interface energy is studied in binary and ternary examples, the latter with vacancies as a non-conserved component.

papers.title: Existence result for a 2 x 2 system of conservation laws with discontinuous flux and applications
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for a one-dimensional 2x2 non-symmetric Keyfitz-Kranzer system of conservation laws with a flux f= f(x,U) that is discontinuous with respect to the spatial variable x. No monotonicity assumption is imposed on the mapping x \to f(x,U). We introduce a Kruzhkov-type entropy condition and establish global existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for initial data with arbitrarily large total variation. The proof relies on a wave-front tracking approximation. The main technical novelty consists in the introduction of adapted Riemann invariant coordinates, specifically designed to account for the discontinuities of the flux, which yield a uniform-in-time bound on the total variation of the approximate solutions U^n(t). As an application, we discuss the second-order ARZ model for vehicular traffic on inhomogeneous roads with abrupt collective changes in the speed law or road capacity.

papers.title: Flows on uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: For a uniformly locally finite metric space $(X, d)$, we investigate \emph{coarse} flows on its uniform Roe algebra $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, defined as one-parameter groups of automorphisms whose differentiable elements include all partial isometries arising from partial translations on $X$. We first show that any flow $σ$ on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ corresponds to a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ such that $σ_t(a) = e^{ith} a e^{-ith}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, allowing us to focus on operators $h$ that generate flows on $ \mathrm{C}^*_u (X)$. Assuming Yu's property A, we prove that a self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ induces a coarse flow on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ if and only if $h$ can be expressed as $h = a + d$, where $a \in \mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ and $d$ is a diagonal operator with entries forming a coarse function on $X$. We further study cocycle equivalence and cocycle perturbations of coarse flows, showing that, under property A, any coarse flow is a cocycle perturbation of a diagonal flow. Finally, for self-adjoint operators $h$ and $k$ that induce coarse flows on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, we characterize conditions under which the associated flows are either cocycle perturbations of each other or cocycle conjugate. In particular, if $h - k$ is bounded, then the flow induced by $h$ is a cocycle perturbation of the flow induced by $k$.

papers.title: Geometric Leaves of Symplectic Groupoids
papers.abstract: A symplectic groupoid of triangular bilinear forms consists of pairs of matrices $(B,A)$ with $A\in \mathcal A$ - the set of real unipotent upper-triangular matrices - and $B\in {\rm SL}_n({\mathbb R})$ such that $\widetilde{A}=BAB^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal A$. The symplectic groupoid possesses a nondegenerate symplectic structure which induces a reflection-equation Poisson algebra on $\mathcal A$. Fock and Chekhov defined a Poisson map from the Teichmüller space ${\mathcal T}_{g,s}$ of genus $g$ surfaces with $s$ (one or two) holes to the space of unipotent upper-triangular $n\times n$ matrices; the image of this map forms a geometric locus. A matrix $A$ in the geometric locus satisfies the rank condition: $\operatorname{rank}\bigl(A+A^{\mathsf T}\bigr)\le 4$ and an additional positivity condition. We describe the coisotropic reduction of the Poisson cluster variety of $\mathcal A$ by the rank condition for $n=5$ and $6$ and show that these coisotropic reductions yield the corresponding geometric loci. Moreover, we analyze in both cases the cluster structures obtained by coisotropic reductions and recover the celebrated cluster structure of ${\mathcal T}_{2,1}$ for $n=5$ and ${\mathcal T}_{2,2}$ for $n=6$. We also discuss the positivity of the geometric cluster variables for $n=3,4,5,6$.

papers.title: Hankel Determinants for Weighted Lattice Paths with Two Horizontal Steps
papers.abstract: We evaluate all Hankel determinants of the formal power series \(G=a/(1+b_1x+b_2x^2+cx^kG)\), where \(k\ge4\). The defining equation arises from a weighted lattice-path model with horizontal steps of lengths one and two. For \(k=4\), the determinants are expressed through Fibonacci polynomials. For \(k\ge5\), explicit formulas describe each residue class of the determinant size modulo \(k\). The proofs combine quadratic transformations with a second-order recurrence for an auxiliary family. As an application, we recover known Hankel evaluations for the square of the weighted Motzkin generating function.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Invariants of Non-Convex Complete Intersections in Weighted Projective Stacks
papers.abstract: In this paper we compute genus-zero orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau threefold complete intersections in weighted projective stacks, regardless of convexity conditions. The traditional quantum Lefschetz principle may fail even for invariants with ambient insertions. Using quasimap wall-crossing, we are able to compute invariants with insertions from a specific subring of the Chen-Ruan cohomology, which contains all the ambient cohomology classes. Quasimap wall-crossing gives a mirror theorem expressing the I-function in terms of the J-function via a mirror map. The key of this paper is to find a suitable GIT presentation of the target space, such that the mirror map becomes invertible. An explicit formula for the I-function is given for all those target spaces and many examples with explicit computations of invariants are provided.

papers.title: A hybrid FEM-PINN method for time-dependent partial differential equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a hybrid numerical method for solving evolution partial differential equations (PDEs) by merging the time finite element method with deep neural networks. In contrast to the conventional deep learning-based formulation where the neural network is defined on a spatiotemporal domain, our methodology utilizes finite element basis functions in the time direction where the space-dependent coefficients are defined as the output of a neural network. We then apply the Galerkin or collocation projection in the time direction to obtain a system of PDEs for the space-dependent coefficients which is approximated in the framework of PINN. The advantages of such a hybrid formulation are twofold: statistical errors are avoided for the integral in the time direction, and the neural network's output can be regarded as a set of reduced spatial basis functions. To further alleviate the difficulties from high dimensionality and low regularity, we have developed an adaptive sampling strategy that refines the training set. More specifically, we use an explicit density model to approximate the distribution induced by the PDE residual and then augment the training set with new time-dependent random samples given by the learned density model. The effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method have been demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments.

papers.title: On the Stieltjes Approximation Error to the Logarithmic Integral
papers.abstract: We study the approximation errors $\varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{li}_{*}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)$ and $\varepsilon_{S}(x)=\operatorname{li}_{S}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)$ arising from the classical Stieltjes--van Boven and pure Stieltjes asymptotic expansions of the logarithmic integral, respectively. Our analysis establishes a top-down reduction based on the discrete error sequence $\varepsilon_n=\varepsilon(e^n)$ and its localized partial variations, for which we derive new, unconditional analytic bounds. By developing precise integral representations for these error increments and establishing sharp, fully explicit upper and lower estima-tes for the underlying kernel integrals, we obtain uniform bounds valid for every integer $n\geq 1$. These discrete results are subsequently lifted to the real domain to provide comprehensive estimates for all real $x\geq e$. In particular, we prove that $\varepsilon(x) = \frac{1}{3} \sqrt{2π/\log x} + O(1/\log x)$ as $x \to \infty$. Furthermore, we deploy these continuous bounds to uncover the fine structural behavior of the pure Stieltjes expansion, demonstrating that $|\varepsilon_{S}(x)| = \sqrt{2π}\,|1/3-α|/\sqrt{\log x} + O(1/\log x)$ as $x\to\infty$, where $n=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ and $α=\log x-n$. This establishes a novel and explicit asymptotic description of the absolute pure Stieltjes error, fully capturing its non-trivial oscillatory dependence on the fractional part of the logarithm.

papers.title: Nonlinear Eigen-approach ADMM for Sparse Optimization on Stiefel Manifold
papers.abstract: With growing interest in machine learning and data science, creating efficient algorithms to optimize various dimension reduction objectives has become particularly important. This paper is concerned with optimization problems on the Stiefel manifold whose objective functions take the form as the sum of a smooth function and a nonsmooth one. A common practice is to split such a problem into a smooth optimization subproblem on the Stiefel manifold and a nonsmooth one and solve them by some version of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Usually the smooth subproblem is solved by standard optimization techniques skillfully adapting to the manifold. However, often the smooth subproblem has strong linear algebra characteristics which, if carefully exploited, can lead to much more efficient solvers than the standard optimization techniques that ignore the characteristics. In this paper, it is proposed to tackle the smooth subproblem through a nonlinear eigen-approach which can fully utilize rich linear algebra structures that dominantly present in objective functions from today's data science applications. We conduct convergence analysis and analyze computational complexity for obtaining an $ε$-stationary point. Numerical experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed algorithm compared to the state-of-the-art approaches.

papers.title: Electromagnetic scattering by Minkowski-type bianisotropic media
papers.abstract: We consider the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves by a bounded stationary inclusion whose effective constitutive law is of Minkowski type. The constant vector $V$ is regarded as a constitutive moving parameter. Such a law arises as an effective description of synthetic moving media and of suitable traveling-wave space--time modulations. Starting from the implicit Minkowski relations, we derive a Maxwell transmission system and its Lippmann--Schwinger volume-integral formulation. The dimensionless parameter $β=|V|/c_Ω$ governs the pointwise constitutive inversion, namely the matrix is invertible precisely for $β\neq1$, while on the subcritical branch $0\leqβ<1$ its inverse admits an explicit convergent expansion. Using the algebraic structure of the cross-product operator, we obtain a spectral characterization of solvability and a quantitative sufficient condition separating the static material contrast from the $V$-dependent contribution which allows to justify the convergence of the corresponding Born series. As an application, we prove that full-aperture electric far-field data at a fixed frequency uniquely determine the support of the inclusion within this perturbative regime without assuming that $V$ is known.

papers.title: General elementary methods meeting elementary properties of correlations
papers.abstract: This is a kind of survey on properties of correlations of two very general arithmetic functions, from the point of view of {\it Ramanujan expansions}. In fact, our previous papers on these links had, as a focus, the "{\it Ramanujan coefficients}" of these correlations and the resulting "{\it R.e.e.f.}", i.e., {\it Ramanujan exact explicit formula}. This holds under a variety of sufficient conditions, mainly under two conditions of convergence involving correlation's {\it \lq \lq Eratosthenes Transform\rq \rq}, namely what we call {\it Delange Hypothesis} (DH) and {\it Wintner Assumption} (WA) (the former implying the latter). We proved, on Hardy-Ramanujan Journal, the {\it Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture} on {\it $2k-$twin primes}, in particular, from (DH) (implying convergence of the Ramanujan expansion, whence {\it R.e.e.f.}); then, we gave a more general proof, from (WA), again {\it entailing the R.e.e.f.}, but from another method of summation for {\it Ramanujan expansions}, that we detailed in arXiv, "On Ramanujan smooth expansions for a general arithmetic function". There we also started to introduce local Ramanujan coefficients. Which we deepen here, entailing a new conditional proof of quoted H-L Conjecture.

papers.title: Crystal Structure of Upper Cluster Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct upper seminormal crystals on the $μ$-supported tropical points of skew-symmetric cluster algebras from their exchange matrices. A generic potential provides an additive categorification in which boundary representations determine the Cartan matrices and generic ranks describe the crystal operators. Under frozen-Jacobi-finiteness and reachability, the raising operators lift to locally nilpotent derivations of the upper cluster algebra. For $τ$-exact boundary pairs, these derivations give integrable actions of derived Kac--Moody algebras in characteristic zero. In particular, the associated Cartan matrices are positive semidefinite. When the generic characters form a basis, this basis is BK-biperfect and the $τ$-exact crystals are normal. We also construct algebraic Tits actions and describe compatibly pointed biperfect bases through a coefficient graph. The theory is illustrated by classical and new examples.

papers.title: Efficient Alternating Minimization with Applications to Weighted Low Rank Approximation
papers.abstract: Weighted low rank approximation is a fundamental problem in numerical linear algebra, and it has many applications in machine learning. Given a matrix $M \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, a non-negative weight matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{n \times n}$, a parameter $k$, the goal is to output two matrices $X,Y\in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ such that $\| W \circ (M - X Y^\top) \|_F$ is minimized, where $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard product. It naturally generalizes the well-studied low rank matrix completion problem. Such a problem is known to be NP-hard and even hard to approximate assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis [GG11, RSW16]. Meanwhile, alternating minimization is a good heuristic solution for weighted low rank approximation. In particular, [LLR16] shows that, under mild assumptions, alternating minimization does provide provable guarantees. In this work, we develop an efficient and robust framework for alternating minimization that allows the alternating updates to be computed approximately. For weighted low rank approximation, this improves the cost of each iteration of [LLR16] from $\|W\|_0k^2$ to $\|W\|_0 k$ where $\|W\|_0$ denotes the number of nonzero entries of the weight matrix. At the heart of our framework is a high-accuracy multiple response regression solver together with a robust analysis of alternating minimization. We also replace the random initialization of [LLR16], whose claimed guarantee fails, by subspace iteration from a Gaussian start, so our total running time of $\widetilde O((\|W\|_0 k+nk^3)\log(1/ε))$ includes the initialization. In exchange, our guarantee needs the weight matrix to be within spectral distance $γn$ of the all-ones matrix for a $γ$ that is polynomially small in $n$.

papers.title: Stability of singular limit cycles for Abel equations revisited
papers.abstract: A criterion is obtained for the semi-stability of the isolated singular positive closed solutions, i.e., singular positive limit cycles, of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$, where $A,B$ are smooth functions with two zeros in the interval $[0,T]$ and where these singular positive limit cycles satisfy certain conditions, which allows an upper bound on the number of limit cycles of the Abel equation to be obtained. The criterion is illustrated by obtaining an upper bound of two positive limit cycles for the family $A(t)=t(t-t_A)$, $B(t)=(t-t_B)(t-1)$, $t\in[0,1]$. In the linear trigonometric case, i.e., when $A(t)=a_0+a_1\sin t +a_2\cos t$, $B(t)=b_0+b_1\sin t+b_2\cos t$, an upper bound of two limit cycles is also obtained for $a_0,b_0$ sufficiently small and in the region where two positive limit cycles bifurcate from the origin.

papers.title: Low Rank Matrix Completion via Robust Alternating Minimization in Nearly Linear Time
papers.abstract: Given a matrix $M\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the low rank matrix completion problem asks us to find a rank-$k$ approximation of $M$ as $UV^\top$ for $U\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times k}$ and $V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ by only observing a few entries specified by a set of entries $Ω\subseteq [m]\times [n]$. In particular, we examine an approach that is widely used in practice -- the alternating minimization framework. Jain, Netrapalli, and Sanghavi [JNS13] showed that if $M$ has incoherent rows and columns, then alternating minimization provably recovers the matrix $M$ by observing a nearly linear in $n$ number of entries. While the sample complexity has been subsequently improved [GLZ17], alternating minimization steps are required to be computed exactly. This hinders the development of more efficient algorithms and fails to depict the practical implementation of alternating minimization, where the updates are usually performed approximately in favor of efficiency. In this paper, we take a major step towards a more efficient and error-robust alternating minimization framework. To this end, we develop an analytical framework for alternating minimization that can tolerate a moderate amount of errors caused by approximate updates. Moreover, our algorithm runs in time $\widetilde O(|Ω| k)$, which is nearly linear in the time to verify the solution while preserving the sample complexity. This improves upon all prior known alternating minimization approaches which require $\widetilde O(|Ω| k^2)$ time.

papers.title: Rational limit cycles of Abel differential equations
papers.abstract: We study the number of rational limit cycles of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$, where $A(t)$ and $B(t)$ are real trigonometric polynomials. We show that this number is at most the degree of $A(t)$ plus one.

papers.title: Homology with the theme of Matlis
papers.abstract: Matlis proved a lot of homological properties of the fraction field of an integral domain. In this paper, we simplify and extend some of them from 1-dimensional (resp. rank one) cases to the higher dimensional (resp. finite rank) cases. For example, we study the weakly cotorsion property of $\Ext(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadratic $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$

papers.title: Variation of Hodge structures for non-Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss unpolarized, complex variation of Hodge structures for non-Kähler manifolds. In particular, consider a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds with central fiber $X$. Suppose that the inclusion of complexes $(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\hookrightarrow (A^\bullet(X),d)$ induces injective maps \[ H^j(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\longrightarrow H^j(A^\bullet(X),d),\qquad j=k,\ k+1. \] Under this condition, we show that the period map is holomorphic and transversal. An essential ingredient for the proof is a deformation theory of filtered $(p,q)$-forms. We prove a jumping formula for filtered de Rham cohomology and obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for its dimension to be invariant under deformation of complex structures.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function
papers.abstract: We use an elementary arithmetic argument, going back to Blom and Fr{ö}berg, to obtain upper and lower bounds for the denumerant function of Sylvester for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$. The bounds hold along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$, share the leading term of the denumerant, and yield its asymptotic behaviour with an explicit error term; for large $n$ and under a mild condition, a polynomial refinement of the lower bound improves on the lower bound of Agnarsson.

papers.title: Testing the number of common factors by bootstrapped sample covariance matrix in high-dimensional factor models and errata
papers.abstract: This paper studies the impact of bootstrap procedure on the eigenvalue distributions of the sample covariance matrix under a high-dimensional factor structure. We provide asymptotic distributions for the top eigenvalues of bootstrapped sample covariance matrix under mild conditions. After bootstrap, the spiked eigenvalues which are driven by common factors will converge weakly to Gaussian limits after proper scaling and centralization. However, the largest non-spiked eigenvalue is mainly determined by the order statistics of the bootstrap resampling weights, and follows extreme value distribution. Based on the disparate behavior of the spiked and non-spiked eigenvalues, we propose innovative methods to test the number of common factors. Indicated by extensive numerical and empirical studies, the proposed methods perform reliably and convincingly under the existence of both weak factors and cross-sectionally correlated errors. Our technical details contribute to random matrix theory on spiked covariance model with convexly decaying density and unbounded support, or with general elliptical distributions.

papers.title: On the Hausdorff measure of sets of non-Lyapunov behaviour, and a Jarnik-type theorem for random Schroedinger operators
papers.abstract: We consider the growth of the norms of transfer matrices of ergodic discrete Schrödinger operators in one dimension. It is known that the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is slower than prescribed by the Lyapunov exponent is residual in the part of the spectrum at which the Lyapunov exponent is positive. On the other hand, this exceptional set is of vanishing Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $ρ(t)$ such that $ρ(t)/t$ is integrable at zero. Here we show that this condition on $ρ(t)$ can not in general be improved: for operators with independent, identically distributed potentials of sufficiently regular distribution, the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is arbitrarily slow has infinite Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $ρ(t)$ such that $ρ(t)/t$ is non-increasing and not integrable at zero. The main technical ingredient, possibly of independent interest, is a Jarník-type theorem describing the Hausdorff measure of the set of real numbers well approximated by the eigenvalues of the Schrödinger operator. The proof of this result relies on the theory of Anderson localisation and on the mass transference principle of Beresnevich--Velani.

papers.title: The Multipartite Ramsey numbers $m_j(C_3, C_m, n_1K_2,n_2K_2,\ldots, n_iK_2)$
papers.abstract: Assume that $K_{j\times n}$ be a complete, multipartite graph consisting of $j$ partite sets and $n$ vertices in each partite set. For given graphs $G_1, G_2,\ldots, G_n$, the multipartite Ramsey number (M-R-number) $m_j(G_1, G_2, \ldots,G_n)$ is the smallest integer $t$ such that for any $n$-edge-coloring $(G^1,G^2,\ldots, G^n)$ of the edges of $K_{j\times t}$, $G^i$ contains a monochromatic copy of $G_i$ for at least on $i$. C. J. Jayawardene, E. T. Baskoro et al. $(2016)$ gave the size of M-R-numbe $m_j(nK_2, C_7)$ for $j \geq 2 $ and $n\leq 6$. Y. Rowshan et al. $(2021)$ gave the size of M-R-number $m_j(nK_2, C_7)$ for $j = 2,3, 4$ and $n\geq 2$. Y. Rowshan $(2021)$ gave the size of M-R-number $m_j(nK_2,C_7)$, for each $j\geq 5$ and $n\geq 2$. In this article we compute the size of M-R-number $m_j(C_3,C_3, nK_2)$ for each $j\geq 7$, $n\geq 1$, $m_j(C_3,C_3, n_1K_2,n_2K_,\ldots,n_iK_2)$ for each $2\leq j\leq 6$, $i\geq 2, n_i\geq 1$, and M-R-number $m_j(C_3,C_4, nK_2)$, for each $n\geq 1$, and small $j$.

papers.title: Eigenvalue estimates of the drifted Cheng-Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish universal eigenvalue inequalities for a drifted Cheng--Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Our approach combines a universal quadratic eigenvalue inequality for operators in divergence form with a Rauch-type comparison theorem and a Bochner-type formula. We evaluate the geometric terms in this quadratic inequality under suitable assumptions on the radial behavior of the coefficient tensor and the drifting function, together with curvature pinching conditions. In the general setting, we establish a Rauch-type comparison theorem for the Cheng--Yau operator and derive two auxiliary estimates from its Bochner-type formula. We then prove integral estimates of independent interest and apply them to obtain the desired eigenvalue inequalities for both the Cheng--Yau operator and the drifted Laplacian, recovering known inequalities for the Laplacian. We also establish a rigidity result for the Cheng--Yau operator on a class of bounded annular domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds. In Euclidean space, this result can be applied, for instance, with the potential function of the Gaussian shrinking soliton. The hyperbolic space is treated separately in two settings, one exploiting the conformal relation between its metric and the Euclidean metric, and the other via its warped product structure, reducing the problem to one dimension. We extend the hyperbolic construction of the fundamental gap for the Laplacian to a class of operators in divergence form. Examples are provided to illustrate the scope and applicability of our results.

papers.title: Combining Determinism and Indeterminism
papers.abstract: Our goal is to construct mathematical operations that combine indeterminism measured from quantum randomness with computational determinism so that non-mechanistic behavior is preserved in the computation. Formally, some results about operations applied to computably enumerable (c.e.) and bi-immune sets are proven here, where the objective is for the operations to preserve bi-immunity. While developing rearrangement operations on the natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$, we discovered that the bi-immune rearrangements generate an uncountable subgroup of the infinite symmetric group (Sym$(\mathbb{N})$) on the natural numbers. This new uncountable subgroup is called the bi-immune symmetric group. The bi-immune symmetric group contains the finitary symmetric group on the natural numbers, and consequently is highly transitive. Furthermore, the bi-immune symmetric group is dense in Sym$(\mathbb{N})$ with respect to the pointwise convergence topology. Moreover, the bi-immune symmetric group contains permutations that are a single infinite cycle on all of $(\mathbb{N})$, even though every one of its generators has only finite orbits. Using an invariant called the {\it crossing number}, we also prove that the bi-immune symmetric group is a meager subset and a proper subgroup of Sym$(\mathbb{N})$.

papers.title: Some homological properties of category $\mathcal{O}$, V
papers.abstract: We compute projective dimension of translated simple modules in the regular block of the BGG category $\mathcal{O}$ in terms of Kazhdan-Lusztig combinatorics. This allows us to determine which projectives can appear at the last step of a minimal projective resolution for a translated simple module, confirming a conjecture by Johan Kåhrström. We also derive some inequalities, in terms of Lusztig's $\mathbf{a}$-function, for possible degrees in which the top (or socle) of a translated simple module can live. Finally, we relate Kostant's problem with decomposability and isomorphism of translated simple modules, addressing yet another conjecture by Johan Kåhrström.

papers.title: A Generalization of the Passivity Theorem and the Small Gain Theorem Based on $ρ$-Stability, with Application to a Parameter Adaptation Algorithm for Recursive Identification
papers.abstract: The usual passivity theorem considers a closed-loop, the direct chain of which consists of a strictly passive stable operator $H_{1}$, and the feedback chain of which consists of a passive operator $H_{2}$. Then the closed-loop is stable. Let $ρ>1$. We show here that the closed-loop is still stable when the direct chain consists of a strictly $ρ^{-1}$-passive $% ρ^{-1}$-stable operator (a weaker condition than above) and the feedback chain consists of a $ρ$-passive operator (a stronger condition than above). Variations on the theme of the small gain theorem (incremental or not) can be made similarly. This approach explains the results obtained in a paper on identification which was recently published.

papers.title: On the fractional Dehn twist coefficients of branched coverings
papers.abstract: We discuss how the fractional Dehn twist coefficient behaves under a fully ramified branched covering of an open book, and give applications to both topological and contact 3-manifolds. Among them, we show that non-right-veering closed braids represent virtually loose transverse links.

papers.title: Iterative Refinement of A Modified Lavrentiev Regularization Method for De-convolution of the Discrete Helmholtz Type Differential Filter
papers.abstract: We analyze an iterated, modified Lavrentiev regularization method (Mitlar) for deconvolving the Helmholtz-type differential filter $G=(I-δ^2Δ)^{-1}$ used in large eddy simulation. The method replaces the Lavrentiev operator $G+αI$ by the convex combination $(1-α)G+αI$; each step costs one Helmholtz solve, exactly as in iterated Lavrentiev regularization. We show that this one-line change has a precise structural meaning: the regularized operator is again a Helmholtz filter, now with the smaller radius $\sqrtα\,δ$, and $J$ refinement steps coincide with van Cittert approximate deconvolution of order $J$ applied to that filter. Consequently the regularization error is governed by the product $αδ^2$ rather than by $α$ alone. We prove sharp error bounds of order $(αδ^2)^{s}$ on a Hilbert scale, $0\le s\le J+1$, with saturation exactly at $s=J+1$; show that for noise-free data the Mitlar error never exceeds the iterated Lavrentiev error, for every datum, every $α$ and every $J$; give a priori parameter choices for noisy data with explicit $δ$-dependence; and prove finite element error bounds whose constants grow only linearly in $J$. Finally we show that the iterates decrease a natural energy functional for every $α>0$, and derive a computable stopping rule that guarantees monotone decrease of a weighted error and always terminates. Numerical examples illustrate the theory and compare Mitlar with a family of Tikhonov--Lavrentiev methods.

papers.title: Reductive group actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study rationality properties of reductive group actions over fields k of characteristic zero. In doing so, we unify Luna's theory of spherical systems with the Borel-Tits theory of reductive groups. Specifically, for any reductive group action, we define a generalized Tits index; its main constituents are a root system and a generalization of the anisotropic kernel. For k-spherical varieties (i.e., those for which a minimal parabolic subgroup has an open orbit), we obtain explicit smooth completions of the set of rational points. Over local fields, this yields genuine compactifications that generalize the maximal Satake compactification of symmetric spaces. Our main tool is a k-version of the Local Structure Theorem.

papers.title: On the (LC) conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the (LC) conjecture of Hochster and Huneke in some non-trivial cases. This has several applications. Recently, Brenner and Caminata answered a numerical evidence due to Dao and Smirnov on the shape of generalized Hilbert-Kunz functions of smooth curves. As applications, we first reprove this by a short argument. Then we give a proof of second numerical evidence predicted by Dao and Smirnov on the shape of generalized Hilbert-Kunz functions of nodal curves. Thirdly, we answer a question posted by Vraciu on the (LC) property of a proposed ring. Inspiring with the (LC) property, we present a connection to the stability theory. This leads us to investigate the stability and the strong semistability of the sheaf of relations on $\{x^2,y^2,z^2\}$ over the Klein's quartic curve. This answers questions of Brenner. After presenting a connection from (LC) to the $F$-threshold, we answer a question posted by Huneke et al. Additional applications and examples are given.

papers.title: Floer field theory for tangles
papers.abstract: We use quilted Floer theory to construct functor-valued invariants of tangles arising from moduli spaces of flat bundles on punctured surfaces. As an application, we show the non-triviality of certain elements in the symplectic mapping class groups of moduli spaces of flat bundles on punctured spheres.

papers.title: Transfer operator for the Gauss' continued fraction map. I. Structure of the eigenvalues and trace formulas
papers.abstract: Let L be the transfer operator associated with the Gauss' continued fraction map, known also as the Gauss-Kuzmin-Wirsing operator, acting on the Banach space. In this work we prove a two-term asymptotic formula for the eigenvalues of L, show their algebraic simplicity, sign alternation pattern, and decrease in absolute value. This settles, in a sharper asymptotic form, the conjectures of K. Babenko and S. Yur'ev (1978), D. Mayer and G. Roepstorff (1988), A.J. MacLeod (1992), Ph. Flajolet and B. Vallée (1995). Further, we find an exact series for the eigenvalues, which also gives the canonical decomposition of trace formulas due to D. Mayer (1976) and K.I. Babenko (1978). This crystallizes the contribution of each individual eigenvalue in the trace formulas.

papers.title: The q-WZ Method for Infinite Series
papers.abstract: Motivated by the telescoping proofs of two identities of Andrews and Warnaar, we find that infinite q-shifted factorials can be incorporated into the implementation of the q-Zeilberger algorithm in the approach of Chen, Hou and Mu to prove nonterminating basic hypergeometric series identities. This observation enables us to extend the q-WZ method to identities on infinite series. As examples, we will give the q-WZ pairs for some classical identities such as the q-Gauss sum, the $_6φ_5$ sum, Ramanujan's $_1ψ_1$ sum and Bailey's $_6ψ_6$ sum.

papers.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
papers.abstract: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

papers.title: Equilateral simplices over general fields
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Schoenberg (1937) characterizes the dimensions $d$ for which $\mathbb{Q}^d$ contains the vertex set of a regular simplex with $d+1$ vertices. We generalize Schoenberg's result to all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$, using elementary Witt theory and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Our generalization also sharpens Schoenberg's theorem and complements more recent work of Lorenz and Zimmermann (2026) by characterizing the admissible edge lengths. In the case of finite characteristic, equilateral simplices with $d+2$ vertices can sometimes exist (F.~Radó 1986), and we characterize this situation as well, again for all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$. We also briefly consider the edge lengths of equilateral simplices of $d$ vertices.

papers.title: Regularization Independence in the One-Dimensional Schrödinger Equation with Delta Potential
papers.abstract: We consider a class of regularizations $\{δ_\varepsilon\}$ of the Dirac delta defined by a uniform $L^1$ bound, the normalization $\intδ_\varepsilon\to1$, and a truncated first-moment condition, with no restriction on sign, shape, support, or scaling. For this class we prove that the transmission and reflection coefficients for the Hamiltonian operator $H_\varepsilon=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-λδ_\varepsilon$ at fixed energy converge to those of the delta interaction. Under the additional assumption that each $δ_\varepsilon$ is bounded, we show that any family of negative eigenvalues of $H_\varepsilon$ bounded away from zero converges to $-λ^2/4$ when $λ>0$, and that no such family exists when $λ<0$. Both convergences are obtained with an explicit rate, expressed through two integrals of $δ_\varepsilon$, directly computable for a given regularization. The bound-state convergence follows from the work of Brasche, Figari, and Teta; here, our contribution is an elementary proof with an explicit rate. Their norm resolvent convergence, however, does not by itself imply convergence of the scattering matrix, which was previously known for families obtained by scaling a single fixed profile; we prove it for a strictly larger class.

papers.title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
papers.abstract: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values. The combinatorics of the polynomials are noncrossing partitions of type $B_d$. This give us a piecewise Euclidean cell structure built using the order complex of the noncrossing partition of type $B_d$. Along the way, we also give a compactification of this space of polynomials.

papers.title: Two-Stage Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: Lenstra showed that mixed-integer linear programming can be solved in polynomial time when the number of integer variables is fixed and the number of continuous variables is arbitrary. Mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) can be solved in polynomial time when the total number of variables is fixed. However, since MIQP is NP-hard already without integer variables, the analog of Lenstra's result fails unless P = NP. Hence, polynomial-time algorithms for MIQP with an arbitrary number of continuous variables must exploit additional structure. We study MIQPs with two-stage structure, which underlies Benders decomposition and two-stage stochastic programming. A few linking variables, including all integer variables, are coupled with many blocks of continuous variables that interact only through them, both in the constraints and in the objective. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for MIQP with an arbitrary quadratic objective when the number of linking variables and the block size are fixed, while the number of blocks, and hence the number of variables, is arbitrary. The case with no blocks is MIQP in fixed dimension. None of our assumptions can be dropped. Unless P = NP, the number of linking variables and the block size must both be fixed, the blocks cannot interact or contain integer variables, and large blocks cannot be allowed even if their objective is linear. Unless FPT = W[1], the exponent of the running time must depend on both the number of linking variables and the block size.

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

papers.title: Automating the Derivation of Advanced Algorithms in Numerical Linear Algebra using Associative Algebras with Involution
papers.abstract: Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the $*$-square root and $(i,j)$ indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these $*$-algebras. The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real $*$-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path $*$-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices. Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable $*$-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined. Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on $2\times2$ real matrices.

papers.title: A family of alternating projection examples whose Cesàro means fail to converge strongly
papers.abstract: In 1965, Bregman proved that the sequence of iterates of the method of alternating projections applied to two closed convex sets with nonempty intersection in a Hilbert space converges weakly to a point in the intersection. The question whether this convergence may actually fail to be strong was settled in a seminal paper by Hundal in 2004. He provided a counterexample featuring a halfspace and a closed convex cone generated by a certain curve. While largely elementary, the details of Hundal's construction and analysis are quite involved. We revisit this seminal example and present a family of such examples that allows for simpler proofs. Our generating curve combines unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a height determined by a scalar function. The orbits converge weakly --- but not strongly --- to the origin, while their norms have a positive limit for which we give explicit lower bounds. We also prove that the associated Cesàro means behave likewise; in fact, this is generalized to alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point. Finally, these orbits allow interpretations in the context of projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.

papers.title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition. A giant component is formed when $p<p_c=1-(2k-1)^{-2}$. The fraction of vertices in the giant component scales as $\exp[-C/\sqrt{p_c-p}]$, a signature of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition. In the non-percolating phase, the cluster size distribution has an algebraic tail with a continuously varying exponent, while at $p=p_c$, it acquires a logarithmic correction. We analyze triadic hypergraphs ($k=3$) in detail and then generalize to higher $k$. We show that the Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component scale linearly with system size. Higher Betti numbers fluctuate between realizations but remain finite, and hence the normalized Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component are asymptotically equal, up to a sign.

papers.title: Permutation codes via spectral graph theory
papers.abstract: We use the Eigenvalue Method to obtain upper spectral bounds on the size of permutation codes in the Hamming, Ulam, Cayley and Kendall metrics. For the Kendall metric, we improve the double-ball upper bound of Buzaglo and Etzion [IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 2015] at minimum distance four and lengths seven and eight. For the Cayley metric, we improve the sphere packing bound, and determine when these spectral improvements occur. We derive theoretical spectral criteria for improvements from the ratio-type bounds of low degree, and show that the quadratic ratio-type bound for the Kendall metric always equals sphere packing. Furthermore, we prove sharp spectral bounds and recover known optimal code sizes for the Hamming and Ulam metrics.

papers.title: Tripod Reordering: A 33-Queue Layout of Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: A queue layout of a graph consists of a linear order of the vertices and a partition of the edges into queues so that no two edges in a single queue are nested. The minimum number of queues needed in a queue layout of a graph is called its queue number. A planar product structure theorem of Dujmović, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt, and Wood (JACM, 2020) states that every planar graph is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph of simple treewidth at most $3$, a clique $K_3$, and a path. The result has been used to show that the queue number of planar graphs is at most $49$. Recently, Bekos, Gronemann, and Raftopoulou (Algorithmica, 2023) investigated how the general approach based on the product structure can be optimized for planar graphs. They claim that an appropriate reordering of the three vertices associated with each bag in the product structure decomposition, called a tripod, reduces the queue number of planar graphs to $42$. We first highlight a gap in their queue layout algorithm: one of the choices required by the algorithm is not guaranteed to exist. Then we show how to address the limitation and provide an alternative tripod reordering mechanism that reduces the upper bound on the queue number of planar graphs to $33$. As a corollary, bipartite planar graphs have queue number at most $22$.

papers.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
papers.abstract: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. Moreover, for a complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of any knot of the family coincides (up to a factor) with the generating series of the semigroup. Let $(X,0)$ be a splice quotient singularity with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link $Σ$ and let $(C,0)$ be a reduced curve-germ embedded in $(X,0)$ defined as the zero locus of the product of end curve functions. We prove, thorugh our topological characterization of complete intersection semigroups, the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cut out by $C$ in $Σ$ and the Poincaré series of the embedded curve. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Furthermore, for any good resolution of $(X,0)$ compatible with the splice quotient analytic structure, we provide an explicit description of the semigroup of integer multiplicities of functions along any divisor of the resolution.

papers.title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
papers.abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Improved last-iterate bounds for SGD with and without replacement
papers.abstract: In this work, we study last-iterate convergence bounds for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on convex and $β$-smooth loss functions and improve the bound from $\cO((\log T)^3/T)$ to $\cO((\log T)^3/(T\log\log T))$ in the interpolation regime. The improvement comes from applying a horizon-dependent multiscale estimate of gradients to the comparison of trajectories. The bound applies to both sampling with replacement and sampling without replacement within one pass.

papers.title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories
papers.abstract: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness. We discuss some of the far-reaching consequences.

papers.title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
papers.abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.

papers.title: Real monopole Floer homology and the Alexander polynomial
papers.abstract: We prove that the Euler characteristic of the framed real monopole Floer homology of the double branched cover of a link is given by the Alexander polynomial evaluated at $\sqrt{-1}$. For knots $K$ with determinant one, this formula shows that Miyazawa's degree invariant of $K$ can be computed in terms of the Alexander polynomial of $K$. The proof involves a new connected-sum formula and oriented skein exact triangles for some new variants of real monopole Floer homology, called the diagonal and cone real monopole Floer homology, which admit mod-two gradings. This is the monopole counterpart of Srivastava's Euler characteristic formula in real Heegaard Floer homology.

papers.title: Encoding rational $Δ$-triples on elliptic curves
papers.abstract: A $Δ$-triple for a natural number $n$ is a triple $(x,y,z)$ of divisors of $n$ with $1<x<y\leq z<\sqrt n$ and $n/x-x=(n/y-y)+(n/z-z)$. The numbers that admit such a triple are those with the $Δ$ property, which governs the existence of certain $n$-simple triangles in factor graphs of split graphs. We allow the three components to be rational numbers, and show that, once the quotient $z/y=a/b$ is fixed, the rational $Δ$-triples for $n$ are exactly the rational points of the elliptic curve $Y^2=n\,ab\,w(w+ab)\bigl(w+(a+b)^2\bigr)$ lying over the interval $-b(a+b)<w<-ab$. Since a rational $Δ$-triple for $n$ amounts to $Δ$-triples for infinitely many of the numbers $κ^2n$, the chord--tangent construction becomes a way of producing new $Δ$-triples from old ones. For perfect squares, the curve always carries a rational point coming from a degenerate triple. This point has order $4$ if $a=b$, and infinite order if $a>b$. As a consequence, for every quotient $a/b>1$ there are infinitely many pairwise non-proportional $Δ$-triples of perfect squares with $z/y=a/b$, in contrast with the fact that perfect squares have no $Δ$-triple with $y=z$. For arbitrary $n$, there are infinitely many rational $Δ$-triples for $n$ with a given quotient if and only if the corresponding curve has positive rank.

papers.title: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
papers.abstract: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$Ω$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust BEST-RQ For Speech Representation Learning
papers.abstract: BEST-RQ, based on random projection and quantization, has been a well-established self-supervised learning approach to learn speech representations from large-scale unlabeled audio due to its high performance and efficiency. However, in BEST-RQ representations learned by random quantization can be sensitive to the choice of quantization targets. To address this issue, we propose a distributionally robust extension of BEST-RQ that seeks representations robust across multiple quantization configurations. Specifically, we define groups by codebooks and formulate the training as a group Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) problem. Rather than optimizing solely for the average loss across groups, our approach adaptively reweights groups to emphasize those performing poorly. Additionally, we regularize DRO with a Kullback-Leibler divergence to prevent excessive distribution deviation. We evaluate our approach on the Multilingual LibriSpeech dataset and show that the distributionally robust BEST-RQ achieves superior performance over the conventional uniform average across multiple codebooks.

papers.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $Δ$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $Δ=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

papers.title: On Koebe theorem for Sobolev mappings on Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider mappings between domains of two Riemannian surfaces. The main subject of the investigation are families of homeomorphisms with moduli inequalities. For such families, we obtain the uniform openness (uniform lightness). As a consequence, we obtain similar results for homeomorphisms of Sobolev classes with finite distortion whenever its maximal dilatations have a majorant integrable on almost all concentric circles. In particular, we obtain the Koebe-type theorem for both direct and inverse Sobolev mappings.

papers.title: Compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability
papers.abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space $L^1$.

papers.title: The higher order regularity problem for elliptic systems with data in Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the well-posedness of the higher order regularity problem in the upper half-space with data in Sobolev Banach function spaces by proving its equivalence to natural weighted estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. The generality of our framework allows for applications to Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement-invariant spaces such as Orlicz spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, as well as their weighted counterparts, among others. This is established for the family of second-order, homogeneous, elliptic, constant complex coefficient systems in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ that admit a distinguished coefficient tensor, a natural condition that always holds in the scalar case and for the Lamé system of elasticity.

papers.title: Making Poisson σ again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $σ$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $Σ$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = Σ\times G \to Σ$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,ω)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,Π)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = Σ\times M \to Σ$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $Σ$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,Π)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $ω$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

papers.title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
papers.abstract: We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $ν$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}\right)^ν$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}\right)^ν$ are isomorphic if and only if $ν$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$. We settle the hook components conjecture of Bergeron (2024) for coinvariant rings, and a conjecture of Bergeron (2020) that the multiplicity of the sign character of $R_n^{(1,2)}$ is $3^{n-1}$. Our results also recover several existing results in the literature. Lastly, we extend our results to the hyperoctahedral group ${\mathfrak{B}_n}$ and prove that the determinant-isotypic components of $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(0,1)}$ and $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell+1)}$ are isomorphic.

papers.title: Sliding 2-handles over 3-handles and the barbell diffeomorphism
papers.abstract: We give three fundamental examples highlighting the relationship between loops of spheres in $\#^k S^2\times S^2$, pseudo-isotopies, and diffeomorphisms of the 4-sphere. First, we describe an explicit pseudo-isotopy and Hatcher-Wagoner family that realizes the barbell diffeomorphism $β$ of the 4-sphere by constructing a finger-Whitney system for the family. From the Hatcher-Wagoner family, we are able to conclude that the example in §7 of ``Pseudo-isotopies of simply connected 4-manifolds'' generates $β$. Next, it is known that the square of $β$ is isotopic to id. We reprove this by building an explicit 2-parameter family of Morse functions that trivializes the Hatcher-Wagoner family for $β^2$. We do this by utilizing exchange points and families of handle slides. In the final example, we show that another Hatcher-Wagoner family, affectionately called the double cross, also generates $β$.

papers.title: A Characterization of Completely Integrally Closed Prüfer $v$-Multiplication Domains
papers.abstract: We generalize a result known for Prüfer domains to show that a PVMD $R$ is completely integrally closed if and only if $\text{Inv}^t(R)$ is an archimedean $\ell$-group. It has been conjectured that a PVMD is completely integrally closed if and only if it is an Archimedean domain. It is known that a completely integrally closed PVMD is an Archimedean domain. We provide an example to illustrate that an Archimedean PVMD need not be completely integrally closed.

papers.title: Orthogonal Splines Associated to Root Systems and Applications to Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}(X)$ be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline $B_X$ with $d$-dimensional direction set $X$ and associated differential operator $D_X$. Assuming that each direction in $X$ appears with even multiplicity i.e $X = [X_0|X_0]$, we may endow $\mathcal{S}(X)$ with a special inner product $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$ which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order $|X_0|$. Then, for the special case when the directions in $X$ are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for $\mathcal{S}(X)$. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under $D_X$ (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation. Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for $\mathcal{S}(X)$, the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into $\mathcal{S}(X)$ is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$, this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When $X$ comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if $f$ is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate $f$ from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.

papers.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
papers.abstract:
The multivariate breeder's equation $Δ ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\inftyλ_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $λ_n$, such that $λ_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_kλ_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

papers.title: Modular $n$-queens in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: A chess queen in $d$-dimensions can move any distance in the direction of any edge or diagonal of the $d$-dimensional hypercube. (That is, a queen can move from a position $x$ to $x+cv$ for any $c$ and any nonzero $v\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$.) We prove that one can place $n^{d-1}$ non-attacking queens on the $d$-dimensional modular board $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ if and only if all prime factors of $n$ exceed $2^d$. The $d=3$ case of this result is a conjecture of van Rees from 1981. Our proof involves both human ideas and substantial AI assistance.

papers.title: Damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
papers.abstract: This work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. This model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. Consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(\M,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \M$. Under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. A logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. We provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.

papers.title: schubmult: Symbolic algorithms and input-sensitive bounds for Schubert multiplication
papers.abstract: We present schubmult, a GPL-licensed Python system for exact multiplication of ordinary, double, quantum, and quantum double Schubert polynomials, as well as independent-alphabet triple and quantum triple products. Its central algorithm expands one factor into filtered column paths and couples them to Pieri computations on the other factor. Dynamic programming shares intermediate states, and the algorithm returns every Schubert-basis coefficient as an exact arithmetic circuit. We prove input-sensitive operation bounds for the entire product, not just a selected coefficient: for inputs of minimal rank $n$, the classical algorithms have complexity $2^{O(n\log n)}$ and polynomial complexity in $n$ for fixed Lehmer-code lengths. The quantum algorithms have the same general bound and polynomial complexity when, in addition, the number of nonzero entries in the Lehmer code of $v^{-1}$ is fixed. We describe the implementation and distinguish it from the algorithms analyzed, verify computations against independent routines and exact identities, and report reproducible timings for flag and Grassmannian workloads. Parabolic quantum products are treated separately via the Peterson-Woodward comparison.

papers.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
papers.abstract: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT. Prompted by this ready conversion of (P)STS to 3-CNF formulas and numerous real-world applications of (P)STS, we explore the intersection of (P)STS with 3-SAT and its counting version \#3-SAT. We explain the properties of (P)STS-generated 3-CNF formulas in terms familiar to the SAT community and experimentally compare them against randomly-generated 3-CNF formulas. We find that PSTS-3-CNF formulas are statistically distinct from randomly generated 3-CNF formulas, in both probability of satisfiability and expected solution count.

papers.title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
papers.abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(β_c(n)=β_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(γ_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/β_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

papers.title: Connected regular $Γ$-distance magic graphs with magic constant zero
papers.abstract: Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group. A $Γ$-distance magic labeling of a graph is a bijection from its vertex set to $Γ$ such that the sum of the labels of the neighbours of each vertex is a fixed element of $Γ$, called the magic constant. The constructions of Kovář and collaborators provide regular distance magic graphs of odd order with consecutive integer labels for every even degree from $4$ to $14$. We adapt these constructions to prove the existence of connected $r$-regular $(A\times\mathbb{Z}_n)$-distance magic graphs with magic constant $0$, where $A$ is any finite Abelian group of odd order, $n$ is odd, and $r\in\{4,6,8,10,12,14\}$, under explicit sufficient conditions on $n$. Here $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. It suffices to take $n\ge13$ for $r=6$, $n\ge19$ for $r=14$, and $n\ge15$ for $r\in\{4,8,10,12\}$.

papers.title: On open weakly 2-semiconvex sets with nonempty 2-nonsemiconvexity-point sets in three-dimensional Euclidean space
papers.abstract: We study general topological properties of open weakly $2$-semiconvex sets in real three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.
