papers.abstract: Inspired by the rigidity of exact Lagrangian submanifolds, a conjecture by P.~Biran and O.~Cornea asks if a simple exact Lagrangian cobordism $W$ in a tame exact symplectic manifold is always ``symplectically trivial'' (i.e. the Lagrangian suspension of an Hamiltonian isotopy). In this short note, we prove a topological version of this conjecture~: if the cobordism has dimension at least $6$, it is always topologically trivial. This extends a previous work of Lara Suarez who reduced the question to proving an injectivity result among fundamental groups.

papers.title: A linear edge bound for k-quasi-planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the $k$-quasi-planar graph conjecture for topological drawings. For every integer $k\ge 2$, a simple graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices admitting a drawing with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $1056(k-1)^2(n-2)$ edges. Thus the number of edges is linear in $n$, with an explicit quadratic dependence on $k$. The result allows multiple crossings between the same pair of edges, including edges with a common endpoint. The proof uses the double of a sphere with boundary to represent graph edges by closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface. The endpoints of geodesic lifts induce partial orders of width at most $k-1$. A stability bound for greedy chain partitions, together with a counting argument over a triangulation, gives the stated edge bound.

papers.title: Global straightening of solution manifolds for state-dependent delay equations
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be an arbitrary open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuously differentiable. Suppose that each derivative $Df(φ)$, $φ\in U$, admits a continuous linear extension $D_ef(φ):C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)\to\mathbb R^n$, such that $D_ef(φ)χ$ depends jointly continuously on $φ\in U$ and $χ\in C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$. We construct a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $U$ onto an open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$ which maps the solution manifold of $x'(t)=f(x_t)$ onto an open subset of the closed subspace defined by $φ'(0)=0$. This resolves an open problem posed by Walther concerning regularization of the entire solution manifold. The diffeomorphism preserves the value at zero and agrees with the original history on $[-h,-τ]$ for any prescribed $τ\in(0,h)$, and is uniformly arbitrarily close to the identity in the supremum norm. It is connected to the identity by a jointly $C^1$ family of diffeomorphisms. The same conclusions hold under the weaker assumption that the finite signed measures representing the derivatives of $f$ have no atom at zero. We also establish a corresponding theorem for separable real Hilbert-valued histories.

papers.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schrödinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-ηp_n})$, where $η>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.

papers.title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
papers.abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the average it produces, which is what entitles one to speak of 'the' universal average at all. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.

papers.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
papers.abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.

papers.title: A spectral Moore problem and the Yang-Koolen conjecture
papers.abstract: We study the maximum order $v(k,θ)$ of a connected $k$-regular graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $θ$. For every real $θ\geq1$, we prove that \[ T(θ) =\limsup_{k\to\infty}\bigl(v(k,θ)-2k\bigr) =2\left\lfloor1+\frac{θ^2}{4}\right\rfloor. \] In particular, $T(θ)>2θ$ for every real $θ\geq4$, disproving the Yang-Koolen conjecture. We also determine $v(k,θ)$ for all sufficiently large $k$ on explicit intervals of $θ$. We prove a jump in the second largest eigenvalue above $1$. For each fixed $1\leqθ<2$ and all sufficiently large $k$, every connected $k$-regular graph of order at least $2k+2$ whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $θ$ is the crown graph. For $θ=\sqrt2$, we prove that $v(k,\sqrt2)=2k+2$ for every $k\geq13$. Finally, we give a new upper bound on $v(k,θ)$.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Transient Centers in Continuous-Time Systems
papers.abstract: Analysis of mathematical models in ecology and epidemiology often emphasizes asymptotic dynamics, such as stable equilibria, periodic orbits, and attractors. However, many biologically relevant trajectories exhibit long transient dynamics in which a relevant observable evolves slowly for an extended period before a comparatively rapid transition occurs. On finite time scales relevant to data collection, management, and intervention, such transient behavior can be more informative than the eventual asymptotic outcome. In this work, we study long-lasting and slowly varying transient dynamics in continuous-time systems through the framework of nonequilibrium transient centers. These centers are points in the state space near which the observable can remain nearly constant for a long time, even when the full state is not near an equilibrium. We develop finite-time escape criteria for identifying such centers and their reachable counterparts. These criteria provide practical conditions under which nearby trajectories can remain in a slow regime for a long period of time before eventually leaving it. We apply the theory to an epidemic model with delay of stability loss. In this model, trajectories may remain close to the disease-free manifold for a long time before the infectious population resurges. The framework developed here describes this behavior as slow evolution near a nonequilibrium transient center followed by finite-time escape from the slow regime.

papers.title: Variance Reduction for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Multiple Local Updates
papers.abstract: Multiple local updates are widely used in decentralized optimization to enhance communication efficiency, often in conjunction with stochastic gradients when exact gradient computation is costly. However, such algorithms generally converge only to a neighborhood of the optimum, whose size depends on the stepsize and the variance of gradient noise. Variance reduction has been incorporated into ADMM-based methods to achieve exact convergence in expectation, but their stepsizes typically scale inversely with both the square root of the network size and the cube of the number of local updates, leading to slow convergence as the network size or the number of local updates increases. In this paper, we propose a novel primal-dual-based decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates variance reduction with multiple local updates, with a stepsize independent of the network size and inversely proportional to the number of local updates (rather than its cube), thereby enabling significantly larger stepsizes and faster convergence. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, we establish the first linear convergence guarantee in expectation for decentralized optimization with multiple local updates under stochastic gradients in the strongly convex setting. Beyond the theoretical guarantee, the proposed method exchanges only one variable per round, halving the communication cost compared with gradient-tracking-based methods. Numerical experiments further demonstrate its advantages in convergence speed and accuracy.

papers.title: Effective threshold dynamics for the cubic nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in three dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider the focussing cubic Klein-Gordon equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$ in the radial setting. Foundational work by Nakanishi-Schlag gives a complete qualitative characterisation of the dynamics near the ground state $Q$, in particular revealing a threshold phenomenon, whereby a co-dimension one Lipschitz manifold separates finite time blow up from scattering solutions in forward time. Our aim in this paper is to derive an effective bound for the scattering norm $\|u\|_{L_t^3([0,\infty);L_x^6(\mathbb{R}^3))}$, for scattering energy class solutions $u$ with data sufficiently near $Q$ and close to the threshold manifold. This requires the development of an induction on energy strategy in a setting where an alternative to the usual Morawetz approach appears necessary.

papers.title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
papers.abstract: We prove joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function for shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$ with arbitrary nonzero real parameters $d_j$ whose absolute values are pairwise distinct, and show that these conditions are optimal. As a consequence, we establish generalized strong recurrence for every finite family of nonzero real parameters, meaning that the corresponding shifts of the Riemann zeta-function simultaneously approximate each other. The only cases for which generalized strong recurrence remains unproved are those involving both zero and nonzero shift parameters, for which it is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. Our proof combines Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem with a generalization of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators and prove a zero-product result.

papers.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
papers.abstract: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.

papers.title: Planarity estimates and classification of ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
papers.abstract: We study space-time proper ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$ that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. We prove codimension reduction and convexity: every such solution is either a static affine $n$-plane, or a flow of hypersurfaces of a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace whose time slices bound convex bodies. By results of Bourni, Langford and Lynch and of Bamler and Lai, the flow is then noncollapsed, and it is a family of shrinking spheres or cylinders, an ancient oval, a bowl soliton or a flying wing, possibly times a Euclidean factor. Space-time properness replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu. The main tool is a parabolically scale-invariant interior planarity estimate for $n\geq5$, obtained from Naff's gradient estimates through a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, where these estimates do not give the gradient terms a sign, we bound them from below as in a previous work. The same localization, applied to the gradient estimate of Lynch and Nguyen and to a second order analogue, gives the derivative bounds from which convexity follows. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

papers.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ with standard generating set $S$, we prove that the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ is contractible for all sufficiently large $t$. We also investigate other finitely generated groups of the form $G=H\rtimes F$ for $F$ finite, and prove that for any finite symmetric generating set $A$ for $H$ such that $A^F=A$, the complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;AF)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$.

papers.title: Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities
papers.abstract: For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplusΛ^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.

papers.title: Extending the V-sequence reduction to arbitrary independent distributions
papers.abstract: A decision maker observes independent random variables sequentially and must stop at an overall maximum, with ties counted as wins. In this short note, we extend the $V$-sequence reduction of Allaart and Islas (2016) to arbitrary independent distributions, including atoms, which were not covered by the original reduction. We spread atoms over ordered intervals without increasing the optimal win probability, then apply the continuous reduction. The resulting comparison uses a common threshold and a common splitting probability at that threshold. It also recovers the sharp universal lower bound previously established by Hill and Kennedy (1992).

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: We prove an expansion in $1/g$ of the Weil--Petersson volumes $V_{g,n}$ that is uniform over all cusp counts, from fixed $n$ to arbitrarily large $n/g$. An explicit leading term and single-factorial remainder bounds give exponentially small relative errors after truncation at a suitable order proportional to $g$. A positive recursion along the string flow connects these volumes to pure $ψ$-class intersection numbers, where Painlevé~I fixes the normalization; uniform coefficient extraction then recovers individual volumes. We determine Zograf's constant $C=1/\sqrtπ$ and resolve Mirzakhani's two questions on volume ratios for growing cusp counts and adjacent coefficient ratios uniformly over all degrees. Via Mirzakhani's integration formula, the same volume estimates control random surfaces at two distinct scales. At $n/\sqrt g\to c\in(0,\infty)$, the entire positive Laplace spectrum below $1/4$ converges to an explicit Poisson point process generated by geodesics cutting off two cusps. Together with Huang's theorem, this characterizes the transition for $n\ge1$: the spectral gap tends in probability to $1/4$ exactly when $n/\sqrt g\to0$, and to $0$ exactly when $n/\sqrt g\to\infty$. At density $n/g\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, we identify the local limit around a typical point; its cusp-filling is conformally a disc. As $λ\to\infty$, these limits approach the infinite Weil--Petersson sphere of Budd and Curien. We prove their parabolicity conjecture and, by a growing-radius coupling, answer their scaling-limit question: after deep cusps are trimmed, the rescaled infinite sphere converges to the Brownian plane.

papers.title: Towards Exact Multidimensional Fluxes: A Structure-Preserving Data-Informed Framework for Riemann Solvers
papers.abstract: Finite volume and discontinuous Galerkin methods evolve the discrete solution using space-time flux integrals over mesh faces, which typically depend on solutions to local Riemann problems. In the multidimensional Riemann problem setting, this integral is difficult to evaluate exactly because of complex wave interactions. In this work, we show that the exact space-time flux integral is a polynomial in the time step and face dimensions. This motivates a learning-based approach, as only the mapping from the initial states to the polynomial coefficients needs to be learned. We propose a structure-preserving, data-informed Riemann solver framework that uses a neural network trained on high-resolution simulation data to learn this mapping. Key structural properties, including consistency and mirror symmetry, are enforced by construction. Provided that the high-resolution simulations converge to the exact flux integrals and the network accurately predicts the coefficients, this framework yields near-exact flux integrals for use in numerical simulations. We demonstrate the framework using classical implosion and explosion problems for the two-dimensional Euler equations. In an unsplit MUSCL-Hancock scheme, the learned Riemann solver remains stable at a CFL number of 0.9, whereas the same scheme using the exact one-dimensional Riemann solver fails. Compared with the latter scheme at CFL=0.45, the learned scheme is slightly more accurate and requires approximately 30% less computational time.

papers.title: Pointwise Riesz potential bounds for rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: We give a complete characterization of the kernels $Ω\in \textup{L}^1(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ for which the rough singular integral $\textup{T}_Ω$ and its associated maximal operator $\textup{M}_Ω$ satisfy pointwise bounds in terms of $\textup{I}_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$ and $\textup{M}_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$, respectively, where $\textup{I}_1$ is the Riesz potential and $\textup{M}_1$ is the fractional maximal operator. We show that these bounds hold if and only if $Ω$ belongs to the homogeneous dual Sobolev space $\dot \textup{W}^{-1,\infty}(\mathbb S^{d-1})$. This characterization yields both a PDE characterization and a geometric characterization of the pointwise bounds. In the Lebesgue scale, we show that, for $d\geq 3$, every rough operator associated to a mean-zero kernel $Ω\in\textup{L}^{d-1,\infty}(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ satisfies these pointwise bounds, and that the exponent $d-1$ is sharp. In dimension $d=2$, we use complex-analytic methods to establish a new pointwise bound in terms of the complex derivatives $\bar\partial f$ and $\partial f$, which are valid for every mean-zero $Ω\in\textup{L}^1(\mathbb S^1)$. As a consequence, we obtain new Sobolev bounds for rough singular integrals in the plane.

papers.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
papers.abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

papers.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.

papers.title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
papers.abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.

papers.title: Free energy and fluctuations of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models and generalized Hopfield models
papers.abstract: We consider the free energy of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models in the high temperature regime, with one spin normalized and the other either normalized or i.i.d. We derive a unified formula for the limiting free energy in both settings. We also prove that the fluctuations of the free energy converge to a Gaussian distribution under mild assumptions. The proof is based on a bipartite multigraph expansion, which also gives free energy results for generalized Hopfield models and log likelihood ratio of spiked rectangular models.

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.

papers.title: On the Structure of Kähler-Ricci Shrinkers
papers.abstract: We prove that every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact. We also prove that every singular Kähler--Ricci shrinker on a Fano cone is a Ricci-flat Kähler cone.

papers.title: Boundedness of radial solutions to the parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the plane with subcritical mass
papers.abstract: We establish uniform-in-time boundedness of radially symmetric global solutions to the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the whole space with mass below $8π$. While global existence is known throughout this subcritical mass range, uniform-in-time boundedness has remained open. On bounded domains, the free energy method of Nagai, Senba and Yoshida (1997) yields both global existence and boundedness under the optimal mass condition. On the whole space, however, the corresponding estimates are not uniform in time due to the behavior of solutions at spatial infinity. Indeed, the free energy of self-similar solutions diverges to $-\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, preventing a direct application of this approach to establish boundedness. The key ingredients are new interior estimates controlling the localized free energy in terms of its dissipation, together with uniform-in-time exterior estimates exploiting radial symmetry.

papers.title: Non-expansive maps between unit balls that send the sphere onto the sphere are linear isometries
papers.abstract: Let $X$, $Y$ be real Banach spaces with closed unit balls $B_X$, $B_Y$ and unit spheres $S_X$, $S_Y$. We prove that every non-expansive map $F\colon B_X\to B_Y$ with $F(S_X)\subseteq S_Y\subseteq F(B_X)$ is the restriction of a surjective linear isometry $X\to Y$. Consequently, a non-expansive bijection of $B_X$ onto itself that fails to be an isometry must map some point of $S_X$ into the open unit ball, so the plasticity of $B_X$ reduces to showing that non-expansive bijections preserve norm 1. The proof shows that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at $0$ with a surjective linear isometry $T$ as its derivative, and then proves $T^{-1}F=\mathrm{id}$ using a quantitative rigidity lemma for non-expansive self-maps $H$ of $B_X$ satisfying $\|a+H(a)\|=2$ for $a\in S_X$; the latter relies on the Baillon-Bruck rate of asymptotic regularity for Krasnosel'skii-Mann iterations. As a corollary, the identity is extremal in the set of non-expansive self-maps of $B_X$ for every Banach space $X$, which together with a result of Bargetz, Dymond and Pirk shows that all surjective isometries of $B_X$ are extremal, answering a question of theirs, including the case of $L^1[0,1]$.

papers.title: Dynamic Regret and Tightened Constraint Violation for Communication-Efficient Distributed Online Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the distributed online bilevel optimization problem with time-varying inequality constraints. In this setting, a multi-agent network is confronted with a hierarchical decision-making task characterized by coupling between the inner and outer optimization levels. We first propose a communication-efficient single-loop distributed online primal--dual algorithm based on communication compression, which tracks both the inner-level solution and the Hessian-inverse-vector product using only one update per-round. We show that this algorithm achieves a dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{θ_1,1-θ_1\}}+T^{θ_1 } P_T+H_{1,T}+E_{1,T})$, where~$θ_1 \in (0,1)$, $P_T$ is the outer-level path variation, $H_{1,T}$ is the inner-level path variation, and $E_{1,T}$ is the gradient path variation alongside a network cumulative constraint violation bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-θ_1/2})$, which is further reduced to $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-θ_1})$ under Slater's condition. Furthermore, to eliminate the dependence of regret on the inner-level and gradient path variation, we propose a novel adaptive multi-loop distributed online algorithm to control the inner-level approximation accuracy at each round. By dynamically adjusting the number of inner-level updates based on a gradient-norm tolerance condition, this algorithm yields an improved dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{θ_1,1-θ_1\}}+T^{θ_1 } P_T)$ which depends solely on the outer-level path variation while maintaining the same network cumulative constraint violation bound. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Lefschetz Properties of complete intersesctions and maximal variation of hyperplane sections
papers.abstract: For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.

papers.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
papers.abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.

papers.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.

papers.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
papers.abstract: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.

papers.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
papers.abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties. We also study the probability that a family of $N$ i.i.d.\ Gaussian points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in convex position and show that a sharp threshold occurs around the value $N=\exp(d/2e)$.

papers.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
papers.abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $ν>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+ν+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.

papers.title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with Hölder Continuous Terms
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of Hölder continuous functions and satisfies the $σ$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $σ= 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (ε^{-1}) ε^{2 (\underlineα - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $ε$-approximate solution, where $\underlineα \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{ö}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.

papers.title: Khovanov and knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
papers.abstract: For fibered positive links, we compute the reduced and unreduced Khovanov homology in homological grading two over both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_2$, and the knot Floer homology in the penultimate Alexander grading. Our Khovanov calculations, combined with the result of Przytycki-Sazdanović, prove that every nontrivial semi-adequate knot has 2-torsion in its unreduced Khovanov homology. This establishes Shumakovitch's conjecture for semi-adequate knots, which include all nontrivial positive knots. The proofs involve induction using the skein exact sequences, with the Hopf link as the base case.

papers.title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
papers.abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $τ\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-2 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $τ\ge0$, including the deterministic case $τ=0$. At each fixed $τ>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/τ}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $τ\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.

papers.title: Optimum solution to a boundary-value problem for an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$ via measure of noncompactness
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncom-pactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.

papers.title: The generator problem for C*-algebras with comparison
papers.abstract: We show that certain classes of unital, simple, separable C*-algebras with comparison are singly generated, including tracially AF algebras and monotracial crossed products of actions on the Cantor space. In particular, we show that simple, separable, tracially AF algebras have generator rank one.

papers.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
papers.abstract: Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum asserts that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, that is, for almost all graphs $G$, every graph with the same spectrum as $G$ whose complement has the same spectrum as the complement of $G$ is isomorphic to $G$. We prove this conjecture by showing that the random graph $G(n,1/2)$ is determined by its generalized spectrum with probability tending to one. The proof combines a local theory of the denominators of the rational orthogonal matrices that relate generalized cospectral graphs, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, Seidel switching, inverse Littlewood--Offord theory over finite fields, rank estimates for random symmetric matrices modulo primes, and a study of the rational factors of the characteristic polynomial of a random symmetric $\pm1$ matrix with zero diagonal.

papers.title: Riemann functions for almost primes and their counting errors
papers.abstract: The real-axis jump of the prime-zeta function gives an integral form of Gram's series for Riemann's $R$-function. Applying the same operation to the almost-prime Dirichlet series defines functions $R_k$, with $R_1=R$. We prove absolute convergence, recover the classical fixed-order Selberg-Delange expansion, and identify the complementary Perron contribution to the exact count. A convergent incomplete-gamma endpoint expansion, together with the remaining lower cut, gives an exact representation of $R_k$, with explicit formulas for ranks one through four and a coefficient recurrence for every fixed rank. We then study the errors $R_k-N_k$. Under the Riemann hypothesis, their normalized mean-square zero spectra retain multiplicities; with simple zeros, the leading oscillations agree for every fixed $k$. An additional weighted logarithmic-gap moment gives a second-order spectrum and a positive constant in the $(\log\log X)^{-2}$ mean-square cancellation rate for consecutive values of $k$. The global spectral passages are justified by a uniform finite contour and a Gaussian-Laplace block estimate.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: The Origin of Symmetry and Its Breaking
papers.abstract: Hessian spectra at trained models in deep learning exhibit a persistent pattern: eigenvalues organize into distinct clusters, including a large bulk near zero and a few isolated outliers. This paper shows that a natural account of these spectral phenomena emerges when the original setting is understood as a departure from a nearby, otherwise hidden, highly symmetric reference. Modifications, including changes to the architecture, data distribution, or parameter metric, expose a nearby reference configuration whose Hessian exhibits rich invariances-ones not accounted for by weight symmetries. There, symmetry enables a precise description of the spectra, forcing high-dimensional kernels and eigenvalues of large multiplicity. Returning to the original configuration breaks the Hessian symmetry and thereby produces the observed hierarchy of clusters and outliers. The framework is developed in some generality, with a detailed analysis of three-layer ReLU networks and applications to convolutional, graph, and transformer models, as well as to the NTK. The same mechanism is further shown to yield analogous spectral structures in layerwise Hessians and the Gauss-Newton matrix.

papers.title: Analytic multiplier ideals of toric plurisubharmonic functions on a toric complex space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study analytic multiplier ideal sheaves of toric plurisubharmonic functions on normal affine toric complex analytic spaces equipped with torus-invariant rational divisors, assuming that a positive integer multiple of the log canonical divisor is Cartier. We describe these sheaves in terms of Newton convex bodies and show that they are globally generated by finitely many meromorphic monomials. Our results generalize the description of An and the formulas of Howald and Blickle for monomial ideals, and recover the descriptions of Rashkovskii and Guenancia on affine space. We also extend this description to weights obtained by subtracting positive rational multiples of monomial ideal weights.

papers.title: Banded Totally Positive Matrices and Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations: Existence, Stability, and Toeplitz Orthogonality
papers.abstract: A positive bidiagonal factorization of a banded totally positive matrix expresses it as a product of unit lower and upper bidiagonal factors with positive off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal matrix. In finite dimension such factorizations always exist, with parameter domains defined by polynomial inequalities. In the semi-infinite case, existence is equivalent to convergence of explicit positive series. Every bounded banded totally positive matrix is an operator-norm limit of matrices admitting these factorizations, through perturbations confined to a fixed initial block. Necessary and sufficient criteria characterize analytic dependence of prescribed factors on perturbations. With fixed initial entries, a relative entrywise criterion allows unbounded factors with different growth rates. For uniformly positive bounded factors with variable initial entries, the criterion involves every pair of factors on each triangular side and the signed triangular inverses. The dimensions of the local factorization families are determined. Normalized LDU factors depend analytically at every interior point of the factorization class. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, a stable positive bidiagonal factorization exists if and only if the symbol polynomial has distinct roots. Root formulas give two polynomial vector families with mixed-type multiple orthogonality for a rectangular matrix of positive measures. One factorization simultaneously attains the smallest possible first off-diagonal entries of both normalization matrices. The weighted linear forms are independent of the factorization. Their Chebyshev expansions yield asymptotic zero spacing inside the support and convergence of normalized kernels to the sine kernel after rescaling by the local zero density.

papers.title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
papers.abstract: We introduce new techniques to study mixed-characteristic special loci in moduli spaces and give several applications, focusing in particular on the moduli space $\mathsf{M}_g$ of curves. These applications include Zariski density results for split Jacobians, non-density results for supersingular loci, and lifting results for algebraic cycles, all under appropriate numerical conditions. Our methods generalize to more-or-less arbitrary moduli spaces mapping to Hodge-type Shimura varieties (and even some settings beyond the Shimura case), and relate to questions raised by Oort and de Jong.

papers.title: An exact compress-with-another threshold in a binary automaton family
papers.abstract: For a state $q$ in a synchronizing automaton, let $μ(q)$ be the minimum length of a word merging $q$ with another initial state. Szykuła asked whether $μ(q)=O(n)$ for strongly connected synchronizing automata and described a binary family attributed to Dżyga, with $n=3p$ states and a conjectured threshold $4n/3$. We specify the boundary transitions omitted from the published piecewise definition and prove that the resulting automata $\mathcal A_p$ satisfy $μ(q_0)=4p=4n/3$ for all $p\geq3$. A shortest word merging $q_0$ with another state is $(ba)^p(ab)^p$. We also construct a reset word of length $3p^2+4p-1$. Consequently, any uniform linear upper bound for $μ(q)$ on binary strongly connected synchronizing automata with corank-one letters has leading constant at least $4/3$.

papers.title: A New insight into the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak approach to Sobolev maps
papers.abstract: Given $p \in (1,\infty)$, let $\operatorname{X}=(\operatorname{X},ρ,μ)$ be a metric measure space such that $(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{d})$ is complete, the measure $μ$ is uniformly locally doubling and $\operatorname{X}$ supports a weak local $(1,p)$-Poincaré inequality. Let $(\operatorname{Y},\operatorname{d},\underline{y})$ be a complete pointed metric space. We prove that the equivalence class (modulo coincidence $μ$-a.e.) of a Borel map $u:\operatorname{X} \to \operatorname{Y}$ with a separable range belongs to the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak--Sobolev class $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{Y})$ if and only if $h \circ u$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X})$ for every $1$-Lipschitz function $h:\operatorname{Y} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $h(\underline{y})=0$.

papers.title: The Benson--Etingof--Ostrik conjecture for finite tensor categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic admits a symmetric tensor functor to a higher Verlinde category. This was conjectured for arbitrary symmetric tensor categories of moderate growth by Benson, Etingof and Ostrik. The proof uses higher Frobenius functors, introduced by the authors in [CF1]. The main effort is directed towards a proof of a conjecture from [CF1] about thick tensor ideals in the representation category of elementary abelian $p$-groups, which implies that the higher Frobenius functors are symmetric monoidal. In fact, we prove a refinement of the latter conjecture that relates tensoring with restricted Steinberg modules to an iterated generalised cohomology of modules of elementary abelian $p$-groups.

papers.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Pellarin's Identity, Carlitz Period, and Anderson Generating Functions over Arbitrary Curves
papers.abstract: We establish three results for a rank-one Drinfeld module over the coefficient ring of a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $ \mathbb F_q$, with a closed point at infinity of arbitrary degree. First, a Tate-algebra unit exists in the module of special functions precisely when this module is free of rank one, that is, when the period lattice is isomorphic to the module of regular differentials; this proves the Gazda--Maurischat conjecture. Second, under the unit-anchor normalization for an isogeny to a principal-period target, a strictly normalized shtuka product and one characteristic residue give the fundamental period; the same defect equation gives the logarithm residue formula. Third, finite étale torsion traces over the field of definition identify the first Frobenius twist of the normalized shtuka differential and express Pellarin's $ \mathcal L(1)$-series at a fundamental period. The source period lattice need not be free.

papers.title: Semi-stable models, local heights and quadratic Chabauty for $X_0(N)^*$
papers.abstract: Quadratic Chabauty computations for $X_0(N)^*$ are complicated by local height contributions at primes of bad reduction. For squarefree $N$, we explain a strategy for constructing a global $p$-adic height for which all the contributions at the primes of bad reduction vanish. As our first main result, we show that such a $p$-adic height exists for all squarefree levels $N>714$. In order to do this, we first give an explicit description of the minimal regular model of $X_0(N)^*$ at primes of bad reduction, and show this model is semi-stable. Each component of this model gives rise to a linear condition which ensures that the contribution at that component vanishes. Using embeddings of quadratic orders into quaternion algebras, we obtain an upper bound for the number of these conditions; when the genus of $X_0(N)^*$ is greater than one more than this bound, there is enough freedom to choose a suitable correspondence, simplifying quadratic Chabauty computations. As an application, we determine the rational points on several curves $X_0(N)^*$ for which this was not done before.

papers.title: On Boston's Unramified Conjecture for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ and McLeman's $(3,3)$-Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $A$ be a complete Noetherian commutative local ring with finite residue field of characteristic $p$. Let $G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ be the absolute Galois group of the rational number field and fix an inertia subgroup $I_p\subset G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ at $p$. We prove that every continuous odd representation $ρ:G_{\mathbf{Q}}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(A)$, unramified outside finitely many primes and with finite $ρ(I_p)$, has finite image if $p>3$ or $A$ has positive characteristic. For $p=3$, the conclusion also holds when the local representation at $3$ is reducible, or the local residual semisimplification has no mod-$3$ cyclotomic self-twist. In particular, this proves the two-dimensional odd case of Boston's unramified Fontaine--Mazur conjecture over $\mathbf{Q}$ for every odd $p$. Furthermore, we deduce finiteness results for conjugate self-dual representations of pro-$p$ Galois groups over imaginary quadratic fields under a ramification condition, and for representations of their unramified pro-$p$ groups of generator rank at most two. As an application, we resolve the sufficiency direction of McLeman's $(3,3)$-conjecture on $p$-class field towers for $p>3$. Namely, we prove that if $K$ is an imaginary quadratic field with $p$-class rank two and the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(K_{\varnothing}(p)/K)$ of the maximal unramified $p$-extension of $K$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$, then the $p$-class field tower of $K$ is finite. For $p=3$, we also rule out infinite towers for ten of the thirteen fourth Zassenhaus quotients classified by Ahlqvist and Pink.

papers.title: A Formalism for Merging Power Series in Solving Multinomial Equations: Master Series and Master Numbers
papers.abstract: It is shown that all solutions of the canonical equation y^a = 1 + a*x*y^b with arbitrary complex exponents a, b (case m = 1) and of its limiting cases - the binomial root y = (1 + a*x)^(1/a) at b = 0, the exponential y = e^x at a = 0, b = 0, and the Lambert equation y = e^(x*y^b) at a = 0 - as well as the logarithms of these solutions (case m = 0), are expressed by a single power master series M(m; a; b; x) = m + x + ((m - a + 2b)/2!) x^2 + ((m - a + 3b)(m - 2a + 3b)/3!) x^3 + ... For multivalued solutions beyond the radius of convergence, a geometric criterion for selecting the conjugate series (the same master series, but with a different set of parameters M(m; a'; b'; x')) is proposed, ensuring branch continuity on the complex plane. This representation of power series in terms of master numbers not only allows one to compute coefficients in degenerate cases where the gamma-function representation loses meaning, but also provides a transparent analytical algorithm for the merge operation on master series. The method is illustrated on problems in gas dynamics and plasma physics, where it is demonstrated that physically realizable states require the application of conjugate series beyond the radius of convergence of the basic expansion.

papers.title: A Proof of the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture for $E$-infinite algebras
papers.abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over an algebraically closed field, we prove that if $A$ is $E$-infinite, then the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture holds for $A$. In fact, we show that if there is a rational ray outside the $τ$-tilting fan of $A$, then $A$ admits an infinite family of $θ$-stable bricks of dimension $d$, for some positive integer $d$ and weight $θ$. To show our main result, from any $τ$-regular component of $A$ with no dense orbit, we obtain a brick component that also has no dense orbit and whose points in general position are $θ$-stable modules for a given weight $θ$. As an important consequence, we conclude that $A$ is stably-discrete (also called multiplicity-free) if and only if $A$ is $E$-finite. Moreover, we prove that Demonet's (lattice point) Conjecture implies the stable Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture. For $E$-infinite algebras, our results settle several open conjectures. Together with our earlier work and recent developments, this leads to important reductions in the study of some challenging open problems.

papers.title: Mechanism-Aware Ensemble Conditioning for Data-Limited Emulation of Extreme Events
papers.abstract: Extreme events in chaotic systems are difficult to learn from short trajectories because they are controlled by finite-time instabilities rather than by frequently observed bulk dynamics. We propose a mechanism-aware conditioning plug-in framework that turns a nudged ensemble of an imperfect model into a non-intrusive sensor of the local instability geometry. In the small-noise regime, the ensemble covariance has the same finite-time deformation kernels that govern local instability, providing a Jacobian-free proxy for local amplifications around a trajectory. A small Feature-Wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) network injects the ensemble geometry into an otherwise unchanged backbone without modifying the low-fidelity model simulator. We demonstrate this interface in two settings: a Transformer-style residual-attention corrector for a controlled low-dimensional chaotic system and a probabilistic recurrent STORN corrector for topographic two-layer quasi-geostrophic (QG) flow. In the low-dimensional benchmark, leading ensemble-covariance directions identify transient instabilities that are also detected by Optimally Time-Dependent (OTD) modes. FiLM conditioning improves 99th-percentile exceedance-frequency errors over an otherwise identical unconditioned Transformer. In QG, an ensemble-conditioned FiLM-STORN model substantially improves long-horizon rare-event statistics in the data-limited regime, including density-tail errors, exceedance frequencies, and spatial exceedance-area distributions relative to an unconditioned STORN trained on the same data. On averaged high-threshold exceedance diagnostics, it also outperforms the unconditioned baseline STORN trained with 20 times more expensive trajectory data. These results show that local instability geometry is not merely interpretable post hoc, but an actionable conditioning signal for data-efficient rare-event emulation.

papers.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.

papers.title: One internal stabilization is enough for resolving self-referential tubes
papers.abstract: This paper shows that one internal stabilization is enough to resolve all the self-referential tubes on an embedding. As an application, this paper gives a complete isotopy classification for embedded surfaces with a common geometric dual in orientable $S^2$-bundle over a surface, provided that the embedded surfaces have greater genus than the base surface of the bundle.

papers.title: Partial factorization and reflexivity of operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space and $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ the algebra of all bounded linear operators on $\mathcal{H}$. A subalgebra $\mathfrak{A}$ in $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ has the left (resp.\ right) partial factorization property if for any invertible operator $S\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, there exists an isometry (resp.\ a co-isometry) $U\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ such that $U^*S, S^{-1}U\in\mathfrak{A}$. We show that if $\mathfrak{A}$ is weak operator topology closed with the left (resp.\ right) partial factorization property, then $\mathfrak{A}$ is the nest algebra associated with its invariant subspace lattice. In particular, if $\mathfrak{A}$ is transitive, then $\mathfrak{A}=\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$. This gives a positive answer to Question 6.3 raised by B.V.R. Bhat and M. Kumar in \emph{Publ. Res. Inst. Math. Sci.} \textbf{60}(2024), 507--537.

papers.title: Benign Geometry and Distributional Robustness of $\mathcal{H}_2$ Synthesis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study standard and distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem of a stabilizing state-feedback controller for discrete-time linear time-invariant systems. Without requiring a nonsingular disturbance controllability Gramian or a positive-definite control penalty, we establish that stationarity of a stabilizing gain in standard $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis is equivalent to global optimality and derive an exact Pythagorean identity for the performance difference. We then generalize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem by considering i.i.d. disturbances with zero mean and uniformly bounded second moments, and extend the stationarity-optimality equivalence to the corresponding distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis. Moreover, we show that every standard $\mathcal{H}_2$-optimal gain is simultaneously optimal for every such distributionally robust problem. Finally, we specialize the framework to Frobenius, Kullback--Leibler, and Wasserstein-2 ambiguity sets and obtain explicit characterizations of their worst-case covariances, which, in turn, provide performance certificates for a common optimal controller.

papers.title: Maximal singular curves over finite fields from elliptic and hyperelliptic curves
papers.abstract: We construct explicit families of maximal singular curves over finite fields. A maximal singular curve is a curve that attains the Aubry-Perret bound, which is the natural extension of the Hasse-Weil-Serre bound on the maximum number of rational points on a smooth curve over a finite field. Starting from a smooth elliptic or hyperelliptic curve $\tilde{C}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ ($q$ odd), we generate singular curves $C$ with non-split singularities or cusps. In our approach we use linear projections of geometric embeddings, and we apply Stöhr's embedding of hyperelliptic Gorenstein curves and the Rosa-Stöhr's theory of trigonal Gorenstein curves. Some of our models attain the Aubry-Perret bound, whenever their normalization is maximal, and the construction is applied to the Tafazolian and Tafazolian-Torres smooth maximal curves to produce the desired family. Finally, we determine the gonality over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of most of the curves we construct.

papers.title: A Weak Topology on Metric Spaces
papers.abstract: We use metric functionals to construct a topology on metric spaces that induces $d$-weak convergence. We show that this topology is invariant under surjective isometries and characterize its convergence in terms of weak metrics. We prove that the topology is $T_1$ on every metric space. For normed linear spaces, we further show that it is Hausdorff and coarser than the classical weak topology. Finally, we construct a sequence in $C[0,1]$ that is unbounded in the sup-norm yet converges $d$-weakly, thereby correcting an assertion in an earlier work.

papers.title: Proof of the singularity conjecture for discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup. We prove that its stationary probability measure on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{R})$ is singular with respect to the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$-invariant probability measure. The proof compares winding variances on finite covers of a closed hyperbolic surface and uses a topological obstruction.

papers.title: Bernoulli flow for Erdős-Rényi graphs
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the Erdős-Rényi graph $\mathbb G(N,p)$ in the regime $Np \gg (\log N)^2$. We establish optimal isotropic delocalization for the bulk eigenvectors $\boldsymbol u$, meaning that $\langle \boldsymbol v, \boldsymbol u\rangle^2 \leq \frac{C \log N}{N}$ with very high probability for any deterministic normalized $\boldsymbol v$. In addition, we prove local spectral universality in the bulk by showing that the local spectral statistics coincide with those of the GOE. The main tool of our proof is a local law for the resolvent of $A$, down to optimal spectral scales and with optimal error bounds. Its proof relies on a new approach to local laws that we call the Bernoulli flow. It is a characteristic flow method in which the usual Brownian process is replaced by a Bernoulli process, where each edge of the graph forms an independent Markov process that jumps at unit rate from closed to open. The spectral parameter flows according to a suitably constructed matrix-valued Bernoulli characteristic flow.

papers.title: Interaction between nonlinear diffusion and mean curvature of a surface with initial discontinuities
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problems for a class of nonlinear diffusion equations where each initial data is given by a characteristic function of an open set $Ω$ in the whole Euclidean space. If the boundary $\partialΩ$ is of class $C^2$ in a neighborhood of a point $x$ on it, then we extract the mean curvature of $\partialΩ$ at $x$ from the initial diffusion at $x$. This corresponds to the author's previous result for the two-phase linear diffusion equation. Applications to some overdetermined problems for nonlinear diffusion equations are given.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces: Thompson and Hilbert Geometries of JB-Cones
papers.abstract: We introduce standard-norm generalized gyrovector spaces: generalized gyrovector spaces whose norm-value line has the ordinary real operations and whose fixed scalar maps are continuous. We prove that every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of two such spaces extends uniquely to a global bijective gyrometric isometry. The proof combines gyromidpoints, point reflections, continuation of local isometry germs, and monodromy; joint continuity of scalar multiplication is derived, rather than assumed. The class includes all nonzero real normed spaces and standardized Möbius, Einstein, and proper-velocity models, and is stable under finite and countable $\ell^p$-products. We also obtain bounded mapping-space examples and, under natural continuity assumptions, standard-norm function-space GGVs $C(K,G)$ for compact $K$. These yield non-Hilbertian and hybrid examples. For every unital JB-algebra, the positive invertible cone carries a one-parameter family of standard-norm GGV structures whose gyrometrics are conjugate to Thompson's metric by power maps. The projective positive cone has a parallel family, based on the variation norm modulo the unit, conjugate to Hilbert's projective metric. The projective structures are contractible. Together with global JB-cone isometry classifications, the abstract theorem yields local-to-global extension and classification results for Thompson and Hilbert geometries. Full-rank density matrices and normalized state spaces of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, including the Albert algebra, give concrete projective examples.

papers.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.

papers.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem an extension of Green Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design (GSCND)[Olfat, L., e. a. (2022), Sreyneath, C. (2021)]. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem CFLP and is known to be NP-hard [Garey, M. R. and Johnson, D. S. (1979)]. This paper formally specifies the decision variables objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming ILP formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP (B) three Fully Polynomial Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing $1+ε$ approximate solutions for $ε:= 0.15$ and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers the exact solver certifies the optimal sampled supported solutions across eight weight combinations while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

papers.title: A non-trivially non-trivial automorphism at an inaccessible cardinal
papers.abstract: We show that, relative to the existence of an inaccessible cardinal, it is consistent that for an inaccessible cardinal $κ$, there is a non-trivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}(κ)/\mathrm{fin}$ whose restriction to $\mathcal{P}(β)/\mathrm{fin}$ is induced by a bijection on $β$ for every $β<κ$. This answers questions posed by Larson--McKenney, Shelah--Steprāns, and Veličković.

papers.title: Cotorsion pairs and model structures induced by resolution dimensions relative to Frobenius pairs
papers.abstract: We explore some methods to obtain cotorsion pairs and model category structures from a Frobenius pair. Specifically, we consider a type of Frobenius pair $(\mathcal{X},ω)$ in an abelian category $\mathfrak{C}$ for which there exists a nonnegative integer $m$ such that every object in the right orthogonal complement $\mathcal{X}^{\perp_1}$ of $\mathcal{X}$ under $\text{Ext}^1_{\mathfrak{C}}(-,\sim)$ has a special $ω^\wedge_m$-precover and a special $[ω^\wedge_m]^{\perp_1}$-preenvelope, where $ω^\wedge_m$ denotes the class of objects in $\mathfrak{C}$ with resolution dimension relative to $ω$ at most $m$. The cotorsion pairs and model structures obtained from these Frobenius pairs will involve the classes $\mathcal{X}$, $ω$, $\mathcal{X}^\wedge_m$, $ω^\wedge_m$, and their orthogonal complements, in the description of its cofibrant, fibrant and trivial objects. As applications of our results, we obtain several cotorsion pairs and model structures related to relative and absolute Gorenstein homological dimensions.

papers.title: Adaptive stabilization of a leaderless bearing-constrained formation with disturbances
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of regulating and maintaining a target formation characterized by a set of bidirectional bearing constraints under disturbances. The agents in the formation are modeled by single integrators with deterministic bounded continuous disturbances of which both actual function and upper bound are unavailable for the control design. Due to the time-varying disturbances, the target formation is time-varying. We propose displacement/bearing-only based adaptive sliding mode control laws to uniformly asymptotically stabilize the time-varying target formation and reject the matched disturbances, and provide sufficient conditions to prevent possible collisions. A time-dependent adaptive design method is provided to convert the displacement-based control law to a bearing-only one. In addition, to alleviate chattering phenomena from sliding mode control, smooth adaptive control laws are introduced to guarantee uniform global boundedness of the desired formation. Finally, simulation results are given to support the analysis.

papers.title: An AFLT-type generalization of the $q$-Baker--Forrester ex-conjecture
papers.abstract: The Habsieger--Kadell $q$-Morris constant term identity, which is equivalent to the famous $q$-Selberg integral, has been generalized in numerous ways since the 1980s. Among these, there are two important generalizations: (i) the $q$-Baker--Forrester ex-conjecture, which was conjectured by Baker and Forrester in 1998 and proved by Károlyi, Nagy, Petrov and Volkov in 2015; (ii) the AFLT-type $q$-Morris identity (equivalently, the AFLT-type $q$-Selberg integral), which was obtained by Albion, Rains and Warnaar in 2021, as a $q$-analog of the result of Alba, Fateev, Litvinov and Tarnopolskiy (AFLT). In this paper, by the Gessel--Xin method and the Macdonald polynomials with prescribed symmetry, we unify these two generalizations.

papers.title: Override and Update in Restriction Categories
papers.abstract: We study the override and update operators on partial functions from the perspective of restriction categories. We propose a definition of override restriction categories, in which both of the operators in question exist. We prove a number of results concerning these operators and their relationship to the structure of the ambient restriction category, as well as relating them to the existing literature on the override and update operators. We provide various examples of override restriction categories and in particular show that every classical restriction category is an override restriction category.

papers.title: Analysis of the Virtual Element Approximation for the Smagorinsky Model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Smagorinsky model for the Navier-Stokes equations within a virtual element framework. Under the standard assumption of small data, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a solution. Assuming more regularity to the solutions, we derive the known \del{suboptimal} convergence rates $h$, using $k>1$, for the a priori error estimates of the Smagorinsky model in two dimensional domains. We additionally prove that divergence-free virtual discretizations provide improved convergence orders, with weaker regularity assumptions than in the finite element literature. We conclude the paper with numerical results that corroborate the theory.

papers.title: Binary Multiple-Node-Erasure-Correcting Codes over Complete Graphs: Constructions, q-Ary Metric Balls, and Duality
papers.abstract: Codes over graphs store symbols on edges of a complete undirected graph on $n$ vertices with a self-loop at each vertex; erasing a node removes all its incident edges. Extending Yohananov, Efron, and Yaakobi's construction, we obtain binary codes correcting any three node erasures at infinitely many prime lengths $n$, unconditionally, with redundancy $3n-2$, one bit above the graph Singleton bound. The earlier construction has the same redundancy but requires $2$ to be primitive modulo $n$, which is not known for infinitely many primes. We give a deterministic decoder for these triple-node codes using $O(n^2)$ binary operations and construct Singleton-optimal binary triple-node codes at $n=6,8,10,12$. When $2$ is primitive modulo an odd prime $n$, we extend their double- and triple-node codes to binary codes correcting $ρ$ node erasures with redundancy $ρn-(ρ-1)$ for $2\leqρ\leq(n+1)/2$, saving $ρ-1$ bits over the binary symmetric rank-metric construction when $ρ<(n+1)/2$. Over every finite field of size $q$, the node weight of a word is the least number of vertices whose erasure removes its support. We give exact formulas for ball volumes in this node metric and prove that, for fixed $q,t$, the radius-$t$ volume is asymptotic to $\binom nt q^{tn-\binom t2}$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain existence and covering bounds; for fixed $q,ρ$, we show that linear $ρ$-node-erasure-correcting codes exist with redundancy at most $ρ\log_q n+O_{q,ρ}(1)$ above the graph Singleton bound. Finally, reformulating Yohananov and Yaakobi's criterion, we show that a linear code over any finite field is Singleton-optimal for $ρ$ node erasures if and only if its dual is Singleton-optimal for erasures of the coordinates inside any $n-ρ$ vertices.

papers.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove effective joint equidistribution for subspaces of fixed dimension in a fixed rigid adelic space over a number field. The joint distribution records the rescaled height, the archimedean position, and the shapes of the subspace and its quotient. More generally, we obtain counting estimates for regions in which the height bound may depend on the position and both shapes. Under a Hölder-type bound for the measure of boundary layers, the estimates have explicit power-saving error terms. We apply these results to counting problems involving slopes, freeness, and semistability, and to Diophantine approximation with prescribed shapes.

papers.title: Thin-Shell implies small-ball deviation via Gaussian tilts
papers.abstract: We show that uniform thin-shell estimates for isotropic log-concave measures $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ yield precise and explicit deviation estimates for the Euclidean norm $|X|$ below the expectation, improving the square-root dependence of Klartag-Lehec to a quadratic one (which is best possible, up to numeric constants). Using the recent Chen-Klartag sharp variance bound, we deduce: $$ μ\left(|X|\le \sqrt{n}-s\right) \le \exp\left\{ -\frac{s^2}{4} \left(1+O\left(\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\right) \right\} \qquad \forall\, s\in(0,\sqrt{n}). $$ In particular, this yields a new and transparent proof that Thin-Shell implies Slicing (by passing through small-ball estimates).
