These results are upper bounds on the universal local order of a cycle; they do not establish attainability for every budget.

papers.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).

papers.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
papers.abstract: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.

papers.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
papers.abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta, and Ghorpade, resolving a longstanding problem on common zeros and determining the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.

papers.title: A Note on the Cut-Locus-Corrected Fréchet Mean Central Limit Theorem
papers.abstract: We record three observations concerning \cite{HLW24}. First, the proof of its Theorem~1 yields the population linearization (13)--(14) at \textit{any critical point} of the Fréchet function $F_μ$, under its remaining geometric and measure-theoretic assumptions; neither \textit{isolation} nor a \textit{nonsingular} Hessian of $F_μ$ is needed. Second, its Theorem~2 is given a shorter proof by applying the M-estimator theorem \cite[Theorem~5.23, pp.~53--54]{vdV98} to negative squared distance in normal coordinates, as opposed to the Donsker argument used there. Third, the above shorter route also helps us establish a CLT for a measurable selection of strict local empirical Fréchet mean with positive definite Hessian, with the cut locus correction, relaxing the assumptions of uniqueness or global minimality, as in \cite{HLW24}. Numerical experiments at the end show the agreement of the Hessian of the Fréchet function at \textit{local} Fréchet means with the (signed) sum of the expected Hessian of the squared distance function and the cut locus correction there.

papers.title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
papers.abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models under gravitational force, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.

papers.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
papers.abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.

papers.title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
papers.abstract: Sullivan's celebrated no-wandering-domain theorem asserts that rational maps have no wandering Fatou components. In this paper, we establish a measure-theoretic counterpart for the Julia set: every wandering continuum in the Julia set of a finite-type entire function has zero area. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we also prove that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if $f$ is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset $E$ of the Julia set, then $f|_E$ is conservative and almost every point of $E$ is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.

papers.title: Infinitary real-valued logic and a refinement of the Kochen-Specker theorem
papers.abstract: We prove that every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables in quantum mechanics is finite, including the obstructions that rest on Gleason's hypothesis of countable additivity. Since Kochen and Specker, such obstructions have been certified by finite configurations of rays, at the level of propositional logic: once a configuration is fixed, the obstruction is the inconsistency of finitely many Boolean constraints. Compactness, the source of these configurations, cannot reach the obstructions that rest on countable additivity: in infinite dimension the finite-dimensional events admit a finitely additive noncontextual valuation, and countable additivity constrains infinitely many events at once. The tool is a theorem of infinitary real-valued logic that takes the place of compactness: every countable theory of closed conditions without models is refuted by a well-founded tree of finite contradictions, given by the winning strategies of a model existence game. Quantum probability is axiomatized by such a theory, whose standard models are exactly those of Gleason's theorem. In the strategy we construct, a hypothetical noncontextual measure is not refuted by a configuration fixed in advance: through countable additivity, the measure itself selects the four-dimensional subspace in which the measure fails. The same logic defines, in the standard models, exactly the $σ$-projective sets of probabilities. Statements about $σ$-projective sets often go beyond ZFC, as the measurability of all these sets does; our theorems are nevertheless proved in ZFC, since the only determinacy they use is that of open games.

papers.title: Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules
papers.abstract: We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Broué--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: A Side Condition Principle With Applications
papers.abstract: We introduce a combinatorial principle $\textsf{SC}(κ)$, for any regular cardinal $κ\ge ω_2$, which asserts the existence of a family $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq [H(κ)]^ω$ of elementary substructures of $H(κ)$ which is closed under finite intersections and satisfies that for stationarily many $N \in \mathcal{Y}$, if $M \in \mathcal{Y}$ and $M \cap ω_1 < N \cap ω_1$, then $M \cap N \cap κ\in N$. We explore the idea of defining forcings with side conditions consisting of finite subsets of such a family $\mathcal{Y}$. If $\textsf{SC}(ω_2)$ holds, then there exists a thin stationary subset of $[ω_2]^ω$, and consequently $\textsf{SC}(ω_2)$ is independent of ZFC. Assuming that $μ$ is a Mahlo cardinal, the Lévy collapse $\mathrm{Col}(ω,<μ)$ forces that $\textsf{SC}(κ)$ holds for all regular cardinals $κ\ge ω_2$. Local instances of $\textsf{SC}$ can be forced using matrices of models or derived as consequences of square principles. We apply the principle $\textsf{SC}$ to define two kinds of forcings: a streamlined version of a strongly proper collapse, and a forcing which is strongly proper on a stationary set and adds arbitrarily many Baumgartner clubs. Finally, we prove two consistency results using forcings derived from $\textsf{SC}$ related to Aronszajn trees, the guessing model principle, strong failures of club guessing, and the higher dominating number.

papers.title: Deterministic Principal Ideals of Dependent Random Operators
papers.abstract: We classify the algebraic principal ideals of alternating quadratic random operators under dimension-free two-sided curvature bounds. For the centered evaluation of a Hilbert two-form, an explicit covariance compensator determines the principal ideal after every fixed compact perturbation. For fixed spectral choices, the compensator is a compact linear function of the full covariance with explicit finite-dimensional approximation bounds; its class modulo the independent Gaussian ideal is intrinsic. For fixed spatial weights of rank at least two and a trace-class kernel, all attainable principal ideals form an exact order interval. Every intermediate ideal is realized by a Gaussian covariance arbitrarily close to the identity while each row retains its standard Gaussian law. For these spatial weights, trace class is also the exact kernel domain for raw evaluation under every law in the curvature class. The proof uses a conditional-residual criterion for linear operators, polarization, and finite-rank approximation. Applications include Wiener area and dependent matrices with doubly monotone variance weights. A logarithmic example separates principal ideals with identical membership in every Schatten class.

papers.title: Overcoming Demand Censoring through Randomization for Risk-Sensitive Newsvendor Learning
papers.abstract: We study online newsvendor learning with bounded demand, censored observations, and convex nonlinear shortage costs. Because stockouts can conceal the shortage magnitudes needed by gradient-based algorithms, we use randomized ordering to construct unbiased subgradient estimates. We characterize admissible randomization distributions within this framework and develop an online inventory policy that combines the resulting subgradient estimates with gradient-based updates. Our regret analysis quantifies the cost of randomization via the estimation variance and an additional loss term. We characterize the randomization distributions that minimize this objective. For piecewise-linear shortage costs, the optimal distribution is computed through a linear-time recursion; for costs with bounded curvature density, it is characterized by a scalar ordinary differential equation. The policy achieves expected regret of $O(T^{2/3})$ against the best fixed order in hindsight over $T$ periods. Under independent demand and suitable curvature of expected losses, the bound improves to $O(\sqrt{T})$. Matching minimax lower bounds establish rate optimality over the corresponding classes with a fixed marginal-cost bound. Both rates extend to nonperishable inventory under uniformly positive conditional expected demand. Numerical experiments on synthetic and retail data show improvements over alternative policies using censored observations.

papers.title: $P$-stationary structural equation modeling: Causal effect identification under temporally incomplete observations
papers.abstract: Causal modeling of discrete-time processes often involves the assumption that the modeled processes are stationary. A general class of linear causal models for discrete-time stationary processes are structural equation processes (SEP), which generalize the well known structural equation model for i.i.d. observations. In this paper, we extend the SEP model from stationary to $P$-stationary processes, which are non-stationary processes whose $P$-periodically sampled subprocesses are jointly stationary. We will use this model to approach the problem of causal effect identification under temporally incomplete observations from a graphical modeling perspective. To have a notion of generic identifiability, we restrict our analysis to $P$-stationary structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) processes, which are SVAR processes whose underlying coefficients can vary $P$-periodically over time. Our findings allow to detect, in any given temporally incomplete observational setting, if a set of $P$-periodic instrumental subprocesses qualifies to identify a causal effect between $P$-periodic subprocesses, and if this is the case, that effect admits an explicit expression as a rational function evaluated at the observational spectral density.

papers.title: Multi-rate high-order regularization with an order-$(p-2)$ oracle
papers.abstract:
We consider unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex function $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ whose $p$th derivative is Lipschitz continuous, with $p\geq3$, when derivative information is available only through order $p-2$. The unavailable tensors $
abla^{p-1}f$ and $
abla^pf$ are reconstructed from central finite differences of $
abla^{p-2}f$. Since the two reconstructions have different point-query costs, we use a block length $m$ for the order-$p$ approximation and a subblock length $\ell\leq m$ for the order-$(p-1)$ approximation. The latter is transported between consecutive reconstruction points using the stored order-$p$ approximation. This leads to an adaptive regularization method that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant. We prove finite termination at an $ε$-approximate first-order stationary point and derive an explicit bound on the number of bundled order-$(p-2)$ oracle queries. For $m=(p-2)n^2$ and $\ell=(p-2)n$, the accuracy-dependent term has dimension--accuracy scaling $n^{3/p}ε^{-(p+1)/p}$. Thus the method retains the $ε^{-(p+1)/p}$ dependence of full order-$p$ regularization while using derivatives only through order $p-2$. Within the dense reconstruction framework considered here, using separate block and subblock lengths gives dimension dependence of order $n^{3/p}$, compared with $n^{4/p}$ when a common length is imposed.

papers.title: Uniformization of topological MV-algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, First, we prove that for every topological MV-algebra the topology is induced by a uniformity. As a application, we obtain that every topological MV-algebra is completely regular and every \(T_0\) first countable topological MV-algebra is metrizable. Second, we study the completion of the canonical difference uniformity in topological MV-algebra. Finally, we construct some examples show that not all topological MV-algebras are canonically completable and the property of canonically completable topological MV-algebra does not imply local order convexity.

papers.title: A $33$-polynomial proof of a three-color Rado number formula
papers.abstract: For $k\ge 3$, let $T_k(3)$ denote the least $N$ such that every $3$-coloring of $[1,N]$ contains a monochromatic solution to $x+(k-1)y=z$. The formula $T_k(3)=k^3+2k^2-2$ is already known: it follows from a Theorem of Chang, De Loera, and Wesley. Their proof uses a symbolic SAT certificate with $685$ polynomials and $9468$ solution triples. The purpose of this paper is to give an independent, explicit proof based on a much smaller certificate. We exhibit a fixed set $\Xmin$ of $33$ polynomials in $k$ and the $144$ polynomial identities $z=x+(k-1)y$ among them, and show that no $3$-coloring of $\Xmin$ avoids a monochromatic identity. The resulting case analysis has $62$ cases, depth $8$, and uses only two elementary rules; it is given in full and independently checked by a program. We also prove that $\Xmin$ is a critical subset of minimum cardinality of the $51$-element set from which it was extracted, and describe the rigid structure shared by all extremal colorings of $[1,k^3+2k^2-3]$. The lower bound is supplied by an explicit recursive coloring. In the notation $s_a(3)$ of the first author, with $a=k-1$, the formula is $s_a(3)=a^3+5a^2+7a+1$, which was conjectured before.

papers.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
papers.abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain the complete bound $2$, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

papers.title: The Rise of Low Precision Floating Point
papers.abstract: Floating point computing has dominated scientific computations since the 1950s because of its versatile ability to approximate real numbers with both sufficiently high precision and sufficiently great range. Since 1985, two specific formats have become standard across the industry, one with 32 bits which is adequate for many purposes and one with 64 bits which allows numbers with both much higher precision and much greater range for applications where these are needed. However, during the past decade, deep learning has come to dominate computation, and narrower floating point formats with lower precision and reduced range have steadily become more common. In this article we discuss this phenomenon, why it is happening, how various 16-bit, 8-bit and even 4-bit floating point formats have been developed, and efforts to standardize these formats.

papers.title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
papers.abstract: The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound. A connection to (generalized) Loewy length is given.

papers.title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
papers.abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
papers.abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $γ_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_jγ_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

papers.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_θ$ --- the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_θ$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators. As a by-product of our findings, we give a complete characterization for $S_θ$, where $θ$ is a finite Blaschke product and also obtained the commutant of $S_θ+ S_θ^{*}$ in that case.

papers.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
papers.abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

papers.title: Webs and exponentially large mu-coefficients
papers.abstract: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.

papers.title: Renewable model averaging for generalized linear models
papers.abstract: Prediction is one of the most important research topics in statistics and machine learning. Moreover, in the domain of streaming data analysis, real-time prediction has become a rapidly growing research field in recent years, owing to the abundance of streaming data. In many fields of scientific research, such as biomedical research, weather forecasting, and traffic management, improving real-time prediction of streaming data is crucial in general. However, the complicated features of streaming data, such as large-scale and high-velocity, impose both theoretical and computational challenges to the development and evaluation of real-time prediction in this field, especially when the investigator has multiple models at hand. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel Renewable Model Averaging method through Quadratic approximation (ReMAQ) for generalized linear model (GLM) for streaming data. By approximating the model averaging procedure for GLMs (which is typically a convex optimization problem) with a quadratic optimization formulation, ReMAQ allows us to update the model averaging prediction sequentially when a new batch of data arrives, without accessing the entire historical data. Moreover, ReMAQ is also computationally efficient as one only needs to consider a quadratic programming problem in each steps of updating. Under certain regular conditions, we also show that the proposed ReMAQ weight is asymptotically equivalent to that by the oracle model averaging based on the inaccessible full data, the asymptotic optimality of ReMAQ is then established accordingly. The proposed method is also assessed by simulation studies. We apply our proposed ReMAQ in the study of the Airline On-Time Performance Dataset and the results demonstrate the superiority our method in practical situations.

papers.title: The convergence-divergence criterion for the Mañé cohomology lemma and Livšic theorem
papers.abstract: We establish a dynamical convergence-divergence criterion for all functions with a prescribed modulus of continuity to have continuous sub-actions. The divergence part of the criterion, which gives functions that do not have any bounded sub-action, is valid for general dynamical systems with a weakly repelling fixed point. This unifies and generalises versions of the Mañé cohomology lemma for uniformly expanding maps, and results of Morris for maps with an indifferent fixed point. One consequence is that for any infinite compact metric space $(X,ρ)$, and Lipschitz Ruelle-expanding map $T:X\to X$, a metric transform $ω$ satisfies Dini's criterion $\int_0 ω(s)s^{-1}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if all functions that are Lipschitz for $ω\circρ$ have continuous sub-actions. Another consequence is that if $T$ is an expanding circle map of Manneville--Pomeau type $α\in(0,1)$, then $ω$ satisfies the convergence criterion $\int_0 ω(s)s^{-1-α}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if all functions that are Lipschitz for $ω\circρ$ have continuous sub-actions. For the latter class of maps, with $ω$ satisfying the convergence criterion, we prove a Livšic theorem for functions $f$ that are Lipschitz for $ω\circρ$: if $\int f\, dμ=0$ for all invariant measures $μ$, then $f=\varphi\circ T-\varphi$ for a function $\varphi$ that is Lipschitz with respect to $D_α(ω)\circρ$, where $D_α(ω)(t)= \int_0^t ω(s)s^{-1-α}\, ds$.

papers.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
papers.abstract: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.

papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

papers.title: The $λ>0$ case for $Δu=λ-c e^u$ type equation on high dimensional spheres
papers.abstract: Motivated by prescribed Chern scalar curvature problems in complex geometry, we study the equation $Δ_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}V+λ(e^V-1)=0$ with $λ>0$ on spheres. For $N\ge4$ and $λ>2(N-2)$ with $λ\ne2N$, we prove the existence of a nonconstant smooth solution that is axially symmetric and symmetric about the equator.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates
papers.abstract: Learned barrier certificates provide a principled mechanism for establishing safety of stochastic systems, but their validity may deteriorate during deployment when the underlying dynamics differ from those used for training. We propose an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits a learned barrier certificate using observed closed-loop trajectories. The monitor is intended to detect loss of statistical support for the deployed barrier condition; it does not by itself guarantee detection before unsafe entry or safety of a subsequent intervention. Specifically, the conditional barrier-drift condition is formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test, and observed barrier increments are transformed into a nonnegative test supermartingale, yielding finite-sample false-alarm control under arbitrary stopping times. Inspired by finite-horizon safety verification, we further introduce a deterministic temporal shaping of the monitoring boundary, making the monitor more conservative early in a prescribed deployment horizon while preserving anytime-validity. The monitor is designed to detect statistical evidence that the safety certificate is no longer consistent with the observed dynamics, rather than to predict unsafe entry. To assess the monitor empirically, we evaluate empirical alarm behavior under valid and invalid certificates. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/runtime-barrier-monitor.

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
papers.abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schröter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.

papers.title: A Non-Dichotomy for CSPs of Stable $ω$-Categorical Structures
papers.abstract: We construct countable, stable, $ω$-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable $ω$-categorical graphs $M_α$ for suitable irrational parameters $α>1$. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs $M_α$ by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound $t$, there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME$(t)$. For an explicit parameter $α$, the restriction to complete instances belongs to $\mathrm{coNP}$ and the full CSP belongs to $Σ_2^{\mathrm P}$. Separating the ages of the $M_α$ using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.

papers.title: A sharp pinching theorem for closed minimal Legendrian submanifolds in the unit sphere
papers.abstract: Let $F:M^n\to\Sph^{2n+1}$ be a minimal Legendrian immersion of a connected closed manifold, where $n\ge3$, and let $B$ be its second fundamental form. We prove that if $|B|^2\le(n-1)(n+2)/n$, then, up to a unitary transformation, $F$ parametrizes a totally geodesic sphere or is a finite covering of the image of the minimal Calabi product of a point and a totally geodesic Legendrian sphere. This proves Conjecture 1 of Luo and Sun [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré C Anal. Non Linéaire 40 (2023), p. 548].

papers.title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
papers.abstract: Optimal control problems become computationally challenging when the system dynamics are nonsmooth, learned from data, or available only through a simulator. In such settings, derivatives may be difficult to obtain, and evaluating different control actions through repeated trajectory simulations can be expensive. We propose Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Optimization (HPDPO), a method that uses numerical costates to guide the search for improved controls. The costates are estimated using finite differences of the numerical model and are used to rank candidate actions. Rather than performing a full remaining-horizon simulation for every candidate, HPDPO evaluates a small set of promising alternatives and accepts a control update only when it decreases the discrete objective. We derive a first-order costate-based approximation for ranking candidate actions and establish descent of the discretized objective under rollout-verified updates. We test the method on scalar and multidimensional control problems, including examples with nonsmooth and learned dynamics. The results show good agreement with analytical or published reference solutions and lower simulation costs than the direct-rollout methods considered. HPDPO requires only forward model evaluations, without analytical or automatically differentiated derivatives of the dynamics or a learned value function.

papers.title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and their related binary LCD codes
papers.abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ which attains the asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov bound, i.e., whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/2)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with previously unknown parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$ and nine binary LCD codes with the best known parameters.

papers.title: Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications
papers.abstract: We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.

papers.title: The price of a weak shadow variable: inference under nonignorable missingness as relevance vanishes
papers.abstract: When an outcome is missing not at random, identification is commonly restored by a shadow variable: a covariate that predicts the outcome but is excluded from the response mechanism. The literature treats the first requirement, relevance, as a yes-or-no condition. We make it continuous, parametrizing it by a scalar that scales the shadow variable's entire contribution to the moment conditions, and ask what inference costs as that scalar vanishes. One functional of the inverse weight governs the answer. We characterize it exactly, show that it fixes the effective sample size, and use it to sharpen the rates of the estimator that avoids the weight. The characterization is concrete. Whether the functional saturates or diverges turns not on boundedness of the outcome but on whether the tilting variable has an atom at its essential supremum: a binary outcome saturates, a uniform one does not. It also bounds how far a scanned set reaches, and that reach grows only as the square root of the logarithm of the sample size, so a thousandfold increase buys one unit of tilt while the set to be scanned widens. A reanalyzed credit-scoring study shows the cost: a characteristic an optimizing selector uses cannot satisfy exclusion.

papers.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
papers.abstract: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. The localization is measured in scale-invariant Lorentz or mixed Lebesgue spaces. The admissible data include all real-valued Schwartz functions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum, without any smallness assumption and without the zero mean condition. We also show that some localization is necessary: there are smooth real-valued initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm, with a logarithmic moment, for which the solution does not scatter in $L^2$.

papers.title: $L_p$-spaces, $1\leq p\ne 2<\infty$, associated with type III and semifinite von Neumann algebras are not isomorphic
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a type III von Neumann algebra, and let $N$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra. We prove that the Banach space $M_*$ does not embed isomorphically into the Banach space $N_*$. More generally, we prove that $L_p(M)$ is not isomorphic to a subspace of $L_p(N)$ for $1\le p<2$. In particular, the Banach isomorphism class of $L_p(M)$ distinguishes type III algebras from semifinite algebras for $1\le p<\infty$, $p\ne2$. This answers several long-standing open questions in the literature.

papers.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
papers.abstract: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of the 2D Boussinesq equations around Couette flow in infinite channel
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the stability threshold of the two-dimensional Boussinesq system around the Couette flow in an infinite channel $\mathbb{R}\times[-1,1]$ under Navier-slip boundary condition. To address nonlinear echo chains induced by temperature-vorticity coupling, we construct a two-level frequency-dependent temporal decomposition, with the two levels matched to the infinite and finite superposition principles for the equation, respectively. By fully exploiting the enhanced dissipation effect at each decomposition level, we prove that if the initial perturbation $(ω^{in}, θ^{in})$ around the Couette flow satisfies $\|ω^{in}\|_{H^4_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^4_y}\leq cν^{\frac{1}{3}}$, and $\|θ^{in}\|_{H^5_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^5_y}\leq cν^{\frac{2}{3}+}$, the Boussinesq system admits a globally asymptotically stable solution. It should be emphasized that the method in this paper provides an effective approach for the hydrodynamic equations with coupling effects.

papers.title: Relative isoperimetry in the three-dimensional cube: classification and quantitative stability
papers.abstract: We compute the relative isoperimetric profile of the three-dimensional unit cube. Up to cube isometries and complementation, its minimizers are corner eighth-balls, edge quarter-cylinders and coordinate slabs, with both adjacent families minimizing at $4π/81$ and $1/π$. At each fixed volume the perimeter deficit bounds the squared $L^1$ distance to the minimizing family, with optimal exponent two. Near each transition the deficit controls the minimum, over the two adjacent families, of squared distance plus excess perimeter. The best constant for distance to the minimizing family decays linearly as the volume approaches a transition. We also obtain the conjectured profile for $(0,β)\times(0,1)^2$, $0<β\le1$, and resolve the three-dimensional case of Brezis's Open Problem~10.1.

papers.title: Strong Uniqueness for Instantaneously Complete Chern-Ricci Flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study strong uniqueness for smooth instantaneously complete Chern-Ricci flows on noncompact complex manifolds. Under suitable reference metric and positivity assumptions, we establish strong uniqueness for initial Hermitian metrics which are Kähler outside a compact set. The initial metric may be incomplete, and no curvature bounds or metric equivalence assumptions are imposed on the evolving solutions. In particular, we obtain strong uniqueness from complete initial metrics in this class with bounded Chern-Ricci curvature. We also prove stationarity of flows from the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and uniqueness of the instantaneously complete flow from the Euclidean metric on the complex unit ball for all positive time. Finally, on complex surfaces, we show that a Ricci flow remaining Hermitian for a fixed complex structure is Kähler at all times if it is Kähler at one time, and derive a corresponding strong uniqueness result for Ricci flows in this class.

papers.title: A method of moving planes for a mixed local-nonlocal parabolic equation with quenching
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a parabolic version of the method of moving planes on systems with a mixed local and nonlocal diffusion operator, that being $\mathcal{L} = -(-Δ)^s + Δ$, where $(-Δ)^s$ is the integral fractional laplacian. We then use this result to study the quenching phenomena occurring in said systems with a singular absorption term of the type $(1-u)^{-p}$. We prove that there exists a range of multiplicative parameters for which every solution presents quenching, and that for any initial datum $u_0$, there exists a small enough multiplicative parameter such as the solution is globally defined. We also prove that the quenching phenomena cannot happen arbitrarily close to the boundary, but they are contained in a compact subset of the domain.

papers.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincaré Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
papers.abstract: The Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincaré constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincaré constant $C_P(μ)\le25$, where $μ$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincaré inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

papers.title: Staircase phase transitions for the extreme eigenvalues of heavy-tailed sample correlation matrices
papers.abstract: We establish phase transitions in the first-order asymptotics of the largest and smallest nonzero eigenvalues of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices formed from data with i.i.d. centered real entries of finite variance, allowing an infinite fourth moment. Because of self-normalization, spectral outliers are driven by collisions of large entries in distinct rows of a common column rather than by individual large entries. The resulting phase transitions depend jointly on the aspect ratio and the entry tail, producing staircase boundaries in the phase diagram. We prove convergence to the corresponding Marčenko--Pastur edges in subcritical regimes and to deterministic outlier levels in supercritical regimes. In critical regimes, Poisson limits for the point processes of spectral outliers and nondegenerate limiting laws for the extreme eigenvalues are established.

papers.title: The commuting scheme of $\mathfrak{g}_2$ and a degree formula for commuting schemes
papers.abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we show that the commuting scheme of the exceptional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}_2$ is Cohen-Macaulay and normal (in particular, reduced). We determine its Hilbert series, show that it has degree $1825$ and is not Gorenstein, and determine an explicit linear system of parameters. A crucial ingredient of (one of) our proofs is a root theoretic formula for the degree of the commuting scheme of any reductive Lie algebra whose Borel subalgebra has a complete-intersection commuting scheme, which includes all classical Lie algebras of small rank as well as $E_6$ and $G_2$. Finally, we give a criterion that implies Cohen-Macaulayness and reducedness of the commuting scheme in any given positive characteristic and use it to show that the commuting scheme is Cohen-Macaulay and reduced for every prime $5\leq p\leq1000$. We also resolve the `bad' characteristic cases and show that the commuting scheme is reduced and Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $3$, and reduced but not Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $2$ where it has degree $438$.

papers.title: Poincaré duality and module topological complexity
papers.abstract: For every simply connected space $X$ of finite rational type with Poincaré duality cohomology, we prove $MTC(X)=TC_0(X)=TC_0^M(X)$: module, rational and monoidal rational topological complexity coincide. Neither formality nor finiteness of the total rational homotopy is required. For every rationally retractive map $f$ between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we prove $relcat(f_Q)\le msecat(f_Q)+1$. This bound is sharp for rationally retractive maps. Both proofs reduce to the same question: can a module nullhomotopy taking values in a split Sullivan model be chosen with values in its kernel ideal? Comparing resolutions of consecutive ideal powers achieves this after increasing the exponent by one; for diagonals, Poincaré duality preserves the exponent. An ideal-preserving form of Hess's construction then converts the module nullhomotopy into a compatible algebra retraction.

papers.title: Normalized ground states as sharp dynamical thresholds for the inhomogeneous NLS with an inverse-square potential
papers.abstract: We study the focusing inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an inverse-square potential, in the mass-supercritical and energy-subcritical regime and in every dimension $N\ge3$. Two lines of research on this model have so far developed separately, namely the scattering theory below the ground state and the variational theory of solutions with prescribed mass. We connect them. We compute explicitly the minimax level $m_a(c)$ of the energy on the Pohozaev manifold of mass $c$, introduced by Hajaiej, Luo and Wang, in terms of the sharp constant of the associated Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. We prove that the minimizers of $m_a(c)$ are exactly the optimizers of this inequality lying on the Pohozaev manifold, and that they are ground states of the stationary problem. This answers a question left open by these authors. We then show that $m_a(c)$ is a sharp dynamical threshold. Below it, the sign of the Pohozaev functional is preserved by the flow. If this sign is positive, the solution is global. If it is negative and the datum has finite variance, the solution blows up in finite time. For the three-dimensional cubic model, the global solutions also scatter, by the scattering criterion of Hajaiej, Luo and Wang read in its scale-invariant form. As consequences, we obtain the strong instability of all normalized ground states, with destabilizing data on the same mass sphere, the strict monotonicity of the threshold with respect to the coupling constant, and a positive lower bound for $m_a(c)$ which is uniform up to the critical Hardy coupling.

papers.title: Homology and higher-order intermediate categories for proper abelian subcategories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an extension-closed proper abelian subcategory of a triangulated category $\mathcal{C}$, and put $\mathcal{D}_\ell=Σ^\ell\mathcal{A}*\cdots*\mathcal{A}$ for $\ell\geq 1$. Assuming that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(Σ^p\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})=0$ for $1\leq p\leq\ell+1$, we construct homology functors $H_i:\mathcal{D}_\ell\to\mathcal{A}$ for $0\leq i\leq\ell$ and prove that triangles in $\mathcal{D}_\ell$ induce natural long exact sequences in $\mathcal{A}$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is Krull--Schmidt, we introduce compatible sequences of subcategories of $\mathcal{A}$ and use them to classify the homology-determined subcategories $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{D}_\ell$ that are closed under extensions and direct summands.

papers.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
papers.abstract: In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.

papers.title: Rational homotopy theory of flag manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $G/P$ be a flag manifold with $G$ simple. We determine the rational homotopy groups $π_{\ast }(G/P)\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and describe the rational cohomology ring $H^{\ast }(G/P;\mathbb{Q})$ solely in terms of the rational homotopy types of $G$ and $P$, respectively. The proof is based on the restrictions of basic Weyl invariants of $G$ to suitable simple factors of $P$, which also address a key nonvanishing issue not settled by earlier approaches of Meier, Shiga-Tezuka, Kotschick, and Terzic.

papers.title: Sectorial normalisation of one resonant biholomorphisms near a fixed point
papers.abstract: In this article, we study germs of biholomorphisms of $(\C^n,0)$, $n\geq 2$ fixing the origin, the linear part at which has all its eigenvalues on the unit circle. We prove the existence of a {\it sectorial} transformation to a polynomial normal form of a non-degenerate 1-resonant biholomorphism under a Diophantine condition. We also give their holomorphic classification. We show that the {\it sectorial} automorphisms of the polynomial normal form are {\it exponentially flat} perturbations of the identity. We deduce the Gevrey character of the formal normalizing transformation and we show how the Gevrey index depends on the Diophantine exponent.

papers.title: Quantifying Long-Range Dependence in Object-Valued Time Series
papers.abstract: Object-valued time series, including distributions, covariance matrices, networks, and compositions, lack the linear structure required by conventional autocovariance-based definitions of long memory. We develop an intrinsic framework for defining and estimating long memory in metric spaces of negative type. An isometric embedding yields a centered Hilbert-valued process, and the trace of its lag-covariance operator provides a signed, additive measure of temporal dependence. Crucially, this trace equals the difference between the marginal mean pairwise distance and expected lagged distance, so the framework and its estimators use only distances between the original objects. We define the memory parameter through the nonsummable decay of this trace and show that it coincides with the usual parameter in Hilbert-valued settings. Estimation uses Bartlett aggregates of distance-based lag measures. Estimating the common marginal distance from the same dependent sample induces a common-centering bias in these aggregates. We derive its finite-sample form and propose iterated block-difference corrections, log-ratio and multi-bandwidth log-slope estimators, and a localized self-consistency refinement. We establish consistency, document substantial bias reduction in simulations, and find long-memory evidence in foreign-exchange return distributions and U.S. electricity-generation compositions.

papers.title: Imaginary Non-CM Fields of $2$-Power Degree
papers.abstract: We establish a new method for the study of imaginary non-CM fields of arbitrary \(2\)-power degree and class number one. In particular, we show that for degrees greater than \(16\), dihedral fields either lie in the ray class field of one of the three imaginary quadratic fields \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-2})\), \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})\),\(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-19})\),\(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-43})\), \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-67})\), whose conductor is supported only on primes dividing \(2\), with explicit upper bounds on the relevant exponents, or are Hilbert class fields of imaginary quadratic fields. We also give a complete classification of the \(161\) imaginary non-CM fields of degree \(16\) with class number one, providing explicit tables of defining polynomials, Galois groups, base fields, and conductors. These \(161\) non-CM fields, together with the six CM fields classified by Louboutin and Okazaki \cite{lou7}, complete the classification of all imaginary fields of degree \(16\) with class number one. For CM fields, the problem reduces to computing relative class numbers via analytic class number formulae, whereas for non-CM fields the absence of a totally real subfield of index \(2\) requires a different approach and leads to a richer variety of Galois groups and ramification patterns.

papers.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
papers.abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.

papers.title: An involution on Dyck paths in the region $\defc\le\min(\area,\dinv)$ that interchanges area and dinv
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit involution on Dyck paths satisfying $\defc\le\min(\area,\dinv)$ that interchanges area and dinv, where $\defc=\binom n2-\area-\dinv$ and $n$ is the semilength. In addition, we give an involution on Dyck paths with $\defc \le 2n-8$ that interchanges area and dinv. Finally, we give an explicit partition formula for the portion of the $q,t$-Catalan polynomial of total degree at least $\binom n2-2n+8$, thereby proving a conjecture of Lee and Li~\cite[Conjecture~4]{LeeLi11}. Altogether our results give a combinatorial explanation of $q,t$-Catalan symmetry in the region $\defc\le\max(2n-8,\min(\area,\dinv))$. Our constructions rely on a number of new combinatorial objects developed here and three main external tools: the dual Dyck insertion of \cite{Hawkes26}, the Garsia--Milne involution principle~\cite{GarsiaMilne81,Doyle19}, and the partition bijection of ~\cite{LoehrWarrington09}. We also explore rational analogs of these results, give an answer to Question~4.9 of Kiem and Lee~\cite{KiemLee24} and consider deficit up to $3n-15$ briefly.

papers.title: A Llarull type theorem on complete noncompact manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq3$, $2\leq k\leq n-1$, and $m=n-k-1$. We prove that a complete, connected, noncompact, oriented manifold $(M^n,g)$ with scalar curvature $R_M\geq k(k-1)$ is isometric to $\mathbb{S}^k\times\mathbb{T}^m_Λ\times\mathbb{R}$ if it admits a smooth proper map of non-zero degree to $\mathbb{S}^k\times\mathbb{T}^m\times\mathbb{R}$ whose spherical component is 1-Lipschitz. We also establish a weighted scalar curvature obstruction at infinity for sphere-torus targets with a higher dimensional Euclidean factor under suitable control of the Euclidean component. These results hold in all dimensions without a spin assumption.

papers.title: Special Lagrangian cones in Deep Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce a matrix generalization of the cone of Harvey and Lawson and prove that it is an exact special Lagrangian manifold. We further show that it belongs to a family of exact special Lagrangian manifolds that foliate the balanced manifold arising in deep learning.

papers.title: Character Nonvanishing under Coprime Actions
papers.abstract: Let a finite group $A$ act coprimely on a finite group $G$, and let $C=C_G(A)$. Navarro asked whether an $A$-invariant irreducible character has linear Glauberman--Isaacs correspondent if and only if it is nonvanishing on $C$. We give counterexamples to this equivalence. We also prove that when $G$ is nilpotent, nonvanishing on $C$ implies that the Glauberman--Isaacs correspondent is linear.

papers.title: Phase transition for the smallest eigenvalue of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices
papers.abstract: We study the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the sample correlation matrix $\mathbf{R}_n$ formed from a $p_n \times n$ data matrix with i.i.d. real entries $ξ$ of mean zero and unit variance, in the high-dimensional regime $p_n / n \to φ\in (0, \infty) \setminus \{1\}$. In the tall regime $φ> 1$, we prove almost-sure convergence of $λ_n (\mathbf{R}_n)$ to the lower Marčenko--Pastur edge $λ_- = (1 - \sqrtφ)^2$ without additional moment assumptions. In the wide regime $φ< 1$, we establish a phase transition at the third-order tail scale. If $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$, the smallest eigenvalue $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to $λ_-$. While if $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to \infty$, then $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to zero. At the critical scale $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to κ\in (0, \infty)$, the point process of eigenvalues in the lower gap $(0, λ_-)$ converges in distribution to a Poisson random measure with explicit intensity. In this critical regime, we also identify the nondegenerate limiting distribution of $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$, which has a continuous density on $(0, λ_-)$ and a positive atom at $λ_-$.

papers.title: The crossing number and the unit-distance crossing number of the Hamming graphs H(d,3)=K_3^{box d}, and their realizations over many coordinate fields
papers.abstract: The Hamming graph H(d,3)=K_3^{box d} (n=3^d vertices) is the graph of single-symbol errors of ternary codes. Can it be drawn in the plane with every edge one unit long and no two non-adjacent vertices a unit apart? It can, for every d, joining two problems into one. Arithmetic: over which coordinate fields is it realizable? As a Minkowski sum of unit triangles (planar for the whole family only in base 3), each H(d,3) has not one faithful realization but a (d-1)-parameter continuum, whose field climbs the constructibility hierarchy (ruler-and-compass, origami, and beyond); yet almost every realization is transcendental, in no number field, matching the exists-R hardness of unit-distance recognition. Combinatorial: beside the ordinary crossing number cr we introduce the unit-distance crossing number udcr(G), the fewest crossings over faithful unit drawings (every edge a unit segment); it is the rectilinear crossing number under unit length, so cr <= rcr <= udcr. We prove cr(H(d,3))=Theta(n^2) (one-page 7/6 n^2 above; spectral bisection Omega(n^2) below) and cr <= 2/3 n^2 via a two-page book layout; and udcr(H(3,3))=231 exactly, with udcr(H(d,3))=O(n^2 log n). A structure theorem makes every faithful planar realization a Minkowski sum, so the realization variety is an explicit (d-1)-parameter flex containing the udcr optimum; the matching udcr=Omega(n^2 log n) is the central open problem. The invariants differ: for cr the crossing-minimal drawings are structurally opaque, whereas the udcr optimum is itself a faithful Minkowski realization. All claims are verified in exact arithmetic with reproducible code and figures.

papers.title: Function spaces, web spaces, and Lawson-compactness in Domain Theory
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the structural properties of function spaces and their connections with Lawson-compactness and web spaces in domain theory. First, using finite-refinement and palette methods, we characterize the topological spaces $X$ for which the function space $[X\to L]$ is an RB-domain for every RB-domain $L$. In particular, we establish the equivalence between this preservation property and the condition that $X$ is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space. We further investigate its relationship with RW$^*$-spaces and obtain partial results concerning the Lawson-Mislove's problem. Second, we construct a countably based topological space $Z$ that is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space, but is neither a wide web space nor a C-space. More precisely, its lattice of open sets is a continuous frame satisfying $κ$-distributivity for every finite cardinal $κ\geq 2$, while failing to be $ω$-distributive. This provides a negative answer to a question raised by Erne and demonstrates that finite distributivity, even at every finite level, does not imply countable distributivity. Finally, by introducing labelled posets and employing constructions based on presheaves over finite sets and their element posets, we prove that every Lawson-compact domain is a Scott-continuous retract of a Lawson-compact algebraic domain, thereby answering a problem proposed by Kou. As applications, we show that the function space from an RB-domain to a Lawson-compact domain is Lawson-compact. Moreover, for an FS-domain $X$, we establish that $X$ is an RB-domain if and only if $[X\to L]$ is Lawson-compact for every Lawson-compact domain $L$. This characterization also yields the existence of an FS-domain $X$ and a Lawson-compact algebraic domain $L$ for which $[X\to L]$ is not continuous. This gives a negative answer to the question raised by Shen et al.

papers.title: Unifying Variational View of Accelerated Primal-Dual Methods
papers.abstract: We develop a unifying variational framework for accelerated primal-dual flows in affinely constrained convex optimization. In particular, it is shown that applying the Euler-Lagrange-Rayleigh (ELR) principle to coupled augmented Bregman Lagrangians systematically generates accelerated dynamics over general Bregman geometries and recovers a family of existing primal-dual mirror and Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) flows as special cases. We then establish $\mathcal{O}(e^{-b_t})$ convergence guarantees for these flows under mild assumptions. Lastly, we show that the proposed framework for algorithmic development extends from finite-dimensional optimization to constrained optimization over probability distributions.

papers.title: Non-uniqueness for the Complex Ginzburg-Landau Equation
papers.abstract: We show that singularities of the three-dimensional cubic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation developing from smooth initial data can induce non-uniqueness of solutions after the time of blowup. The solutions we study start as backward self-similar solutions, and the source of the non-uniqueness is an unstable eigenvalue of the linearization around the forward self-similar profile generated by the singularity. We establish the existence of this eigenvalue, and hence the non-uniqueness, by a computer-assisted proof for specific values of the parameters in the equation. The work is in part motivated by similarities to conjectured behavior for the Navier-Stokes equation, with which the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation shares several important properties, such as an energy inequality and the scaling symmetry.

papers.title: Adaptively Incorporating Directional Hints into Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: We study zeroth-order optimization of nonconvex functions with the aid of directional hints, which are cheap but potentially inaccurate approximations of the true gradient direction, given by linear subspaces at each iteration. To leverage these hints adaptively while maintaining robustness to their quality, we introduce Control-Variate Zeroth-Order Descent (CV-ZOD), a new framework that refines the classical zeroth-order gradient estimator with a control variate that can be set based on the directional hints. We first show that the oracle algorithm that optimally sets the reference vector and step size at each iteration achieves a convergence rate that interpolates between the first-order $O(1/T)$ rate and the zeroth-order $O(d/T)$ rate, depending on the quality of the hints along the trajectory. We then develop a practical variant of CV-ZOD that achieves the same oracle guarantee up to logarithmic factors, without any prior knowledge of the hint quality. We validate the method empirically on simulation-based scientific optimization tasks, demonstrating sustained progress on nonconvex landscapes where zeroth-order descent is slower and existing guided methods stall as guidance deteriorates.

papers.title: On a basepoint issue in the tempered dual of $p$-adic $SL(n)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of $G = \mathrm{SL}(n,F)$. Consider the action on the discrete series of $M$ of the group of unitary unramified characters of $M$ (where a character acts by twisting). Given an orbit $\mathcal{O}$ for that action, let $W_\mathcal{O}$ be the global stabilizer of $\mathcal{O}$ in the Weyl group of $M$. We construct families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ for which the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ has no fixed point. More precisely, let $n \geq 8$ be an integer that is not prime and not equal to $9$. We attach families of orbits without fixed points to any divisor $m \geq 2$ of $n$ such that $m \;| \; q-1$ where $q$ is the order of the residue field of $F$. The Levi subgroup $M \subset G$ for the corresponding families has $m$ blocks of size $k\geq 2$ and $2$ blocks of size $m$. The core of the paper is the construction of superculpidal representations of $\mathrm{GL}(m,F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(k,F)$ satisfying some conditions that we require to construct the families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ that we expects. In addition, we study the fixed point problem for the dimensions $n$ that we excluded above, i.e., prime or small dimensions. We prove that there is always a fixed point under the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ in those cases.

papers.title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
papers.abstract: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $q(β)$ depending on a parameter $β$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $β\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $q(β)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at inverse temperature $β$. In that case, the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (also known as unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of R{é}nyi $α$-entropies as $β\to\infty$.

papers.title: A SHARP MASS THRESHOLD FOR BOUNDEDNESS IN A CRITICAL QUASILINEAR CHEMOTAXIS MODEL WITH INDIRECT SIGNAL PRODUCTION: THE RADIALLY SYMMETRIC CASE
papers.abstract: A critical quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production in space dimensions higher than two is studied under radial symmetry. Exploiting the variational structure of the system, the existence of a sharp mass threshold M\textsubscr{c} > 0 is established: all solutions with mass below M\textsubscr{c} are global and bounded, while those with mass above M\textsubscr{c} and sufficiently negative energy are global but blow up in infinite time. Moreover, the value of the critical mass M\textsubscr{c} is related to the best constant of a variant of a Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.

papers.title: Orthogonal polynomials which are eigenfunctions of a partial differential operator
papers.abstract: We study orthogonal polynomials of $d = d_1+d_2$ variables with respect to a wrapped product weight function $\Wb(\bm x,\bm y) = W_1(\bm x/ρ(\bm y)) W_2(\bm y)$ for $(\bm x, \bm y) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1} \times \mathbb{R}^{d_2}$, where $ρ$ is either linear or the square root of a nonnegative quadratic polynomial, and identify all such polynomials that are eigenfunctions of a second-order linear differential operator. For $d =2$, it is known that there are primarily, up to affine transformations, five families of such polynomials, which are products or wrapped products of classical orthogonal polynomials of one variable; all five families have their counterparts in higher dimensions, but no characterization is known in dimension three or higher. Our study explores viable wrapped product families, finds explicit second-order differential operators for two new families of orthogonal polynomials in $d= d_1+d_2$ variables that have not been studied before when either $d_1>1$ or $d_2 > 1$, and provides, in particular, a complete list of such operators among all wrapped product orthogonal polynomials when $d = 3$. The list also includes four families that are eigenfunctions of a fourth-order differential operator, whereas no second-order operator is available. Moreover, orthogonal polynomials on the corresponding wrapped quadratic surfaces that are eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator on the surface are also studied.

papers.title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamical systems for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose accelerated inertial primal-dual dynamics for convex optimization problems with nonlinear convex inequality constraints. The proposed dynamics combine Nesterov accelerated vanishing damping $α/t$, a projected augmented-Lagrangian multiplier, and tangent extrapolation of the constraint mapping. Without assuming strong convexity, we establish global well-posedness and simultaneous $\mathcal O(t^{-2})$ decay rates for the constraint violation and the objective residual when $α\geq3$ and the extrapolation parameter satisfies a suitable compatibility condition. Under stricter parameter conditions, with $α>3$, we further prove that the primal-dual trajectory converges to a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker pair, both residuals decay as $o(t^{-2})$. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Uncomputable trisection invariants of 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that two invariants of smooth 4-manifolds defined in terms of trisections are uncomputable: the trisection genus and the Kirby-Thompson L-invariant. That is, there does not exist an algorithm that takes as input a triangulated closed orientable 4-manifold and outputs one of these quantities. The result on the L-invariant resolves the second part of Problem 4.116 in the K3 problem list. In the same spirit, we show that the PL multisection genus of PL manifolds is uncomputable in dimensions at least four.

papers.title: The Higher-Dimensional Nitsche Conjecture: Sharp Bounds and Rigidity
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge3$ and let $h:\A(r,1)\to\A(R,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an onto homeomorphism with harmonic coordinate functions. We prove the sharp Nitsche bound \[ R\le R_{n,+}(r):=\frac{nr}{n-1+r^n}, \] and, when $h$ interchanges the two ends, the strictly stronger sharp bound \[ R\le R_{n,-}(r):=\frac{nr^{n-1}}{1+(n-1)r^n}. \] In each case, equality holds only for the corresponding radial harmonic homeomorphism, up to an orthogonal transformation. Both bounds and their equality cases extend to bounded harmonic maps in every dimension $n\ge2$. This requires nonzero degree of $h/|h|$ on interior spheres, $|h|\ge R$, and the corresponding $L^2$ limits of the modulus at the two ends. In the plane, we also prove the nonzero-winding-number conjecture of Iwaniec--Kovalev--Onninen [\emph{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{24} (2011), 345--373], without endpoint modulus conditions. We prove a sharp $L^1$ contraction theorem for vector measures associated with spherical couplings. The first marginal is uniform, while the second is unrestricted. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing zonal kernels, the optimal constant is the degree-one multiplier.
