papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=η^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $η\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $η^{q^n}=-η$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $δ=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-δ)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $δ=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.

papers.title: Regularity and Asymptotic Radial Symmetry of Solutions to Mixed Local-Nonlocal Parabolic Equations
papers.abstract: We study the regularity and the long-time asymptotics of the solution to the following mixed local-nonlocal parabolic problem \[ \left\{ \begin{alignedat}{2} \partial_t u - Δu + (-Δ)^s u &= f \qquad &&\text{in }Ω\times(0, T), u&=0 \qquad &&\text{in }\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminusΩ\bigr)\times[0, T), u(\,\cdot\,,0)&=u_{0} \qquad &&\text{in }Ω, \end{alignedat} \right. \] where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded domain, $s\in(0,1)$ and $(-Δ)^s$ denotes the fractional Laplacian. We first develop the well-posedness theory for the problem on finite time intervals ($0<T<+\infty$). Existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established in the natural energy space, followed by interior $H^{2,1}$-regularity and global $L^\infty$-bounds. Then, under the restriction $s\in(0,1/2)$ and $0<α\le 1-2s$, we prove that weak solutions become classical ones, obtaining $C^{2+α,1+α/2}$-regularity up to the boundary via the method of continuity and a perturbation argument. The accompanying a priori estimate guarantees that these classical solutions can be extended globally in time, thereby allowing us to consider the parabolic problem on the whole half-line ($T=+\infty$). Finally, for the special case $Ω=B_1(0)$ and $f=0$, we employ the moving-plane method together with the previously established boundary regularity to show that every positive classical solution is attracted, as $t\to +\infty$, by a steady state that is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing.

papers.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

papers.title: Critical radial Green potential heat flow: A tension-controlled residue and a two-bubble example
papers.abstract: We compare two heat flows for the same corotational map of a disk into a warped product of two spheres, with the same fixed boundary values. The ordinary harmonic map heat flow develops a singularity in finite time. When the domain metric is instead determined by the critically normalized Green potential of the current energy distribution, the solution exists for all time. Two harmonic spheres of energy $4π$ form at separated scales, in addition to a nonconstant harmonic root. The energy and the image diameter of the necks tend to zero without restriction to a sequence of times. The main estimate controls the difference between the inner source mass and its critical value by the weighted tension. This is necessary because that difference is integrated over a neck of unbounded logarithmic length. Along a sequence of times the Green metric on the middle neck is asymptotically cylindrical after a spatially constant normalization.

papers.title: Fingerprints of feedback cycles in stationary diffusions
papers.abstract: When does the stationary density of a $d$-dimensional diffusion process driven by standard Brownian motion uniquely determine its drift? In general, it does not: the $d$ drift components enter the stationary Fokker-Planck equation only through a single scalar divergence. We consider drifts whose component functions only depend on a subset of their input variables, and encode this dependence with a directed graph. We exclude 2-cycles, which admit rotations that leave the stationary density invariant, but otherwise allow arbitrary graphs, including those with feedback cycles. We show that if the stationary density is sufficiently $s$-concave, e.g., strictly log-concave, then the drift is uniquely determined among graph-structured drifts in a weighted Sobolev space. For drifts with linear self-regulation, a single locally strictly convex level set of the stationary density is sufficient to identify the drift in the region it encloses. Both results follow from Raychaudhuri equations. Excluding 2-cycles allows treating nontrivial rotational and symmetric terms simultaneously, extending the scope of the corresponding Bochner- and Reilly-type arguments. We illustrate the results by recovering the Hill-type regulation of a stochastic genetic repressilator from samples of its stationary distribution.

papers.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
papers.abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.

papers.title: Tail behaviour of infimum of Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: We investigate the upper tail of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$, where $X$ is a centred Gaussian process (GP) with continuous sample paths on a nonempty compact metric space $\mathcal T$. As suggested by the findings of [1], the exponential rate is governed by an optimal-measure problem, while the exact prefactor depends on the local geometry of the corresponding contact set. In the full-contact regime, we strengthen the known Gumbel max-domain of attraction property of the distribution of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$ by establishing the von Mises condition. For fractional Brownian motion on $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, with Hurst index $H\in(0,1/2)$, we also determine the order of the logarithmic correction to the leading Gaussian exponential. For finite contact sets, we distinguish dominated, smooth-critical, and rough-critical regimes and derive exact asymptotics of $P\{\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)>u\}$ as $u\to\infty$ under suitable local assumptions. We illustrate our findings with examples including fractional Brownian motion and the fractional Brownian sheet.

papers.title: Optimal Batching with Abandonment: Threshold Policies Under Risk-Neutral and Risk-Sensitive Criteria
papers.abstract: We study optimal batching in a discrete-time Markovian system with Bernoulli arrivals and independent item abandonment. Each batch earns a per-item processing reward and incurs holding, abandonment, and fixed stopping costs. We formulate the batching decision as an optimal stopping problem and characterize optimal threshold policies under risk-neutral, risk-seeking, and risk-averse criteria. Under risk neutrality and the entropic risk-seeking criterion, the value function admits a forward-recursion representation, and the resulting reduced objectives are strictly unimodal. In the risk-seeking case, the objective is strictly discretely concave, yielding an explicit marginal-cost condition. For risk aversion, the unregularized entropic continuation branch may diverge, precluding standard fixed-point arguments. We therefore study a regularized robust surrogate formulated as a minimax problem with a relative-entropy penalty and capped likelihood ratio. We establish the existence of an optimal threshold policy and derive an explicit truncated-Gibbs worst-case distribution. We also study repeated batch clearing under both the long-run average and discounted criteria, for which the threshold objectives remain strictly unimodal. Numerical experiments examine threshold sensitivity to system parameters, costs, and risk preferences.

papers.title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
papers.abstract: We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$. Our results rely on a natural connection between chromatic resilience to edge removal and improper graph colouring. This work provides counterpoint to the work of Sudakov and Vu (2008) and Alon and Sudakov (2010), which treated chromatic resilience for $G_{n,p}$ subject to the addition, rather than removal, of edges.

papers.title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Hessian-Driven Nesterov Acceleration with Adam-Style Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Stochastic first-order methods use sampled gradients to reduce per-iteration costs, but estimation errors can slow convergence and, in some settings, cause divergence. To improve gradient accuracy while retaining acceleration, we develop scalar and diagonal versions of VR-Adam-SHANG for smooth stochastic convex optimization. The methods combine STORM-type recursive estimation, Adam-style preconditioning, and SHANG's accelerated interpolation and correction, using at most two stochastic gradient evaluations per iteration without full-gradient refreshes. Under unbiased sampling, bounded variance, and mean-square smoothness of gradient noise, polynomial steps with prescribed initialization yield $O(1/K)$ mean-square gradient-estimation error and expected objective-gap bounds combining $O(1/K^2)$ initial-energy decay with an $O(1/\sqrt K)$ stochastic term after $K$ iterations. These guarantees require neither monotonicity of the preconditioner nor a uniform positive lower bound on its eigenvalues. The analysis also establishes polynomial-step convergence of projected nonrecursive Adam-SHANG-s, filling a gap in its original theory. Experiments compare the methods at matched sample-gradient budgets. In every tested setting, at least one of the two versions achieves the lowest mean terminal objective gap among all compared methods.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Stability of Weakly Asymmetric Burgers Vortices: A Circulation-Independent Asymmetry Threshold and Optimal Decay
papers.abstract: Burgers vortices are stationary solutions of the Navier--Stokes equations in a background straining flow and serve as a model for vortex tubes in three-dimensional turbulence. In this paper, we consider weakly asymmetric strains and establish the local nonlinear asymptotic stability of the corresponding Burgers vortices against small three-dimensional perturbations for arbitrary circulation. Our proof exploits the specific axial structure of the linearized operator, combining a two-dimensional resolvent analysis with decay estimates for axial derivatives to control the full three-dimensional evolution. A first-moment decomposition isolates the slow modes, and Gaussian resolvent bounds are transferred to polynomially weighted spaces. This yields nonlinear stability with the endpoint exponential decay rate $(1-λ)/2$, where $λ$ denotes the strain asymmetry, without any additional polynomial factor in time. An exact nonlinear first-moment law demonstrates that this rate is optimal over the full admissible perturbation class, including at zero circulation.

papers.title: Onsager--Machlup Theory and Transition Pathways for Degenerate Stochastic Systems with Multiplicative Noise
papers.abstract: Noise-induced transitions between metastable states are central to many nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems, and most probable transition pathways provide an effective means of revealing the underlying transition mechanisms. In this work, we develop an Onsager--Machlup framework for degenerate stochastic dynamical systems driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise. We first derive the Onsager--Machlup action functional for the additive-noise case using the Girsanov transformation, and then extend the result to multiplicative noise through a Lamperti-type transformation. The resulting functional provides a variational characterization of the most probable transition pathway, from which we derive the associated Hamilton--Pontryagin boundary value problem. We further recast the variational problem as an equivalent optimal control problem and propose a neural-network-based numerical method for computing the most probable transition pathways. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed computational approach.

papers.title: The geometry of anisotropic propagation for multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats: A zero-sum stopping game approach
papers.abstract: We study the propagation geometry of multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats. Using geometric optics techniques and viscosity solution theory, we prove that the associated rate functions converge locally uniformly to the unique viscosity solution of a variational inequality with singular initial data. We identify this limit as the value of a zero-sum stopping game whose zero set determines the Wulff shape. This zero set coincides with that of the positive part of the value function of an unconstrained optimal control problem if and only if Freidlin's condition holds. When Freidlin's condition fails, we derive a pointwise characterization of the stopping-game zero set, yielding a convex hull representation. These results then yield explicit Wulff shapes and directional spreading speeds for all habitat speed. As the habitat speed increases, the Wulff shape evolves from a large ball to a truncated ball. It then develops conical, cylindrical, and paraboloidal boundary components attached to spherical parts, before eventually becoming a smaller ball. Some of these geometric transitions occur while both axial spreading speeds remain unchanged. Moreover, by characterizing the optimal trajectories, we distinguish two mechanisms of nonlocal speed selection and show that such selection can occur in oblique directions even when it is absent in both axial directions.

papers.title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: LLMs are powerful but incur substantial inference cost, which can be exploited by malicious users to induce overly long outputs, increasing latency and operational expense. Prior resource consumption attacks either coerce repetition or suppress the end-of-sequence token by lowering its logit value. However, with autoregressive, sampling-based generation, the search space grows exponentially with length and small deviations or unstable trajectories can derail optimization, limiting attack effectiveness and stability. To address this issue, we introduce Chatter Attack, a novel class of resource consumption attacks that optimize adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, thereby avoiding search-space explosion while still eliciting long responses. Specifically, Chatter Attack triggers self-doubt using short doubt-inducing phrases as the target, and sustains this state throughout generation via inference attention loss and global entropy loss. To extend to black-box settings, we further propose a novel Bayesian Prompt Optimization (BPO) method, which models the objective function globally by constructing a discrete token kernel, efficiently exploring the entire search space using prior information. Extensive experiments across multiple models and datasets show that our method outperforms baselines, with maximum response length increases to 31.5$\times$, and revealing practical resource-depletion risks for real-world LLM inference services.

papers.title: Support enumerators of two-row grids and comb posets
papers.abstract: We enumerate lattice points of preorder polytopes by support size for two-row Ferrers posets and recursively defined comb posets. For two-row posets, the order-ideal inequalities give a reflected-walk model in the nonnegative quadrant. Its transfer operators have a rank-one commutator, from which we derive an identity with five independent parameters. A matching-parameter specialization factors into the enumerators of a Motzkin excursion and a Motzkin bridge and proves the conjectured product of type~A and type~B Narayana polynomials for a two-row grid with its maximum removed. The general identity also records the two row supports separately. For combs, maximum ideal excess leads to a scalar recursion and a cubic generating function with independent spine and tooth weights. This proves a compositional-inverse conjecture of Athanasiadis and Chapoton and gives explicit $γ$-coefficients by Lagrange inversion. We prove $γ$-positivity for all two-row Ferrers cell posets and for the combs. The truncated-grid enumerators have simple negative zeros.

papers.title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
papers.abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

papers.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
papers.abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

papers.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
papers.abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

papers.title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
papers.abstract: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

papers.title: Stretched near-groups
papers.abstract: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$. In particular, the known existence of $C_{m^2}+m^2$ near-group categories for all positive integers $m$ implies the existence of Haagerup--Izumi fusion categories for all cyclic groups. As a further application, we provide a general conductor bound severely restricting the existence of stretched near-group categories, and for infinitely many abelian groups $G$ of square order, among them $C_4\times C_2^{2j}$ with $j\geq2$, we show that a near-group fusion category $G+k|G|$ exists if and only if $k=0$.

papers.title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
papers.abstract: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.

papers.title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
papers.abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

papers.title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
papers.abstract: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.

papers.title: On the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem for $k$-trees
papers.abstract: The famous Kőnig-Egerváry theorem is equivalent to the statement that a graph is bipartite if and only if the matching number equals the vertex cover number for every induced subgraph. Bessy, Ochem, and Rautenbach (J. Graph Theory 91 (2019) 73-87) generalized this theorem to $k$-paths by introducing the class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint paths of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such paths. They provided complete structural characterizations of graphs in $\mathcal{G}_k$ for $k \in \{3, 4\}$, and for odd $k$ when no cycle of order less than $k$ is present. Inspired by this nice work, we extend the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem to $k$-trees (i.e., trees with exactly $k$ vertices). We define the class $\mathcal{J}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint trees of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such trees, and provide complete structural descriptions of graphs in $\mathcal{J}_k$ for all $k \ge 3$.

papers.title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
papers.abstract: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible. In particular, when all classrooms have different sizes, the smallest possible size of the largest classroom is $d+\lceil (n-d-1)(n-d)/(2k)\rceil$ if $k<(n-d-1)/2$, and it is $n$ or $n+1$ otherwise. This extends the results of Siriseriwan and Sripatak, who studied the case $d=0$.

papers.title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schrödinger system
papers.abstract: We identify $p_*(n)=(n-1)/(n-3)$, $n\geq 5$, as the sharp exponent for Liouville theorems concerning a two-component elliptic Schrödinger system with self-focusing interactions and repulsive intercomponent coupling. We consider the strictly copositive regime, in which the repulsion strength is smaller than the geometric mean of the two self-interaction strengths. Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) established a Liouville-type nonexistence result in the range $1<p<p_*(n)$. For every $p_*(n)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct bounded, nontrivial, nonnegative entire solutions whenever the repulsion strength approaches the copositivity threshold from below. The construction combines a compact variational functional, a periodic spectral gap, and uniform exterior estimates that remove a truncation. Our result gives a negative answer to the open question posed by Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) of whether strict copositivity implies nonexistence of nontrivial nonnegative entire solutions throughout the Sobolev subcritical range when $n\geq 5$.

papers.title: Optimal Dividends and Voluntary Liquidation under Omega-Type Regulatory Termination
papers.abstract: We study a joint optimal dividend and voluntary liquidation problem for a company whose surplus follows a spectrally negative Lévy process and is subject to Omega-type regulatory termination. Dividend payments are modeled as a singular control, while voluntary liquidation is an optimal stopping decision with a state-dependent liquidation payoff. When the surplus falls below a regulatory solvency threshold, an Omega clock accumulates the time spent in distress and may terminate the firm before voluntary liquidation occurs. Under dynamic programming and continuity assumptions for an auxiliary Markov subproblem, we characterize its value as the smallest controlled stochastic supersolution of the associated quasi-variational inequality. We prove that any regular stochastic solution with a dividend barrier coincides with the value function over all admissible dividend and liquidation policies, and hence is unique within this class. Using $ω$-scale functions, we construct single-band, singleton, and no-liquidation candidates, establish sufficient conditions for global optimality, and give conditions under which these candidates supply the unique regular barrier stochastic solution. Brownian and Cramér--Lundberg examples illustrate how regulatory parameters affect dividend and liquidation boundaries and generate transitions between policy regimes.

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact Kähler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: Monotonicity of Wang's recursive sequence and logarithmically complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the inverse tangent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a sequence $b_n$, posed by Fei Wang, which is defined by $b_1=\frac13$ and a convolution-type recursive relation. We derive the generating functions of $nb_n$ and of $b_n$, the latter of which is $\ln\frac{\operatorname{arctanh}x}{x}$, and represent $b_n$ as a moment integral over $[0,1]$ with a positive density. From this representation we prove that the sequence $b_n$ is positive and logarithmically convex, that the sequence $nb_n$ is strictly decreasing, and that the ratio $\frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}$ is strictly increasing in $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with limit $1$, which answers Wang's problem. We also give a determinantal expression and closed-form formulas for $b_n$ involving Stirling numbers of the first kind and partial Bell polynomials. Finally, we prove that the function $\frac1{\arctan x}$ is logarithmically completely monotonic on $(0,\infty)$.

papers.title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

papers.title: Token graphs of stars
papers.abstract: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ has as vertices the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. Let $S_n$ be the star with $n$ leaves. Since every edge of $S_n$ is incident with the center, $F_k(S_n)$ is the inclusion graph of the $(k-1)$- and the $k$-subsets of the leaves. We use this identification to determine its diameter, radius, girth, Wiener index and number of spanning trees, and to decompose $F_k(S_{n+1})$ into $F_k(S_n)$ and $F_{k-1}(S_n)$ joined by a matching; the parameters of $F_k(S_n)$ that are already known, such as its connectivity, independence number, automorphism group and spectrum, are collected in an appendix. The two parameters that the identification does not settle are the domination and the packing numbers. For the domination number we prove, for fixed $k \ge 3$, that $(1-\frac{k-2}{k-1}π_k-o(1))\binom{n}{k-1} \le γ(F_k(S_n)) \le (1-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{k-2}{k-1})^{k-2}+o(1))\binom{n}{k-1}$, where $π_k$ is the Turan density of the complete $(k-1)$-uniform hypergraph on $k$ vertices; for $k=3$ both constants are equal to $\frac{3}{4}$, so that $γ(F_3(S_n))=(\frac{3}{4}+o(1))\binom{n}{2}$, and the upper bound takes the exact form $γ(F_3(S_n)) \le \binom{n}{2}-\lfloor (n+1)^2/8 \rfloor$, which is attained for all $3 \le n \le 10$. For $k=4$ we improve the upper bound to $(\frac{17}{27}+o(1))\binom{n}{3}$, which matches the lower bound if Turan's conjecture $π_4=\frac{5}{9}$ holds. We show that the packing number of $F_k(S_n)$ equals the maximum size $A(n+1,4,k)$ of a binary constant-weight code, and we characterize when the packing and the domination numbers coincide, namely, for $2 \le k \le n-1$, exactly when $n=2k-1$ and a Steiner system $S(k-2,k-1,2k-1)$ exists; in that case both parameters equal the Catalan number $C_k$.

papers.title: Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
papers.abstract: In this article, we study heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian-process surrogates, namely Student-$t$ processes, $α$-stable processes and Gaussian processes with heavy-tailed noise. These are Gaussian scale mixtures, and the position of the mixing variable decides whether the tails can be learned from a single realization. For process-level mixtures with a free amplitude, the profile likelihood of the mixing law is data-free and is maximized by the Gaussian law, the plug-in predictive is a data-free transformation of the Gaussian-process predictive, and no estimator can be consistent for the mixing law over the model along one path. For observation-level mixtures with symmetric $α$-stable noise, the tail index is identifiable. Further, for one-dimensional inputs under fixed-domain asymptotics with $α_0<2$ and compact hyperparameter sets, a cross-fitted plug-in estimator and the Laplace marginal-likelihood estimate computed at the global posterior mode attain the efficiency bound of the model with a known regression function, also for Matérn-$5/2$ sample paths. We also characterize small-sample failures of the Laplace approximation as folds of a posterior-mode branch and give a diagnostic. Finally, in a repeated Bayesian optimization study, observation-level tails reduced regret under gross outliers, as did Student-$t$ noise, and no degradation was detected under Gaussian noise.

papers.title: The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
papers.abstract: For integers $t\ge 2$ and $\ell\ge 3$, let $R^t_{t-1}(C_\ell)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $t$ colours contains a cycle of length $\ell$ whose edges use at most $t-1$ colours. Bucić and Khamseh determined the analogous number for paths and asked for its value for cycles. We answer this question for three colours: we show that $R^3_2(C_\ell)=\ell+\lfloor(\ell+1)/6\rfloor$ for every $\ell\ge 11$, and we determine the values for $3\le \ell\le 10$.

papers.title: Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish on $R^n\times R^m$ a Fefferman--Stein type distribution function inequality in which the nontangential maximal function of the product Poisson extension is controlled by the Lusin area integral function: \[ |\{N>λ\}|\le C\left(|\{A>λ\}|+λ^{-2}\int_{\{A\leλ\}}A^2\,dx\right). \] The central idea is to establish a local $L^2$ estimate for the radial maximal function. This yields a new proof of the corresponding one-parameter inequality, avoiding Green's formula and the treatment of sawtooth regions, and extends to the multiparameter setting.

papers.title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
papers.abstract: By a $\textit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $ν$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $ν(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $ν(x)=\bot$, where $\bot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{\bot,\top\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of these noetherian forms, and in fact, all noetherian forms of the category of groups.

papers.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

papers.title: A Multistage Extension of Witsenhausen's Counterexample with Linear Signaling
papers.abstract: We study a multistage scalar extension of Witsenhausen's counterexample in which controller 1 observes the initial state exactly, whereas every subsequent controller observes only a local noise-corrupted state and does not inherit its predecessors' observations, so that every nonterminal action both regulates the state and shapes the signal available to the next controller. Restricting the signaling controllers to linear policies while leaving the terminal controller unrestricted, we compute the exact value within this class and reduce the optimization to a deterministic dynamic program in a single propagated variance. The optimal intermediate gains are shown to have a shrinkage form, and the value functions of that program are concave. For two stages, the benchmark admits a closed form on a matching locus, where for small effort weights it has two distinct minimizers, and at the standard parameter instance on that locus a two-point nonlinear policy strictly improves upon it. For three stages, numerical continuation at a reference instance reveals three distinct local minima, and two values of the initial variance at which the lowest of the three changes abruptly. Under the terminal-cost normalization we further prove, for every finite horizon, that the optimal linear value becomes asymptotically equal to the signaling-idle benchmark as the initial variance tends to infinity.

papers.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
papers.abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Ampère equations with Hölder continuous right-hand sides
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Ampère equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<α<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^α$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,β}$ bounds for every fixed $0<β<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.

papers.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
papers.abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.

papers.title: A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
papers.abstract: We introduce self-module Lie bialgebras as a common framework for bialgebra structures associated with different types of Manin triples of Lie algebras. A self-module Lie algebra is a Lie algebra with a specified representation on its underlying vector space; equivalently, it is an NS-Lie algebra expressed in different notation. We define a generic Manin triple as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with a nondegenerate bilinear form and two complementary isotropic Lie subalgebras, and establish the equivalence among standard generic Manin triples, suitable matched pairs of Lie algebras, families of matched pairs of self-module Lie algebras and self-module Lie bialgebras. The framework recovers Lie, pre-Lie and anti-pre-Lie bialgebras as special cases and admits examples outside these three families. We also introduce the self-module Lie Yang-Baxter equation and show that its solutions yield self-module Lie bialgebras and admit the $\mathcal{O}$-operator characterization. Finally, we obtain solutions in semi-direct product self-module Lie algebras, including constructions arising from self-bimodule pre-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
papers.abstract: The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness. The loss of ordinary expansiveness removes homoclinic rigidity, so we introduce a proximal analogue of pre-injectivity. Our main result shows that, for a surjective action of an infinite countable cancellative left-amenable semigroup on a compact metric space, m-expansiveness plus weak specification forces every continuous equivariant map injective on each proximal set to be surjective. The proof uses entropy detection at a fixed scale, a strict entropy gap from weak specification, and finite multiplicity to produce proximal pairs from uniformly close points. We also give a one-dimensional variant under shadowing and examples clarifying the assumptions.

papers.title: An Arbitrary-Order Distributional Finite Element Method for the Curl--Dev Grad Stokes System
papers.abstract: We develop an arbitrary-order distributional finite element method for the three-dimensional curl--dev grad Stokes system governed by the Hessian complex. On tetrahedral meshes, the method couples degree-$(k+1)$ nonconforming symmetric-tensor virtual elements, degree-$k$ tangential-normal continuous traceless tensor elements, and Raviart--Thomas elements of index $k$, without additional virtual-element stabilization. Building on zero-extension curl--div theory, we derive a well-posed distributional saddle-point formulation with an $H(\operatorname{div})$ vector multiplier. A divergence-augmented discrete norm equivalence controls the full Raviart--Thomas space modulo translations and underpins mesh-uniform stability for each fixed $k\ge0$. We establish optimal $O(h^{k+1})$ energy error estimates and an optimal $O(h^{k+2})$ $L^2$ error estimate for the full symmetric-tensor approximation, under suitable regularity and load approximation assumptions. As an application, the method supplies the Stokes block of a decoupled triharmonic scheme with optimal Hessian error estimates. Numerical experiments support the predicted convergence rates for computable quantities.

papers.title: Data Center Power Flexibility Characterization: A DeepSets Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Data centers can provide power flexibility through the scheduling of computing workloads, cooling systems, and batteries. Characterizing this flexibility online is useful but challenging because of the complex coupling among these resources. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a role-conditioned cross-head DeepSets reinforcement learning approach to characterize the power flexibility interval of a data center at each time step. First, we formulate the flexibility characterization problem as a Markov decision process that jointly models the three resources under a carbon budget, with actions specifying the upper and lower endpoints of the power flexibility interval. We then design DeepSets actor and critic that represent delay-tolerant workloads as an unordered set, enabling the proposed approach to accommodate varying numbers of workloads with a fixed number of trainable parameters. Finally, because maximizing the width of the flexibility interval requires moving its endpoints in opposite directions, we develop a role-conditioned cross-head decoder that distinguishes their respective roles while keeping them coordinated. Case studies on the Google Cluster Data show that the proposed approach provides more than twice the daily flexibility of the standard soft actor-critic method with nearly zero carbon overshoot while using 87.7% fewer trainable parameters.

papers.title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
papers.abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_α C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(α)$ and letting $C_α=\langleα\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_α$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $α$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[α]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_θH$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
papers.abstract: We treat a symmetrized mixed-oscillator deformation family of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$, $N,n\geq1$, with even mixed coefficients $β_{u,i}$ and one odd square-zero parameter. We derive the deformed bracket from an oscillator realization, show that its coefficient is determined by the realization, and exhibit an explicit odd primitive, normalized by its vanishing on $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Every odd primitive differs from it by a unique inner derivation. For $N=1$ this is the case $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$ treated earlier. With multiple odd parameters the deformed bracket is the sum of the single-parameter deformations and is again trivial. The trivialization, however, is not additive: it is the product of the single-parameter trivializations followed by a nonsymplectic change of the bosonic generators. The main results are formalized in Lean~4, with the algebras constructed by generators and relations; what is not formalized is stated in the appendix.

papers.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schrödinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.

papers.title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
papers.abstract: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2πsx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.

papers.title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
papers.abstract: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent space has dimension at most two, then it is a formal power series ring in two variables. The nilpotence bound follows by conjugating level subgroups. To deduce the dimension bound, we replace the Fourier pairing in the classical nilpotence method with an inequality comparing the dimension of each finite-level generalized eigenspace with that of its Hecke eigenspace. We apply these results to modular curves and definite quaternion algebras.

papers.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
papers.abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.

papers.title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
papers.abstract: We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

papers.title: On-the-Fly Reduced Bases Through the Lens of Augmented Krylov Methods
papers.abstract: On-the-fly reduced order models (ROMs) are widely used in applications where multiple queries of large-scale models are required in an iterative method, like PDE-constrained optimization or fluid-structure interaction. When compared to classical offline--online ROMs, they have the advantage of being agnostic to any precomputed training data, mesh or geometry, which makes them more general linear/nonlinear solver accelerators. The main goal of this work is to study the effect of using a reduced basis constructed on-the-fly to accelerate a restarted Krylov algorithm, and to formally bridge this category of data-driven methods with classical augmented Krylov methods. The guiding principles of on-the-fly reduced basis will be translated into the framework of Krylov subspace methods, for a Petrov-Galerkin projection method. Previous corrections generated by the algorithm are stored in a snapshot matrix, and a singular value decomposition (SVD) is used to determine a reduced subspace containing the most significant directions. It will be shown that this approach can be embedded in the framework of Krylov methods with augmented or deflated restart, but with a different, data-driven recycling strategy. An analytical study will be presented to determine the consequences of augmentation by ROM-based vectors. Numerical experiments on a convection-diffusion problem with various degrees of convection will show that the proposed methodology yields results comparable to classical iterative linear solvers in some regimes, especially for nearly symmetric or skew-symmetric operators. At equal sizes of the augmentation basis, the convergence was sometimes faster with the proposed framework than with deflation methods.

papers.title: Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
papers.abstract: For even $t$ and an $n$-set $X$, an $(n,t)$-splitting system is a family ${\mathbb{B}} \subseteq 2^X$ with the property that for each subset $Y \in {X \choose t}$, there exists $B \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $|B \cap Y| = t/2$. The problem of interest is to determine the minimum size of such splitting systems. We show that any $(n,t)$-splitting system has size at least of order $t$, improving the previous lower bound of $\sqrt t$ while the best known upper bound is of order $t^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Optimal Polynomial-Query Approximation for Consistent Submodular Maximization with Short Lookahead
papers.abstract: Elements arrive one at a time, and after each arrival an algorithm holds a set of at most $k$ arrived elements. Its goal is a held set whose value under a monotone submodular function is close to the best value that $k$ arrived elements can achieve. The recourse of an update is the number of elements inserted into or removed from the held set, and we require it to be bounded independently of $k$ and of the number $n$ of arrivals. With evaluations only on sets of arrived elements and polynomially many of them, the best ratio a randomized algorithm can achieve is $2-\sqrt{2}\approx0.5858$. We show that seeing future arrivals raises the best ratio for polynomially many evaluations to $1-1/e\approx0.6321$, for deterministic and for randomized algorithms; no algorithm with polynomially many evaluations exceeds $1-1/e$, even when all elements are available at once. For every $\varepsilon>0$, a deterministic algorithm that sees the next $\lceil\varepsilon k/3\rceil$ arrivals keeps a set of value at least $1-1/e-\varepsilon$ times the optimum at every time, changes $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ elements per arrival and makes $(n+1)^{O(\varepsilon^{-2})}$ evaluations. With the whole arrival sequence known in advance, a deterministic algorithm attains the same ratio with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ changes per arrival. A randomized algorithm with the same short lookahead makes $O(n^2k)$ evaluations, changes $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ elements per arrival, and attains the same ratio in expectation at each fixed time. The main tool is a greedy algorithm with an explicit guarantee for each of its partial solutions combined with each initial segment of the known future arrivals. A second tool moves between two such solutions one element at a time while keeping the value high, and the deterministic algorithm times each move using upper bounds on the optimum from failed searches.

papers.title: The Escobar Constant for Two-dimensional Disks
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian surface homeomorphic to a closed disk, with boundary length $L$. We establish sharp upper bounds for its Escobar constant under upper bounds on the Gaussian curvature. If $K_g\leq 0$, then $I(M,g)\leq 2/π$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to a Euclidean disk. If $K_g\leqκ$ for some $κ>0$, $L<2π/\sqrtκ$, and $\operatorname{Area}_g(M)<2π/κ$, then $I(M,g)\leq\frac{4}{\sqrtκL}\arcsin(\frac{\sqrtκL}{2π})$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to the geodesic disk of the same perimeter contained in an open hemisphere of the sphere of constant curvature $κ$. We also discuss the higher order Escobar constant for planar domains. In particular, we construct counterexamples to Hassannezhad and Siffert's conjecture.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
papers.abstract: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

papers.title: On Size-Biased Distributions and the Chainability of Positive Infinitely Divisible Distributions
papers.abstract: Bar-Lev and Letac (2025) introduced the concept of chainability of infinitely divisible distributions on $\mathbb R$. In this note, we show that a simpler notion of chainability can be used for infinitely divisible distributions on $[0,\infty)$. We derive some properties and give a probabilistic interpretation in terms of so-called size-biased distributions. As an application, we discuss simulation from size-biased distributions associated with an important class of tempered stable distributions.

papers.title: Local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations in a bounded domain in two and three space dimensions. We establish the local exact controllability around a constant equilibrium state. Our proof relies on the observability and controllability analysis of a suitably reformulated linearized system, together with a fixed point argument in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main novelty of this paper is to overcome the structural difficulties arising from the divergence free constraint and the strong coupling between the fluid and magnetic variables. To accommodate the solenoidal constraint, we introduce a magnetic potential formulation and develop a mixed coordinate approach.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
papers.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hatβ$ we realize $π_1(S^3\setminus\hatβ)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

papers.title: Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM
papers.abstract: Sparse hierarchical nonlinear programming (SH-NLP) based on the $\ell_0$-norm provides a powerful framework for integrated, efficient hierarchical decision-making in robot kinematic control, for example in the presence of a large set of possible end-effector candidate locations. While Sequential Sparse Hierarchical Quadratic Programming (S-SHQP) with interior-point method based SHQP sub-problem solvers exploit the hierarchical, sparse structure of such problems, they are less amenable to effective warm-starting between subsequent, coherent control steps. In this work, we formulate an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to efficiently solve related SHQP sub-problems. We introduce efficient substitutions for auxiliary variables representing $\ell_0$-norm surrogates. The solver efficiently handles separable decision functions by evaluating linear algebra expressions in the appropriate order. Results in large-scale kinematic and dynamic control show reduced computation times of up to 23.5% compared with a structure-exploiting interior-point method in low- to moderate-accuracy regimes. Furthermore, hierarchical decision-making is extended to whole-body dynamic control for humanoid walking, where the need for high-accuracy solutions is highlighted.

papers.title: Dual Model Predictive Control through Sampling-Based Belief Propagation
papers.abstract: We propose a sampling-based dual model predictive control (MPC) approach that combines belief propagation with parameterized feedback policy optimization. By sampling uncertain dynamics and process noise, we approximate the evolution of the hyperstate over the prediction horizon, allowing future control decisions to adapt to anticipated observations and belief updates. This enables the controller to account for the future value of information without explicit exploration incentives. We establish almost-sure uniform convergence of the sample-average objective to the finite-horizon expected objective over a compact policy class. The approach is specialized to Bayesian linear regression and evaluated on stochastic systems with constant and time-varying uncertain dynamics. We compare our approach to certainty equivalent control, and an MPC that optimizes over open-loop control sequences rather than feedback policies, demonstrating the benefits of our method in terms of both control performance and information gain.

papers.title: A seven-element interval of power-semiring varieties
papers.abstract: We determine the interval between the varieties generated by the nonempty and full power semirings of a semigroup satisfying \(xy\approx x^2\). It has two elements for a one-element semigroup, three for a nontrivial left-zero or null semigroup, and seven otherwise, without any finiteness assumption. In the seven-element case the interval is \([\Rvar,\Rvar^0]\), where \(\Rvar=\Mod_{\rm ai}\{xy\approx xz\}\) and \(\Rvar^0\) is its zero-adjunction variety. Every word absorption valid in \(\Rvar\) but not in \(\Rvar^0\) is equivalent over \(\Rvar^0\) to one of six relative identities. We give exact absorption criteria and finite bases for all seven varieties. Three have basis rank two and four have basis rank three; their two-generated free algebras have orders \(15\), \(24\), or \(35\). We also count the finite-rank free algebras of both endpoints.

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Line-Search Quasi-Newton Method for Discounted Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a line-search quasi-Newton (LSQN) method for discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs). The method maintains an inverse model to approximate the inverse of the current policy Jacobian and refines it through an inner learning procedure that preserves existing secant conditions and achieves the prescribed accuracy in at most $n$ queries in exact arithmetic for an MDP with $n$ states, even when the initial inverse model is singular. A sign-based direction correction combined with an Armijo line search ensures monotonic decrease of the Bellman residual norm across policy changes without requiring a value-iteration fallback. We prove global Q-linear residual convergence and local Q-superlinear convergence of the value iterates from arbitrary finite initial value vectors and inverse models, without requiring a unique optimal policy. Numerical experiments show competitive performance against nine baselines, while public benchmarks demonstrate that the inner learning procedure typically requires far fewer than $n$ learning queries.

papers.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
papers.abstract: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

papers.title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
papers.abstract: The full strong Fourier extension estimate for the unit sphere is established in every ambient dimension at least three. The finite Knapp boundary is obtained by combining a uniform diagonal estimate on rescaled spherical graphs with a transverse product bound. A Whitney decomposition and a dyadic dual pairing yield strong type at the exact scaling exponents. The critical local estimate and the strict mixed range come from the recent work on Euclidean local smoothing.

papers.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
papers.abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

papers.title: Almost sharp global well-posedness and low-regularity blow-up for the two-dimensional periodic Zakharov system
papers.abstract: We study the Zakharov system on an arbitrary fixed rectangular two-dimensional torus with initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$. For the Schrödinger regularity $s$, Kishimoto proved local well-posedness for $1/2\leq s\leq1$ and global well-posedness for $9/14<s<1$ below the Euclidean cubic ground-state mass. Under the same mass condition, we prove global well-posedness for every $1/2<s<1$, with polynomial bounds for the Sobolev norms. We add quartic and quintic corrections to Kishimoto's resonantly modified energy. The main difficulty is to cancel the interactions obstructing the global iteration without introducing singular coefficients near resonance or losing control of the higher-order terms generated by differentiation. The coefficients exploit cancellations between successive nonlinear interactions. Away from resonance, they cancel the problematic terms; near resonance, algebraic rearrangements avoid division by small phases and preserve sufficient frequency decay. For every $s<1/2$, we also construct solutions with arbitrarily small initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$ whose wave component blows up in finite time while the Schrödinger component remains bounded in $H^s$. We combine explicit approximate solutions supported on three Fourier modes with stability at $H^{1/2}\times L^2$. Choosing successively larger frequencies controls the nonlinear interactions among infinitely many approximate solutions and makes the accumulated errors summable, while their wave amplitudes produce blow-up. These results identify $s=1/2$ as the threshold between global well-posedness and the existence of such blow-up solutions, with the endpoint unresolved.

papers.title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
papers.abstract: We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

papers.title: Jacobi fields and Jacobi sections for semisprays on Lie algebroids: transverse variations and equivalences
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields associated with semisprays on Lie algebroids. First, we characterize compatible transverse variations in terms of Lie algebroid morphisms. This characterization leads to a variational description of Jacobi sections: a section along an integral curve of a semispray is a Jacobi section if and only if it arises as the infinitesimal variation of a compatible transverse variation of a dynamical variation satisfying a suitable condition on its image in the base. We also investigate the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields through the anchor map. We prove that every Jacobi section projects to a Jacobi field, and establish a converse when the corresponding base variation is contained in a single leaf of the characteristic foliation.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

papers.title: Linear bounds and sharp exponential growth for commuting matrix algebra
papers.abstract: For any $m$ pairwise commuting matrices $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{m}\subset \M_n(\F)$, we prove $\dim_\F \F[A_1,\cdots, A_m]\leq (2^m-1)(n-1)+1$, answering Bergman's question on the existence of a linear bound for a fixed number $m$.

papers.title: Minimum-Time Interceptor Selection and Obstacle-Avoiding Path Planning for Heterogeneous UAVs
papers.abstract: Selecting the most suitable unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to intercept a moving target is challenging when multiple vehicles have different speeds, initial headings, turning capabilities and launch delays, particularly in environments containing obstacles. This paper develops a computationally efficient framework that integrates minimum-time interceptor selection with obstacle-avoiding path planning for heterogeneous UAVs. The interception problem for each UAV is formulated as a minimum-time optimal control problem and solved numerically using an arc-parameterised nonlinear programming model based on Dubins-type paths. The candidate trajectories consist of minimum-radius circular arcs, straight-line segments and tangential obstacle-boundary arcs, with exact geometric distance constraints imposed to ensure obstacle avoidance along the entire path. To improve computational efficiency, a closed-form lower bound on interception time is incorporated into a bound-and-select algorithm that eliminates UAVs unable to improve the best verified feasible interception time. The proposed pruning strategy preserves the best computed interception decision obtained through full enumeration while reducing computational effort. Numerical experiments investigate the effects of target speed, UAV turning radius, launch delay and obstacle configuration. Across 20 randomly generated scenarios involving up to eight UAVs, the proposed approach reduces average computational time by approximately 85$\%$ for eight-vehicle teams without changing the selected interceptor or its computed interception time. The proposed approach provides an efficient method for selecting a single UAV and generating feasible Dubins-type interception trajectories in obstacle-constrained environments.

papers.title: Technical Report: Partially Asynchronous Distributed Optimization on Riemannian Manifolds
