papers.abstract: There is a large body of work on distributed optimization for problems in Euclidean space. However, many existing algorithms and analyses do not directly transfer to problems defined on manifolds. Therefore, in this paper we propose a distributed asynchronous optimization algorithm for problems on Riemannian manifolds. The algorithm we develop is a parallelized form of Riemannian block coordinate descent in which all agents can compute and communicate asynchronously. We assume only "partial asynchrony", namely that all delays in computations and communications obey some finite bound, and we omit the common assumptions of convexity of the objective and compactness of the manifold. Under mild conditions, we prove that agents' iterates drive the Riemannian gradient of the objective to zero, and we derive a rate of convergence for the norm of the gradient. In simulations, we compare to a synchronous baseline algorithm under varying communication delays and numbers of agents. In example problems, we empirically show that our algorithm converges up to 8.5 times faster and attains up to 24 times lower suboptimality over a finite horizon.

papers.title: The Logic of Emergence
papers.abstract: ``Emergence'' refers to the fact that different mathematical languages and theories seem to be required to describe scientific theories that operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Highly circumscribed, special cases of emergence have been investigated using many different formal tools, including coarse-graining (over space and / or time), renormalization, dimension reduction, broken symmetry, and various formulations of causality. Here we extend the mathematics of model theory to unify and extend these earlier investigations. As a preliminary application of our framework, we investigate canonical examples of emergence, including the emergence of genetics from chemistry, of psychology from neurobiology, and of different forms of collective behavior from the laws governing their constituent parts. By exploiting the power of model theory we also uncover many aspects of emergence that were previously obscured. In particular, we uncover some of the rich hierarchical structure that relates different scientific fields. For example, we show that scientific fields can be related via a collection of multiple partial orders, all defined over the same set. On the other hand, under an alternative relation among scientific fields, one which allows cycles, we show that it is possible that the set of all of scientific fields must collapse into a single scientific field. Going forward, these investigations point to the formal tools that might need to be developed in order to arrive at a deeper understanding of this emergent hierarchy of scientific reality.

papers.title: A weak Galerkin finite element method for the coupled Stokes-Biot problem
papers.abstract: In this paper,we consider a stable numerical method for the Stokes-Biot model. We adopt the standard formulation of the Stokes equations coupled with the mixed formulation of the Biot system involving the additional total pressure variable. We construct the semi-discrete scheme on polygonal meshes by employing weak Galerkin finite element methods for spatial discretization. It is convenient to incorporate the interface conditions into the semi-discrete scheme via the edge-based degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we give a fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler method. We establish the well-posedness of these two schemes and provide a rigorous error analysis. Finally, we present some numerical examples to verify the convergence and stability of our algorithm under a wide range of some physical parameters.

papers.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
papers.abstract: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

papers.title: The critical Cauchy boundary for Gibbs partitions
papers.abstract: We study critical Gibbs partitions whose component law is in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive stable law of index one. In the dense phase, we prove a local limit theorem for the number of components and functional limits for their sizes. We also describe convergent and divergent condensation regimes, and a phase transition at a boundary in which the dense and condensation contributions compete.

papers.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erdős--Sós $(9,6)$-problem
papers.abstract: For integers $e\ge3$, let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. The lower-bound part of a longstanding conjecture of Erdős, Frankl, and Rödl from 1986 asserts that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, resolving the first open case not covered by the classical construction of Ruzsa and Szemerédi in 1976, which established $f_3(n,6,3)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$. We also establish near-quadratic lower bounds for $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ with $e=9,10,11$. We further extend the result for $e=6$ to every fixed uniformity $r\ge4$.

papers.title: Automaticity of structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions
papers.abstract: We study structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions, building on arXiv:2604.12637 and providing its technical supplement. We develop an automata-based framework to characterize their occurrence and derive verifiable combinatorial criteria. We also introduce simplifications for the construction and analysis of these automata, including tensor-product decompositions, that clarify the mechanisms underlying structural defects and their emergence.

papers.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. I
papers.abstract: Let $λ$ be the Liouville function. We prove Let $λ$ be the Liouville function. We prove \[ \mathcal{I}_λ(X)=\int_{\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{1\leqslant n\leqslant X}λ\left(n\right)\mathrm{e}\left(nα\right)\right| \mathrm{d}α \gg X^{\frac{1}{4}}. \] This removes the $X^\varepsilon$ loss in the previous result of Pandey and Radziwiłł~\cite{PandeyRadziwill2026}. In the second paper in this series, we will prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log \mathcal{I}_λ(X)} {\log X} \geqslant\frac{1}{3}. \]

papers.title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
papers.abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm. We propose Kernelized Stable Fluids with Sparse Cholesky Preconditioning (KSF-Chol) in order to address this shortcoming and make the algorithm thereby suitable for engineering problems and scientific computing. The algorithm is modified by replacing the linear interpolation approach with kernel interpolation in the advection step. We accelerate the computationally expensive kernel interpolation by using sparse Cholesky preconditioning and a near-/far-field approach and optimize both methods for computations on a uniform Cartesian grid. KSF-Chol achieves per time step a near-linear computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log^d(N/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{chol}}))$ in space and time. We test KSF-Chol against reference solvers and numerical reference data on multiple 2D and 3D benchmarks and demonstrate a significantly reduced numerical diffusion as well as a competitive accuracy concerning the computation of relevant flow quantities.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
papers.abstract: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 137 (2019) 112--117] asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every positive integer $m$. We show that, for all integers $k\ge3$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$ satisfying $m>8t+ε$, where $ε\in\{0,1\}$ and $m\equivε\pmod2$, there is a graph with chromatic number and choice number both equal to $k$ that is not $(km+t:m)$-choosable. This answers their question negatively for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge10$. In particular, our construction yields a $3$-choosable graph on $91$ vertices that is not $(6:2)$-choosable, answering a question of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni [Adv. Comb. (2019), Paper No.~5]. More generally, for every fixed $b\ge1$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$, we construct an $(a:b)$-choosable graph that is not $(am+t:bm)$-choosable for all sufficiently large $a$, with an explicit bound on $a$. Let $F(a,b)$ be the supremum of the strong fractional choice numbers of $(a:b)$-choosable graphs. We prove that for every fixed $b\ge1$, $F(a,b)-\frac ab$ tends to infinity as $a\to\infty$.

papers.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
papers.abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions as well as Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.

papers.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gröbli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

papers.title: Exchange graphs and $τ$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the connected components of support $τ$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected precisely when the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules and has Cartan rank one. There are then exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero $τ$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra is connected. Suppose the defining partial tagged triangulation is nonempty and all its endpoints are punctures. Then the realization of the support $τ$-tilting complex is homotopy equivalent to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Signed endpoint vectors give an explicit homotopy equivalence. Under the same endpoint hypothesis, $τ$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates and give a surface criterion distinguishing the root sets of types $A$, $D$ and $C$. The homotopy construction also applies to Brauer graph algebras with arbitrary vertex multiplicities.

papers.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
papers.abstract: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, Škrekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. We also show that the $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$ list-size bound is best possible for graphs with maximum average degree arbitrarily close to $8/3$ from below. As an immediate consequence, our theorem implies that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.

papers.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
papers.abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.

papers.title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
papers.abstract: Collision-free motion planning for multi-agent robotic systems remains an active research area because of the complexity of coordinating robot trajectories, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. Importantly, the analytical difficulty of nonconvex collision-avoidance constraints has so far driven the development of exclusively numerical methods. We derive a complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots with zero initial and final velocities, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective. We prove that these trajectories belong to eight distinct contact families and determine which family applies for each configuration of initial and final positions. We analyze the geometrical properties of the optimal trajectories and provide a numerical algorithm for computing them. These insights have already been adopted to improve the performance of numerical methods for multi-agent motion planning by several orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Local $Tb$ theorems with applications to the Neumann problem and caloric measure
papers.abstract: We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calderón-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. We obtain the following applications: - If $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq 2$, is a bounded domain with Ahlfors regular boundary satisfying the interior corkscrew condition, and the Neumann problem for the Laplacian in $Ω$ is solvable with data in $L^p$ for some $1<p<\infty$, then $\partialΩ$ is uniformly rectifiable. The proof applies the matrix-valued version of the theorem to the Cauchy-Clifford operator. - In the parabolic space $\mathbb{P}^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(σ)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $σ$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

papers.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Functor of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
papers.abstract: We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups to give the explicit formula for products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Besides the computation, We also develop a theory that reconstructs a genuine equivariant spectrum as the homotopy limit of a finite diagram of homotopy fixed-point spectra, Tate spectra, and only one localization spectrum at the terminal of the diagram. We call it the Tate compression theory. From it we also give a filtration for $π_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

papers.title: Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for Efficient Stationary Tail Computation in High-Dimensional Reflected Brownian Motions
papers.abstract: Stationary tail computation for high-dimensional reflected Brownian motions (RBMs) remains computationally challenging. Building on NN4MGF's shared-coordinate basic-adjoint-relationship (BAR) framework, we develop Holomorphic Cauchy Networks (HCNs). Native complex-valued rational Cauchy subnetworks enforce holomorphicity on pole-free domains, removing sampled Cauchy-Riemann penalties and their input-derivative graphs. Exact origin anchoring and boundary-coordinate exclusion enforce structural identities, while anchored interactions represent dependent transforms. Under holomorphic-log assumptions, we establish simultaneous value and first-derivative approximation for the constrained architectures and a mixed-derivative lower bound for coordinate-only representations under nonzero cross-covariance. Closed-form real-axis derivatives and sequential backpropagation further control memory. On the same NVIDIA H100 NVL, the tested 30D HCN configuration uses approximately tenfold less peak allocated memory and has 9.7-fold lower mean update time than NN4MGF; extrapolation to the respective scheduled update counts gives a projected full-schedule update-time ratio of 58.2. With 64 million sampled base inputs per high-dimensional run, HCN reaches 50 dimensions on a laptop GPU with 6.367% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8. Degree-matched comparisons yield lower reported mean relative errors over the primary evaluation ranges, including 1.422% versus 6.684% on the 2D Harrison non-product benchmark. On a 10D correlated RBM benchmark, HCN achieves 3.829% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8 against a simulation reference, compared with 19.386% for an independent-marginal baseline.

papers.title: The Separated Orlicz Bump Theorem in $L^2$
papers.abstract: We prove a separated entropy bump theorem for two-weight $L^2$ inequalities for positive operators defined by Carleson sequences on a probability space with a general filtration. The bump conditions use conditional averages of martingale maximal functions and involve the first power of the entropy penalty, removing the square appearing in the separated condition of Treil and Volberg. As a consequence, we obtain separated Orlicz bump estimates for a class of doubling Young functions. The final section describes a direct Orlicz argument that removes the doubling assumption and the monotonicity assumption on $\frac{Φ(t)}{t\log t}$, and discusses extensions to other exponents. These results apply, in particular, to sparse operators. The proof uses principal sequences, a natural global extension of principal sets, and combines a good-$λ$ estimate with a weighted Carleson embedding to obtain the required testing inequalities.

papers.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
papers.abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.

papers.title: Sharp enumeration and growth of admissible sets of integers
papers.abstract: A set of positive integers is admissible if equal sums of finite subsets always have equal numbers of summands. Let $a(N)$ count the nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and let $b(N)$ count those with maximum $N$. We prove $\log a(N)\sim\log b(N)\simπ\sqrt{2N/3}$, establishing the sharp logarithmic asymptotic proposed by Nicolas. More generally, let $Q_h(N)$ count the subsets for which each integer has subset-sum representations of at most $h$ distinct cardinalities. Uniformly for all positive integers $h,N$, we prove $\log Q_h(N)\asymp\min\{N,\sqrt{hN}\}$ with absolute implied constants. Every infinite set satisfying the same condition for some fixed $h$ has counting function $o(\sqrt x)$. At $h=1$, the latter two results settle conjectures of Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy, strengthening the proposed vanishing lower limit to a full limit. The proofs record each subset sum together with its cardinality and use the counting theorem of Campos and the structure theorem of Carpenter, Defant and Kravitz. The sharp count also uses Nicolas's partition enumeration and an elementary construction of a long restricted-sum progression. Finally, we give an exact partition formula for the odd sets with separated alternate cardinality layers suggested by Nicolas.

papers.title: Almost global existence for quadratic Schrödinger equations in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the two-dimensional quadratic Schrödinger equation $(i\partial_t+Δ)u=λ_1u^2+λ_2\overline u^{\,2}$ with initial data of size $\varepsilon$ in a weighted $H^2$ space. We prove almost global existence, with a lifespan of at least $\exp(c/\varepsilon)$ and decay at the optimal linear dispersive rate $t^{-1}$. Our proof is based on the space--time resonance method introduced by Germain, Masmoudi, and Shatah. The main new ingredient is the construction of a Besov-type profile space $\mathcal Z$, together with one-sided weighted bilinear estimates and spatially localized nonstationary phase estimates. This framework allows us to close the bootstrap argument without controlling the global second spatial moment of the free profile.

papers.title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
papers.abstract: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. We also prove that every witness to $K_4$, of arbitrary order, has a $K_4$ minor with every branch meeting its original odd set. The roots need not be prescribed or have distinct colours. In six colours, we prove that a fibre of size at most two forces a $K_5$ minor rooted in the original odd set, with no bound on the other fibres. In particular every six-colour witness on at most seventeen vertices has such a model. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The qualitative clique-target existence problem has been solved in recent work; our results concern exact source-order bounds and control of the original odd set.

papers.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
papers.abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.

papers.title: Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
papers.abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $α<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in parametric regressions involving stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for three classes of heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We also develop limit theory for functionals of strongly nonstationary heavy-tailed fractional processes. We demonstrate that the proposed methods, particularly a weighted extension of IVX, facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes mildly and nearly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/α<d<2-1/α$, where $α\in(1,2]$. A related weighted instrumental-variable estimator is also considered, primarily for estimation purposes.

papers.title: Increased-order generalized synchronization in memristive neurons: dissipativity analysis and data-driven control
papers.abstract: We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses next-generation reservoir computing to learn predictors from uncoupled full-state trajectories and an affine synchronization map through dynamical consistency. The resulting sampled-data controller achieves small residual tracking errors without access to the governing equations. Relative to a reference map within the data-driven framework, the learned map reduces median control effort approximately eightfold while improving tracking accuracy. These results connect synchronization-map selection with conditional convergence guarantees and reduced control requirements.

papers.title: Codimension of Brill-Noether Loci on Abelian Surfaces and the First Segre Invariant
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an abelian surface of Picard rank 1 with ample generator $H$. We show that, for a Mukai vector $\mathbf{v}=(r,mH,χ)$ with $r,m\geq 1$ and $χ\leq 0$, the first Brill-Noether loci $\{E \;|\; H^0(E)\neq 0\}$ in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$ is nonempty of the expected codimension $1-χ$. As an application, we study the rank 1 Segre invariant on these abelian surfaces. Specifically, for $\mathbf{v}$ a Mukai vector of a $μ$-stable sheaf of $\mathrm{rank}\geq 2$, we compute the Segre invariant of the general sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$, and we determine the numbers which arise as the Segre invariant of a sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$.

papers.title: A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.

papers.title: Perron--Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and continuous compact type kernels satisfying a positivity condition. Let $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u dμ=1$, and put $α=\int u^2 dμ$ and $β=\int u^3 dμ$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $ρ$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $ρ(1)=1$ and $\logρ(t)=\frac{α^2}{2β}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L<\infty$, $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)=w_rβ^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}ρ(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At criticality, the leading constant depends on the kernel only through $β$, under the stated normalization of $u$. At $t_n=1+λn^{-1/3}$, exact component identities combine with these asymptotics to give fixed size factorial densities and local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobás-Janson-Riordan models. With sizes rescaled by $β^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $αβ^{-2/3}λ$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)μ(dx)$. For every bounded uniformly positive countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.

papers.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
papers.abstract: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-Šmulian theorems.

papers.title: On the dimension conjecture for global Galois deformation rings in characteristic two
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes. Let $G_{K,S}$ be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic extension of $K$ unramified outside $S$. We prove two refined lower bounds for the Krull dimension of unrestricted global Galois deformation rings of continuous absolutely irreducible representations of $G_{K,S}$ over finite fields of characteristic $2$. As applications, we construct the first counterexamples to the dimension conjecture in every dimension $n\geq 2$ over every number field with a real prime. Over every totally real number field, these constructions also yield the first examples of such universal deformation rings that fail to be complete intersections. Furthermore, we propose a modified dimension conjecture over arbitrary number fields and in every dimension.

papers.title: Complete gradient Yamabe solitons
papers.abstract: In this paper, all complete gradient Yamabe solitons of dimension at least three are classified. More precisely, we show that complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds. We also classify nontrivial complete shrinking and expanding gradient Yamabe solitons.

papers.title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
papers.abstract:
We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(Ω)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-Δ+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

papers.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
papers.abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.

papers.title: A recurrence in logarithmic Möbius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler-Maclaurin
papers.abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted Möbius sums by combining Möbius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.

papers.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We investigate block sensitivity and certificate complexity of monomial rotation-symmetric Boolean functions, obtaining exact formulas and structural classifications for several families. For odd-degree monomial rotation-symmetric functions, the equality $s(f)=n$ established in our earlier work yields $bs(f)=C(f)=n$. For quadratic monomial rotation-symmetric functions, we determine both measures completely and prove that block sensitivity equals certificate complexity. For consecutive quartic monomials, we determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity in every residue class of the number of variables. Our principal result is an exact global block-sensitivity formula for consecutive monomials of every even degree $d\ge4$. Writing $n=q(d+2)+ρ$, where $0\leρ<d+2$ and $q\ge\max\{2,d/2-1\}$, we prove \[ bs(F_{d,n})=n-\min\left\{\left\lceil\fracρ{2}\right\rceil,d+2-ρ\right\}. \] We also establish the corresponding sensitivity formula by a self-contained argument, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between sensitivity and block sensitivity as the degree varies. For certificate complexity, we obtain exact pointwise formulas for structured run-and-gap configurations and establish additional global equalities, including $C(F_{6,8q+5})=bs(F_{6,8q+5})=8q+2$ for $q\ge2$. Our methods combine cyclic run decomposition, parity arguments, explicit sensitive-block constructions, and constant-subcube certificates. The exact global certificate complexity for arbitrary even degrees remains open.

papers.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
papers.abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are important structured families in the theory of Boolean functions, where cyclic invariance permits compact algebraic descriptions while retaining nontrivial local behavior. We investigate their sensitivity through binary necklaces and monomial orbit sums. In the necklace quotient of the Boolean cube, ordinary adjacency does not record the number of coordinate flips: we give a directed flip-multiplicity formula involving stabilizers and distance-two near-periods, and derive exact local sensitivity formulas when the number of variables is an odd prime. For monomial rotation symmetric functions we determine sensitivity for all odd degrees and for quadratic orbit sums. For the consecutive-monomial family of every even degree $d\ge4$, we prove a run-cluster inequality and obtain the eventual exact formula $s(F_{d,n})=n-\min\{r,d+2-r\}$, where $n\equiv r\pmod{d+2}$, under the stated length hypothesis. The consecutive quartic case follows explicitly. We also evaluate sensitivity for cyclic run-threshold functions. Our results provide exact combinatorial and complexity-theoretic information about cyclic Boolean functions and clarify how cyclic symmetry governs local sensitivity.

papers.title: Equilibria and Consensus in Mixed Weighted-Average and Weighted-Median Opinion Dynamics: The Consensus-Promoting Role of Weighted-Average Individuals
papers.abstract: How individuals respond to their neighbors' opinions shapes whether a networked group reaches consensus. This paper analyzes synchronous discrete-time opinion dynamics on a fixed influence network, where individuals use either weighted-average (WA) or weighted-median (WM) opinion-aggregation mechanisms with individual-specific inertia coefficients. We characterize equilibria through graph-theoretic conditions on opinion level sets and WA balance equations, proving that every solution converges to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. We define type-dependent cohesive sets, whose WA members assign all their influence weight to the set and WM members assign at least half. The absence of two disjoint such sets gives a necessary and sufficient graph-theoretic criterion for consensus from any initial condition. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent dissensus. Converting WM individuals to WA cannot create type-dependent cohesive sets and preserves existing guarantees of consensus from any initial condition. If the conversion eliminates every disjoint pair of these sets, the converted system also guarantees consensus from any initial condition. Four numerical studies examine the locations and proportion of weighted-average individuals, as well as the influence weights, while comparing the consensus criterion with finite-horizon simulation outcomes. In the four network ensembles with 100 individuals, the observed frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with WA proportion at each tested simulation horizon. This trend supports the consensus-promoting role of WA individuals, although individual realizations need not follow it.

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet energies. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.

papers.title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function $ζ_K$. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey, Odlyzko announced the stronger bound $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$ without proof. No improvement on Hoffstein's bound has since appeared with a published proof. We construct a comparison kernel from a linear combination of three identities and show that Hoffstein's original parameters give $h(K)<0.825$ for sufficiently large $n_K$. We generalise Hoffstein's method via Stechkin's trick and prove $h(K)<0.58$ for all sufficiently large $n_K$, giving the best proved estimate to date. Moreover, $ζ_K$ has at least $c n_K$ non-trivial zeros with imaginary part in $[0,0.58]$, counted with multiplicity, for some $c>0$ and $n_K$ large enough.

papers.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $Φ$. A subset $S\subseteqΦ$ is closed if $α,β\in S$ and $α+β\inΦ$ imply $α+β\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings, a simultaneous separation lemma for positive imaginary roots, and a lemma on when the sum of two positive imaginary roots is again a root. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.

papers.title: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares and higher powers
papers.abstract: Let $ν_1(n)$ and $ν_2(n)$, respectively, denote the number of representations of the natural number $n$ as the following form \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^8, \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^3+p_4^4+p_5^5+p_6^6+p_7^8, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are primes in both above cases. In this paper, it is proved that $ν_1(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$ and $n\equiv\pm1\pmod3$. Moreover, we also establish that $ν_2(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$. These results improve and enhance the earlier work of Andrade [1] and Wang-Tian [17], respectively.

papers.title: The optimal information complexity of VC learning
papers.abstract: Steinke and Zakynthinou(2020) introduces the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework of analyzing the information complexity of learning algorithms based on algorithm-dependent information-theoretic quantities. We study one of these quantities, the evaluated Conditional Mutual Information (eCMI). It has been an interesting question whether the optimal PAC guarantee for VC classes can be recovered from the algorithm-dependent analyses via CMI. And we show that it is possible to recover this guarantee by constructing a learning algorithm whose eCMI is of order O(d) in the realizable case, where d is the VC-dimension of the concept class. Specially, our algorithm is a randomized Majority-of-5 base learners with optimal in-expectation generalization guarantee.

papers.title: Nonlinear lower-tail large deviations at criticality
papers.abstract: We introduce general methods to derive lower tail large deviation principles, for a variety of nonlinear problems of combinatorial interest. These methods are especially effective in "critical" regimes, where the nonlinearities are not sparse enough for Poissonian lower tails (e.g., Janson's inequality does not provide a sharp tail bound), but the situation is not so dense that combinatorial effects dominate (e.g., we cannot directly apply the theory of hypergraph containers or the relative entropy framework of Kozma-Samotij). In particular, these are regimes where one expects interesting phase transitions to occur. Our results have a number of consequences related to subgraphs in random graphs, answering various questions of Warnke and Jenssen-Perkins-Potukuchi-Simkin. For example, consider a random graph $G\sim \mathbb G(n,p)$, and let $L_\triangle(n,p)=\log\Pr[G\text{ is triangle-free}]$. The first-order asymptotics of $L_\triangle(n,p)$ have long been known in all parameter ranges except the critical regime where $p$ has order of magnitude $1/\sqrt n$. We are able to fill this gap: for any fixed $c>0$, we show that $n^{-3/2}L_\triangle(n,c/\sqrt n)$ converges to a limit expressed in terms of a two-parameter variational problem, which has a single phase transition at $c\approx 4.341$. In contrast, we show that there is no such phase transition for the probability that $G$ is $C_{2\ell}$-free, for any fixed even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. We also obtain some applications in combinatorial design theory. Addressing conjectures of Glock-Kühn-Lo-Osthus, Kelly, and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin, we obtain new estimates on the number of order-$n$ Steiner triple systems with no Pasch configuration and the number of order-$n$ Latin squares with no $2\times 2$ Latin subsquare (both tight up to a factor of $\exp(o(n^2))$).

papers.title: Distributed Learning of $α$-Potential Functions in Strategic Multi-agent Systems
papers.abstract: We study the problem of computing the tightest \(α\)-potential approximation of a general-sum game over continuous action spaces, within a prescribed class of potential functions and when each player has access only to its own utility function. The difficulty is twofold: the approximation error involves a worst-case search over an infinite set of unilateral deviations, and the required utility information is distributed across players. For a linear-in-parameters potential class, we use an exact finite-tuple reformulation that separates the problem into a global outer search over deviation tuples and distributed convex inner problems. We develop a primal--dual inner oracle tailored to this structure and establish a uniform one-sided accuracy guarantee. This oracle can be combined with global outer search to obtain an end-to-end guarantee on the outer optimization error. We also develop a projected zeroth-order outer method as a computationally lighter alternative for higher-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy--computation tradeoff between the two outer-search methods and show that the proposed optimization framework can improve upon analytical \(α\)-potential constructions.

papers.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
papers.abstract: Let $θ$ be an ordinal and let $(N_α)_{α\leqθ}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $ρG$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_α=\overline{N_α}^{ρG}$ and $H_α=GK_α$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_α$ mark the first stages at which points of $ρG$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $θ$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,θ]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $δ<θ$ the successive factor $N_{δ+1}/N_δ$ is compact exactly when $δ+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:ρG\toρ(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{ρG}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $ρG\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $ρN\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(ρG)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $ρG\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $ρN$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.

papers.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for Lévy laws
papers.abstract: Moving an atom and splitting it symmetrically can give the same weak change in a Lévy characteristic, yet produce Wasserstein errors of different orders. We explain this through first- and second-order expansions of the distribution function for infinitely divisible laws with a Gaussian factor. The expansions are uniform over Lipschitz tests and include distributional directions from moving atoms. When the first response is nonzero, analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When it vanishes, a finite second displacement moment gives a quadratic response, with a positive coefficient whenever the dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, we prove matching bounds in terms of grid-alignment variance and construct a linear program with a controlled optimization gap. We also determine the sharp transition as Gaussian smoothing vanishes. The appendices give proofs, metric speed and length, and multivariate and state-dependent extensions.

papers.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
papers.abstract: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with symmetric stable common jumps of index $0<α<1$. A positive-strip estimate makes empirical Poisson acceptance errors negligible at the sampling scale. Given the full Poisson master, the conditional laws converge in probability to a centered Gaussian kernel in a negative Sobolev path space. In dimension one, quantile coupling preserves this limit for microscopic marks with relative tail remainder $O(x^{-ρ})$, where $ρ>\tfracα{2}$. A second-order tail expansion identifies the response when this condition fails: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify the transition from a stable to a Brownian rank error. In a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws but different path fluctuations. Rank coupling gives a functional Gaussian limit. Clock coupling admits no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.

papers.title: On the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps of degree 4
papers.abstract: Every non-linear plane Cremona map can be decomposed into quadratic maps, and the minimum number of quadratic maps required is called its quadratic length. It is known that plane Cremona maps of degree 3 have quadratic length either 2 or 3. In this paper, we study the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps $\varphi$ of degree 4. Recall that either $\varphi$ is de Jonquières, i.e. it has a base point of multiplicity 3, or it is not de Jonquières. In the latter case, $\varphi$ has quadratic length 2, whereas in the former case we prove that $\varphi$ has quadratic length 3, 4, or 5, and we classify those maps that reach the upper bound.

papers.title: On the hit problem of rank five
papers.abstract: Let $P_q$ be the graded polynomial algebra $\mathbb F_2[x_1,x_2,\ldots ,x_q]$ over the prime field of two elements, $\mathbb F_2$, with the degree of each $x_i$ being 1. We study the {\it hit Peterson problem} of finding a minimal set of generators for $P_q$ as a module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra, $\mathcal{A}.$ In this note, we present the minimal sets of $\mathcal{A}$-generators for $P_5$ in the cases where the degree are sufficiently general.

papers.title: A Log-Star Comparison Between Expectation Threshold and Fractional Expectation Threshold
papers.abstract: We proved a log-star comparison between the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ and the fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ for any nontrivial increasing family $\mathcal F$ on a finite ground set $V$ of size $|V|=N$. Specifically, we show that $$q_f(\mathcal F)\le64\log_2^*(N+2)\,q(\mathcal F),$$ where $\log_2^* x$ is the iterated logarithm of base-2. Using similiar methods, one can extend this result to the following stronger form: there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that \[ q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(l(\mathcal F)),\quad q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)), \] where $l(\mathcal F):=\max\{2,\max_{S\in\min\mathcal F}|S|\}$ and $\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)$ denotes the VC-dimension of $\min\mathcal F$. On October 7, 2026, OpenAI released a result proving the equivalence of fractional and integral thresholds, which supersedes the findings in this note. The authors are keeping this note for historical reference.

papers.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems
papers.abstract: We characterize, up to logarithmic factors, the optimal higher-order oracle complexity of finding approximate solutions to composite monotone inclusion problems, formed by the sum of a smooth single-valued monotone operator and a maximal monotone set-valued operator. We introduce the Anchored Extra-Proximal (AEP) framework, which combines an anchored extrapolation step with an inexact anchored proximal update satisfying a relative-error condition. This framework recovers the composite Fast Extragradient method in the first-order setting and yields natural higher-order extensions through Taylor approximations of the smooth operator at the extrapolated point. For every $p\geq 2$, assuming that the $(p-1)$th derivative of the single-valued operator is $L_p$-Lipschitz continuous and the initial distance to a solution is at most $R$, we combine AEP with a bisection line search to obtain a $p$th-order method that attains a tangent residual of at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}((L_p R^{p}/\varepsilon)^{\frac{2}{3p-1}})$ oracle calls. We complement this result with a worst-case lower bound of $Ω((L_p R^p/\varepsilon)^{\frac{2}{3p-1}})$ for every deterministic algorithm in the $p$th-order oracle model, without imposing any prescribed update structure. For the subclass of smooth nonexpansive fixed-point problems, we further establish a lower bound of $Ω(\min\{R/\varepsilon, {(L_p R^{p}/\varepsilon)}^{\frac{2}{3p-1}}\})$. By choosing between AEP and Halpern iteration, we match this lower bound up to logarithmic factors, thereby also settling the deterministic oracle complexity of smooth nonexpansive fixed-point problems.

papers.title: On the $W^{2,p}$ solvability for mixed boundary value problems
papers.abstract: We establish global $W^{2,p}$ solvability for the Poisson equation with mixed Dirichlet--Neumann boundary conditions in two classes of domains in all dimensions $n\geq 2$. For $C^{1,α}$ domains with a Reifenbeg flat interface, we obtain the optimal range $1<p<4/3$, provided that $α>1-1/p$. For Lipschitz polyhedra with facewise boundary decompositions, we obtain solvability for $p$ close to $1$. In both settings, we establish endpoint $W^{2,1}$ solvability for data in an adapted atomic Hardy space. Applications of the methods to Lamé systems are also discussed.

papers.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Exponential Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.

papers.title: A global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with quadratic convex generator and unbounded terminal condition
papers.abstract: We establish a global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with an unbounded terminal condition and a generator that has quadratic growth and is convex in $Z$. The control domain need not be convex, and the diffusion coefficient may depend on the control. In this setting, the BMO martingale estimates used for quadratic BSDEs with bounded terminal conditions are no longer directly available. To overcome this difficulty, we work under an equivalent probability measure associated with the optimal trajectory and establish the estimates needed for the variational analysis. In particular, using a representation formula for convex quadratic BSDEs with conditional estimates, we derive estimates for the backward-state perturbations under this fixed measure. These estimates allow us to justify a second-order expansion of the cost functional and obtain the global stochastic maximum principle.

papers.title: Locally Closed Prime Ideals and Isotropy Induction in Kumjian--Pask Algebras over Commutative Rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative unital ring and let $Γ$ be a row-finite, strongly aperiodic higher-rank graph with no sources and a nonempty finite vertex set. We determine the prime ideals that occur as annihilators of modules induced from simple isotropy modules. They are parametrised by maximal tails of $Γ$ and prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ for which the fraction field of $R/\mathfrak p$ is obtained by inverting a single element. Under the product description of the prime spectrum, these are precisely its locally closed points. The realisation argument uses a dense periodic orbit in every finite maximal-tail quotient. We also construct an explicit faithful simple module for the Leavitt algebra $L_R(1,2)$ whenever $R$ is a Goldman domain. Consequently, $L_{k[t]_{(t)}}(1,2)$ is primitive although its coefficient ring is not a field. In this example the zero ideal is locally closed but not completely irreducible. We obtain full prime-to-primitive coincidence for coefficient rings with finite spectrum and for semilocal rings of Krull dimension at most one, and transfer the results to split pullback Kumjian--Pask algebras. For pullbacks over an uncountable field, the full primitive spectrum is described without assuming algebraic closedness.

papers.title: Propagation failure in heterogeneous FitzHugh--Nagumo systems via coupled upper and lower solutions
papers.abstract: Traveling waves are fundamental objects in reaction--diffusion systems; however, spatial heterogeneities can distort or inhibit their propagation. Determining whether a given heterogeneity results in propagation failure remains challenging, particularly in systems with coupled components. In this paper, we present explicit constructions of stationary coupled upper and lower solutions tailored to specific heterogeneities for a one-dimensional FitzHugh--Nagumo system. By leveraging the mixed quasimonotone structure of the system, these barriers yield sufficient conditions for the failure of propagation for families of trapped initial conditions. The stationary constructions establish directional signal blocking in FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron models with localized reaction heterogeneities, including light-gated ionic conductances, and with abrupt geometric variations; the resulting stationary barriers persist for sufficiently small recovery diffusion. Additionally, we introduce explicit almost stationary barriers, which provide conditional bounds on the expansion of componentwise threshold regions in homogeneous media.

papers.title: A note on the diameter of graphs of two-dimensional simplex codes
papers.abstract: Let $\Gs(2,q)$ denote the graph induced in the Grassmann graph by the $q$-ary simplex codes of dimension $2$. We determine its diameter for every prime power $q$. The cases $q=2,3$ are elementary, while the diameter for $q=4$ follows from a known description of the distance relation. We prove that the diameter equals $3$ for every $q\ge5$, so that it is $0$ for $q=2$, $2$ for $q=3$, and $3$ for all $q\ge4$. The proof uses the realization of two-dimensional simplex codes as projective lines and a ratio criterion for collinearity of simplex points. A consequence of a theorem of Marshall Hall on finite abelian groups yields a bridge lemma and gives the uniform upper bound $3$. To obtain the matching lower bound for $q\ge5$, we construct an explicit diagonal pair of simplex lines and rule out a common neighbor by two independent arguments, one based on moments and the other on products. For $q\ge7$, we also give an independent counting proof. The case $q=4$ is treated separately. In particular, for $q\ge4$ the simplex-code graph is not isometrically embedded in the ambient Grassmann graph.

papers.title: A Complex Structure on A Rational Homology Six-Sphere with Two-Torsion
papers.abstract: We construct a compact, smooth, simply connected complex threefold. Its second and third integral homology groups are cyclic of order two, and its remaining homology groups agree with those of the six-sphere.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Early Stopping for SGD via the Discrepancy Principle
papers.abstract: We study early stopping for stochastic gradient descent with a constant step size applied to noisy linear inverse problems with polynomially decaying spectrum. The iteration is stopped by the discrepancy principle, that is, as soon as its residual reaches the prescribed noise level. For Hölder source conditions below a saturation level determined by the polynomial decay, we prove that the mean-square reconstruction error at the stopping index is bounded by the classical rate, up to an explicit factor involving the step size and the incoherence of the design, and that the expected number of iterations is of the order of the oracle stopping index. The rate is minimax-optimal for deterministic noise whenever the spectrum contains an eigenvalue at the oracle scale and this factor stays bounded. The step size is restricted by a spectrum-weighted incoherence condition. The analysis allows rank-deficient designs and inconsistent observations.

papers.title: Distributed Linear Programming on GPU Clusters at Extreme Scale
papers.abstract: Large linear programs can exceed the memory of a single compute node. Although first-order methods replace sparse factorizations with GPU-suited matrix-vector products, other solver phases can reintroduce a single-node memory limit. We present SHARDLP, a distributed GPU LP solver that keeps the matrix and primal-dual state partitioned from sharded input through solution output. On the Google PDLP benchmark, SHARDLP solves ten of eleven instances, compared with eight in the published CPU PDLP study. On the largest benchmark, eight H200 GPUs solve a 1.185-billion-variable, 6.338-billion-nonzero LP in 9.9 minutes; the published CPU experiment reports 21.06 hours on different hardware. Beyond this benchmark, separately checked multi-node solves reach up to 13.604 billion variables and 40.807 billion nonzeros, while validated executions span up to 76 GPUs across 29 compute nodes. For column-partitioned solves, support-aware communication skips GPUs that store no coefficients for a row; on an LP with 2.76 billion nonzeros, it cuts modelled communication by 92.97% and improves solver time by 1.27x-1.52x. The code for SHARDLP is available at https://github.com/ArnaudDeza/ShardLP.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or Möbius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8π$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,α}$ for every $α<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.

papers.title: On smooth affine surfaces with the cohomology of a smooth curve
papers.abstract: We prove that if a smooth affine complex surface has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as a smooth curve whose compactification is of positive genus, then it admits a smooth morphism to the curve with fibers isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^1$. In particular, every such surface is the total space of a torsor for a line bundle on the curve. The motivation comes from Jouanolou's trick, to which this result gives a kind of converse in dimension $2$. We also give an example in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$ which has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as $\mathbb{P}^1$ and simply connected but does not admit a smooth $\mathbb{A}^1$ fibration over $\mathbb{P}^1$.

papers.title: Bounded Harmonic Functions on Products with a Parabolic Factor
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected complete parabolic Riemannian manifold and $N$ is a connected complete stochastically complete Riemannian manifold, then every bounded harmonic function on $M\times N$ is independent of the $M$-variable. Equivalently, pullback by the second projection induces an isometric isomorphism from the space of bounded harmonic functions on $N$ onto that on $M\times N$. In particular, the product of two parabolic manifolds has the bounded Liouville property, thereby answering Problem~16 of Grigor'yan's survey in the affirmative. The key analytic input is a total-variation memory-loss property of the heat kernel on a parabolic manifold. We establish this property by showing that the time-one heat kernel defines an aperiodic Harris recurrent transition kernel and then applying the row-merging theorem of Jamison and Orey.

papers.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
papers.abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $ρ:π_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_ρ$ be the energy function on Teichmüller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ ρ_{g,h,d}:π_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ τ(ρ_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{ρ_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.

papers.title: Sidon sets with $Δ$-separated sumsets in additive number theory
papers.abstract: The set $A$ is a $B_h$-set if every element of the sumset $hA$ has a unique representation as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. A $B_2$-set is also called a Sidon set. A $B_{h,Δ}$-set is a $B_h$-set $A$ whose sumset $hA$ is $Δ$-separated, that is, $|x-x'| \geq Δ$ for all $x,x' \in hA$ with $x\neq x'$. Upper and lower bounds are obtained for the cardinality of the largest $B_{2,Δ}$-sets contained in $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$, that is, sets $A \subseteq \{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ such that, if $a,b,c,d \in A$ and $\{a,b\} \neq \{c,d\}$, then $|(a+b)-(c+d)| \geq Δ$.

papers.title: Quadratic Stiff Damping and Full-Step Asymptotic Preservation in a Two-Stage Fourth-Order Finite-Volume Method for Cattaneo Relaxation
papers.abstract: We couple a previously analyzed L-stable sequential two-stage fourth-order time formula to a specified fifth-order finite-volume residual for the periodic Goldstein--Taylor/Cattaneo equation in one and two dimensions. The required second time derivative is chosen as the exact derivative along the semi-discrete trajectory, $\mathcal G_h(U)=D\mathcal L_h(U)\mathcal L_h(U)$. For our linear reconstruction and flux, applying the same conservative face operator to $V=\mathcal L_h(U)$ yields this derivative exactly. A central face flux produces a skew-adjoint divergence--gradient pair, allowing a fixed-grid full-step asymptotic-preserving (AP) theorem for the implemented operator; for the specified central-flux discrete heat target, a wave-speed Rusanov flux has the same derivative closure but fails that target. This statement is not a claim about Rusanov-type discretizations in general. Within the previously established L-stable parameter interval, $C_q=5/183$ is the unique fixed coefficient within the admissible family, in the sense of the asymptotic damping exponent, that cancels the leading inverse-stiffness amplification, giving $R(-x)=O(x^{-2})$ rather than the generic $O(x^{-1})$ as $x=Δt/δ\to\infty$. Independent high-precision scalar calculations and the actual two-dimensional finite-volume transverse mode verify the exponent up to $x=10^5$; a mixed slow--fast state shows the resulting flux-error advantage for specified data. This damping statement does not optimize finite-stiffness accuracy or computational efficiency. The AP statements below concern the fixed-grid linear periodic problem with exact stage solutions; no mesh-uniform or nonlinear AP result is claimed.

papers.title: Toward a Unified Statistical Theory of Multi-View Pretraining for Neural Knowledge Graph Learning
papers.abstract: Knowledge graph learning offers a powerful framework for representing and inferring structured knowledge, with broad practical applications.
