The IRHC feedback has been shown to preserve the port-Hamiltonian structure of the corresponding open-loop systems. We analyze how the control parameters and the time discretization affect convergence rates and oscillation frequencies and compare the IRHC feedback with the corresponding IDA-PBC feedback obtained by omitting an additional correction term. For the reduced center of mass dynamics, we derive explicit predictions for continuous- and discrete-time spectral decay rates and oscillation frequencies and verify these predictions numerically. For the full nonlinear particle system, the controller comparison is done by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.

papers.title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear elliptic equations of variable exponent type, \[ -Δ_{q(x)}u+|u|^{q(x)-2}u=f(x,u), \] on non-compact Riemannian manifolds with symmetry. We consider complete warped products \[ M=\mathcal R\times_φY,\qquad g_φ=dr^2\oplusφ(r)^2g_Y, \] where $\mathcal R$ is a non-compact interval, possibly with boundary, and $Y$ is a compact homogeneous manifold. We establish sufficient conditions on the warping function ensuring a Ricci lower bound, a uniform non-collapsing volume condition, and the orbit-growth hypothesis of the abstract existence theorem proved in \cite{JFA}. We also obtain comparison bounds for the admissible warping functions. We analyze the corresponding radial equations for the admissible exponential and linear models $φ(r)=e^{ar}$ and $φ(r)=ar$, with $r\geq r_0>0$. For a constant diffusion exponent $q=k$, we consider explicit decaying profiles $u=φ^{-σ}$, which belong to $L_1^k(M)$ provided $σk>\dim Y$ in the exponential case and $σk>\dim Y+1$ in the linear case. Under additional explicit parameter restrictions, these profiles solve a resonant equation with a positive bounded coefficient, a construction distinct from the superlinear regime of the abstract existence theorem. Finally, we establish logarithmic reductions for constant and variable radial exponents, and justify the passage from radial identities to weak formulations against arbitrary compactly supported interior test functions.

papers.title: Neutral Ricci spectra of homogeneous Riemannian four-manifolds
papers.abstract: It is shown that every quadruple of real numbers with two positive and two negative entries is the Ricci spectrum of some left-invariant Riemannian metric on a Lie group of dimension four. Consequently, for eight out of the fifteen possible Ricci signatures of four-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds, one can determine precisely which spectra in each given signature actually occur. We also describe the Ricci spectra realized by left-invariant metrics on a certain class of 2-step solvable Lie groups of all dimensions $n>2$.

papers.title: Regular multi-types and the Bloom conjecture II
papers.abstract: Let $M\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ $(n\geq2)$ be a smooth pseudoconvex real hypersurface. We prove that, for every $1\leq s\leq n-1$, the regular $s$-contact type, the $s$-commutator type, and the $s$-Levi type coincide at every point of $M$, thereby resolving Bloom's conjecture in any dimension. The solution in dimension three was obtained in 2021 by the second and the third authors. Moreover, for any smooth rank $s$ subbundle $B\subset T^{1,0}M$, we establish the equality of the commutator type and the Levi type associated with $B$, giving an affirmative answer to the generalized D'Angelo conjecture.

papers.title: Mellin Transform formulas for special values of Goss $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we provide formulas for the special values of dual Goss $L$-functions of Drinfeld modules at any non-negative integer in terms of the determinant of the values of a motivic map, extensively studied by both authors in 2026, for a large class of Anderson modules. Our result may be seen as a function field analogue of conjectural formulas for special values of motivic $L$-functions in terms of algebraic Mellin integrals.

papers.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
papers.abstract: We develop a conforming virtual element framework for differential forms on general polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. Recursive local Hodge-Laplace boundary value problems define a trimmed virtual de Rham complex, from which moment constraints yield a complete subcomplex. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial spaces of differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom and computable polynomial projections. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and both complexes have cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual families, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and mesh-uniform norm equivalences in all form degrees. We further derive canonical interpolation error bounds and discrete Poincar'e inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge-Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity. Moreover, the two conforming complexes are cochain isomorphic to their fully discrete counterparts (J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2025, doi:10.4171/JEMS/1602), and the norm equivalences provide a key analytical bridge between the conforming and fully discrete formulations.

papers.title: Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a new set of tools for establishing the number rigidity of point processes which are particularly well suited for the spectral processes of stochastic operators. These tools allow one to prove the number rigidity of a wide class of stochastic operators that had been previously inaccessible to the standard methods in the area, such as the variance of linear statistics, which require being able to precisely analyze correlations between individual points. We propose an alternative mechanism which uses a pathwise comparison between the growth rate of the unperturbed eigenvalues and the cumulative random noise which allows one to convert the probabilistic problem into a more tractable perturbation theory problem. This new approach allows us to prove the rigidity of previously inaccessible operators including those with heavy tailed perturbations or complex correlation structures. As a demonstration, we use these tools to prove the number rigidity of new classes of stochastic Schrödinger and Sturm-Liouville Operators which are resistant to analysis using the standard rigidity toolkit.

papers.title: On the Order of Privacy and Smoothing in Functional Mean Estimation
papers.abstract: Differential privacy (DP) is a leading framework for privacy protection, yet privacy mechanisms tailored to functional data analysis (FDA) remain relatively underexplored. For functional mean estimation, we investigate a fundamental question regarding the ordering of privatization and estimation by comparing two canonical pipelines: Fit-Then-Protect (FTP), which smooths trajectories before privatization, and Protect-Then-Fit (PTF), which privatizes observations at discrete time points before smoothing. When data are observed without error, we prove that FTP achieves strictly smaller mean squared error than PTF asymptotically (as the sample size increases) under the same $μ$-Gaussian differential privacy ($μ$-GDP) budget in both finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and infinite-dimensional reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). Simulation studies support our theory and explore settings with observation error and fitting constraints, demonstrating that FTP outperforms PTF under small observation noise, whereas PTF can become preferable in high-noise settings. In addition to this comparison, we establish a novel GDP guarantee for Gaussian perturbations taking values in a Banach space, extending existing results beyond the RKHS setting.

papers.title: On the Principal Eigenvalue of the $(p,A)$-Laplacian with Sign-Changing Morrey Potentials: Complete Continuity, Optimization, and Differentiability
papers.abstract: We establish a unified framework to study the continuity and complete continuity of the principal eigenvalue functional $λ_1(V,m)$ associated with the following $(p,A)$-Laplacian operator involving both sign-changing potential $V$, and positive weight $m$ in a Morrey space: \begin{align*} -Δ_{p,A}(u) + V|u|^{p-2}u &= λm|u|^{p-2}u \quad \text{in}\,\, Ω, u &= 0 \quad\quad\quad \quad\quad \text{on}\,\, \partialΩ, \end{align*} where $1<p<N$, $λ\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter, and $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N (N \geq 2)$ is a bounded domain with boundary $\partial Ω$. As a consequence, we investigate the existence and uniqueness of optimal principal eigenvalues $λ_1(V,m)$ over a weakly compact subset of the Morrey space. Finally, we derive a formula for the derivative of $λ_1(V,m)$ with respect to regular perturbations of potential $V$, and positive weight $m$ within a closed subspace of Morrey space. Our results develop analytic tools to overcome the lack of separability and reflexivity in Morrey spaces to investigate this eigenvalue problem. In particular, the study is new even for the linear case $p=2$. We also emphasize that the tools established are applicable for a wide class of PDEs with coefficients in Morrey spaces.

papers.title: Box-Cox Transformations of Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract: We consider Box-Cox transformations of correlation matrices, $Φ_α(C)=\mathrm{vecl}\{(C^α-I)/α\}$, with Jacobian $J_α$. The family nests the raw correlations at $α=1$, the generalised Fisher transformation (GFT), $C\mapsto\mathrm{vecl}(\log C)$, at $α=0$, and the negated off-diagonal concentration coordinates at $α=-1$. The inverse problem is a strictly convex program for every $α$, so every member is injective. The map is onto $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, $d=n(n-1)/2$, if and only if $α\le0$, such that $α=0$ defines the boundary for unrestricted parametrizations. For $α>0$ the image is bounded. The conditioning obeys the bound $κ(J_α)\leκ(C)^{|1-α|}$, where $κ(C)=λ_{\max}(C)/λ_{\min}(C)$, and on the surjective range the exponent is smallest at $α=0$. Under Gaussian sampling with $n\geq3$, the asymptotic covariance of the transformed sample correlations is the identity at independence for every member, but only $α=0$ retains the identity to first order in the correlations, whereas the leading joint third cumulant at independence vanishes only at $α=1/3$. Finally, applying the transformation to the diagonal rescaling of $C$ that makes the result hollow adds a new family to the existing correlation parametrizations. For every $α$ the rescaling solves a strictly convex problem and the inverse is explicit, and the scaled coordinates are unrestricted exactly when $α=0$, where they recover the known global normal coordinates, centred at independence, for the efficient information metric of the correlations.

papers.title: Braid Groups in Lean : Formalizing Dehornoy's Subword Reversing Algorithm
papers.abstract: We formalize the group-theoretic definition of infinite and finite Artin braid groups in Lean. We implement a polynomial-time procedure for determining equivalence in the braid group known as Dehornoy's subword reversing algorithm. Termination and correctness of this algorithm are shown using rectangular grids, which are a specific form of van Kampen diagram. The literature only hints at a proof linking rectangular grids to braid equivalence. We present a novel, three-stage proof of this result, introducing partial grids and associated size metrics.

papers.title: A generalization of the Gauss Lemma
papers.abstract: We give a generalization of the Gauss Lemma for normal exponential maps and a covering criterion as a consequence.

papers.title: The variational formulation of the follow-the-leader model
papers.abstract: We provide a variational formulation of a finite-dimensional Follow-the-Leader system through a minimizing-movement scheme based on a discrete transport distance with nonlinear mobility. Despite the degeneracy of the kinetic action at maximal density, we prove finiteness of the distance, $C^1$ regularity of geodesics, and suitable Euler--Lagrange relations. For a decreasing external potential, we show that the JKO scheme yields an approximate implicit Euler discretization of the Follow-the-Leader dynamics. Consequently, as $τ\to0^+$, the piecewise affine interpolations converge, up to a subsequence, to a $C^1$ solution of the continuous Follow-the-Leader system. This complements the many-particle convergence theory for the discrete nonlinear-mobility transport distance by establishing the continuous-time limit at fixed number of particles.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
papers.abstract: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $ρ>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $ρ$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.

papers.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
papers.abstract: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.

papers.title: Exploring the Regular and Singular Loci of Group Representation Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be the Borel Subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$, and let $G_m=\langle x,y,z\mid x^2y^3=z^{2m+1}\rangle$, $m\geq2$. The $G_m$ are parafree of rank two and deviation one. We compute the integral homology of the regular and singular loci of $X_m=\mathrm{Hom}(G_m,B)$. Each $X_m$ is a four-dimensional irreducible affine variety with the homotopy type of a two-dimensional torus. Its singular locus is a disjoint union of $16m$ affine lines. The regular locus has Betti numbers $b_0=1$, $b_1=2$, $b_2=16m+1$, and $b_3=b_5=16m$, with all other Betti numbers zero. Thus, although each $X_m$ has the homotopy type of a torus and its singular locus is a disjoint union of contractible lines, removing the singular locus creates $16m$ additional independent homology classes in each of degrees $2$, $3$, and $5$, arising from the transverse link $S^2\times S^3$. We also establish that the regular loci are not affine.

papers.title: Malliavin structure for conditionally independent random variables
papers.abstract: We consider a countable family of random variables which are conditionally independent given a latent random variable $Z$. Given $Z$, the random variables are independent. Hence the Malliavin calculus for independent random variables applies for each value of $Z$. We show that these constructions fit together. We obtain the chaos decomposition, the domains of the Malliavin operators, the Mehler formula and the carré du champ operator, with conditional expectations given $Z$ in place of ordinary expectations. For normal approximation, conditioning on $Z$ and the infinite de Jong theorem of Döbler give mixed normal approximations of degenerate U-statistics, in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. Working under the unconditional probability, we obtain a de Jong type bound for U-statistics whose kernels are products. In both cases, the fluctuations of the conditional variance appear as an additional term, which cannot be removed. As an application, we consider subhypergraph counts in a random $3$-uniform hypergraph built on a latent random graph. For the count centred at its conditional mean, we obtain an explicit rate in Wasserstein distance. It reduces to the known rate for the Erdős--Rényi hypergraph when the latent graph is complete. The count centred at its mean is a pattern count in a non-uniform hypergraph with independent edges, which gives a necessary and sufficient condition for its asymptotic normality.

papers.title: Limit laws for the friendship paradox in random geometric graphs
papers.abstract: The friendship paradox says that, on average, the neighbours of a vertex have more neighbours than the vertex itself. We study the size of this effect, the average over all vertices of the mean degree of the neighbours minus the degree of the vertex, in the random geometric graph on the torus with the maximum-norm distance. We determine its limit law in every regime of the connection radius and quantify the approximation by non-asymptotic error bounds in the Kolmogorov distance or the total variation distance. We also give its exact mean for every $n$ and every radius below one half. For a fixed radius the limit is not Gaussian but a weighted sum of centred exponential variables; when the radius shrinks and the expected degree grows, the statistic is asymptotically Gaussian, with a Berry--Esseen bound; for bounded expected degree it is Gaussian at the classical rate; and when the expected degree tends to zero it is asymptotically Gaussian, Poisson or identically zero, depending on how fast the radius shrinks. When the expected degree is large, the proofs rest on the vanishing of the first Hoeffding projection, which makes a degenerate $U$-statistic of pairs of points the source of the fluctuations; it is analysed by Fourier series for a fixed radius and by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs for a shrinking radius. For bounded expected degree we use normal approximation for local functionals, and for vanishing expected degree the Chen--Stein method.

papers.title: Percolation on grandparent graphs of Bienaymé trees
papers.abstract: We consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the grandparent graph of a Bienaymé tree, obtained by adding to the tree an edge between every vertex and its grandparent. We show that the critical parameter $p_c$ is the unique solution of an explicit equation involving the generating function of the offspring distribution, and we study how $p_c$ depends on this distribution beyond its mean $m$. When $m\geq 1.569$, the offspring distribution concentrated on the (one or two) integers closest to $m$ is the unique maximiser of $p_c$ among all offspring distributions with mean $m$, and its critical parameter is $\frac1{m^2}-\frac1{m^3}+O\left(\frac1{m^4}\right)$ as $m\to\infty$; more generally, for two distributions that are comparable in the convex order, $p_c$ is larger for the smaller of the two distributions under the condition that its support bounded some explicit $N(m)$ of order $m^4$. These restrictions cannot be removed: the convex order alone does not determine the order of the critical parameters, even among distributions with support bounded by $O(m^4)$, and the extremal property fails for $m$ close to $1$. Finally, for every $m>1$, the critical parameter $p_c$ can be arbitrarily close to $0$ for general offspring distributions with mean $m$. If we only consider offspring distributions that do not charge $0$, so that the obtained tree is almost surely infinite, this remains true if and only if $m\geq 2$.

papers.title: The Matrix Kawada--Itô Theorem and Harmonic Rigidity on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: A positive $M_n$-valued measure on a locally compact group need not have positive convolution products: matrix multiplication preserves neither self-adjointness nor positivity. We prove that this obstruction disappears completely at an idempotent. If $μ\in M(G,M_n)$ is positive and $μ*μ=μ$, then all its matrix values commute and there is a unique finite decomposition \[ μ=\sum_{j=1}^r m_{K_j}\otimes E_j, \] where the $K_j$ are distinct compact subgroups and the $E_j$ are pairwise orthogonal nonzero projections. The result holds for arbitrary locally compact groups, without countability assumptions or a priori commutativity. The proof combines projection-valued dilations, rigidity of contractive idempotent Fourier coefficients, and faithfulness of the regular representation on finite measures over $G\times G$. For normalized positive matrix convolution semigroups, we further identify the Cesàro harmonic projection with convolution by such an idempotent, even if mass escapes to infinity. Its surviving matrix directions are exactly those uniformly confined to a compact subset of the group, yielding an explicit direct Haar-channel decomposition for all $1<p<\infty$ (orthogonal in $L^2$). A bounded Zeno product formula and independent density, atomic, and subgroup-support classifications illustrate the rigidity.

papers.title: Attractivity Implies Lyapunov Stability for Multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini Systems
papers.abstract: We study the linear multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini recurrence with uniformly bounded boundary data prescribed on the open coordinate faces. Attractivity is understood in the sense of Pringsheim convergence, in which all discrete indices tend to infinity. We establish that attractivity alone implies Lyapunov stability, and consequently is equivalent to asymptotic stability, for an arbitrary number of discrete directions. Our proof combines inheritance of attractivity by lower-dimensional subsystems, a Baire-category uniform boundedness argument, and word-sum estimates to control coordinate slabs outside the Pringsheim tail. We use a generalized spectral stability criterion proved in a separate companion preprint, without reproving that criterion here. We also obtain a uniform exponential interior estimate and contrast our boundary/convergence convention with an earlier two-dimensional attractivity theorem.

papers.title: Division ring extensions and a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a family of division ring extensions and compute their left and right dimensions. In characteristic zero, we obtain a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture: a hereditary right pure semisimple ring of infinite representation type. For each prime $p\ge3$, we construct in characteristic $p$ a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(p+2)$.

papers.title: Multiscale Closing Index (MCI) for measuring structural similarity between 2D point sets
papers.abstract: We introduce Multi-scale Closing Index (MCI), a new dissimilarity measure for evaluating the alignment of two 2D point sets. MCI is bounded between 0 and 1 and is based on multiscale mathematical morphology operations, with smaller values indicating greater structural agreement. The measure was motivated by the need to assess the quality of registration between point sets representing cell populations in biological images. To evaluate its behaviour under controlled conditions, we generated synthetic point clouds from Perlin-noise-based spatial structures, following established approaches for simulating biologically plausible spatial organization. We assessed MCI between those point clouds and different transformed versions, obtained by local perturbation, point removal, translation, rotation and addition of impulsive noise. Across these experiments, the dissimilarity MCI increased gradually and consistently with perturbation severity, while showing a clear discontinuity between clouds originating from the same underlying spatial structure and point clouds generated from different structures. We further compared MCI with commonly used point-set distances, including Hausdorff-based measures and Sliced Wasserstein distance. These experiments show the ability of MCI to capture structural agreement and quantify deviations between point sets, highlighting its potential as a complementary metric for evaluating two-dimensional point-set registration.

papers.title: Finding geometric criteria for negative eigenvalues of the Neumann--Poincaré operator
papers.abstract: Motivated by a question of Grigori Rozenblum, we study how the geometry of the boundary of a convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ affects whether the Neumann--Poincaré operator on $\partialΩ$ has negative eigenvalues. First, we show that a flat face on the boundary of a bounded, convex Lipschitz domain produces an infinite-dimensional negative spectral subspace. For convex domains with $C^{1,α}$ boundary, we bound the number of negative eigenvalues from below by the Dirichlet eigenvalue counting function of a projected patch over which the chords are sufficiently short. A Rellich identity gives a sufficient condition on a defining function to exclude negative eigenvalues. We also report numerical computations, which led us to the theoretical results.

papers.title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers. We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model. For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{μ-1}/μ$ for limiting average degree $μ$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $δ\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{δ-1}/δ$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $δ\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.

papers.title: Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman spaces are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider weighted Bergman spaces over open unit disk corresponding to nonnegative integrable radial functions with positive mass arbitrarily close to the unit circle. Then we show that Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the weighted Bergman space are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map. This result generalizes the classical characterization of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space due to Brown and Halmos. Moreover, we prove that there is no compact Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman space.

papers.title: Extreme-value asymptotics for smallest enclosing balls of spherically symmetric samples
papers.abstract: Let $R_n$ denote the radius of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ sample of spherically symmetric random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $D_n$ be the sample diameter. While the asymptotic behaviour of $D_n$ is well understood, much less is known about $R_n$. Starting from a classical result of Daniels for planar Gaussian samples, we develop a point-process approach to the asymptotic behaviour of $R_n$ in the three classical extreme-value regimes. We obtain limit theorems in the Gumbel, Fr'echet and Weibull cases, with the limiting laws described by geometric functionals of Poisson point processes. In dimension two, the Gumbel limit can be identified explicitly and is universal within the corresponding max-domain of attraction. We also study the asymptotic relationship between $R_n$ and $D_n$ and the supporting configurations of the smallest enclosing ball.

papers.title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We propose a fixed-point acceleration method for optimization over probability measures, applicable to a variety of machine learning problems. We represent probability measures as pushforwards of a reference distribution through a neural network map and equip the parameter space with the induced pullback Wasserstein metric. This geometric structure allows natural gradient descent to be interpreted as a fixed-point iteration on a Riemannian manifold. We accelerate this iteration using Riemannian Anderson mixing method, which exploits historical residuals to capture approximate second-order information without forming Hessians. In the present parametric setting, the manifold is represented by Euclidean coordinates endowed with a point-dependent metric, simplifying retraction and vector transport. We evaluate the method on multimodal sampling, PDE-based inverse problems, aggregation dynamics, Bayesian logistic regression, and generative modeling. Across the tested tasks, Anderson mixing reduces the number of natural-gradient iterations and achieves competitive performance relative to SGD and Adam in terms of both loss-gradient evaluations and wall-clock time. These results suggest that fixed-point acceleration is an efficient tool for improving the computational efficiency of training on parametric Wasserstein methods.

papers.title: Row-sparse ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses with a few extra rows: local search with approximation guarantees
papers.abstract: For a rank-$r$ matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses $H$ with few nonzero rows give least-squares solutions that are fast to evaluate and use few variables. A known determinant-based local search finds one with exactly $r$ nonzero rows and 2,1-norm within an essentially tight factor $r$ of the minimum at an exact local optimum. We let the nonzero rows of $H$ lie in a set $K$ of $k\ge r$ indices and study how to choose $K$. We bound the loss of this restriction (restricted over unrestricted minimum 2,1-norm) by a simple geometric certificate and establish that a local search maximizing the squared rank-$r$ volume of the corresponding columns of $A$ gives loss at most $\sqrt{k(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$, where $1+ε$ is the swap tolerance. With $ε=0$ this is $r$ at $k=r$ and less than $\sqrt{2r}$ for $k\ge2r$; with $ε=1/k$ the search runs in polynomial time on rational data. The same support yields an ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverse with spectral norm within a factor $\sqrt{1+(n-k)(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$ of that of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. The loss guarantees hold for every norm on the rows. In general, our certificate bound is tight up to a factor depending only on $k/r$, and on some instances, for a suitable row norm, so is the loss bound; for the 2,1-norm, however, the certificate can overestimate the loss by a factor $\sqrt r$. The local search is the Fedorov exchange algorithm of 0/1 D-optimal design; this yields a fast implementation and, via the Kiefer-Wolfowitz theorem, supports of at most $r(r+1)/2+1$ rows with certificate at most $\sqrt r$, best possible in general. On instances from earlier work, the observed loss is far below the guarantee, and the method matches two ADMM heuristics when few rows are removed and otherwise gives 2,1-norms up to 27% smaller, one to two orders of magnitude faster.

papers.title: How many points does it take to see the homotopy of a space? Minimal acyclic categorical models
papers.abstract: Every connected homotopy type is the classifying space of a small category, but this general result gives little control over the categories involved. We study finite acyclic categorical models and measure their complexity by the number of objects. Our main tool is the sink lemma, which describes the addition of a sink as the attachment of a cone along an explicit map. Using it, we determine the minimum number of objects required to model spheres, bouquets of spheres, Moore spaces of cyclic groups, real projective spaces, and lens spaces. We also exhibit infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic rigid minimal models of the sphere. To include spaces admitting no finite model, we introduce a truncated invariant measuring the minimum number of objects required for a finite acyclic category to approximate a space through degree n. Spreading a finite monoid over n+1 objects produces such a category with an n-connected map to the monoid's classifying space. For every nontrivial finite group, this bound is optimal, although its classifying space admits no finite acyclic model.

papers.title: Tensor value and the 9/4 bound for matrix multiplication
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent result that the exponent of matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 valid over every field. Our main tool is a fractional symmetrized variant of the tensor value introduced by Coppersmith and Winograd, used in place of spectral points (tensor characters) in the original proof. We prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums, whose summands share one tensor factor and occupy independent subspaces in the other two. Together with the degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof, this inequality yields the bound.

papers.title: Euler trace congruences over local fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\QQ_p$ with uniformizer $π$ and residue field $\FF_q$. For each $r\ge1$, we determine the largest integer $E_r$ such that $\Tr(A^{q^r})\equiv\Tr(A^{q^{r-1}})\pmod{π^{E_r}}$ for every integral matrix $A$ with a prescribed residual similarity class. We give formulas for both nilpotent and nonnilpotent residual classes and construct integral lifts attaining the resulting exponents. We also exhibit local fields with the same ramification index and residue field for which the optimal exponents differ, even when $r$ and the residual similarity class are fixed.

papers.title: Borel rigidity for higher rank lattices
papers.abstract: In this paper we focus on rigidity in descriptive set theory. Building on cocycle superrigidity results of Popa, Furman and Ioana, we prove rigidity in the purely Borel context for the orbit equivalence relations arising from the shift actions and translation actions of lattices in semisimple Lie groups with higher rank. Our results sharpen work of Adams and Kechris.

papers.title: On the strong Arnold conjecture for Grassmannians
papers.abstract: On several families of flag varieties, we provide examples of degenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms exhibiting significantly smaller numbers of fixed points than predicted by the strong Arnold conjecture.

papers.title: A Regular First-Order Calculus for the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao Geometry
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of intrinsic differentiability for functionals on the space of finite nonnegative measures equipped with the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) distance, also known as the Hellinger--Kantorovich (HK) distance. The resulting static first-order calculus accounts simultaneously for spatial transport and mass reweighting. We characterize regular barycentric logarithms through optimal semicouplings and measurable selections at the transport threshold, and prove their tangency at arbitrary finite source measures. The defining expansion extends to non-optimal semicouplings, with remainder of smaller order than the square root of their cost. This yields differentiation formulas for simultaneous transport and reweighting and uniqueness of the gradients. We also give a sufficient criterion in terms of regular flat derivatives. We characterize differentiability of one half the squared WFR distance by a common optimal Monge transport--growth representation with no target mass created from the cone vertex. Equivalently, the regular barycentric logarithm is unique and its norm equals the distance; the gradient is minus this logarithm. Finally, we formulate the corresponding calculus on probability measures. On $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, WFR differentiability implies intrinsic Wasserstein differentiability, with the transport component of the WFR gradient coinciding with the Wasserstein gradient. Whenever a flat derivative exists, one quarter of the reaction component agrees almost everywhere with its centered representative. As a byproduct we obtain a Wasserstein differentiability result for the squared $\mathrm{WFR}$ distance.

papers.title: Deformation of Associative Submanifolds joining Minimal Surfaces in Hyperbolic Geometry
papers.abstract: Donaldson and Thomas proposed a Floer-type theory on a Calabi-Yau threefold $M$, generated by the complex curves, and whose boundary operator is given by counting appropriate associative submanifolds in $M\times \mathbb{R}$. We consider a similar setting, in which the Calabi-Yau manifold is replaced by the twistor space $Z$ of an oriented hyperbolic 4-manifold $X$ and the $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$ project to minimal surfaces in $X$. We give a formula for the virtual dimension of (a subset of) the moduli space of associatives asymptotic to a pair of $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$, proving it equals the difference of the Morse indices of the corresponding minimal surfaces in $X$.

papers.title: Divergence Rates for Orbits of Semigroups of Holomorphic Functions
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior for forward and backward orbits of one-parameter semigroups of holomorphic self-maps of the unit disk. For both types of orbits, we determine the asymptotic growth rate of hyperbolic length and compare it with the total speed of the semigroup, obtaining sharp constants that depend on the intrinsic properties of the semigroup and on the starting point. In the process, we discover new characterizations for standard notions in the theory of semigroups. We further explore, from a potential theoretic scope, the rate by which compact sets in petals of semigroups degenerate to a boundary point in the backward dynamical setting.

papers.title: On a Problem of Gordon and Hughes: The 11-adic Properties of Meromorphic Modular Functions on $\mathrm{X}_0(22)$
papers.abstract: Congruence families occur throughout the theory of modular forms. These families superficially resemble one another, though they can vary substantially in their overall difficulty. One major complication resides in the topology of the modular curve associated with a given congruence family. All previously studied families are associated with curves of genus 0 or 1. The existence of a family associated with a curve of genus 2 (and the associated difficulties of a proof thereof) was first speculated upon by Gordon and Hughes. We give the first explicit congruence family associated with $\mathrm{X}_0(22)$, a modular curve of genus 2, and prove it. We also propose two families of conjectures associated with the same modular curve.

papers.title: The maximum size of $3$-distance binary codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for every positive integer $n \ge 24$, the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of vectors from $\{-1,1\}^n$ with at most three distinct Hamming distances is equal to $\binom{n}{3}+n$. The threshold $n=24$ is best possible.

papers.title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane developed by Haiman.

papers.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
papers.abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.

papers.title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. For an odd prime power $q$, consider polynomials over $\mathbb F_{q^n}$ of the form $\sum_{0\le i\le j<n}a_{ij}x^{q^i+q^j}+L(x)$, where $a_{ij}\in\mathbb F_{q^n}$ and $L$ serves as an $\mathbb F_q$-linear endomorphism of $\mathbb F_{q^n}$. In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not $2$, and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.

papers.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
papers.abstract: Dallard, Milanič, and Štorgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor. We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.

papers.title: Fourier Positivity and Sharp Poincaré Inequalities on Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove sharp dimension-free $L^1$-Poincaré inequalities on Hamming cubes, a sharp quadratic $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on product Poisson spaces, and a sharp pseudo-Poincaré inequality on finite abelian Cayley graphs. These inequalities use a generalization of the Beckmann boundary introduced by Ivanisvili, Xie, and Zhang. In particular, we prove that the optimal dimension-free constant in the classical $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on the Hamming cube is $\sqrt{π/2}$, answering a question of Ivanisvili et al. Semigroup duality and explicit Malliavin weights reduce these estimates to integrals of first absolute moments of centered Bernoulli and Poisson sums. The key ingredient is a Fourier positivity principle, which shows that replacing the coefficients by their absolute values can only increase these integrals. For the underlying Bernoulli functional at subquadratic exponents, we also characterize the maximizers and determine their exact phase transitions.

papers.title: SparseModesNet for coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical system in heterogeneous porous media
papers.abstract: Coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) models describe interactions among displacement, fluid pressure, and temperature in geothermal systems. Fine-mesh simulations over many time steps are costly, particularly with heterogeneous permeability and thermal conductivity or fracture networks that alter fluid and heat transport. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) reduces the number of unknowns but can require many modes because its reconstruction is linear. We apply SparseModesNet to reconstruct coupled THM solutions using a small set of selected modes and a neural-network nonlinear decoder. Starting from a larger collection of candidate modes, SparseModesNet selects modes to reduce reconstruction error rather than simply retaining those with the highest energy. We compare SparseModesNet with POD on three problems: a two-dimensional heterogeneous medium, a two-dimensional connected fracture network, and a three-dimensional geometry based on Utah FORGE fractures. We evaluate reconstructed displacement, pressure, and temperature fields, as well as pressure- and temperature-based quantities of interest. We also test temporal interpolation by training on a subset of snapshots and reconstructing omitted snapshots within the same time interval. For the same reduced dimension, SparseModesNet achieves smaller reconstruction errors than POD and accurately recovers the solution fields and selected geothermal quantities of interest.

papers.title: Some normal abelian surfaces in $\mathbf{P}^3$
papers.abstract: Every complex projective surface is birational to a singular surface $S \subseteq \mathbf{P}^3$, but it is unclear whether one can ask that $S$ have only isolated singularities. In particular, it was a folk question as to whether an abelian surface could admit such a model. We present examples to show that there do exist normal abelian surfaces in $\mathbf{P}^3$. One of these examples deforms in a one-parameter family.

papers.title: Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs
papers.abstract: We study kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples, with a focus on how the regularity of the target should determine the choice of the kernel. We establish embeddings of analytic operators into vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and derive finite-sample, high-probability guarantees that quantify the uncertainty due to random sampling: in the noiseless setting, suitable analytic kernels yield rates exponential in a fractional power of the sample size, while Sobolev-type kernels yield polynomial rates. We apply the theory to the solution operator of a parametric elliptic PDE, where the training data are themselves finite-element approximations, and obtain bounds that separate the sampling and discretization contributions to the error and prescribe how the mesh size should be coupled to the sample size. The results are illustrated numerically.

papers.title: New persistent chain spaces: identifying and computing the relevant persistent Laplacians of a filtration
papers.abstract: Persistent homology (PH) summarizes the topological features of data that persist across scales, but it is insensitive to many geometric properties. Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret. In this paper, we show that this redundancy has a precise structure. For each pair of filtration values, we decompose the space of chains underlying the persistent up-Laplacian into the contributions inherited from the neighboring pairs and a remaining part, which we call the new persistent chain space. We show that the new persistent chain spaces of all earlier pairs form a direct sum decomposition of this space, so that every persistent up-Laplacian in the filtration is determined by them. Moreover, the new persistent chain spaces are non-trivial only at pairs given by the persistence pairing in the same and in the next homological dimension, so that the persistence pairing determines exactly where the persistent up-Laplacian can change. Experiments on several types of point clouds show that evaluating persistent Laplacians only at these pairs reduces the computation time, both for our implementation and for existing software.

papers.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.

papers.title: Simply connected quotients of fake quadrics
papers.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a short introduction to their arithmetic construction, aimed at low-dimensional topologists, and studies their holomorphic and antiholomorphic quotients and their fundamental groups. The running example in the paper comes from a quaternion algebra over a totally real cubic field. The lattice is generated by three explicit pairs of matrices. A holomorphic involution gives (after resolving the singularities) a simply connected minimal complex surface of general type with $p_g=0$ and $K^2=4$, a smooth $4$-manifold homeomorphic but non-diffeomorphic to $CP^2$ blown up $5$ times. An antiholomorphic involution gives a smooth four-manifold homeomorphic to $S^4$, with a knotted torus as branch locus.

papers.title: An extension of the notion of algebraic entropy
papers.abstract: The definition of algebraic entropy presents a difficulty in the general setting of filtered algebras, which makes it necessary to distinguish between filtered algebras and finitely filtered algebras. While algebraic entropy is well defined in the finitely filtered case, extending this notion to arbitrary filtered algebras is not immediate. To address this issue, we realize a filtered algebra as the limit of a strict direct system of finitely filtered algebras and define its entropy as the supremum of the entropies of the algebras in the system. This extension is consistent with the original definition, when the algebra is finitely filtered, the extended entropy agrees with its algebraic entropy. This new setting allows us to extend the definition of the algebraic entropy to path and Leavitt path algebras of infinite graphs.

papers.title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coarse-to-Fine Finite Element Solver for Heterogeneous Darcy Flow
papers.abstract: Quantum linear system algorithms offer theoretical potential for solving large sparse systems from PDE discretizations. However, applying them directly to fine-scale problems remains impractical on near-term hardware because of limited qubits, restricted circuit depth, and noise. They also prepare a quantum state rather than solution coefficients, whose recovery requires measurement and reconstruction. In this work, we develop a hybrid quantum-classical coarse-to-fine finite element framework for heterogeneous Darcy flow. We investigate whether a measured quantum coarse solution improves fine-grid initialization and reduces subsequent classical solver work. Rather than solve the full fine-scale system on a quantum device, we apply a method inspired by the Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS) to the Galerkin coarse system. We reconstruct the approximate coarse solution from measurements, prolongate it to the fine grid, and use it to initialize a classical preconditioned iterative solve.} Numerical experiments on steady heterogeneous Darcy flow and a time-dependent SPE10-based problem show that measured quantum coarse solutions can improve fine-grid initialization, while classical correction recovers accurate pressure fields. The effect on classical solver iterations depends on the problem. All quantum computations were simulated using Qiskit Aer.

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
papers.abstract: We study the variance of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf p}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|X_{j+1}-X_j-N(p_{j+1}-p_j)|$ of $X\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ for fixed $n\ge3$ and fixed $\mathbf p$ with all $p_i>0$, as $N\to\infty$. We prove $\mathrm{Var}(d_{\mathbf p})=N\,v(\mathbf p)+O(1)$, where $v(\mathbf p)$, the variance of the sum of absolute values of the limiting Gaussian edge vector, is expressed through the exact multinomial edge variances and correlations and Nabeya's covariance formula for folded bivariate normal variables. Unlike in the uniform case, non-adjacent edge pairs generally contribute to $v(\mathbf p)$. The $O(1)$ remainder is controlled by a lattice Edgeworth expansion and Poisson summation; it oscillates with the lattice phases $\{N(p_{j+1}-p_j)\}$, and for $n=3,4$, where a pair of edges exhausts the bins, the summation runs over a sublattice coset. The formula reduces to the known uniform result (the classical Hoel--Kamat variance), gives a closed form when the reference law is a symmetric comb, and has a shape-independent large-bin limit for positive $C^1$ profiles. For the statistic $d_{\mathbf r}$ centered at a reference law $\mathbf r\ne\mathbf p$ the absolute values linearize: when every edge is mismatched the variance is that of a linear form in the counts up to an exponentially small error, and in mixed (triangular-array) regimes it is given to $o(N)$ by bivariate folded-normal covariances. The two-bin formulas are recorded from the companion preprints, and exact finite-$N$ reductions for $n\le4$ are used for validation.

papers.title: Generalized and Classical Harnack Inequalities for semilinear equations on Carnot Groups
papers.abstract: We prove generalized and classical Harnack inequalities for non-negative smooth solutions of divergence-form semilinear subelliptic equations on Carnot groups. The proof combines smooth horizontal Gauss--Green and coarea formulas, energy estimates for level sets, a Vitali covering argument, and a horizontal Keller--Osserman barrier. The companion paper, Reference [10], develops the geometric foundations and extends the estimates to weak solutions with nonsmooth data.

papers.title: Hostages
papers.abstract: Our house has been taken over. It is not completely destroyed, but many of its essential functions and facilities no longer work as they used to. Essentially, they are out of our control. Artificial intelligence, through its large language models (LLMs), has taken it. And we, the inhabitants of the house, without really noticing what was happening, and surprised by the effectiveness of LLMs, have handed over our most sacred belongings: the capacity to think about a problem, the joy of having an idea that solves it, the beautiful effort needed to consolidate an idea in our common language. And there is no turning back. We are mathematicians, and our whole world is in check. We wonder: is it checkmate? Can we take back control of our house, which will undoubtedly not work in the same way? Paradoxically, the weapons that attacked us are built on some of our own ideas. Of course, it is not entirely our work. The computer science knowledge needed to develop these large models evolved in both its theoretical and its material aspects. As technology evolved (infinitely small processors, infinitely large computing centers), turning quantity into quality, computer scientists encoded into software the ideas needed to produce these tools (let us not call them weapons). These notes look into the past and the future of the mathematical profession. What will inevitably happen? What will remain and what will disappear? And, in consequence, what is our line of action? To organize the ideas, after some introductory historical comments, we try to answer the questions: (1) Is mathematics necessary for the development of our society? (2) Will mathematicians be necessary in the near future? (3) How the profession will change, through a list of exercises: open questions and possible actions.

papers.title: Isometric Classification of Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the norm obtained by summing the $L^1$ norms of all weak derivatives through order $k$, including the function itself, determines both $n$ and $k$ on the real Sobolev space $W^{k,1}(\R^n)$. Every surjective linear isometry for this norm is given by a translation, a signed permutation of the coordinates and multiplication by a fixed sign $c\in\{-1,1\}$.

papers.title: Bayesian Inverse Problems for EUV reflectometry with regularized JKO scheme
papers.abstract: We study a Bayesian inverse problem in EUV reflectometry, where optical constants and layer thicknesses are inferred from angle- and wavelength-resolved reflection measurements. The physical process is modeled and evaluated using an efficient forward model based on the transfer matrix method. As an alternative to computationally expensive sampling-based inference, we employ an Eulerian, entropically regularized Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler divergence via proximal steps in the Wasserstein space. Using the Benamou--Brenier dynamic formulation and a Hopf-Cole transform, each JKO step is reformulated as a pair of heat equations coupled only through their initial and terminal conditions, enabling an efficient fixed-point solver. The resulting high-dimensional densities are discretized on tensor-product grids and represented in tensor-train format, exploiting Kronecker structure for scalable computation. Preconditioning based on estimated posterior moments further improves tractability. We test the method with numerical experiments on EUV reflectometry data for a ruthenium--silicon ($\ce{Ru}$ on $\ce{Si}$) specimen and compare the learned tensor-train posterior to ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) reference samples. We demonstrate a use case in which we are able to reuse the tensor-train posterior to obtain samples for shifted target distributions with less computational effort than a comparable MCMC method.

papers.title: Symmetric Zassenhaus splittings for bounded and unbounded operators
papers.abstract: We establish rigorous local-error bounds for the entire family of symmetric Zassenhaus splittings for possibly unbounded operators, under explicit assumptions on commutator bounds, regularity-preserving flows, and conjugation identities. Truncated symmetric Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansions yield an explicit coefficient formula for the Zassenhaus exponents and identify vanishing commutator expressions. In order to extend these cancellations to the realm of unbounded operators, we prove a general theorem on finite expansions of multiple operator conjugations with controlled integral remainders. For splittings of order 2n, our argument gives the sufficient commutator-length bound 4n-1, revealing regularity requirements that are not apparent from the formal order calculation. Using the Schrödinger equation with a quadratic potential as an example, we show that the order-dependent regularity requirements can reduce to one fixed weighted Sobolev space for all splitting orders.

papers.title: Modal weak Kleene logics: algebraic semantics and Jónsson-Tarski representation
papers.abstract: In this paper we continue the work started in [Bonzio & Zamperlin 2025] by investigating the algebraic semantics for modal external weak Kleene logics. In order to do so we study the global modal logics associated with the three-valued Kripke models introduced in the previous article, showing how these systems are algebraizable. We proceed by defining their algebraic counterparts, obtaining the classes of modal Bochvar and modal Halldén algebras, whose structure theory we investigate via Płonka sum decomposition. Of particular interested is the interaction of the modal operator with the homorphisms of the Płonka decomposition. These results allow us to prove representation theorems for these expanded modal algebras in the style of the Jónsson-Tarski representation for Boolean algebras with operators. As a consequence, we also obtain algebraic semnatics for the local modal logics from which the work originated.

papers.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
papers.abstract: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions. Using numerical simulations, we show how parameters such as the size of the system, the average degree of the nodes and the strength of the interactions alter the behaviour of the transition to synchronization with respect to the known theoretical results that are derived for globally coupled infinite systems.

papers.title: Regularity of planar Griffith minimizers with connected cracks through a monotonicity formula
papers.abstract: We prove a new monotonicity formula for the two-dimensional Neumann elasticity equation with connected boundary. From this we deduce a regularity result for two-dimensional minimizers of the Griffith energy with connected crack set: the crack may be partitioned into regular points, triple junctions, and cracktips. We give a classification of the global minimizers of the Griffith energy with connected crack set. Finally, we discuss some consequences of the monotonicity formula on the evolution of the stress intensity factors along a crack, which may present independent interest.

papers.title: Solver-Free Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Edge Selection
papers.abstract: Decision-focused learning trains prediction models to improve downstream decisions, but many methods require costly solver calls or optimal-solution labels. We propose a solver-free decision-focused learning framework for NP-hard edge-selection problems with uncertain parameters in the objective, the constraints, or both. A neural optimization layer is first trained without solution labels, using problem objectives and constraint penalties. Graph-informed edge scoring and iterative refinement encourage concentrated and structurally consistent continuous decisions. The layer is then frozen, and a prediction model is trained through its continuous output using a problem-specific loss evaluated under observed parameters. At deployment, the predictor, optimization layer, and a lightweight decoder produce decisions without solving the original NP-hard problem. Experiments on the asymmetric traveling salesperson and endpoint-free orienteering problems show consistently better decision quality than prediction-focused learning and improvements over most evaluated decision-focused baselines. Our framework requires less training time than the evaluated decision-focused baselines, even when optimization-layer pretraining is included. Neural deployment also produces decisions faster than solver-based deployment, offering a better quality-efficiency trade-off. The layer also reduces training cost in existing decision-focused methods when used as an approximate optimization oracle.

papers.title: Can a Language Model Write the Weights? An Empirical Study of LLM-Written Scoring Networks for Column Generation and MILP Branching, with a Bus-Driver Scheduling Application
papers.abstract: This paper was generated by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic) under the author's direction; all results come from computations run on the author's machine, and every reference was checked. Weight-space programming (WSP) is the idea that a large language model (LLM) can write the weights of a small neural network directly, guided only by reading forward-pass outputs, with no gradient training. We test whether WSP can improve exact operations research algorithms where they rely on cheap scoring rules. In four studies, an LLM wrote small multilayer perceptrons that (i) select arcs, labels and ng-neighbourhoods inside column generation for the vehicle routing problem with time windows, and (ii) choose branching variables in SCIP's branch-and-bound. The algorithms stay exact whatever the weights; a bad network only costs time. In column generation, no lever gave a material gain. In branching on synthetic classes, a hand-written network solved independent-set instances in 0.37x the time of SCIP's default rule (18 paired instances, Wilcoxon $p<10^{-5}$) and matched or beat networks trained by imitation of strong branching, but on 39 MIPLIB 2017 instances it solved 19 versus 24. In an application built from the real GTFS feed of Atlanta's transit agency (MARTA), a crew scheduling set-partitioning model solved by a native C plugin with SCIP's factory settings, the LLM-written rules took 0.63x the default's time on 32 held-out instances ($p<10^{-4}$), but SCIP's plain pseudocost rule did exactly as well (ratio 0.99, $p=0.19$). In these settings, the gains came from being cheap, not from what the LLM wrote. All code, logs and the numbers behind every figure are released.

papers.title: The splitting of the stable space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms
papers.abstract: We prove that the space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms on a smooth $G$-manifold $M$ has a tom Dieck style splitting, after stabilization. As an intermediate step, we introduce a space of isovariant $h$-cobordisms on $M$ and prove that this space also has a splitting, even before stabilizing. This completes the proof of the equivariant version of Waldhausen's stable parametrized $h$-cobordism theorem. Along the way, we establish several foundational results on equivariant smooth manifolds with corners.

papers.title: Supercuspidal and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of cardinality $q$, and let $(K_n)$ be a tower of principal congruence subgroups attached to a lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in the Lie algebra. We show that the proportion of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors carried by supercuspidal representations is $δ_{\mathrm{ell}}(Λ)+O(q^{-n/4})$, where the elliptic density $δ_{\mathrm{ell}}(Λ)>0$ is the probability that a random element of the dual lattice $Λ$ is nonzero on the Lie algebra of the unipotent radical of every proper parabolic subgroup. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$ this limit was anticipated by Howe. The error improves to $O(q^{-τn/4})$ with an explicit $τ\in(1,2]$, except when $\mathrm{char}\,F=2$ and $\mathbf{G}$ has an isotropic direct factor which over $\bar F$ is a product of adjoint groups of type $\mathrm{B}_d$. We determine when $δ_{\mathrm{ell}}(Λ)=1$, give an explicit bound uniform in $F$ for reductive models, and deduce a bound uniform over the completions of a global field. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis on congruence quotients, a quantitative Sard theorem for parabolic incidence maps and a Jacquet-module argument; it uses neither a classification of supercuspidal representations nor the exponential map.

papers.title: M-Estimation in Censored Regression Model under Endogeneity
papers.abstract: This paper develops a general M-estimation framework for censored regression models under endogeneity. A two-stage estimation is proposed to address the issue of endogeneity in the first stage and the issue of censoring in linear regression models in the second stage. The issue of endogeneity is addressed via instrumental variables using the control function approach. The issue of censoring in linear regression models is addressed via M-estimation using a suitably defined class of loss functions yielding a class of estimators. Thus, the proposed general M-estimation framework nests several existing estimators as special cases for the respective loss functions. Moreover, this provides flexibility of accommodating a broad range of robust loss functions that have not previously been studied in the context of censored regression. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the proposed class of estimators. An empirical study based on simulated datasets is conducted to illustrate general M-estimation for various choices of loss functions and to examine the finite-sample performance of various resulting estimators.

papers.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
papers.abstract: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $λ$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $λ\ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $λ\ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

papers.title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
papers.abstract: We present a data-driven representation of the finite-horizon behavior of deterministic controllable continuous-time LTI systems. We first introduce a notion of persistency of excitation for continuous-time signals that does not require the signal to be differentiable. We then show that, when the input is persistently exciting in this sense, the closure of the range of a Hankel integral operator built from a single input-output trajectory equals the behavior of the system over a finite time horizon. This result provides a nonparametric representation of system trajectories directly in terms of measured data, without requiring an explicit parametric model of the system.

papers.title: Singular Vortex in the Large Deviation of Empirical Current for Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process
papers.abstract: We prove a large deviation estimate for singular current observables of the two-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process. In particular, the observable has a non-standard large deviation scaling $N^2(\log N)^{-1}$ due to the presence of singular vortices, whereby trajectories rotating near the origin point yield an enhanced contribution to the current observable. The proof combines the heuristics of Bodineau-Derrida-Lebowitz 2008, the averaging method of Jara-Menezes 2018, and novel cancellation and multi-scale renormalization arguments developed by this paper.

papers.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
papers.abstract: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).

papers.title: Mutual-visibility in (d, 5)-graphs with excess
papers.abstract: The author investigates mutual visibility in regular graphs of girth at least 5, with particular emphasis on graphs with excess. A general upper bound on the mutual-visibility number is established in terms of the degree and order. More significantly, an algebraic inequality is derived that restricts the mutual-visibility number of $(d,5,+δ)$-graphs. As applications, the mutual-visibility number of the Robertson graph is shown to be 9, and upper bounds are obtained for the $(5,5)$-cages and the $(6,5)$-cage.

papers.title: Angular Besov Refinement of the Spherical Stein--Tomas Theorem
papers.abstract: The spherical Stein--Tomas inequality maps $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$ into $L^4(\mathbb R^3)$. We study its refinement in which the angular input is measured by the strictly weaker Besov norm $B^0_{2,4}(\mathbb S^2)$. The central separated-band inequality bounds the squared $L^2$ norm of the product of extensions from degrees $L\ll K$ by $C(L/K)$ times the squared input norms. An exact spherical-Hankel expansion controls the far field, while angular-momentum leakage and transversality handle the Fresnel region. We construct scale-separated, normalized angular bands for which the extension norm is equivalent to the $\ell^4$ norm of the coefficients. This proves that the fourth-power summation is optimal and quantitatively distinguishes the result from the classical $\ell^2$ summation. As an application, small angular Besov data generate small $L^4$ solutions to the cubic nonlinear Helmholtz equation in $\mathbb R^3$, with a smallness condition that remains sharp on multiscale data even when their $L^2$ norm is arbitrarily large or infinite. The associated on-shell nonlinear scattering amplitude has improved angular $B^0_{2,4/3}$ regularity, and its leading cubic term is quantitatively decoupled across widely separated angular bands.

papers.title: The probability that a branching random walk does not hit a point
papers.abstract: We study the probability that a branching random walk in ${\bf Z}^d$ driven by a Galton-Watson tree conditioned to have $n$ vertices does not hit a fixed point. For $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this probability behaves like $n^{-α/4}$ in logarithmic scale, where $α=4$ when $d=1$, $α=2\sqrt{2}$ when $d=2$, and $α=(\sqrt{17}-1)/2$ when $d=3$.

papers.title: Sharper energy scaling bounds of the singularly perturbed Tartar square
papers.abstract: In this article, we discuss the scaling behaviour of the singularly perturbed Tartar square, revisiting the results by [Rüland-Tribuzio '22]. Therein, it was proven that both lower and upper bounds satisfy a behaviour of the same type, up to a small mismatch of logarithmic powers. We show by an improvement of the ansatz free lower bound that the logarithmic powers indeed match and that the bounds are of order $\exp( - C \log(\varepsilon^{-1})^{1/2} )$ for suitable constants $C = C_{\rm low}$ and $C = C_{\rm upp}$, where $\varepsilon$ denotes the singular perturbation parameter. More specifically, the bootstrap argument in the Fourier space is refined by resorting to Fourier multipliers enjoying $L^\infty$-bounds which are constructed via de la Vallée Poussin kernels. Regarding upper bounds, we perform iterated branching constructions sharpening the upper bound of [Winter '97] which resorted to an iteration of laminates as a competitor. Eventually, the mismatch of upper and lower bound is quantified, and for quadratic energies we obtain the bounds $C_{\rm low} \leq 7.0339$ and $C_{\rm upp} \geq 2 \log(2) - ν$ for any $ν>0$.

papers.title: The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in $L_\infty$
papers.abstract: We settle the uniform small deviation conjecture for the Brownian sheet in every dimension $d\ge2$, namely, that the logarithmic exponent is $2d-1$. Our proof proceeds through sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates for the associated anchored mixed Sobolev embedding in the uniform norm. Their connection to small deviations is known from the Kuelbs--Li theorem. To establish the entropy estimates, the key is a probabilistic small ball inequality for smooth tensor product atoms whose exceptional set has Gaussian measure exponentially small in the number of atoms. Its proof combines a count of dyadic rectangles with tools from probability, in particular Ehrhard's Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality. This also yields sharp entropy and Kolmogorov number estimates for embeddings of periodic mixed Sobolev, Besov and Nikol'skii classes with smoothness $r>1/2$ in $L_\infty$.
