papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a monoid and let $G$ denote its quotient groupoid. We introduce the Riemann-Zariski space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ associated with $H$ and prove that it is a spectral space. We then show that, if $H$ is an $s$-Prüfer monoid, the space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ is homeomorphic to the prime $s$-spectrum of $H$ endowed with the Zariski topology. Next, given a finitary ideal system $r$ on $H$, we prove that the space of $r$-ideals $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$, endowed with the Zariski topology, is spectral, and that the prime $r$-spectrum of $H$ is proconstructible in $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$. We also introduce a new topology on the set $\mathcal{X}$ of all generalized $H$-module systems and study its properties. In particular, we show that $\mathcal{X}$ and its subspace $\mathcal{X}_{\textup{fin}}$ of finitary generalized $H$-module systems are spectral spaces. Finally, we provide a characterization of those subsets of the set of overmonoids of $H$ that are quasi-compact.

papers.title: Novel technique based on Léja Points Approximation for Log-determinant Estimation of Large matrices
papers.abstract: The computation of the Log-determinant of large, sparse, symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices is essential in many scientific computational fields such as numerical linear algebra and machine learning. In low dimensions, Cholesky is preferred, but in high dimensions, its computation may be prohibitive due to memory limitation. To circumvent this, Krylov subspace techniques have proven to be efficient but may be computationally expensive due to the required orthogonalization processes. In this paper, we introduce a Newton-Léja interpolation based approach for estimating log-determinants, where the implementation is only based on matrix multiplications and a rough estimation of eigenvalue bounds of the matrix. The method employs an adaptive stopping criterion to select the degree of interpolation according to the data and introduces a centered, scaled-based formulation for computing the logarithmic divided differences. By combining Newton-Léja interpolation with a randomized algorithm called Hutch++, we obtain a matrix-free log-determinant estimation framework that avoids explicit matrix factorization and Krylov basis orthogonalization. We establish approximation error bounds for the Newton-Léja interpolation and derive an inexact oracle error bound that separates stochastic trace estimation from the approximation errors in the projected and residual components. Numerical experiments on both large sparse synthetic matrices (Gaussian Markov Random fields) and large-scale real-world matrices demonstrate that our method substantially reduces computational time while retaining competitive accuracy, thereby confirming its effectiveness, scalability, and favorable accuracy-cost trade-off for large-scale log-determinant estimation compared with stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ) and related stochastic trace-estimation methods.

papers.title: Revisiting the Algebraic and Analytic Descriptions of Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: The Wintner-Wielandt theorem exposes a fundamental incompatibility between the canonical commutation relation (CCR) and the Hilbert-space formulation of quantum mechanics. While the conventional approach preserves the CCR by extending the Hilbert-space framework to a rigged Hilbert space, this work develops the complementary alternative. Retaining the Hilbert space, the unavoidable trace obstruction requires a boundary modification of the CCR, consistently realizable only in a space of finite, albeit arbitrarily large, dimension. In this setting, the eigenvalue problems of position and momentum admit explicit solutions within the Hilbert space. We show that the highest-energy components of the position eigenvectors retain a non-vanishing uniform weight, implying that the full spectrum remains relevant. The resulting autonomous matrix algebra also yields a new physical observable, the action difference. In the position basis, this observable gives rise to a momentum matrix with a discrete Cauchy kernel. After an alternating phase transformation, this matrix acts on plane waves in the infinite equidistant lattice model as the Schroedinger momentum operator, revealing a structural connection between the algebraic and analytic approaches. This framework retains the standard Hilbert-space spectral theory and remains closely connected to the familiar analytical structure of quantum mechanics, including the momentum operator and the uncertainty principle.

papers.title: A family of matrix flows converging to normal matrices
papers.abstract: The celebrated Antezana-Pujals-Stojanoff Theorem states that the iterated Aluthge transforms of an arbitrary matrix converge to a normal matrix. We introduce a family of matrix flows that share this convergence property by defining them through ordinary differential equations. The family includes a continuous analogue of the Aluthge transform, as well as a differential equation discussed by Haagerup in the context of II$_1$ factors. We also examine the same type of flows in the setting of Hilbert space operators equipped with unitarily invariant norms.

papers.title: Soft-Radial Projection for Constrained End-to-End Learning
papers.abstract: Constrained end-to-end learning trains neural networks whose outputs must satisfy feasibility constraints, such as resource, budget, or operational limits. While projection and optimization layers guarantee constraint satisfaction, boundary-based projections can introduce unfavorable optimization geometry: regions of the unconstrained output space are mapped to the same active face of the feasible set. This makes the resulting map locally rank-deficient, suppressing gradients in constrained directions and potentially impairing optimization - a bottleneck known as gradient saturation. We propose Soft-Radial Projection (SRP), a differentiable reparameterization layer that maps unconstrained network outputs into the relative interior of a convex feasible set by smoothly rescaling rays from a strictly feasible anchor point. Unlike hard radial or orthogonal projections, the resulting map is one-to-one and has a full-rank Jacobian almost everywhere, while guaranteeing strict feasibility. We prove that constrained networks equipped with SRP retain universal approximation guarantees. For polytopes and balls, the layer admits a closed-form forward pass, while for general convex sets, the ray-boundary intersection reduces to a one-dimensional search. Experiments on decision-focused learning benchmarks demonstrate strong solution quality at low computational cost, with particularly favorable results in portfolio optimization and substantially lower inference latency than differentiable optimization layers in the evaluated settings.

papers.title: The symmetrized sum of finite $q$-multiple harmonic sums with one exceptional index
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give explicit expressions for $q$-harmonic sums on $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ indices. The case $A=1$ has been extensively studied, and a variety of identities, explicit evaluations, and structural properties are known. Likewise, numerous explicit evaluations are available for $q$-multiple zeta values and $q$-harmonic sums with uniform indices $A-\cdots-A$. Although several methods are available for treating non-uniform indices, explicit evaluations for the pattern $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ remain comparatively scarce. The case $A=2$ was settled only recently. In this paper, we extend this framework to the general case $A\ge3$ as the total sum with the theory of the elementary symmetric functions, though we do not generally evaluate each summand at a prescribed position of $A$. We obtain explicit formulas in terms of binomial coefficients and degenerate Bernoulli numbers. Some expressions about $2-\cdots-2,A,2-\cdots-2$ are also shown.

papers.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
papers.abstract: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-δ})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $δ>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.

papers.title: Surrogate-based Optimization via Clustering for Box-Constrained Problems
papers.abstract: Global optimization of large-scale, complex systems such as multi-physics black-box simulations and real-world industrial systems is important but challenging. This work presents a novel Surrogate-Based Optimization framework based on Clustering, SBOC for global optimization of such systems, which can be used with any surrogate modeling technique. At each iteration, it uses a single surrogate model for the entire domain, employs k-means clustering to identify unexplored domain, and exploits a local region around the surrogate optimum to potentially add three new sample points in the domain. SBOC has been tested against sixteen promising benchmarking algorithms using 52 analytical test functions of varying input dimensionalities and shape profiles. It successfully identified a global minimum for most test functions with substantially lower computational effort than other algorithms. It worked especially well on test functions with four or more input variables. It was also among the top six algorithms in approaching a global minimum closely. Overall, SBOC is a robust, reliable, and efficient algorithm for global optimization of box-constrained systems.

papers.title: Matrix Factorization Framework for Community Detection under the Degree-Corrected Block Model
papers.abstract: Community detection is a fundamental task in data analysis, and block models provide an approach for identifying diverse community structures. The degree-corrected block model (DCBM) is an established model that captures node degree heterogeneity. However, inference methods are computationally costly and sensitive to initialization, while cheaper alternatives, such as spectral or modularity-based approaches, may be less effective at recovering certain non-assortative structures. In this work, we show that DCBM inference can be reformulated as a constrained nonnegative matrix trifactorization problem. Leveraging this insight, we propose a scalable community detection method with a theoretically grounded initialization providing an initial partition for inference algorithms. Our approach is agnostic to network structure and applies to any graph representable by a DCBM. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmark networks show that our method achieves community recovery comparable to, and sometimes better than, that achieved by the DCBM inference methods, while being faster: it processes a graph with 100,000 nodes and 500,000 edges in about 30 seconds. Moreover, the initialization significantly improves solution quality. Overall, this work provides a scalable and robust framework for community detection and highlights the benefits of a matrix-factorization perspective for the DCBM.

papers.title: Piecewise Smooth Dynamical Systems Regularized by Convolution
papers.abstract: We present a general regularization procedure for piecewise smooth vector fields whose discontinuity locus is a variety of normal crossings type. We show that such regularization can be smoothed through a finite sequence of blowings-up, thereby reducing the problem to the study of the dynamics of a smooth vector field in a manifold with corners. The procedure will be illustrated in the cases of piecewise smooth vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with discontinuity locus $x=0$ or $xy=0$, and on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with discontinuity locus $xyz=0$. We will see that some unexpected dynamical phenomena such as Bogdanov-Takens bifurcations and Bykov cycles may arise even in the case of piecewise constant vector fields.

papers.title: Cyclic sieving phenomena for trees and tree-rooted maps
papers.abstract: We prove cyclic sieving phenomena satisfied by corner-rooted plane trees (alias ordered trees). The sets of rooted plane trees that we consider are: (1) all trees with $n$ nodes; (2) all trees with $n$ nodes and $k$ leaves; (3) all trees with a given degree distribution of the nodes. Moreover, we consider four different cyclic group actions: (1) the root is moved to the next corner along a tour of the tree; (2) only trees in which the root is at a leaf are considered, and the action moves the root to the next leaf; (3) only trees in which the root is at a non-leaf are considered, and the action moves the root to the next non-leaf corner; (4) only trees in which the root is at a node of degree $δ$ are considered, for a fixed $δ$, and the action moves the root to the next corner of this type. We prove a cyclic sieving phenomenon for each meaningful combination of these sets and actions. As a bonus, we also establish corresponding cyclic sieving phenomena for tree-rooted planar maps.

papers.title: Cellular free resolutions for normalizations of toric ideals
papers.abstract: For any toric ideal $I$ in a polynomial ring $S$, we provide a combinatorial description of a free resolution of the integral closure of the $S$-module $S/I$. These new complexes arise from an extension of Bayer--Sturmfels' theory of cellular free resolutions. As applications, we unify several constructions for a resolution of the diagonal embedding of a toric variety, and compare the locally free resolutions for toric subvarieties introduced by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev and Brown--Erman.

papers.title: Absolute incidence theorems and tilings
papers.abstract: We give a precise definition of incidence theorems in plane projective geometry and introduce the notion of absolute incidence theorems, which hold over any ring. Fomin and Pylyavskyy describe how to obtain incidence theorems from tilings of an orientable surface; they call this result the master theorem. Instances of the master theorem are always absolute incidence theorems. As most classically known incidence theorems are instances of the master theorem, they are absolute incidence theorems. We give an explicit example of an incidence theorem involving 13 points that is not an absolute incidence theorem, and therefore is not an instance of the master theorem.

papers.title: Regularity for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate dead-core problems for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption, \begin{equation*} |Du|^{p} F(D^{2}u) - u_{t} = λ_{0}(x,t)\, u^μ\, χ_{\{u>0\}}(x,t) \qquad \text{in } \quad Ω_{T} := Ω\times (0,T), \end{equation*} where $0\le p<\infty$, $0<μ<1$ and $u \geq 0 $ is a bounded viscosity solution satisfying $0\le u_t\le A_0u^μ$ in the viscosity sense for some $0\le A_0<\infty$. We establish a sharp and improved parabolic $C^α$-regularity estimate along the free boundary $\partial \{ u > 0 \}$, where \[ α:= \frac{2+p}{1+p-μ} > 1 + \frac{1}{1+p}. \] Moreover, we establish weak geometric properties of solutions, such as non-degeneracy and uniform positive density. As an application, we obtain a Liouville-type theorem for entire solutions and gradient bounds. Finally, as a byproduct of our approach, we derive a new formulation of the gradient decay property and establish a Harnack-type inequality on time slices. It is worth noting that the results presented here extend those in da Silva {\em et al.}(Pacific J. Math., \textbf{300} (2019), 179--213) and (J. Differential Equations., \textbf{264} (2018), 7270--7293) to the degenerate setting, and can be viewed as a parabolic analogue of da Silva {\em et al.} (Math. Nachr., \textbf{294} (2021), 38--55) and Teixeira (Math. Ann., \textbf{364} (2016), 1121--1134).

papers.title: Sharp Convergence to the Half-Space for Mullins-Sekerka in the Plane
papers.abstract: We revisit the HED Method for the Mullins-Sekerka evolution in the plane. We identify a natural notion of distance, intrinsic to the interface itself. Using this distance, the energy, and the dissipation, we develop natural assumptions on the flow and, assuming existence of a solution satisfying these conditions, obtain not just the algebraic rate (already previously derived by Chugreeva, Otto, and M.G. Westdickenberg) but also the sharp leading order constant for the convergence to the flat limiting interface. To carry this out, we introduce a lemma that obtains optimal algebraic decay behavior (rate and prefactor) from given variational information.

papers.title: Exponential Decays of Steklov Eigenfunctions for the Magnetic Laplacian
papers.abstract: Consider the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $Λ_β$ associated with the Schrödinger operator $(D+β\A)^2$ with a magnetic potential in a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$, where $β>1$ is the field strength parameter. Assume that the magnetic field $\B=\nabla \times \A$ is of finite type. We show that if $β>β_0$, the ground state for $Λ_β$ decays exponentially away from a neighborhood of the subset of $\partialΩ$, on which $\B$ vanishes to the maximal order.

papers.title: Optimal Dividend, Reinsurance and Capital-Injection Strategies for Collaborating Business Lines: The Case of Excess-of-Loss Reinsurance
papers.abstract: This paper considers an insurer with two collaborating business lines that must make three critical decisions: (1) dividend payout, (2) a combination of proportional and excess-of-loss reinsurance coverage, and (3) capital injection between the lines. The reserve level of each line is modeled using a diffusion approximation, and the insurer aims to maximize the weighted total discounted dividends paid until the first ruin time. We obtain the value function and the optimal strategies in explicit or semi-explicit form. We then prove that the optimal dividend payout strategy for bounded dividend rates is of threshold type, while for unbounded dividend rates it is of barrier type. Under the diffusion approximation, the optimal combination of proportional and excess-of-loss reinsurance is shown to be pure excess-of-loss reinsurance. We also show that the optimal level of risk ceded to the reinsurer decreases as the aggregate reserve level increases, and that reinsurance is phased out line by line. The optimal capital-injection strategy involves transferring reserves to prevent the ruin of one line. Finally, numerical examples are presented to illustrate these optimal strategies.

papers.title: Phase transition for conditional covariance matrices estimated by importance sampling, and implications for cross-entropy schemes in high dimension
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent high-dimensional reliability algorithms, we study a random matrix model corresponding to the estimation by importance sampling of $Σ_A$, the covariance matrix of a Gaussian vector conditioned by a rare event $A$. For such models, we show that, in contrast to most random matrix models, the minimal sample size to ensure an accurate estimation of $Σ_A$ needs to grow superlinearly in the dimension. More precisely, if $n$ is the sample size and $d$ the dimension, we show that the estimation of $Σ_A$ is accurate if $n/d \gg L$ and not accurate if $n/d \ll L$ where $L$ is the maximum likelihood ratio. Moreover, we relate the asymptotic behavior of $L$ to $λ_1$, the smallest eigenvalue of the auxiliary covariance matrix, which suggests that $L$ (and thus the minimal sample size) will be larger for small values of $λ_1$. Numerical experiments confirm that this insight carries over to recent cross-entropy algorithms, with the best performing algorithms being also the ones with the largest smallest eigenvalue. Although backed up by our theoretical result, this result is surprising as these algorithms were not designed to act on the spectrum.

papers.title: Semibricks and wide subcategories in extended module categories
papers.abstract: For $d\geq 1$, we define semibricks and wide subcategories in the $d$-extended hearts of bounded $t$-structures on a triangulated category. We show that these semibricks are in bijection with finite-length wide subcategories. When the $d$-extended heart is the $d$-extended module category $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}Λ$ of a finite-dimensional algebra $Λ$ over a field, we define left/right-finite semibricks and left/right-finite wide subcategories in $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}Λ$ and show bijections with $(d+1)$-term simple-minded collections, generalising the bijections between $2$-term simple-minded collections, left/right-finite wide subcategories and left/right-finite semibricks in $\mathrm{mod}Λ$. We use a relation between semibricks and silting complexes to characterise which mutations of $(d+1)$-term silting complexes are again $(d+1)$-term.

papers.title: Embedding Calculus, Goodwillie Calculus and Link Invariants
papers.abstract: We study Goodwillie-Weiss embedding calculus through its relationship with Goodwillie's functor calculus. Specifically, building on a result of Tillmann and Weiss, we construct a functorial complement for \(T_{n}\)-embeddings that takes values in Heuts's categorical \(n\)-excisive approximation of pointed spaces. We also establish an analogue of Stallings' theorem for lower central series in the context of \(T_{n}\)-embeddings of \(P \times I\) into \(D^{d}\) for any compact manifold \(P\). As an application, we show that the embedding tower of string links detects Milnor invariants.

papers.title: Optimal In-context Adaptivity and Distributional Robustness of Transformers
papers.abstract: We study in-context learning problems where a Transformer is pretrained on tasks drawn from a mixture distribution $π=\sum_{α\in\mathcal{A}} λ_α π_α$, called the pretraining prior, in which each mixture component $π_α$ is a distribution on tasks of a specific difficulty level indexed by $α$. Our goal is to understand the performance of the pretrained Transformer when evaluated on a different test distribution $μ$, consisting of tasks of fixed difficulty $β\in\mathcal{A}$, and with potential distribution shift relative to $π_β$, subject to the chi-squared divergence $χ^2(μ,π_β)$ being at most $κ$. In particular, we consider nonparametric regression problems with random smoothness, and multi-index models with both random smoothness and random effective dimension. We prove that a large Transformer pretrained on sufficient data achieves the optimal rate of convergence corresponding to the difficulty level $β$, uniformly over test distributions $μ$ in the chi-squared divergence ball. Thus, the pretrained Transformer is able to achieve faster rates of convergence on easier tasks and is robust to distribution shift at test time. Finally, we prove that even if an estimator had access to the test distribution $μ$, the convergence rate of its expected risk over $μ$ could not be faster than that of our pretrained Transformers, thereby providing a more appropriate optimality guarantee than minimax lower bounds.

papers.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
papers.abstract: In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process. The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-Łojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points. In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general Łojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.

papers.title: Stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics and its zero-mass limit
papers.abstract: We introduce a stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics with positive mass and study its zero--mass limit. The new aspect of this paper is that we only fix the initial and terminal probability distributions of the positions of particles under consideration, but not those of their velocities, with Heisenberg's uncertainty principle in mind. In the zero--mass limit, we show that the minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is tight if and only if the initial momentum (=(mass)$\times$(velocity)) of a particle converges to zero. We also prove that the limit of minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is a minimizer of a standard stochastic optimal transport for continuous semimartingales.

papers.title: Galois Action and Localization in Number Fields
papers.abstract: For a Galois number field $K$, the Galois group $\text{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$ acts on the class group $\text{Cl}_K$ in a very natural way: $σ\cdot[I]=[σ(I)]$ for any $σ\in \text{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$, $[I]\in \text{Cl}_K$. In this paper, we will explore how the unique properties of this group action work together to elucidate the relationship between these two groups -- developing and expanding upon some known results from a new perspective. To this end, we explore the class groups of localizations of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. These turn out to be powerful tools for understanding $\text{Cl}_K$ and overrings of $\mathcal{O}_K$. The paper concludes with some interesting observations about normset arithmetic and complexity -- topics intimately related to this action.

papers.title: A depth-zero principal-series block whose Hecke algebra has a non-trivial two-cocycle
papers.abstract: Recently the authors have shown that every Hecke algebra associated to a type constructed by Kim and Yu is isomorphic to a Hecke algebra for a depth-zero type. An example in the literature has been suggested as a counterexample to this result. We show that the example is not a counterexample, and exhibit some of its interesting properties, e.g., we show that a principal series, depth-zero type can have a Hecke algebra with non-trivial two-cocyle, a phenomenon that many did not expect could occur.

papers.title: Decentralized Estimation and Control for Leader-Follower Networked Systems with Asymmetric Information Structure
papers.abstract: In this paper, the decentralized estimation and linear quadratic (LQ) control problem for a leader-follower networked system (LFNS) is studied from the perspective of asymmetric information. Specifically, for a leader-follower network, the follower agent will be affected by the leader agent, while the follower agent will not affect the leader agent. Hence, the information sets accessed by the control variables of the leader agent and the follower agent are asymmetric, which will bring essential difficulties in finding the optimal control strategy. To this end, the orthogonal decomposition method is adopted to achieve the main results. The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: Firstly, the optimal iterative estimation is derived using the conditional independence property established in this paper. Secondly, the optimal decentralized control strategy is derived by decoupling the forward-backward stochastic difference equations (FBSDEs), based on the derived optimal iterative estimation. Thirdly, the necessary and sufficient conditions for the feedback stabilization of the LFNS in infinite-horizon are derived. Finally, the proposed theoretical results are applied to solve the decentralized control problem of a leader-follower autonomous underwater vehicle (LF-AUV) system. The optimal control inputs for the AUVs are provided, and simulation results verify the effectiveness of the obtained results.

papers.title: Certified Monodromy Groups for Families of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: The monodromy group of a family of algebraic varieties is the group of isometries of the homology of a generic fibre, induced by parallel transport along a loop in the base space. We present a method to compute the monodromy group of families of generically smooth projective hypersurfaces using certified numerical algebraic geometry. This leads us to develop efficient algorithms for computing the discriminants of these families, which is of independent interest. Our flagship example is the case of families of symmetric cubic surfaces. The monodromy group is the Galois group of the 27 lines. We find that, when imposing symmetry, this Galois group is often a small subgroup of the Weyl group $W(E_6)$. We also include computational results for symmetric quartic surfaces.

papers.title: Differentiable Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: The efficient computation of parametric solution sensitivities is a key challenge in the integration of learning-enhanced methods with nonlinear model predictive control, as their availability is crucial for many learning algorithms. This paper discusses the computation of solution sensitivities of general nonlinear programs using the implicit function theorem and smoothed optimality conditions treated in interior-point methods (IPM). We introduce sequential barrier quadratic programming (SBQP), which generalizes SQP with an IPM quadratic programming (QP) solver by allowing the barrier parameter to approach a prescribed nonnegative target value, recovering classical SQP when this target is zero. Previous works are limited to convex or unconstrained formulations, or lack an implementation for efficient sensitivity evaluation. The publication is accompanied by an efficient open-source implementation within the `acados` framework, providing both forward and adjoint sensitivities for general optimal control problems, achieving speedups exceeding 3x over the state-of-the-art solvers `mpc.pytorch` and `cvxpygen`.

papers.title: On the regularity of entropy solutions to stochastic degenerate parabolic equations
papers.abstract: We study the regularity of entropy solutions for quasilinear parabolic equations with anisotropic degeneracy and stochastic forcing. Building on previous works, we establish space-time regularity under a non-degeneracy condition that does not require an assumption on the derivative of the symbol of the corresponding kinetic equation, a restriction imposed in earlier studies. This allows us to obtain regularity results for certain equations not accounted for by prior theory, albeit with reduced regularity exponents. Our approach uses a kinetic formulation with two transport equations, one of second order and one of first order, leveraging a form of "parabolic regularity" inherent in these equations that was not utilized in previous studies.

papers.title: Rough Heston model as the scaling limit of bivariate cumulative heavy-tailed INAR processes: Weak-error bounds and option pricing
papers.abstract: We study nearly unstable bivariate cumulative heavy-tailed INAR($\infty$) processes and show that, under a one-factor parameterization and a suitable scaling, they converge to the rough Heston model. This yields a discrete-time microstructural route to the joint price-variance dynamics and gives explicit formulas linking the INAR asymmetry parameters to the leverage correlation and diffusion scale of the limiting volatility process. For pricing, we reduce the exact finite-$τ$ Fourier--Laplace transform recursion to a quadratic discrete Volterra equation and compare it with the rough Heston fractional Riccati equation. Under a transform-strip condition for the continuous model and bounded-Riccati regularity, every fixed bounded frequency window admits a uniform transform-error bound of order $τ^{-α}+τ^{-(1-α)}$. The finite-$τ$ transform is entire, and a uniform exponential-moment estimate then removes the Fourier cutoff and yields convergence of the exact, untruncated call prices. We also develop an FFT-accelerated CDQ simulator with $\mathcal O(τ\log^2τ)$ complexity per path and use it to price European and path-dependent options, benchmark the Markovian case $α=1$, and analyze the model-implied volatility surface.

papers.title: Kernel Metrics and Learning for Borel MDPs: Identifiability and Adaptive Control
papers.abstract: We consider a Markov decision process with standard Borel spaces and an unknown transition kernel under the average cost criterion. We do not impose any parametrization on the set of possible kernels. To facilitate our analysis, we first develop implication relations between several topologies on kernels defined by pointwise, continuous, or uniform weak convergence; we then review robustness properties on the space of kernels, and finally we establish compactness conditions on the space of kernels. Building on this regularity analysis, we then present two data-driven identifiability results; the first one being Bayesian and the second one empirical. Our conditions for the Bayesian setting are significantly more relaxed compared with prior work which considered either finite or parametric models, though we do not obtain a rate of convergence. Our analysis is asymptotic and builds on measurability in terms of the tail $σ$-field of the available information. Identifiability results are then used to design near-optimal adaptive control policies which alternate between periods of exploration, where the controller acts according to a policy which is conducive to the identification of the true kernel, and periods of exploitation where the controller's information on the kernel is utilized. We will establish that such policies are near optimal. In summary, our contribution is with regard to the general standard Borel setup where there is no apriori parametric representation.

papers.title: Virtual double categories of relations relative to fibrations
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between virtual double categories and fibrations, or (hyper)doctrines, in the context of categorical logic. We present a construction that produces a virtual double category of relations internal to a fibration with finite products. We characterize the class of fibrations called elementary existential fibrations, a fibrational counterpart of regular logic, as those for which the induced virtual double category is a cartesian equipment. We also show that cartesian equipments arising in this manner are exactly those that satisfy the Frobenius axiom studied by Walters and Wood in the context of cartesian bicategories. Some logical principles, such as the comprehension axiom for predicates and the extensional equality predicate, are characterized as properties of the double categorical structure.

papers.title: The Yoneda embedding in simplicial type theory
papers.abstract: Riehl and Shulman introduced simplicial type theory (STT), a variant of homotopy type theory which aimed to study not just homotopy theory, but its fusion with category theory: $(\infty,1)$-category theory. While notoriously technical, manipulating $\infty$-categories in simplicial type theory is often easier than working with ordinary categories, with the type theory handling infinite stacks of coherences in the background. We capitalize on recent work by Gratzer et al. defining the $(\infty,1)$-category of $\infty$-groupoids in STT to define presheaf categories within STT and systematically develop their theory. In particular, we construct the Yoneda embedding, prove the universal property of presheaf categories, refine the theory of adjunctions in STT, introduce the theory of Kan extensions, and prove Quillen's Theorem A.

papers.title: Traits and tangles: An analysis of the Big Five paradigm by tangle-based clustering
papers.abstract: Using the recently developed mathematical theory of tangles, we re-assess the mathematical foundations for applications of the five factor model in personality tests by a new, mathematically rigorous, quantitative method. Our findings broadly confirm the validity of current tests, but also show that more detailed information can be extracted from existing data. We found that the big five traits appear at different levels of scrutiny. Some already emerge at a coarse resolution of our tools at which others cannot yet be discerned, while at a resolution where these _can_ be discerned, and distinguished, some of the former traits are no longer visible but have split into more refined traits or disintegrated altogether. We also identified traits other than the five targeted in those tests. These include more general traits combining two or more of the big five, as well as more specific traits refining some of them. All our analysis is structural and quantitative, and thus rigorous in explicitly defined mathematical terms. Since tangles, once computed, can be described concisely in terms of very few explicit statements referring only to the test questions used, our findings are also directly open to interpretation by experts in psychology. Tangle analysis can be applied similarly to other topics in psychology. Our paper is intended to serve as a first indication of what may be possible.

papers.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Brändén and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.

papers.title: Generalised Buchberger and Schreyer algorithms for strongly discrete coherent rings
papers.abstract: Let M be a finitely generated submodule of a free module over a multivariate polynomial ring with coefficients in a discrete coherent ring. We prove that its module MLT(M) of leading terms is countably generated and give an algorithm for computing explicitly a generating set. This result is also useful when MLT(M) is not finitely generated. Suppose that the base ring is strongly discrete coherent. We provide a Buchberger-like algorithm and prove that it converges if and only if the module of leading terms is finitely generated. We also state a constructive version of Hilbert's syzygy theorem by following Schreyer's method.

papers.title: Matroid products via submodular coupling
papers.abstract: The study of matroid products traces back to the 1970s, when Lovász and Mason studied the existence of various types of matroid products with different strengths. Among these, the tensor product is arguably the most important, which can be considered as an extension of the tensor product from linear algebra. However, Las Vergnas showed that the tensor product of two matroids does not always exist. Over the following four decades, matroid products remained surprisingly underexplored, regaining attention only in recent years due to applications in tropical geometry and the limit theory of matroids. In this paper, inspired by the concept of coupling in probability theory, we introduce the notion of coupling for matroids -- or, more generally, for submodular set functions. This operation can be viewed as a relaxation of the tensor product. Unlike the tensor product, however, we prove that a coupling always exists for any two submodular functions and can be chosen to be increasing if the original functions are increasing. As a corollary, we show that two matroids always admit a matroid coupling, leading to a novel operation on matroids. Our construction is algorithmic, providing an oracle for the coupling matroid through a polynomial number of oracle calls to the original matroids. We apply this construction to derive new necessary conditions for matroid representability and establish connection between tensor products and Ingleton's inequality. Additionally, we verify the existence of set functions that are universal with respect to a given property, meaning any set function over a finite domain with that property can be obtained as a quotient.

papers.title: Identifying Drift, Diffusion, and Causal Structure from Temporal Snapshots
papers.abstract: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are a fundamental tool for modelling dynamic processes, including gene regulatory networks (GRNs), contaminant transport, financial markets, and image generation. However, learning the underlying SDE from data is a challenging task, especially if individual trajectories are not observable. Motivated by burgeoning research in single-cell datasets, we present the first comprehensive approach for jointly identifying the drift and diffusion of an SDE from its temporal marginals. Assuming linear drift and additive diffusion, we show that non-identifiability can only arise if the initial distribution possesses generalized rotational symmetries. We further prove that even if this condition holds, the drift and diffusion can almost always be recovered from the marginals. Additionally, we show that the causal graph of any SDE with additive diffusion can be recovered from the identified SDE parameters. To complement this theory, we adapt entropy-regularized optimal transport to handle anisotropic diffusion and introduce APPEX (Alternating Projection Parameter Estimation from $X_0$), an iterative algorithm designed to estimate the drift, diffusion, and causal graph of an additive noise SDE, solely from temporal marginals, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated data from linear additive noise SDEs.

papers.title: Best-Worst Disaggregation: An approach to the preference disaggregation problem
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Best-Worst Disaggregation (BWD) method, a novel approach that integrates the principles of the Best-Worst Method (BWM) into the disaggregation framework to enhance the consistency and reliability of derived preference models. An optimization model is formulated to determine the most suitable additive value function that fits the preferences expressed by a decision-maker or expert. The method incorporates a consistency analysis to quantify and improve the reliability of the judgments and is extended to handle interval-valued preferences. We also developed an approach to identify a reference set, which is used for pairwise comparisons to elicit the value functions and weights. A case study in logistics performance evaluation demonstrates the practicality and effectiveness of BWD. By coupling a structured human-elicitation protocol with an inference engine and a consistency-feedback loop, BWD provides a human-centered building block for evidence-sensitive decision-support systems

papers.title: Functional Extreme-PLS
papers.abstract: An extreme dimension reduction method is proposed, extending the Extreme-PLS approach to the discretized functional framework, where the covariate lies in the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space ($L^2([0,1])$) but is partially observed on a dense time grid. The ideas are partly borrowed from both Partial Least-Squares (PLS) and Sliced Inverse Regression (SIR) techniques. Accordingly, the method relies on the projection of the covariate onto a subspace and maximizes the covariance between its projection and the response conditionally on an extreme event capturing tail information. The covariate and the heavy-tailed response are supposed to be linked through a nonlinear inverse single-index model, and the objective is to infer the index in this regression framework. A new family of estimators is proposed, and its asymptotic consistency with convergence rates under the model is established. Assuming mild conditions on the noise, most of the assumptions are stated in terms of regular variation, unlike those commonly imposed for SIR and single-index regression. In addition, the theoretical analysis is expanded to include a model-free consistency result in probability for the empirical tail-moments in a general separable Hilbert space. Finally, the results are illustrated through a finite-sample study with synthetic functional data and high-frequency financial data, highlighting the effectiveness of the dimension reduction in capturing tail dependence and supporting extreme risk management.

papers.title: A uniform trigonometric R-matrix for the exceptional series
papers.abstract: The exceptional series is a finite list of points on a projective line with a simple Lie algebra attached to each point. This list of Lie algebras includes the five exceptional Lie algebras. We give a uniform trigonometric $R$-matrix for the exceptional series in the representation $L\oplus I$, where $L$ is the quantum deformation of the adjoint representation and $I$ is the trivial representation. We construct a sixteen dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit2)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^2(L\oplus I))$ and a 287 dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit3)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^3(L\oplus I))$. The $R$-matrix lives in $A^\square(\mathit2)$ and satisfies the Yang-Baxter equation in $A^\square(\mathit3)$; it interpolates the trigonometric $R$-matrices for the points in the exceptional series.

papers.title: Commutation relations for two-sided radial SLE
papers.abstract: We study the commutation relation for 2-radial SLE in the unit disc starting from two distinct boundary points. We follow the framework introduced by Dubédat~[12]. Under an additional requirement of the interchangeability of the two curves, we classify all locally commuting 2-radial SLE$_κ$ for $κ\in (0,8)$: it is either two-sided radial SLE$_κ$ with spiral of constant spiraling rate or chordal SLE$_κ$ weighted by a power of the conformal radius of its complement. Namely, for fixed $κ$ and starting points, we have exactly two one-parameter families of locally commuting 2-radial SLE curves. We also discuss the semiclassical limit of the commutation relation as $κ\to 0$. In particular, we show that the limit for the second family with an appropriately chosen power of the conformal radius is a chord that minimizes a modified chordal Loewner energy, which is unique only when the endpoints are not antipodal.

papers.title: Triple product $p$-adic $L$-functions for finite slope families and a $p$-adic Gross-Zagier formula
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize two results of H. Darmon and V. Rotger on triple product $p$-adic $L$-functions associated with Hida families to finite slope families. We first prove a $p$-adic Gross-Zagier formula, then demonstrate an application to a special case of the equivariant Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for supersingular elliptic curves.

papers.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
papers.abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.

papers.title: A GL(3) converse theorem via a "beyond endoscopy" approach
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the converse theorem for Maass forms on ${\rm GL}(3)$ using a technique that is inspired by Langlands' philosophy of "beyond endoscopy", thereby implementing these ideas for the first time in a higher rank setting.

papers.title: On local cohomology modules over ramified regular local rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show examples of local cohomology modules over ramified regular local ring, having finite set of associated primes. In doing so we consider our ramified regular local ring as Eisenstein extension of an unramified regular local ring sitting inside it. In ramified regular local ring for extended ideal (from the unramified one) set of associated primes of a local cohomology module is always finite. Using the Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, we construct examples of local cohomology of non extended ideal, whose set of associated primes is finite. In particular, we choose those non extended ideals whose minimal primes are extended ideals which are all cohomologically complete intersection.

papers.title: Qin's Algorithm, Continued Fractions and 2-dimensional Lattices
papers.abstract: In his ``Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections''(1247), Jiushao Qin introduced ``the Dayan method of deriving unity'' for computing modular inverses, an essential component of his treatment of the Chinese remainder theorem. A distinctive feature of Qin's algorithm is its use of a state consisting of four nonnegative integers arranged in a matrix. In this paper, we investigate the mathematical structure of these states and their connections with continued fractions and two-dimensional lattices. By introducing a signed version of the state, we obtain a natural matrix representation that reveals the convergents of continued fractions and gives direct derivations of several classical results. We then show that the signed states form bases of a family of two-dimensional lattices arising from modular congruences. In particular, we prove that a shortest lattice vector can be obtained from the rows of a signed state or their sum or difference. We also study the monotonicity of the inner products of the state vectors and discuss a subsequent result that locates a shortest vector in one of two consecutive states. It is surprising that a shortest lattice vector is found in a highly structure sequence of states. These results demonstrate that the state structure of Qin's algorithm provides a unified framework for understanding modular inversion, continued fractions, and shortest vectors in two-dimensional lattices.

papers.title: A homotopical consequence of branched covers
papers.abstract: We prove that the profinite completion of a pseudomanifold is the Artin-Mazur's etale homotopy type construction on its branched covers, which was implicitly conjectured by Sullivan in his MIT note (page 272) around 1970. This is a consequence of the existence of enough $K(π,1)$ open dense subspaces in a pseudomanifold.

papers.title: Automatic Synthesis of Low-Complexity Translation Operators for the Fast Multipole Method
papers.abstract: The FMM is the leading approach for attaining linear complexity in the evaluation of long-range (e.g. Coulomb) many-body interactions. We demonstrate a new, hybrid symbolic-numerical method for the automatic synthesis of all families of translation operators required for the execution of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM). Our method is dimension-independent (demonstrated in 2D and 3D) and applicable to any translation-invariant kernel. Low complexity in translation operators for the FMM is usually achieved by algorithms specialized for a potential obeying a specific partial differential equation (PDE). Absent a PDE or specialized algorithms, Taylor series based FMMs or kernel-independent FMM have been used, at asymptotically higher expense. When symbolically provided with a constant-coefficient elliptic PDE obeyed by the potential, our algorithm can automatically synthesize translation operators requiring $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, where $p$ is the expansion order and $d$ is dimension, compared with $\mathrm{O}(p^{2d})$ operations in a naive approach carried out on (Cartesian) Taylor expansions. This is achieved by using a compression scheme that asymptotically reduces the number of terms in the Taylor expansion and then operating directly on this "compressed" representation. Judicious exploitation of shared subexpressions permits formation, translation, and evaluation of local and multipole expansions to be performed in $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, while an FFT-based scheme permits multipole-to-local translations in $\mathrm{O}(p^{d-1}\log(p))$ operations. We demonstrate computational scaling of code generation and evaluation as well as numerical accuracy through numerical experiments on a number of potentials from classical physics.

papers.title: Factorized $q$-difference equations and their fundamental solutions
papers.abstract: We construct fundamental solutions of a class of factorized $q$-difference equations in terms of Jacobi theta functions and Zwegers' $μ$-functions. To obtain a formal series solution $f_0$ for a factorized $q$-difference equation, we present a $q$-analogue of the fundamental relation (often called the Wronski-type relation) between the elementary symmetric polynomials and the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. We also provide some formulas for the image of the $q$-Borel summation of the formal series solution $f_0$. As an application, we give another proof of the expressions due to S. Y. Kang and S. P. Zwegers of the universal mock theta functions and higher level Appell functions in terms of $μ$-functions.

papers.title: On the functoriality of the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms
papers.abstract: We construct an $(\infty,1)$-functor that takes each smooth $G$-manifold with corners $M$ to the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms ${\mathcal H}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$. We also give a stable analogue ${\mathcal H}^{\mathcal U}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$ where the manifolds are stabilized with respect to representation discs. The functor structure is subtle to construct, and relies on several new ideas. In the non-equivariant case $G=e$, our $(\infty,1)$-functor agrees with previous constructions of the smooth $h$-cobordism space as a functor to the homotopy category.

papers.title: Holed cone structures on 3-manifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce holed cone structures on 3-manifolds to generalize cone structures. In the same way as a cone structure, a holed cone structure induces the holonomy representation. We consider the deformation space consisting of the holed cone structures on a 3-manifold whose holonomy representations are irreducible. This deformation space for positive cone angles is a covering space on a reasonable subspace of the character variety.

papers.title: E-backtesting
papers.abstract: In the recent Basel Accords, the Expected Shortfall (ES) replaces the Value-at-Risk (VaR) as the standard risk measure for market risk in the banking sector, making it the most important risk measure in financial regulation. One of the most challenging tasks in risk modeling practice is to backtest ES forecasts provided by financial institutions. To design a model-free backtesting procedure for ES, we make use of the recently developed techniques of e-values and e-processes. Backtest e-statistics are introduced to formulate e-processes for risk measure forecasts, and unique forms of backtest e-statistics for VaR and ES are characterized using recent results on identification functions. For a given backtest e-statistic, a few criteria for optimally constructing the e-processes are studied. The proposed method can be naturally applied to many other risk measures and statistical quantities. We conduct extensive simulation studies and data analysis to illustrate the advantages of the model-free backtesting method, and compare it with the ones in the literature.

papers.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $Σ$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to Σ$ be a tubular neighborhood of $Σ$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $Σ$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $Σ$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$. In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $Σ$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus Σ$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $Σ$.

papers.title: Periodic solutions of symmetric Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of periodic solutions of Hamiltonian system $\dot z(t)=J \nabla H(z(t))$, where $H$ is symmetric under an action of a compact Lie group. We are looking for periodic solutions in a nearby of non-isolated critical points of $H$ which form orbits of the group action. We prove Lyapunov-type theorem for symmetric Hamiltonian systems.

papers.title: The maximal monotonicity of the subdifferential in locally convex spaces via upper envelopes
papers.abstract: We establish equivalent conditions for the convex subdifferential to be maximal monotone in general settings, expressed in terms of the associated upper envelopes.

papers.title: On a characterization of spaces satisfying open mapping and equivalent theorems
papers.abstract: We study open-mapping, continuous-inverse and closed-graph properties for maps whose domain and range belong to the same class of Hausdorff topological vector spaces. Quotient and graph stability imply equivalence of these properties. In the locally convex setting, we characterize barrelled infra-Pták spaces and barrelled Pták spaces as largest classes determined by the closed-graph property, Banach test spaces and appropriate nearly-open image conditions.

papers.title: Relationship between quandle shadow cocycle invariants and Vassiliev invariants
papers.abstract: As one of the problems in his list [20], T. Ohtsuki proposed to study relations between quandle cocycle invariants and quantum invariants. The aim of this paper is to answer one of those questions. We prove that the coefficient of the finite perturbative expansion of the quandle shadow cocycle invariant defined by $(\Z /p\Z)$-Laurent polynomial quandle is Vassiliev invariant for any braids.

papers.title: A note on polynomial sequences modulo integers (revised version)
papers.abstract: For a real polynomial $P(x)$ we study the integer sequence $λ(P)=(\lfloor P(k) \rfloor)_{k\ge1}$ modulo integers. We show that for nonlinear $P$ the sequence $λ(P)$ is uniformly distributed (u.d.) in $\mathbb{Z}$ if and only if $P$ has an irrational coefficient other than the constant term. In fact, if all non-constant coefficients of a nonlinear $P$ are rational, then $λ(P)$ fails to be u.d.\ modulo every prime in a set of primes of positive density. We also study completeness: $P$ is complete modulo $m$ if $\lfloor P(x) \rfloor$ meets every residue class modulo $m$. For $P$ of even degree we prove that $λ(P)$ meets every residue class modulo every integer if and only if $P$ has an irrational non-constant coefficient. The same holds for every polynomial $P(x)=ax^n+c$ with $n\ge2$, and for every nonlinear $P$ with $P(x)-P(0)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$. For linear $P$, both properties are characterized completely, and the two notions differ.

papers.title: The finite volume method on Sierpiński simplices
papers.abstract: In the sequel, we extend the Strichartz average approach for the Laplacian, which uses average values of a function over basic sets, rather than pointwise ones as classically done in the literature, and goes back to the seminal work of~S.~Kusuoka and~X.~Y.~Zhou, to Sierpiński Simplices. To our knowledge, the finite volume method had not been applied before to fractals themselves, with their intrinsic Laplacian. We build the finite volume scheme for the heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, give its consistency error, a stability condition of Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy type, obtained by means of an inclusion between the spectrum of the finite volume matrix and the one of the graph Laplacian, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Numerical results are given in the case of the Sierpiński Gasket and Tetrahedron, and compared with the finite difference method.

papers.title: The Finite Difference Method, for the heat equation on Sierpiński simplices
papers.abstract: In the sequel, we extend our previous work on the Minkowski Curve to Sierpiński simplices (Gasket and Tetrahedron), in the case of the heat equation. First, we build the finite difference scheme. Then, we give a theoretical study of the error, compute the scheme error, give stability conditions, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Contrary to existing work, we do not call for approximations of the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Integer matrices that are not copositive have certificates of less than quadratic complexity
papers.abstract: A real symmetric matrix is called copositive if the corresponding quadratic form is non-negative on the closed first orthant. If the matrix fails to be copositive there exists some non-negative certificate for which the quadratic form is negative. Due to the scaling property, we can find such certificates in every neighborhood of the origin but their properties depend on the matrix of course and are hard to describe. If it is an integer matrix however, we are guaranteed certificates of a complexity that is at most a constant times the binary encoding length of the matrix raised to the power 3/2.

papers.title: Line crossing problem for biased monotonic random walks in the plane
papers.abstract: A $β$-biased monotonic random walk in the plane moves from $(x,y)$ to $(x+1,y)$ or $(x,y+1)$ with probabilities $1/(β+1)$ and $β/(β+1)$. We study $Φ_β(α,d)$, the probability that the walk started at the origin ever visits a lattice point strictly above the line $y=αx+d$, and $Ψ_β(α,d)$, the probability that it visits a lattice point \emph{on} the line after leaving the origin. For integer slopes $α=p$ we show $Φ_β(p,d)=ρ^{\lfloor d\rfloor+1}$, where $ρ$ is the smallest positive root of $y^{p+1}-(β+1)y+β=0$, give the Fuss--Catalan series for $ρ$, identify $ρ$ with the extinction probability of a Galton--Watson process, and compute the exact law and mean of the first crossing point. We prove that the return probability is $Ψ_β(p,0)=(p+1)(1-β/((β+1)ρ))$, which equals $(p+1)/(β+1)$ for $β\ge p$. For rational slopes $α=r/s$ we obtain $Φ_β$ in closed form from the $s$ large roots of the kernel $\tfracβ{β+1}z^{r+s}-z^r+\tfrac1{β+1}$, and $Ψ_β$ as a ratio of Green's functions. For arbitrary real $α$ we prove that the walk crosses every line $y=αx+d$ almost surely if and only if $β\geα$, and we establish the two-sided bound $e^{-θ(d+1)}\leΦ_β(α,d)<e^{-θd}$ with an explicit Lundberg exponent $θ$. Finally, $α\mapstoΦ_β(α,0)$ is a pure jump function: it is constant on $[0,β]$, continuous at every irrational point and has a jump at every rational $α>β$.

papers.title: Convergence of iterated restricted mean values to harmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let $δ$ be a continuous positive function on $Ω$ with $B(x,δ(x))\subseteqΩ$ for every $x\inΩ$. Let $σ(f)(x)$ denote the average of $f$ over the ball $B(x,δ(x))$. Restricted mean value theorems give conditions under which a fixed point of $σ$ must be harmonic. We study the dynamical counterpart of this question: the behavior of the iterates $σ^k(f)$. We show that for \emph{every} bounded domain and every bounded measurable $f$ that is continuous at the points of $\partialΩ$, the iterates $σ^k(f)$ converge locally uniformly in $Ω$ to the Perron--Wiener--Brelot solution of the Dirichlet problem with boundary values $f|_{\partialΩ}$, and that the convergence is uniform on $\overlineΩ$ for all continuous $f$ if and only if $Ω$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem. This contains and extends earlier results for $C^{2,α}$ domains with $C^{2,α}$ data and for strictly convex domains with continuous data. We also give explicit rates of convergence: an algebraic rate $O(1/k)$ on domains with a uniform exterior ball condition and a geometric rate on convex domains, when $δ$ is comparable to the distance to the boundary.

papers.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
papers.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(Λ)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $Λ$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(Λ)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $Λ$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.

papers.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fréchet sequence spaces over trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fréchet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of Köthe spaces $λ_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.

papers.title: Positivity Improving Quantum Markov Operators
papers.abstract: A Markov operator on a matrix algebra, that is, a unital completely positive map, is called positivity improving if it maps every nonzero positive element to an invertible one. This is the noncommutative counterpart of a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries. We show that positivity improvement is self-dual and equivalent to a faithful quantum Markov--Dobrushin--Doeblin minorization. We also compare the scalar trace minorization with the optimal common-lower-bound construction of the quantum Markov--Dobrushin coefficient. We then characterize positivity improvement through the Kraus space of the map: a Markov operator is positivity improving if and only if the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal complement of its Kraus space contains no operator of rank one. As a consequence the Kraus rank of a positivity improving Markov operator on the algebra of $d\times d$ matrices is at least $2d-1$, and an explicit Hankel-type channel shows that this bound is attained in every dimension. Although deciding positivity improvement is NP-hard in general, we obtain complete and effectively checkable classifications for qubits and qutrits, together with families of examples (Pauli, Weyl and Werner--Holevo channels) showing that all our estimates are optimal. Finally we show that, in infinite dimensions, positivity improvement no longer implies any contraction of the Markov operator.

papers.title: A recursion relation for the coefficients of Swinnerton-Dyer type polynomials
papers.abstract: We study a family of polynomials that are very closely related to the Swinnerton-Dyer polynomials. As main result, we determine a recursion relation for the coefficients of this family of polynomials. We briefly explain our own and others' interest in this family of polynomials.

papers.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $μ$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

papers.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
papers.abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
papers.abstract: Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.

papers.title: Exact optimality of augmented order-of-addition designs
papers.abstract: We prove that, for the pairwise-ordering model with at least three components, adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design among all exact designs of the enlarged size, allowing replication. We also establish the corresponding result for foldover designs: adding any reversal pair to a foldover order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design within the foldover class at the enlarged size. Both augmentations also minimise the average prediction variance and a covariance-scaled information discrepancy, and maximise the minimum relative efficiency. The key step represents the scaled discrepancy through signed comparisons of triples and derives a sharp integer lower bound; classical spectral inequalities then give the exact-size optima, and signed four-component relative-order counts characterise equality. Complete reversal pairs additionally protect the estimation of pairwise-ordering effects against arbitrary reversal-invariant nuisance means. At the smallest estimable five-component foldover size, exact enumeration identifies five determinant-optimal classes with different prediction and balance properties, and a seven-component example shows that deleting a reversal pair need not be optimal even when it minimises the discrepancy. Constructions through ten components illustrate the attained run sizes.

papers.title: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
papers.abstract: Low-rank approximation is a basic tool for inference from large and noisy data matrices. However, when noise variances differ across entries, a setting known as heteroskedasticity, the noise can distort the observed spectrum, producing spurious components and obscuring weak signals. To address these challenges, we develop BRINE (Blind Resolvent-based Iterative Noise Equalizer), a data-driven procedure that iteratively rescales rows and columns to equalize the average noise variance across both dimensions. Under suitable conditions, this procedure restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal or noise structure. A key idea underlying our approach is to equalize the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing the unknown noise variances. At the population level, we identify a potential function that characterizes this equalization and motivates an iterative minimization procedure. We prove convergence of the iterations to the true equalizer for arbitrary positive variance profiles, with a geometric rate under mild conditions. The updates can be estimated directly from noisy data, and we establish probabilistic error bounds for the scaling factors. Simulations and experiments across diverse biological data modalities and preprocessing pipelines illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: On Lipschitz Explosion in Deep Neural Networks with Normalization: Consequences for Optimization and Adversarial Robustness
papers.abstract: Can a network look stable at every layer and still be exponentially unstable as a whole? The Lipschitz constant of a neural network is a basic stability quantity appearing in optimization guarantees, generalization bounds, and robustness certificates. Deep networks naturally admit two such notions, input Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to data perturbations, and parameter Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to weight perturbations. We prove that, for deep networks with normalization layers, with batch normalization as the canonical example, both Lipschitz constants can grow exponentially with depth and hence with parameter dimension, even under strong per-layer norm control such as $\|W_\ell\|_2\le 1$, and already for linear activations. Thus, a mechanism widely used to stabilize training can create severe worst-case instabilities that are invisible locally, i.e., from layerwise norm bounds alone. Parameter-Lipschitz explosion turns Lipschitz-dependent nonsmooth optimization guarantees into exponential-in-dimension bounds for deep normalized networks, while input-Lipschitz explosion makes worst-case Lipschitz-based generalization and robustness certificates vacuous. The latter also yields a concrete rank-separation mechanism for adversarial vulnerability. The theory predicts that perturbations introducing new singular directions should be amplified much more strongly than perturbations at the same noise level that remain within the input's original singular subspace. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 support this prediction, showing that rank-creating perturbations cause substantially sharper drops in accuracy, confidence, and margins than same-subspace perturbations.

papers.title: Cantor's onion: a uniformly quasiregular map whose Julia set is a Cantor set of spheres
papers.abstract: For integers $d,m\ge2$ with $1/d+1/m<1$, we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{S}^3$ of degree $d^2+m^2$ whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps $z^d+λ/z^m$, built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension $2+s$, where $d^{-s}+m^{-s}=1$, and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy $\log(d^2+m^2)$.
