In particular, the full proof combines tools of classical analysis and functional analysis, such as localisation by continuous cutoff functions, Stone-Weierstrass approximation of continuous functions by signature polynomials, the Hahn-Banach theorem and a support detection lemma for compactly supported real signed Borel measures.

papers.title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.

papers.title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
papers.abstract: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

papers.title: Exact regions for the symmetrized Blest coefficient
papers.abstract: Spearman's rho treats all ranks alike, yet in many comparisons of two rankings an agreement at the top matters more than one at the bottom. Blest's rank correlation builds this preference into Spearman's rho, and its symmetrized version $η$, introduced by Genest and Plante, does so without favoring either of the two rankings. How far can such a top-weighted coefficient stray from other rank correlations? We answer this question for Spearman's rho, Blomqvist's beta and Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ by determining the exact set of values that $η$ and each of these coefficients can attain jointly. Given Spearman's rho, $η$ can differ from it by at most $27/128$, and the extreme values of $η$ are attained only when the two rankings agree perfectly on the top ranks and are completely reversed on the bottom ranks, or vice versa. Given Blomqvist's beta, $η$ obeys exactly the same sharp bounds as Spearman's rho. For Chatterjee's rank correlation, both boundary curves are explicit and are attained by copulas with densities. Here symmetrization has a surprising effect. Compared with Blest's original coefficient, $η$ has a narrower range at fixed Spearman's rho, but near independence a wider range at fixed Chatterjee's rank correlation, where $|η|$ can come close to $\sqrt{11ξ/5}$ while Blest's coefficient stays below $\sqrt{32ξ/15}$. The proofs combine explicit Kantorovich potentials from optimal transport with a convex relaxation that turns out to be exact.

papers.title: Domination and maximal intersecting families in comaximal graphs of commutative rings
papers.abstract: The comaximal graph $\mathcal{G}(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ has as vertices the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical, two being adjacent if they generate $R$ as an ideal. For rings with $k\ge 4$ maximal ideals, only the bounds $2\leγ(\mathcal{G}(R))\le k$ were known, to our knowledge. We prove $γ=γ_t=γ_c=k$ whenever $3\le k<\infty$, without finiteness or Artinian hypotheses, classify the minimum dominating sets, and determine the domatic number. Independent dominating sets correspond to maximal intersecting families of subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$; we obtain a closed formula for the independent domination number of every finite non-local ring, which can be exponentially larger than the domination number. The proofs rest on the class sizes of the blow-up description of $\mathcal{G}(R)$ due to Moconja and Petrović, which we determine for every ring with finitely many maximal ideals, finite or infinite; with them, domination problems on $\mathcal{G}(R)$ become weighted extremal problems on subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$, and the formula for the independent domination number follows from the multiplicative form of these sizes. We also treat rings with infinitely many maximal ideals, graph polynomials, and lattices whose maximal ideals are prime.

papers.title: Sigmoid Tensor Decomposition for Compact Representations of Binary Data
papers.abstract: Nonlinear low-rank decompositions are receiving growing attention as a way to represent structured data with fewer parameters than conventional linear methods. Existing nonlinear approaches have focused mainly on matrices, which limits their ability to capture multidimensional structure. We propose a nonlinear tensor decomposition based on sigmoid nonlinearization in the Tucker and tensor-train formats. A binary tensor is represented by a low-rank real-valued score tensor, whose parameters are estimated by minimizing the binary cross-entropy loss. The resulting optimization problem is jointly nonconvex, but becomes convex with respect to one factor or score block when the remaining factors are fixed, as in the corresponding matrix case. We evaluate the method on several structured binary tensors and compare it with conventional Tucker and tensor-train decompositions across a range of common ranks. These results indicate that sigmoid nonlinearization is particularly effective in the low-rank regime, where it can provide more accurate binary reconstructions than conventional linear tensor decompositions at comparable model sizes.

papers.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
papers.abstract: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action. We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(EΦ^2+P(Φ))}dΦ$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $dΦ$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(Φ)=\fracλ{4}Φ^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.

papers.title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

papers.title: LithoSAGE: Spatially Adaptive and Geometrically Equivariant Neural Operators for Computational Lithography
papers.abstract: Operator learning offers an efficient surrogate for lithography simulation, replacing costly numerical solutions with direct model inference. However, existing learning architectures are not designed to simultaneously provide geometric equivariance and adaptability to layout windows with different physical extents, and thus their generalization capability is limited. To address this problem, we propose LithoSAGE, a spatially adaptive and geometrically equivariant neural operator method trained on lithography data. Within its basic Fourier neural operator architecture, spectral weights are expressed as continuous functions of normalized radial frequency through a learnable sum of Gaussians. This representation preserves the geometric properties of the lithography system and incorporates rotation and translation equivariance, spatial interaction decay, and direct evaluation on different layout windows. Experiments predict aerial images from mask layouts and resist images from aerial images, demonstrating the geometric equivariance and spatial adaptivity of LithoSAGE. Comparisons with other architectures also assess prediction errors and parameter efficiency.

papers.title: Hypocoercivity for a thermostatted Boltzmann equation
papers.abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. Its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. The reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. For the isotropic cutoff kernel, with Maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common Gaussian upper bound and Gaussian moment bound. These bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. The estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. For any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local Maxwellian. When particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. Once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.

papers.title: Isomorphisms and automorphisms of minimal comaximal hypergraphs of commutative rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with exactly $n\ge 2$ maximal ideals and let $k\ge 2$. We study the minimal $k$-uniform comaximal hypergraph $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$, whose vertices are the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical and whose edges are the irredundant $k$-element comaximal families. For $2\le k\le n$ we show that $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ is a blow-up of the hypergraph of irredundant $k$-coverings of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and that its reduced form reconstructs the maximal ideals up to permutation; for $k>n$ there are no edges. We obtain a general description of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{H}_k(R))$ and characterize isomorphisms of such hypergraphs. For $3\le k\le n$ its automorphism group properly contains that of the comaximal graph, and for finite rings with $n\ge 3$ and every $2\le k\le n$, $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ has the same isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph, namely $|J(R)|$ and $R/J(R)$. The case $k=2$ recovers and extends the automorphism results for comaximal graphs obtained previously. We also compare the minimal and non-minimal comaximal hypergraphs and identify a condition under which the latter has the same automorphism group and isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph. The same method determines the vertex set and the automorphism group of the $k$-zero-divisor hypergraph of a product of integral domains, and shows that for finite products of finite fields this hypergraph determines the ring.

papers.title: Parameter-dependent inhomogeneous boundary-value problems in spaces of continuously differentiable functions
papers.abstract: We investigate a broad class of linear inhomogeneous boundary-value problems of order $r$ for systems of ordinary differential equations depending on a parameter $μ$ belonging to an abstract metric space $\mathcal M$. The solutions belong to the spaces of continuously differentiable vector-valued functions $(C^{(n+r)})^m$, $n\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, $m, r \in \mathbb{N}$. The boundary conditions have the most general form $By=c$, where $B$ is an arbitrary continuous linear operator from $(C^{(n+r)})^m$ to $\mathbb{C}^{rm}$. Thus, they may contain derivatives of the unknown vector-valued function of integer and/or fractional orders up to $n+r$ inclusive. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the continuous dependence of solutions on the parameter $μ$. Furthermore, we prove that the solutions of the original problems can be approximated in the space $(C^{(n+r)})^m$ by solutions of systems of ordinary differential equations with polynomial coefficients, polynomial right-hand sides, and multipoint boundary conditions, where the approximating problems are constructed independently of the right-hand sides of the original problem.

papers.title: Tilting bundles and modifying modules in relative dimension one
papers.abstract: For projective morphisms $π:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over noetherian complete local rings, with fibres of dimension at most one and $\mathbf{R}π_*\mathcal{O}_Y\cong\mathcal{O}_X$, we construct a tilting fan from cones of pretilting bundles. Maximal cones parametrize tilting bundles, and facet adjacency encodes irreducible mutation. Completeness in positive rank is equivalent to finiteness of tilting bundles modulo line-bundle twists. For closed fibres that are split ADE highest-root cycles or their Stein contractions, we identify tilting bundles with chambers of restricted affine Tits cones and determine the fan. Over normal Gorenstein complete local domains, reflexive pushforward takes pretilting bundles on normal projective birational models with fibres of dimension at most one and $π^!\mathcal{O}_X\cong\mathcal{O}_Y$ to modifying modules. Pushforwards of canonical tilting bundles recover models as module blowups and detect contractions by additive containment, yielding an Auslander--McKay embedding. The hypersurfaces $R=S[[u,v]]/(uv-f)$, with $S$ a regular complete local ring and $f\in S$ a nonzero nonunit, generalize type $A$ Du Val surfaces and $cA_n$ threefolds to arbitrary dimension. We classify modifying modules by divisor flags and rank-one reflexive twists; flag blowups turn the embedding into an equivalence. If $f$ has $r\ge2$ prime factors counted with multiplicity, reflexive pushforward on any maximal-flag model gives a mutation-preserving surjection from tilting bundles, parametrized by chambers of affine type $\widetilde{A}_{r-1}$, to maximal modifying modules. Its fibres are affine Weyl group orbits determined by repeated factors. All maximal-flag models and maximal modification algebras are derived equivalent. These algebras are noncommutative crepant resolutions exactly when $S/(p)$ is regular for every prime factor $p$ of $f$.

papers.title: Boundary-preserving randomized neural network methods for Poisson equations on general two- and three-dimensional domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a boundary-preserving randomized neural network method for Poisson equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in two and three dimensions. A linear lifting imposes the boundary conditions exactly, without balancing penalty weights between interior and boundary residuals. We construct the liftings by generalized barycentric coordinates and transfinite interpolation on convex and nonconvex polygons and polyhedra, and by radial parameterization on star-shaped curved domains. Numerical experiments on different domains show that the proposed method substantially reduces errors compared with the standard randomized neural network method.

papers.title: A stability order barrier and SSP bound for Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients: AI-assisted proofs
papers.abstract: We prove three results about Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients. First, every $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least two has SSP coefficient at most $2s$; the bound is sharp and is attained by a known diagonally implicit method, so full implicitness gives no advantage over DIRK at second order. This extends the second-order DIRK result of Kocsis \& Németh to full coefficient matrices and settles a conjecture of Ketcheson, Macdonald & Gottlieb. These proofs were found with the assistance of AI tools, which uncovered an interesting relationship between the Butcher matrices for SSP methods and phase-type distributions, and led to the proof of the second result: a bound on the SSP coefficient of $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least three. The third result in this work is a proof that a third-order Runge--Kutta method with entrywise non-negative $A$ and $b$ cannot be algebraically stable. This algebraically intensive proof was also AI-assisted. This paper describes the iterative process of AI-assisted results, and presents an approach that centers human understanding and creativity in the AI-assisted mathematical endeavor.

papers.title: A characterization of purely atomic von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal semifinite trace $τ$, and let $Φ$ be an Orlicz function. We prove that the noncommutative Orlicz space $L^Φ(M,τ)$ is contained in $M$ if and only if $M$ is purely atomic and there is $δ>0$ such that $τ(e)\geqδ$ for every nonzero projection $e\in M$. We also prove that every left $M$-module map on $L^Φ(M,τ)$ is bounded. As a consequence, a left ideal of $M$ contained in $L^Φ(M,τ)$ and dense in it admits an $M$-invariant algebraic complement if and only if it is equal to $L^Φ(M,τ)$. These results extend a theorem of Fidaleo and Zsidó from $L^2$ to all noncommutative Orlicz spaces.

papers.title: Darboux transformations of linear birth-death processes
papers.abstract: In a previous paper we characterized the lower-upper (LU) and upper-lower (UL) factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth-death process whose Darboux transformations are again generators of birth-death processes. Here we apply these results to several classical models with linear rates and explicitly known spectral measures: the $M/M/\infty$ queue (Charlier polynomials), the linear birth-death processes (Meixner and Laguerre polynomials), and the linear models of Ismail, Letessier and Valent (associated Laguerre polynomials). For each of them we compute the factors in closed form, determine the admissible ranges of the parameters, and describe the rates, spectral measures and orthogonal polynomials of the Darboux-transformed processes.

papers.title: A positive answer to Barsotti and Carman's question on unit groups of Burnside rings of fusion systems
papers.abstract: Let F be a saturated fusion system on a finite 2-group S, and let B(F) be the Burnside ring of F. Barsotti and Carman proved that when S is abelian, B(F)^*=B(S)^* if and only if F=F_S(S). Barsotti and Carman asked on page 728 of their paper whether there exists a counterexample to Corollary 9.3 for a nonabelian 2-group. We have given a positive answer. Our main conclusion is that the following are equivalent for all finite 2-groups: (1)F=F_S(S); (2)B(F)^*=B(S)^*; (3)For every maximal subgroup M of S, 1-[S/M] is in B(F)^*.

papers.title: Quantifying the remaining search space in analogue optimisation
papers.abstract: Benchmarking analogue optimisers requires certifying not only how close a returned energy is to the optimum, but also how many better configurations may remain. Semidefinite relaxations provide rigorous bounds on the ground-state energy and selected observables, yet reveal little about the size of this residual search space. We introduce a deterministic, instance-specific upper bound on the number of binary configurations whose energies improve upon a returned state by a prescribed margin. Combined with a semidefinite energy interval, this yields a complementary certificate of both the magnitude and multiplicity of any possible improvement. To judge an analogue optimiser's native performance, we provide a generalisation of the framework to obtain bounds on the Haar volume of the remaining continuous phase-space. To further characterise the remaining search space, we extend our bounds to resolve regions in configuration space in both the binary and continuous setting. Our approach couples a variational-Chernoff reduction with an elimination bound of the resulting partition function. Comparisons with exact enumeration and independent Haar sampling are consistent with the bounds on small instances. In numerical experiments at $N=1000$, even the largest family-median bound restricts the potentially improving binary configurations to less than $10^{-144}$ of the full configuration space, while the largest upper bound on the corresponding Haar volume is of order $10^{-499}$.

papers.title: Reversible Dynamics, Asymmetric Actions: Parking as a Trajectory-Level Affordance
papers.abstract: Drivers are often told to back into a tight parking space, not drive in nose first. The advice looks paradoxical, because a slow car is dynamically reversible: reverse its speed and replay the steering backward, and it retraces a feasible path. Played backward, though, reverse-in shows a car driving forward out of the space. Reverse-in and forward-in are different tasks: they share a start position but end facing opposite ways. We separate three clearances between car and obstacles. Static fit $F$ is the clearance the parked car keeps at its best acceptable destination pose. Eventual access $A_\infty$ is the clearance it can keep all the way there with unlimited corrections. Resource-bounded access $A_K$ is the clearance that survives a budget of $K$ reversals, switches between forward and reverse. They satisfy $F\ge A_\infty\ge A_K$. In one fully specified scene (one car, bay, aisle and start), a certified argument proves $A_\infty=F=0.5000$ m for both tasks. In this scene, all certified forward/reverse asymmetry therefore arises at finite $K$: it lies in how many corrections each task needs, not in the clearance either can eventually keep. With one reversal, an explicit path gives reverse-in at least $0.4410$ m clearance. A certified reachability argument caps forward-in's one-reversal clearance at $d_0<0.1720002$ m. With two reversals, forward-in gets at least $0.2833$ m. To keep a clearance strictly above any $d$ with $d_0\le d<0.2833$ m, reverse-in thus needs exactly one reversal and forward-in exactly two when both tasks move forward first. If both move in reverse first, the counts are two and three. The contrast depends on the start position (Section 4.15). Proposed experiments test whether observers distinguish fit, eventual access and budgeted access. They compare these with simpler cues, such as how the turning body sweeps, and learned manoeuvre labels.

papers.title: Multiplicity via symmetry for the Minkowski mean curvature equation: Dirichlet and Neumann problems
papers.abstract: We consider the Minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =λu+μh(x,u) \quad \text{in } Ω, \quad \mathcal B u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial Ω, $$ where $\mathcal B \in \{ \mathcal D, \mathcal N \}$ is a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition and $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the Neumann case. Moreover, $λ, μ\geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. Using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $λ>λ^\mathcal B_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $μ\geq0$, where $λ_k^\mathcal B$ are the corresponding Laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $λ^\mathcal B_0=0$. Moreover, if $H(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $λ\in[λ^\mathcal B_k,λ^\mathcal B_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $μ$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.

papers.title: On the Spectral Dependence of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Tracking
papers.abstract: We study how the spectral geometry of the mixing matrix enters the convergence of decentralized stochastic gradient tracking (GT) for smooth strongly convex problems. General bounds contain the factor $Δ_λ^{-3}$ in the higher-order stochastic term, where $Δ_λ$ is the absolute spectral gap. We show that, even for two agents with identical quadratic objectives, the exact steady-state mean-square disagreement scales as $α^2σ^2Δ_λ^{-3}$ as the nontrivial eigenvalue approaches $-1$, provided the stepsize $α$ is sufficiently small relative to the gap. Here $σ^2$ is the gradient-noise variance. By unrolling the disagreement recursion, we establish a stochastic bound that averages all nontrivial eigenvalue contributions for diagonalizable mixing matrices, up to an eigenvector conditioning factor. As a real or complex eigenvalue approaches the unit circle away from $1$, its contribution grows as the inverse cube of its distance to the circle; growth can be slower near $1$. For symmetric mixing with gaps $p$ at $1$ and $ν$ at $-1$, the weighted sum $θ_1/p+θ_2/ν^3$ replaces the prior factor $(Δ_λν^2)^{-1}$. For $N$ agents, $Nθ_1$ and $Nθ_2$ count the nonnegative and negative nontrivial eigenvalues, respectively. On a symmetric family, a finite-horizon lower bound for the average iterate matches the worst-case factor $p^{-1}+ν^{-3}$ up to universal constants. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scaling.

papers.title: Constructive Probability, Foundations and Numerical Analysis for mathematical finance and machine learning
papers.abstract: This monograph sets out a constructive theory of stochastic processes in the continuum, in the sense of constructive field theory: the continuum is not postulated but reached as the limit of a sequence of lattice approximations, with the renormalisation the limit requires exhibited rather than assumed, and the limit controlled by estimates that can be checked. The primitive object is not a sigma-algebra but de Finetti's prevision, the price of finitely many gambles at a fixed resolution, which coherence turns into a conditional expectation. The theorem at the centre of the book, called plainly the fundamental theorem, is at once de Finetti's fundamental theorem of probability, the fundamental theorem of Bayesian statistics, and the one-period fundamental theorem of asset pricing; the financial vocabulary is a convenience only. The applications are two, mathematical finance and machine learning, and they are one mathematics read in opposite directions: an assessment is a price in the one and a prediction in the other, and both are computed by one adjoint recursion, the adjoint of a propagation in the first case and backpropagation in the second. Carried through, the two directions give sharp rates of convergence rather than asymptotic orders: for the moments of Ito diffusions, for the value function of Feynman-Kac semigroups, and for the measure changes of the fundamental theorem, the last as a limit theorem for reweighted generators, under a condition keeping the reweighting well behaved. A measure change is thus calculated, not postulated: a lattice approximation with Farkas' lemma computes it, completeness makes it unique, and the passage to the continuum is earned by the regularity of what is computed. Sixty-seven Python scripts regenerate every numerical table, and much of the finite-dimensional core of the argument has been verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: P-curvature from a TQFT viewpoint
papers.abstract: This paper is motivated by the recent discovery, in symplectic topology, of a relation (partly proved, partly conjectural) between quantum connection and quantum Steenrod operations. We introduce an abstract TQFT framework, based on certain features of the definition of deformed symplectic cohomology, in which such a relation holds generally.

papers.title: The Approximation Property without the Bounded Approximation Property in a Separable Banach Space and Its Dual
papers.abstract: We investigate whether a dual Banach space with the approximation property (AP) must necessarily have the bounded approximation property (BAP). Using a quantitative renorming theorem for the space of absolutely summable sequences, we establish a direct-sum construction yielding a negative answer. More precisely, we construct a separable Banach space (X) such that both (X) and its dual (X^*) have the approximation property, while neither space has the bounded approximation property. The construction uses a sequence of equivalent renormings of (\ell_1) with increasingly restrictive finite-dimensional approximation bounds. By assembling these spaces through a (c_0)-direct sum, we obtain a dual space whose approximation property is preserved, but whose approximation constants cannot be uniformly bounded. We establish the required transfer principles, including the preservation of approximation bounds under complemented coordinate projections and the descent of the bounded approximation property from a dual space to its predual. We also provide an explicit complex-scalar version of the construction. The argument separates the external quantitative renorming input from the direct-sum construction and its functional-analytic consequences. In particular, the resulting example demonstrates that the approximation property of a dual space does not imply its bounded approximation property, even when the predual is separable and both spaces possess the approximation property.

papers.title: A Story of Algebra and Categories I: Algebraic Theories
papers.abstract: This is the first part of a series of expository notes on homotopical and categorical algebra. It charts a course from ordinary algebraic structures such as monoids, groups, and rings to their various homotopy-coherent generalizations and equivariant versions. The emphasis is on the ideas that lead to and connect the constructions, as well as where and how they appear in nature.

papers.title: Clique partitions and distinct color sets in list colorings
papers.abstract: For an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) and an integer \(m\ge n\), let \(f'(G,m)\) be the minimum number of distinct color sets used by proper colorings from \(m\)-element lists that are disjoint at distinct nonadjacent vertices. A clique-partition assignment gives a common list to the vertices of each part of a clique partition and uses disjoint lists on different parts. In this paper, we construct a graph on \(20\) vertices for which these assignments do not attain \(f'(G,20)\), and a fixed graph on \(25\) vertices for which they fail to attain the minimum for every allowed list size. For every triangle-free graph \(G\) on \(n\ge2\) vertices, we prove \[ f'(G,m)=\binom{m}{2}^{ν(G)}m^{n-2ν(G)} \qquad (m\ge n), \] where \(ν(G)\) is the size of a maximum matching, and characterize all minimizing assignments in terms of maximum matchings. For clique blow-ups of each fixed odd cycle of length at least five, we determine the minimum up to constant factors uniformly over the blow-up size and all allowed list sizes, and obtain an exponential separation from the clique-partition value. We also prove that a noncomplete graph \(G\) satisfies \(f'(G,n)=n^2\) if and only if all edges of its complement have a common endpoint. These results disprove the general clique-partition conjecture of Gravier, Maffray, and Mohar (\emph{Discrete Mathematics}, 2003) and its extension by Wu and Zhang (\emph{Applied Mathematics Letters}, 2006), while establishing both triangle-free conjectures.

papers.title: Towards a twistless converse theorem
papers.abstract: We prove a finiteness theorem for Dirichlet series satisfying the Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation expected of a holomorphic newform. For any fixed level $N$, even weight $k$, and exponent $σ$, only finitely many such series have Dirichlet coefficients $\ll n^σ$. No hypotheses on twists by Dirichlet characters are assumed. The proof combines a combinatorial spanning theorem for Ramanujan sums with an operator-theoretic argument that uses two distinct primes to establish discreteness of the possible Hecke eigenvalues.

papers.title: Free $T_n$-Heyting algebras
papers.abstract: ${T}_n$-Heyting algebras form a subvariety of Heyting algebras and are characterized by the property that a chain of prime filters in such an algebra has at most $n-1$ elements. We study some basic properties of these algebras and determine the structure and number of elements of the free ${T}_n$-Heyting algebra with a finite number $r$ of free generators, $FT_n(r)$.

papers.title: The parity of the number of missing integers in partitions
papers.abstract: Missing integers in partitions have been studied by many authors. A missing integer of a partition is a positive integer smaller than its largest part that does not occur as a part. We investigate parity biases for the number of missing integers in partitions and overpartitions. For every integer $c\ge2$, we prove that the coefficients $a_c(n)$ of $(-cq;q)_\infty/(-q;q)_\infty$ are eventually strictly positive and provide an effectively computable threshold. The proof uses the circle method, combining a saddle-point analysis on the major arc with explicit uniform estimates on the minor arcs. Specializing to $c=2$ and $c=3$, and verifying the remaining finite cases, we show that partitions and overpartitions of $n$ with an even number of missing integers outnumber those with an odd number for $n>34$ and $n>27$, respectively. We further prove that, for $n>10$, the difference between the numbers of ordinary partitions with an even and an odd number of missing integers is smaller than the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. These results confirm three conjectures of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra. We also give a combinatorial interpretation of $a_c(n)$ for every integer $c\ge4$ in terms of colored partitions, generalizing the partition and overpartition interpretations of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra for $c=2$ and $c=3$, respectively.

papers.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary functions, boundary convexity estimates and a domain deformation argument.

papers.title: Global Solvability in Critical Sobolev Spaces for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields
papers.abstract: In this work, we present global solvability results, in critical Sobolev spaces, for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields.

papers.title: Construction of Transverse Metrics from Transversely Elliptic Operators on Foliated Manifolds
papers.abstract: The existence of a transverse metric on a foliated manifold is typically used as a framework for studying transversely elliptic basic differential operators. This article details a method for constructing such a transverse metric directly from the principal symbol of the operator. Consequently, rather than treating the transverse metric as a mere working assumption, we demonstrate that its existence is a necessary condition for the very presence of a transversely elliptic operator.

papers.title: XM4D: 4D Reconstruction through Certifiable Geometric Optimization
papers.abstract: Accurate 4D reconstruction remains challenging: jointly estimating camera motion, scene geometry, and non-rigid deformation entails highly nonconvex optimization, making global optimality difficult to guarantee. We present XM4D, a framework for accurate and efficient 4D reconstruction built upon certifiably globally optimal geometric optimization. By separating the estimation of camera motion from non-rigid deformation, we formulate both stages as structured quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQP) that admit semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations and verifiable global optimality certificates. For camera motion estimation, we lift static point tracks into 3D using foundational depth prediction models and formulate a scaled bundle adjustment problem that jointly estimates camera poses, depth scales, and static landmarks. By analytically eliminating translations and landmarks, we reduce the problem to a QCQP over scaled rotations. For non-rigid reconstruction, we represent dynamic motion using an embedded deformation graph (EDG) and show that its tracking, rigidity, and temporal regularization objectives similarly reduce to a rotation-only QCQP. Both problems admit SDP relaxations that we solve efficiently with a GPU-accelerated Burer-Monteiro solver based on Riemannian optimization. The recovered geometry further initializes dynamic Gaussian splatting for photometric refinement. Extensive experiments across seven benchmarks demonstrate accurate camera motion estimation on both static and dynamic scenes, efficient optimization that scales to thousands of frames, and state-of-the-art novel-view rendering quality.

papers.title: Topological classification of Bazaikin spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a topological classification of Bazaikin spaces whose sixth cohomology groups have orders prime to \(5\). Moreover, we obtain an estimate for the number of diffeomorphism types among these spaces.

papers.title: Group-free radial Kunze-Stein phenomenon on affine buildings
papers.abstract: We give a geometric proof of the radial Kunze--Stein phenomenon on the good vertices of a thick, locally finite, regular affine building of irreducible type. The proof uses a positive spherical function, its joint eigenvalues for sphere averages, and the growth of vector-distance spheres. Conjugation by this function and complex interpolation yield a weighted $\ell^2$ estimate and the boundedness of radial operators with $\ell^p$ kernels for $1\leq p<2$. We also present proofs by the averaging operators norms, by the Schur test and by Helgason transform. A further interpolation gives weighted mixed-exponent estimates. No transitivity assumption on the automorphism group is required; in particular the argument applies to buildings of type $\widetilde A_2$ without a Bruhat--Tits realization.

papers.title: The minimal excludant and the least $r$-gaps of $\ell$-regular partitions
papers.abstract: The minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition $λ$ is the smallest positive integer that is not a part of $λ$. In this paper we study an analogue of this statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions with $\ell\geq2$, that is, partitions in which no part is divisible by $\ell$. Recently, Meher \cite{Meher} defined the minimal excludant for $\ell$-regular partitions. Motivated by Meher \cite{Meher}, for an $\ell$-regular partition we define its least $r$-gap as the smallest positive integer not divisible by $\ell$ that appears fewer than $r$ times as a part, and we obtain the two-variable generating function for the number of $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ with a given least $r$-gap. Let $σ^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ be the sum of the of the mex values over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ and least $r$-gaps over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ respectively. Using Jacobi's triple product identity, we derive explicit expressions for the generating function of $σ^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$, with separate formulas for even and odd $\ell$. We also show that the sequence $\{σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)\}_{n\ge0}$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Also, using Ingham's Tauberian theorem, we establish Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ when $\ell=4,5,7$ and $r\ge1$ is arbitrary. Lastly, we prove $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}$ is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such n up to X grows at least like log log X.

papers.title: Local and 2-Local Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Zinbiel Algebras
papers.abstract: We study local and $2$-local derivations of finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebras. Over any field of characteristic zero, every Zinbiel algebra $A$ with $A^2 \neq 0$ and $\dim A \leq 4$ admits a proper local derivation. The proof uses a filtration argument. We exhibit two five-dimensional Zinbiel algebras with nonzero multiplication whose derivations are all central. Every local derivation on either algebra is therefore a derivation, so the minimum dimension for local rigidity with nonzero multiplication is five. Annihilator-valued interpolation gives a general construction of proper local derivations. When $A^3 = 0$, the multiplication tensor describes all derivations and local derivations. For a finite-dimensional nilpotent algebra $A$ over any field, we show that every $2$-local derivation is a derivation if and only if $\dim(A/A^2) \leq 1$. The proof combines the annihilator interpolation of Sh. Ayupov, K. Kudaybergenov and B. Omirov with a one-generator argument. When all derivations are central, every $2$-local derivation is obtained by composing a homogeneous map $A/A^2 \to \text{Ann}(A)$ with the quotient map, and every such composition is a $2$-local derivation. The five-dimensional examples extend to locally rigid Zinbiel algebras with nonlinear $2$-local derivations in every dimension at least five. We also show that derivations given by left multiplication form a Lie ideal of nilpotency class at most two and give sufficient conditions for the existence of left outer derivations. This ideal is zero in our locally rigid examples.

papers.title: Extending graph metrics to hyperspaces of vertex sets: optimization and reinforcement learning applications
papers.abstract: An undirected connected graph can be interpreted as a metric space by considering the path distance between its vertices. Extending this perspective, we explore how walks in the graph, viewed as sequences of subsets of vertices $V$, fit into a more general framework where the path distance emerges as a special case of broader metrics that define hypertopologies on the space of subsets of $V$. In this paper, we propose a general framework to address this issue, motivated by the extension of recent reinforcement learning algorithms on graphs through Lipschitz function extensions. Our approach demonstrates how models for dynamical systems and related machine learning techniques can be adapted to (quasi-pseudo-metric) hyperspaces, offering a novel perspective for the analysis and modeling of dynamical systems. Finally, we illustrate the practical relevance of our theoretical contributions through a concrete graph optimization example, highlighting the utility and effectiveness of our proposed approach.

papers.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
papers.abstract: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

papers.title: Three-critical hypergraphs of maximum local edge connectivity two
papers.abstract: For a hypergraph \(G\), let \(χ(G)\) denote its chromatic number and \(λ(G)\) the maximum, over pairs of distinct vertices, of the minimum size of an edge cut separating the pair. A hypergraph is \(3\)-critical if its chromatic number is three and every proper subhypergraph is two-colorable. In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of the \(3\)-critical hypergraphs with \(λ(G)\le2\). We prove that these are precisely the hypergraphs generated from ordinary odd cycles and an explicit family of labeled-tree hypergraphs by admissible Toft splits. This characterization includes a necessary and sufficient condition for a prescribed split to preserve \(λ\le2\). The condition involves only cuts in the first factor and the two traces on the split edge. More generally, we establish an exact cut formula for splits at degree-\(k\) vertices of \((k+1)\)-critical hypergraphs, for every \(k\ge2\). We further prove that the smallest member of this critical class outside the family generated by hyperwheels and both forms of the Hajós join has eight vertices and is unique up to isomorphism. Together, these results resolve two issues left open by Schweser, Stiebitz, and Toft in \emph{Journal of Combinatorics} (2022): the characterization of hypergraphs with \(λ(G)=2\) and \(χ(G)=3\), and whether hyperwheels and Hajós joins suffice to generate all \(3\)-critical hypergraphs in this connectivity range.

papers.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
papers.abstract: We study a genus-two hypergeometric family whose Jacobians have real multiplication by $\Q(\sqrt5)$. We identify the relevant primitive factor and integral rank-two monodromy; at one real embedding the projective image is $Δ(2,5,\infty)$, while the conjugate image is nondiscrete. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ Borel covers are quadratic pullbacks of genus-one triangular modular curves. The same rank-two systems have finite-field hypergeometric Frobenius traces, yielding the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation twisted by the character of $2$.

papers.title: Quantifying and minimizing collision intensity in stationary crowd flow
papers.abstract: We develop a continuum model to quantify kinematic collision risk in stationary crowd flow. From the density-weighted inward relative flux, we derive a collision functional based on the symmetric velocity gradient. For incompressible flows with constant density, this functional is convex and positively homogeneous of degree one in a combination of second derivatives of the stream function. We minimize it subject to prescribed boundary flux. On bounded simply connected domains with Lipschitz boundary, under a finite-energy lifting assumption, we prove existence of minimizers in a relaxed class that allows this derivative combination to be a vector-valued Radon measure. We show that disks are the only domains with a nontrivial zero-trace kernel, corresponding to rigid rotation about the center. Using the compact embedding for functions of bounded deformation, we prove that relaxed energy sublevels are compact without normalization on every other admissible domain, and after removing one rotational component on disks. We identify the relaxed functional with the strong $W^{1,1}$ lower semicontinuous envelope of the functional on the prescribed-trace class with integrable controlled derivatives. Then, we derive optimality conditions via convex duality. We construct explicit radial flows on annular sectors and prove that they minimize the energy over the full admissible classes, including nonradial competitors. On the square, distinct minimizers with the same prescribed boundary flux have different local collision intensities. The square--disk comparison shows that the saddle flow loses optimality when the domain changes, even after normalization.

papers.title: A Lagrangian Approach to Uniqueness for Active Scalars in Generalized Mean Oscillation Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a unified Lagrangian framework for the uniqueness of weak solutions to a broad class of two-dimensional inviscid active scalar equations in generalized mean oscillation spaces. Under common structural assumptions on the Biot--Savart kernels, we identify mean oscillation spaces that ensure an Osgood condition for the velocity, and establish uniqueness in these classes. For the two-dimensional Euler equations, we establish uniqueness for vorticities whose mean oscillation grows mildly at small scales, extending beyond $\mathrm{BMO}$. For the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) and incompressible porous media (IPM) equations, we obtain uniqueness in spaces logarithmically rougher than $C^{0,1}$. We also obtain what are (to our knowledge) the strongest known uniqueness results for the $α$-SQG equation, $0<α<1$, in spaces logarithmically rougher than critical Hölder spaces $C^α$. The framework also applies to various logarithmically perturbed models, yielding uniqueness in the corresponding sharp regularity classes. The proof combines a sharp regularity estimate for the velocity with a stability estimate for integral operators under measure-preserving rearrangements. This provides a single uniqueness argument for the entire family under common structural assumptions on the kernels.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of nonergodic directions in higher genus via effective equidistribution
papers.abstract: For each fixed $g\ge3$, we prove that non-uniquely ergodic directions have Hausdorff dimension $1/2$ on almost every area-one surface in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{odd}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is odd, and in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{nonhyp}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is even. We construct these directions through cyclic splittings into $g$ slit tori. Effective equidistribution of Lindenstrauss--Mohammadi--Yang supplies sufficiently many children at each normal input. We estimate cusp and periodic-orbit failures with the original branching weights and prove that their total mass loss is summable. The surviving path measure yields the dimension lower bound, also for directions nonergodic for flat area.

papers.title: Continuous Space-Time Finite Element Simulations for Biomedical Flows with Large Boundary Motion and Time-Periodicity
papers.abstract: We present an axisymmetric continuous simplex space-time finite element method for incompressible fluid flow. Compared to conventional time-stepping methods, the space-time approach has several advantages. First, the motion of the domain is incorporated into the space-time geometry, allowing for large boundary motion without remeshing or projection of the solution. Second, the method allows for time-periodic solutions to be computed directly, without the need to simulate multiple cycles. Third, the space-time mesh can be partitioned in time as well as in space, which enables parallelism in time. The method is demonstrated on an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in a rigid tube. The balloon inflation is modelled based on measured data, and includes a travelling wave along the balloon. The method is able to resolve complex flow features such as jets and recirculation zones. A refinement study shows convergence under temporal, spatial and combined space-time refinement. In weak scaling tests up to 960 ranks, the cost per solver iteration remains approximately constant, and partitioning the mesh into time slabs improves the convergence of the linear solver compared to partitions that cut through both space and time.

papers.title: Recurrence and Uniqueness Criteria for Markov Processes from Moments of Integral-Type Functionals
papers.abstract: We investigate recurrence and uniqueness of continuous-time Markov chains using moments of integral-type functionals. Unlike the classical criteria from Chen (2004) and the Feller-Reuter criterion, we develop general unified conditions for recurrence and uniqueness of Markov processes based on moments of integral-type functionals. The associated criteria follow directly from these conditions whenever the mean functionals can be expressed explicitly. As applications, explicit recurrence and uniqueness criteria are derived for single-birth, single-death, and birth-death processes on trees.

papers.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.

papers.title: Newton Steps are Faster for Linear Complementarity Problems
papers.abstract: Linear Complementarity Problems (LCPs) with sufficient matrices form a well-studied class of problems, dating back from the foundational works of Cottle and Dantzig (1968). LCPs capture convex quadratic programs, and admit reductions from problems such as discounted stochastic games or mean-payoff games. While the original approach for solving these problems was based on pivoting methods, in their 1991 book, Kojima, Megiddo, Noma, and Yoshise introduced an interior point method (IPM) with running time that is polynomial in the input size, but which depends linearly on a certain parameter called the handicap number of the matrix. Despite the ensuing rich literature on sufficient LCP IPMs, the linear dependence on the handicap number has not been improved since then. We present an IPM whose running time depends on the square root of the handicap number. The algorithm can decrease the duality gap by a constant factor in $O\left(\min\left\{\sqrt{n} (1+κ),n^{9/8}\sqrt{1+κ}\right\}\right)$ iterations. Curiously, this can already be achieved using standard Newton updates. We analyze the IPM in a norm defined by a local weighting, where centralizing Newton steps quadratically converge to the central path, without any dependence on the handicap number. The weights arise from a characterization by Rump (Linear Algebra and Its Applications, 1997, 1998, 2003) of the sign-real spectral radius and its relation to sufficiency; another ingredient of our proof is a new operator norm characterization of the handicap number. Moreover, the connection to Rump's work also enables us to show coNP-completeness of testing sufficiency, and approximation hardness of the handicap number.

papers.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
papers.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojević--Grujić--Živaljević conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.

papers.title: Interlacing of the Volume and Half-Volume Spectra
papers.abstract: We give a direct proof of the weak interlacing inequalities \[ω_p\leq\widetildeω_p\leqω_{p+1}\] between the volume and half-volume spectra of a closed connected Riemannian manifold $M^{n+1}$, $n+1\geq3$. We also prove that, for a residual set of smooth metrics, the area of every smooth embedded half-volume CMC boundary lies outside the rational span of the areas of smooth closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces. For dimensions $3\le n+1\le 5$, these results yield strict interlacing for generic metrics and a lower bound of order $A^{n+1}$ for the number of distinct half-volume CMC boundaries with area at most $A$.

papers.title: Holomorphic planes in $M\times \mathbb{T}^2$ from weakly exact Lagrangians in $M$
papers.abstract: Let $(M,ω_M)$ be closed symplectic manifold containing a closed Lagrangian submanifold $L$ with $ω_M$ vanishing on $π_2(M,L)$. We prove that there is a nonconstant $J$-holomorphic plane $u:\mathbb{C}\rightarrow M\times \mathbb{T}^2$ for any almost complex structure $ J$ on $M\times \mathbb{T}^2$ tamed by $ω_M\oplusω_{\text{std}}$.

papers.title: A Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual stable Grothendieck functions
papers.abstract: We give a closed boundary formula for multiplication by power sums in the dual stable Grothendieck basis. The off-diagonal coefficients are signed binomial coefficients supported on corner-connected broken ribbons, which are skew diagrams connected through edges or vertices and containing no square of four boxes. For such a diagram, the smallest power-sum index with a nonzero coefficient is the number of boxes plus the number of edge-connected components minus one. All larger indices give nonzero coefficients when the boundary statistic is positive and zero coefficients when it vanishes. The diagonal coefficient is minus the number of removable corners of the indexing partition. The formula evaluates the stable specialization of Nguyen's Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for K-k-Schur functions. We give two independent proofs, one using Newton's identity and the dual Pieri rules and the other using determinantal formulas and Schur complements.

papers.title: On the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space endowed with a Finsler metric obtained from a Minkowski metric by a conformal deformation. We first derive the conformal transformation formulas for the fundamental tensor, the Cartan tensor, and the Chern connection of the conformally related Finsler metrics. Based on these formulas, we express the anisotropic mean curvature in the Gaussian space in terms of the corresponding anisotropic mean curvature with respect to the original Minkowski metric, and derive the associated evolution equation. Finally, we establish the short-time existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions by reformulating the geometric evolution equation as a strictly parabolic quasilinear partial differential equation.

papers.title: Singular viscosity-exponent limit for one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with far field vacuum
papers.abstract: We consider the limit $δ\to1^+$ for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity $μ(ρ)=ρ^δ$ and far field vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result on the viscosity-exponent limit $δ\to1^+$ for strong solutions with far field vacuum. With far field vacuum, the diffusion coefficient $ρ^{δ-1}$ does not converge uniformly to $1$ on $\mathbb R$ as $δ\to1^+$. The main difficulty is to obtain uniform estimates for this limit. By introducing some new weighted density variables, we establish local well-posedness and uniform estimates without requiring $ρ_0^{(δ-1)/2}\in L^2(\mathbb R)$. We prove strong convergence to the known global $δ=1$ solution obtained in \cite{WenZhangDCDS2025} on a local time interval independent of $δ$. With one additional order of regularity of the initial data and the limit solution, the convergence holds on every fixed finite time interval, and the maximal life-spans of the $δ>1$ solutions tend to $+\infty$ as $δ\to1^+$.

papers.title: The Zhukovskiy-Volterra gyroscope: geometry and reduction
papers.abstract: We describe a symplectic reduction of the Zhukovskiy integrable case of motion of a rigid body about a fixed point with a gyroscope in $\mathbb R^n$ to an integrable magnetic flow on a sphere $S^{n-1}$. We also present Zhukovskiy's geometric interpretation of motion of the Euler top with a gyroscope, aka the Zhukovskiy--Volterra gyroscope, and perform a symplectic reduction of this system to an integrable magnetic flow on a $2$-dimensional sphere.

papers.title: Geometric Functional Inequalities for Markov Processes: An Invitation via the Langevin Diffusion
papers.abstract: Functional inequalities provide a language for reasoning about the long-time properties of ergodic Markov processes in terms of their macroscopic geometry. This article offers an informal introduction to functional inequalities for readers who are more familiar with probabilistic tools based around couplings, Lyapunov techniques, and similar. The main ideas are developed through the overdamped Langevin diffusion, where various functionals related to this convergence admit particularly transparent expressions, and for which the key associated inequalities -- namely, the Poincaré and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities -- are especially well-studied. We explain the qualitative content of these inequalities, what they imply about convergence to equilibrium, how they transform and compose under natural operations, and how they interface with classical probabilistic approaches. Related inequalities are discussed more briefly, and an annotated guide is provided for readers wishing to enter the wider literature.

papers.title: Online Optimization for Controlling HVAC Systems
papers.abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems account for a significant portion of buildings' energy consumption, motivating the design of energy- and cost-efficient control strategies. However, conventional strategies employ simple, reactive control, without incorporating a model. Therefore, in this paper we adopt an economic model predictive control framework and focus on designing online algorithms to solve the control input design problems with a limited computational budget. In particular, we propose two tailored online algorithms based on projected gradient descent, with a custom projection routine, and the projected primal-dual method. We discuss the pros and cons of both algorithm designs, focusing in particular on computational efficiency. We further compare them through numerical experiments simulating the control of an HVAC system over the course of a day. The results show that computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC systems control are indeed possible. Moreover, the performance closely matches that of a baseline algorithm with unlimited computational budget, in terms of reference temperature tracking and comfort temperature range enforcement.

papers.title: Instability of Self-Similar Implosions for the Compressible Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We prove that all known regular self-similar implosion solutions of the isentropic compressible Euler equations are unstable to shock formation. The perturbations can be chosen to be small in a class determined by the regularity threshold of the background. The proof relies on an amplification mechanism which occurs along the surface of the backward sonic cone from the implosion point. Motivated by our main results, we formulate an implosion censorship conjecture for the compressible Euler equations, stating that classical implosions are unstable to shock formation.

papers.title: Second-order geometric consistency of nonlinear FE-HMM on surfaces via corrector non-degeneracy
papers.abstract: We analyze the geometric variational crime of nonlinear finite element heterogeneous multiscale methods (FE--HMM) for $p$-growth monotone laws on curved surfaces, $p\ge2$. The practical method projects discrete gradients onto the exact tangent planes; we compare it with the exactly lifted method on the same discrete space. Without further hypotheses, the difference is $O(h_g^{p/(p-1)})$ in the metric induced by the cell correctors. The optimal order $O(h_g^2)$ holds with a constant given by a weighted negative moment of the corrected gradients, evaluated along the practical solution only; no bounds on discrete gradients in $L^\infty$ are used. The negative moment is a sufficient condition for the lower shifted $p$-structure of the discrete homogenized flux, which for $p>2$ is not available in general. For the model law and a fixed cell mesh, its uniform boundedness is equivalent to a finite-dimensional directional criterion on degenerate correctors, and for laminates it holds with an explicit bound, uniform in the cell mesh. With macro--micro quasi-optimality and an estimate for coefficient sampling, the reconstructed microscopic field converges as $O(h+H^{\min{s,1}}+h_g^2)$, where $H^s$ is the cell approximation rate. Experiments on a torus with an exact closest-point lift and a transported anisotropic $p=4$ material show second-order geometric convergence up to $98,304$ macroscopic quadrature points, each with a fully solved nonlinear cell problem, with bounded a posteriori constants for both load treatments.

papers.title: On strongly convex Kähler--Berwald manifolds
papers.abstract: For every real Berwald strongly convex complex Finsler manifold $(M,F,J,\hat\nabla)$, if the Cartan nonlinear connection satisfies the parallelism condition $\hat\nabla J=0$, we construct a good complex vertical connection $D$, prove that $D$ is the complex Rund connection, and $F$ is Kähler-Berwald. The inverse direction also can be seen from the construction and proof. As an application, we prove that on an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $M=G/H$, $G$-invariant complex Finsler metrics are Kähler--Berwald. Besides, we obtain the characterization of strongly pseudoconvex holomorphically invariant complex Finsler metrics on the classical domains of type-IV.

papers.title: Nonlinear optimal stopping and domineering claims
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear optimal stopping and domineering claims in a Brownian--Poisson filtration, under a nonlinear evaluation induced by a Lipschitz BSDE driver satisfying a comparison condition. A nonlinear domineering claim is a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-martingale dominating the reward process at every stopping time. We first establish the existence of such claims for every optional reward in $\mathcal{S}^2$. For left-limited, right-upper semicontinuous rewards, we prove a local dual representation at every stopping time: the nonlinear optimal stopping value equals the essential infimum of the values of all domineering claims defined on the remaining stochastic interval. This infimum is attained by a claim constructed from the associated reflected BSDE. We further show that a global domineering claim attains the value at a prescribed stopping time if and only if the reflection processes have accumulated no increase up to that time, with the appropriate endpoint convention. When the reward is right-upper semicontinuous in $\mathcal{E}^f$-expectation and the family of contact times is nonempty, its essential infimum is optimal. Under strict comparison, we also establish a necessary contact condition for optimality. No convexity assumption on the driver is required.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing NLS on $\mathbb T^3$
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness for the focusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the standard three-dimensional torus for initial data below the mass-corrected energy and Sobolev-norm thresholds determined by the Euclidean ground state. This gives a subthreshold focusing counterpart to the defocusing theorem of Ionescu and Pausader. The proof combines the periodic profile analysis with the recent nonradial Euclidean scattering theorem of Su and Zhao. The mass correction yields an invariant region and a nonnegative energy decomposition, placing every Euclidean profile below both ground-state thresholds. Uniform bounds on finite intervals follow from a contradiction argument on shrinking time intervals.

papers.title: On the classification of $2$-distance-primitive graphs of small valency
papers.abstract: A non-complete vertex-transitive graph is called 2-distance-primitive if a vertex stabilizer acts primitively on both the first and second distance neighborhoods of the vertex. Recently, Ruan, Liu and Jin [Discrete Math. 347 (2024), 113978] showed that every connected 2-distance-primitive graph of valency at most 9 either belongs to certain known families or satisfies a collection of further restrictions, with the socle of a vertex stabilizer isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ or $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$. In this paper, we resolve these remaining cases and thereby obtain a complete classification of connected 2-distance-primitive graphs of valency at most 9. We also give a short proof of the main result of Ruan, Liu and Jin and identify additional graphs omitted from their list.

papers.title: Singular values of iterated Aluthge transforms of compact operators
papers.abstract: Yamazaki proved that the norms of the iterated Aluthge transforms of an operator converge to its spectral radius, and Ando showed that for matrices the singular values of the iterates converge to the moduli of the eigenvalues. We prove that the latter holds for every compact operator on a Hilbert space and every generalized Aluthge transform $Δ_t$ with $0<t<1$: for every $j$, the $j$-th singular value of the $n$-th iterate converges to $|λ_j(T)|$, and the products of the $k$ largest singular values, as well as the Ky Fan norms, decrease monotonically to their limits. This is the Aluthge counterpart of the Yamamoto--Davis theorem. We also determine the limit in the Schatten $p$-norm whenever $T$ belongs to a strictly smaller Schatten class.

papers.title: Global existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows with large initial data and vacuum
papers.abstract: For periodic initial data that allow vacuum, we establish the global-in-time existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows, under the condition that the bulk viscosity coefficient is sufficiently large and a geometric angular constraint is imposed on the initial direction field. Our results remain valid for arbitrarily large initial energy. Furthermore, under appropriate additional assumptions imposed on the pressure, we also establish the uniqueness of the constructed solutions.

papers.title: Anti-ribbon shaped Young diagram decomposition
papers.abstract: We introduce a sliding procedure on diagrams which splits the standard Young tableaux of a corner-crossed diagram, in particular of a skew shape, along a finite binary tree whose leaves are anti-ribbon diagrams. Combined with standardization, this yields a decomposition of semi-standard Young tableaux into tableaux of anti-ribbon shape, indexed by standard tableaux and governed by their descent sets. As applications, we obtain expansions of Schur functions and Schur multiple zeta functions in terms of their anti-ribbon type analogues; at the level of Schur functions, this is a tableau-level form of Gessel's fundamental quasisymmetric expansion.

papers.title: Critical Curve for Three-Dimensional Radial Wave Systems with Distinct Speeds
papers.abstract: We study radially symmetric solutions to the three-dimensional semilinear wave system with distinct propagation speeds \[ u_{tt}-c_1^2Δu=|v_t|^p\ , \ v_{tt}-c_2^2Δv=|u_t|^q\ , \ c_1, c_2>0\ , c_1\neq c_2\ . \] For \(1<p,q<2\), we prove that \[ Γ(p,q) = 2+\max\left\{\frac1p,\frac1q\right\}-pq=0 \] is the exact critical curve separating small-data global existence from finite-time blow-up. More precisely, sufficiently small, compactly supported radial initial data give rise to global solutions when $Γ(p,q)<0$. On the other hand, for a class of initial data, the corresponding solutions blow up in finite time, with an upper bound for the lifespan, when $Γ(p,q)\geq 0$.

papers.title: Algebras, Kernels and Correspondences
papers.abstract: This is a nearly complete draft of our paper in which we attempt to do three things. First, we show that when formulated in the context of reproducing kernel correspondences over Rieffel's category, Normod-$M$, the Kolmogorov decomposition/representation theorem of Ball, Marx, and Vinnikov is functorial in $M$. Second, we investigate relations between our work and the work of Clouâtre and Hartz concerning multipliers of reproducing kernels. This investigation leads to interesting questions about the geometry of the matricial unit disc associated with a correspondence over $M$. And third, we describe how some of the recent work of Salomon, Shalit and Shamovich may be formulated in our setting. This leads to the notion of subvarieties, their quotients, and their relation with the structure of reproducing correspondences.

papers.title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
papers.abstract: The present paper establishes the Richardson dispersion law, predicting the particle separation with time according to $\E R_t^2 \sim t^3$, as well as anomalous dissipation for the associated tracer, for a random Hölder continuous velocity vectorfield with controlled sweeping.

papers.title: Hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics for accelerating saddle-point searches
papers.abstract: We propose a hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) method for accelerating saddle-point searches. The method constructs a Newton correction on the unstable subspace from the available negative eigenpairs, while BFGS updates based on projected secant information approximate the inverse Hessian on the stable subspace. By combining Newton and quasi-Newton corrections, the method incorporates curvature information in both subspaces while preserving the ascent-descent structure of HiSD. Accounting for the evolving stable subspaces, we establish local $Q$-superlinear convergence of the full-memory version near nondegenerate saddle points under suitable assumptions. We further develop a limited-memory version for large-scale problems and provide fixed-step and line search strategies. Numerical experiments show local convergence behavior consistent with the theory and demonstrate acceleration on ill-conditioned problems and degenerate saddle manifolds in neural-network loss landscapes. The method also supports efficient upward and downward saddle searches for a liquid crystal model, further illustrating its broad applicability to saddle-point computation.

papers.title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: Minimizing nonsmooth nonconvex objectives over general convex sets using no derivatives of the objective, together with structural access to the constraint set, poses a fundamental geometric difficulty: at boundary points, the feasible direction cone may fail to be closed, preventing the construction of finite sets of search directions that capture all feasible descent directions. We develop a feasible-directions framework for problems structured as the difference between a continuously differentiable function and a convex function over a closed convex set, and access the objective without knowledge of its decomposition, through exact line searches along feasible segments. To address the geometric obstruction, we introduce $η$-feasible directions, which remain uniformly separated from the boundary of the feasible direction cone, enabling finite-direction search even in the presence of nonlinear constraints. We present two algorithmic realizations of this framework. The first assumes access to an $η$-direction oracle and extends feasible-directions methods from linear to general convex constraints. The second replaces the oracle by a noise-augmented randomization scheme that constructs spanning directions from the affine-hull inner normal and almost surely avoids nonsmooth boundary points when initialized outside that set. Under curvature bounds and Lipschitz continuity of the smooth component's gradient, we jointly control the spanning coefficients and feasible step lengths of the oracle construction. This yields finite-time approximate $d$-stationarity along every unit feasible direction admitting a prescribed positive step length.
