The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.

papers.title: Compatible Hamel Topologies, Real Valued Isomorphisms and Rational Scalar Continuity
papers.abstract: We study Hamel character topologies on the real line in two parts. Part I treats the full real-orbit (TVG) and the rational-parameter (TVGQ) dual pairs. A divisibility-chain criterion decides compatibility on the rationals and on Q/Z. Compatible subsets of one chain have a compatible join, but two different chains need not: an explicit Chinese remainder construction gives two compatible topologies with an incompatible join. This answers the compact-union question negatively, disproves the Greatest Compatible TVG Conjecture for every nonzero rational-valued Hamel functional, and shows that the corresponding rational and real dual pairs admit no Mackey topology. We classify additive homomorphisms and isomorphisms of the real-valued observation spaces and their automorphism groups, prove that both prime square-denominator topologies are non-nuclear, classify sequences converging for every coefficient functional, and show that the real parameters of continuous characters of the integers with the mixed-prime metric form a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Part II studies real vector spaces whose Hausdorff additive group topology makes every fixed rational scalar multiplication continuous (TVGQ). A rational-valued Hamel functional and a rational parameter space S generate precompact, modular and real-valued observation topologies whose exact scalar ring is the multiplier ring of S. We compute their completions and character groups, classify the precompact TVGQ topologies, characterize universal separating sequences, show that local compactness and sigma-compactness force the scalar ring to be a field, classify isomorphisms within each modular family (exactly 2^c types), identify greatest-compatible existence with the unrestricted Mackey problem, and prove that all compatible topologies for the rational Hamel pair are non-Baire.

papers.title: Tangle Invariants Valued in Derived Categories of Sheaves and the Rouquier Complex
papers.abstract: We develop effective calculation tools for constructing categorified invariants of tangles and knots, following the work of Cautis and Kamnitzer. These invariants, originally constructed by means of Fourier-Mukai transform functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on certain iterated flag varieties, can be given an alternative algebraic description by using tilting bundles. We use this method and provide several examples of its application, in the hope of showing its utility to explicit pen-and-paper computations. This tilting-bundle method also allows us to lift the construction from derived to homotopy categories of complexes of modules, reducing the calculation of tangle invariants to a type of categorified matrix algebra, where the matrices in question have maps between their elements and calculations get turbocharged with chain homotopy.

papers.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
papers.abstract: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism. If $M$ is null-bordant, $Z(M)$ is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of $Z(S^d)$ which is fixed to be $Z(S^d)^{χ(M)/2}$ for even $d$ and can be removed for odd $d$. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In $d=4$ the obstruction is the signature: $Z(M)/Z(S^4)^{χ(M)/2}$ can be extracted if and only if $σ(M)=0$. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class $p_1$ has a local expression and thus $e^{iθσ(M)}=e^{\frac{i}{3}θ\int_M p_1}$ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the $4+1$-dimensional invertible phase with partition function $(-1)^{\int w_2w_3}$ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and $\mathbb{CP}^2\times S^1$, give opposite signs.

papers.title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data
papers.abstract: Data arising in scientific applications often exhibits complex nonlinear structure. Identifying and parameterizing said nonlinearities can enable better modeling, enhance predictive analysis, data interpolation, denoising, and anomaly detection. In this paper, we develop theoretical and computational methods to detect and parametrize Euclidean point cloud data lying near a wedge sum of tori. Specifically, we use persistent cohomology and cup products to identify the distinct toroidal components, and on each component, we optimize over low-energy multivariate trigonometric polynomials for best data fit. The ensuing optimization problem reduces to generalized ridge regression, which can be solved efficiently via standard techniques. We demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in both synthetic and real datasets, including interpolation of low frame-rate recurrent videos, attractor recovery in quasiperiodic dynamical systems, and the parametrization of gene-space cycle data for parasites and humans.

papers.title: Efficient counting of 2 x 4 LEGO brick buildings
papers.abstract: We outline the algorithmic advances behind our recent computation of the number 8364925094730088313 of ways to combine eleven 2 x 4 LEGO bricks.

papers.title: Every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph with $r\geq 17$ contains a second Hamilton cycle
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Sheehan states that every Hamiltonian $4$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle. A natural problem is to find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every Hamiltonian $r$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle when $r\geq k$. Thomassen proved that $k\leq 300$. Improving Thomassen's result, Haxell, Seamone, and Verstra{ë}te proved that $k\leq 23$. We improve this bound by proving that every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph contains a second Hamilton cycle whenever $r\geq 17$. Our new idea is to establish a transversal theorem for set systems on a cycle using Harris's results on the Moser--Tardos algorithm for Local Lemma. We then apply Thomassen's theorem on independent dominating sets to obtain a second Hamilton cycle. For $r\ge 18$, we also give some algorithms to find such a transversal.

papers.title: Classification and $C_2$-cofiniteness of rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights
papers.abstract: We obtain classification results for rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights. More precisely, we prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of OZ type strongly generated by its conformal weight two subspace $V_2$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of Virasoro minimal models. We also prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type generated as a vertex algebra by its conformal weight one subspace $V_1$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of simple affine vertex operator algebras associated with finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras at positive integral levels. Consequently, Zhu's conjecture that rationality implies $C_2$-cofiniteness holds for both classes, and every such rational vertex operator algebra is regular.

papers.title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
papers.abstract: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of $\mathcal{C}$-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most $2$, which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most $2$; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.

papers.title: Regularity Theory for the Equation $\det(D^2u) = f(u)$ in Two Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the interior regularity of convex solutions to $$\det D^2u = f(u)$$ in planar domains, with no regularity or monotonicity assumptions on $f$. In particular, when $f$ is bounded between positive constants, we show that $u$ is locally $C^{1,\,1}$, and that its level sets near a critical point are asymptotically ellipses. Our analysis relies on a new monotone quantity for a second-order flow satisfied by the support functions of the level sets of $u$. As a byproduct of our methods, we obtain Liouville theorems that generalize a classical result of Jörgens, and include a complete classification of global solutions in 2D to an obstacle problem studied by Jin-Tu-Xiong. As another application, we obtain regularity and rigidity results for rotating-wave solutions of the semigeostrophic equations from meteorology.

papers.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension five
papers.abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of five-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Rather than solving the overdetermined quadratic Jacobi system modulo $\mathrm{GL}(5,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses Levi--Malcev theory and nilradical stratification. In the non-solvable case, the Levi factor is three-dimensional, $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ or $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$, acting on a two-dimensional radical; this yields exactly five classes, including the indecomposable $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^2$. In the solvable case, Schur's bound on commutative subalgebras of $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ implies $\dim\mathfrak{n}\in\{3,4,5\}$, eliminating one- and two-dimensional nilradicals. The nilpotent case $\dim\mathfrak{n}=5$ has nine classes: three decomposable and six indecomposable, including $\mathfrak{h}_5$ and two filiform algebras. For $\dim\mathfrak{n}=4$, classification reduces to normal forms of outer derivations for $\mathbb{R}^4$, $\mathfrak{h}_3\oplus\mathbb{R}$, and $\mathfrak{n}_4$ under automorphism and scaling. For $\dim\mathfrak{n}=3$, it uses two-dimensional abelian subalgebras of $\mathrm{OutDer}(\mathfrak{n})$ containing no nonzero nilpotent operators. The work also computes minimal faithful representation dimensions $μ(\mathfrak{g})$, gives a dictionary with classical tables, and designs a deterministic identification algorithm.

papers.title: Coupled free energy and a diagonal approach to coupled Kähler-Einstein metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the coupled free energy $F_{-γ}^{\rm cp}$ which is a natural generalization of the free energy functional defined by Berman. In the Fano case, our coupled free energy provides a diagonal approach to the coercivity of the coupled Ding functional. We also define the non-Archimedean coupled free energy $F_{-γ}^{\rm cp,NA}$ on the space of finite energy measures on the Berkovich analytification. As a consequence of the regularization process of the non-Archimedean entropy established by Boucksom-Jonsson, Chi Li and Trusiani, we prove that the existence of a unique coupled Kähler-Einstein metric is equivalent to the stability condition that there exists $ε>0$ such that $F_{-1-ε}^{\rm cp,NA} \geq 0$ on the space of measures associated with a test configuration for the anticanonical line bundle. As a coupled version of the work by Berman, we show that the law of the empirical measure satisfies a large deviation principle whose rate function is the coupled free energy under the assumption that a conjecture by Hultgren is true. We also introduce a coupled version of the microscopic stability thresholds and prove that a uniformly coupled Gibbs stable Fano manifold has a unique coupled Kähler-Einstein metric. This is a generalization of the results by Fujita-Odaka and Berman.

papers.title: Hypergraphs with zero uniform Turán density at intermediate levels
papers.abstract: An $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is uniformly dense with respect to $j$-graphs if, up to a small error, at least a prescribed proportion of the $r$-cliques of every $j$-uniform hypergraph on the same vertex set are edges of $H$. For a forbidden hypergraph $F$, its uniform Turán density at level $j$ is the supremum of these density bounds over arbitrarily large $F$-free hypergraphs with the error tending to zero. For every $r\ge4$ and $1\le j\le r-3$, this paper proves that this Turán density is zero precisely when $F$ admits a vertex ordering in which every $(j+1)$-set shared by two edges occupies the same positions in both edges. This generalizes the zero-density characterizations of Erdős at $j=0$ and of Reiher, Rödl, and Schacht at $j=r-2$, and establishes the latter authors' proposed extension to the remaining nontrivial levels. Consequently, at level $j$, every positive uniform Turán density of a possibly infinite forbidden family is at least $N^{-N}$, where $N=\binom r{j+1}$. The proof combines hypergraph regularity with adjacent exchanges in spreadable random hypergraphs.

papers.title: Limits of Generalized Magnitudes of Dissimilarity Spaces
papers.abstract: For a finite symmetric nonnegative dissimilarity matrix $D=(d_{ij})$ with zero diagonal, we study the high-resolution limit ($t\to \infty$) of $\mathbf{1}^T(e^{-td_{ij}})^+\mathbf{1}$. We prove that this limit always exists in the extended real line and is rational whenever finite, without weightability or invertibility assumptions. At fixed cardinality, a finite rational polyhedral fan governs rank and leading asymptotics. Consequently, only finitely many finite limits occur, and every limit admits an integer-data realization at the same cardinality. In contrast, allowing cardinality to vary, every rational pair of zero-pattern magnitude and high-resolution limit is realized using dissimilarities in $\{0,1,2\}$; adding the level $3$ permits either infinite limit with any rational zero-pattern magnitude. We also classify all limits on at most four points. Moreover, we derive an exact Schur decomposition valid under persistent singularity. Finally, it is shown that positive semidefiniteness at some positive scale is equivalent to equality of dissimilarity rows for every zero-distance pair, in which case the limit counts the zero-distance classes.

papers.title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
papers.abstract: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) describe complementary quantum measurements: certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. In dimension six, triples of MUBs are known, but whether a fourth basis could exist remained unresolved for over three decades. OpenAI recently reported a proof that none exists. Here we use the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, to characterize all sets in dimension six. We prove that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix. Since none of them extend to a fourth basis, this also proves that no four MUBs exist. Our proof rests on a new topological result that all order-six complex Hadamard matrices except Tao's form a connected space. Connectedness reduces the classification of triples to finitely many overlapping four-dimensional phase balls. We certify with interval arithmetic that these balls cover the space and for every pair of MUBs represented in a ball, we then determine all third bases that extend it. Dimension six is now the first non-prime-power dimension in which all sets of MUBs are classified.

papers.title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
papers.abstract: We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure space with an action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})\times\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. In this dictionary, Virasoro primary operators are quantum automorphic forms and their scaling dimensions correspond to the spectrum of a quantum Laplace operator. The Virasoro crossing equations express associativity of multiplication on the quantum measure space. For compact theories, the algebra is a type III$_1$ factor. Liouville CFT is realized as $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting on itself by left and right translations. Virasoro boundary conditions correspond to quantum measure spaces with an action of a single copy of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. When the boundary spectrum is discrete, these are noncommutative counterparts of compact hyperbolic surfaces. The formulation accommodates models both with and without extended chiral algebras. It bridges the Virasoro conformal bootstrap with categorical and von Neumann algebraic approaches to 2d CFT.

papers.title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
papers.abstract: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^γ$, where $γ\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $γ$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.

papers.title: Lifts of Brauer characters and vertex pairs for odd primes
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group, and let $\varphi\in\IBr_p(G)$ have vertex $Q$. We prove that $\varphi$ has at most $|Q:Q'|$ lifts to ordinary irreducible characters, establishing Cossey's conjecture for odd primes.

papers.title: $ω$-limit sets of triangular maps over periodic orbits of the base
papers.abstract: Let $F(x,y)=(f(x),g(x,y))$ be a continuous triangular map of the unit square and let $z=(x_0,y_0)$ be a point such that $ω_f(x_0)$ is a periodic orbit $\{p_0,\dots,p_{m-1}\}$ of $f$. Then $ω_F(z)=\bigcup_{i}\{p_i\}\times M_i$ for nonempty compact sets $M_i$, and we ask which $m$-tuples $(M_0,\dots,M_{m-1})$ occur. For $m=1$ the answer is a theorem of Kolyada and Snoha. We show that a tuple occurs if and only if there are continuous surjections $M_i\to M_{i+1}$, indices modulo $m$, whose composition around the cycle is chain transitive. This is a cyclic version of classical facts due to Dowker and Friedlander, Sharkovsky, Hirsch, Smith and Zhao, and Kolyada and Snoha. It yields two necessary conditions: no $M_i$ is one of the exceptional sets of Kolyada and Snoha, and there are continuous surjections $M_0\to M_1\to\dots\to M_{m-1}\to M_0$. We prove that these conditions are also sufficient when every $M_i$ has uncountably many connected components, and when every $M_i$ has countably many components of which only finitely many are nondegenerate. In particular the sections of one $ω$-limit set need not be homeomorphic. Every tuple satisfying the two conditions falls into one of these cases or into a single remaining class, in which the sections have countably many components and infinitely many of them are nondegenerate; that class is studied in a companion paper.

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Stochastic Optimal Control on Positive Cones
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic optimal control problems in which the state is constrained to a proper cone. Specifically, we consider risk-neutral, risk-averse, and risk-seeking formulations within a single entropic-risk framework. We investigate classes of problems whose Bellman operator preserves affine functions and characterize their optimal value functions and feedback policies for both finite-horizon and time-average infinite-horizon problems. Additionally, we establish convergence and state-bound results under finite-step cost observability. Moreover, we demonstrate an exact connection between entropic-risk optimal control on proper cones and deterministic infsup control for systems whose dynamics and stage costs are affine in the disturbances. In addition, we provide examples of classes of systems for which explicit solutions can be obtained.

papers.title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
papers.abstract: Given graphs $F$ and $H$, the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H)$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that every red-blue colouring of $E(G)$ contains either a blue induced copy of $F$ or a red induced copy of $H$. A conjecture of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl asserts that, for every fixed graph $F$, this number is polynomial in $v(H)$. We prove this conjecture, showing that there is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $$r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H) \leq v(H)^{Cv(F)^2}$$ for all graphs $F$ and $H$. The proof combines a variant of a random geometric construction of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl with the hypergraph container method.

papers.title: On Natural Exponential Families with Log-Affine Generalized Variance
papers.abstract: We study natural exponential families whose generalized variance, the determinant of the covariance matrix, is log-affine in the natural parameter. Without any assumption on the natural parameter domain, we show that every such family is regular and that it is Gaussian when its generalized variance is constant. Consequently, a sample of size $n>d$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ comes from a non-degenerate normal law exactly when the conditional expectation of the sample generalized variance given the sample mean is a positive constant. Every non-Gaussian family puts mass on a facet of its convex support, and, as for a Poisson count, its height above that facet takes only integer multiples of a fixed step. More generally, its displacement away from any exposed face that carries mass has nonnegative integer coordinates in a suitable basis. A local inequality between third and fourth cumulants singles out the Poisson--Gaussian families and yields a complete classification of the infinitely divisible ones. Geometrically, a semi-flat Kähler tube, whose potential has constant Hessian determinant, is flat if some multiple of its metric is projectively induced near a point.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi Mode: Budget-Aware Routing of Optimizers By Online Landscape Probes
papers.abstract: The best classical optimizer for a continuous black-box problem depends on its budget and landscape. Existing routers decide from the dimension and budget, past improvement or features fitted to one benchmark, and few test an optimizer's implicit assumptions online. AMM (Adaptive Multi Mode) routes a known budget among quasi-Newton, trust-region, coordinate, multistart and evolution-strategy optimization engines with online probes of curvature, plateaus, separability, kinks, basins and fractal structure. Each probe has a default, a dimension-by-budget validity range and a cost charged to the budget. In its pre-registered development loop on bbob, 32 of 36 predictions held over the last 16 confirmations. AMM was then tested once on held-out bbob instances 101-110 (D=2-40, 10*D-1000*D) against up to seven competitors. It has the highest target share in 382 of 600 function-dimension-budget cells (236 outright, 146 tied) and, by a descriptive posterior rule, is credibly behind in 35, mostly at 10*D and 30*D. At every budget it also leads the controls built from its own engines (the best engine alone, the best engine per dimension and budget, and a greedy schedule), narrowly at 10*D and 30*D, and nevergrad's NgIohTuned. In pre-registered runs its lead over IPOP-CMA-ES holds under affine and box transformations, on box-constrained bbob and, pooled, on rotated f2-f4, but rotating the separable f3 and f4 removes most of the lead there. On held-out MA-BBOB its final share at 2000*D is level with IPOP-CMA-ES's and its anytime area lower. We published AMM as an open-source Python package (pip install amm-optimizer; https://github.com/BjBodner/amm-optimizer).

papers.title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
papers.abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.

papers.title: A property of boundary extensions of atomic singular inner functions
papers.abstract: Using a property of the Hilbert transform, we prove a measure theoretic result concerning the extensions of atomic singular inner functions to the circle. Various alternative proofs are presented using the mean value theorem for harmonic functions and a well-known property of Blaschke products. Using the main result, we establish several facts concerning atomic singular inner functions and their logarithms.

papers.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
papers.abstract: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$. This gives a local solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing $f$. Its velocity satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow 1}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$. Together, the two papers present a readable and accessible account of OpenAI's Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes. We claim no original mathematical contribution.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $Φ(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).

papers.title: The pliability of del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We study $G$-Mori fibre space models of $G$-del Pezzo surfaces, focusing on surfaces over non-closed fields. We construct explicit examples of birationally rigid sextic del Pezzo surfaces and give a negative answer to a generalization of Kollár's question on birational rigidity and field extensions: a sextic del Pezzo surface of Picard rank $1$ can fail to be birationally rigid over its ground field but become birationally rigid after an algebraic field extension. We interpret this phenomenon in terms of the failure of injectivity of natural maps in nonabelian Galois cohomology induced by the inclusion of automorphism groups into birational automorphism groups. We also show that finite pliability is unbounded: for every integer $d\geqslant2$, we construct a sextic del Pezzo surface of index $3$ over a field of characteristic zero whose pliability is exactly $3^d+1$.

papers.title: Largest Sperner families with bounded VC-dimension
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Frankl proposed in the 1980s states that for $n\ge2d$, every Sperner family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ of VC-dimension at most $d$ has at most $\binom{n}{d}$ members. We prove this conjecture for every fixed $d$ and large $n$, and show that equality holds only when $\mathcal{F}$ is $\binom{[n]}{d}$ or $\binom{[n]}{n-d}$.

papers.title: Deterministic Fault-Tolerant Connectivity Oracles with Subquadratic Space
papers.abstract: A fault-tolerant (FT) connectivity oracle for an $n$-vertex graph $G=(V,E)$ determines whether $G- F$ is connected for any query set $F\subseteq E$. When the number of failures is unrestricted, prior constructions exhibited a sharp contrast between randomization and determinism: randomized oracles use only $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space [Duan and Pettie, SICOMP 2020], whereas no deterministic construction was known to improve upon storing $G$ explicitly, requiring $Θ(n^2)$ bits in the worst case. The promise that $F\subseteq E$ is essential for subquadratic space: allowing arbitrary queries $F\subseteq V\times V$ forces quadratic space. For queries containing at most $f$ failures, Khanna, Konrad, and Putterman [SODA 2027] recently constructed deterministic oracles using $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{f}n)$ space that also report approximate distances with polylogarithmic stretch. Their result improves upon the classical $O(fn)$ space bound for deterministic connectivity oracles [Pătraşcu and Thorup, FOCS 2007], but offers no space savings over storing $G$ when $f=Θ(n^2)$. We present the first deterministic connectivity oracles with subquadratic space for failure sets of unrestricted size, using $\widetilde{O}(n^{7/4})$ space. We also establish the first polynomial separation between deterministic and randomized connectivity oracles, proving that every deterministic oracle requires $\widetildeΩ(n^{3/2})$ bits in the worst case. For queries containing at most $f$ failures, we obtain deterministic connectivity oracles using $\widetilde{O}(f^{2/5}n)$ space, improving the dependence on $f$ in the bound of Khanna et al., and prove a lower bound of $\widetildeΩ(f^{1/4}n)$ bits.

papers.title: Hessenberg character
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.

papers.title: Morphisms of $A_\infty$-algebras and modules
papers.abstract: $A_\infty$-algebra is a chain complex equipped with a coherent multiplicative structure, i.e. a multiplication which is commutative up to (higher) chain homotopy. Similarly $A_\infty$-module over such algebra is equipped with its coherent action. These notions are used to represent cohomological information contained in topological multiplicative structures. One of the key tools of the theory are minimal models, which are useful in cohomological computations. In this thesis author presents certain sufficient conditions for a morphism of $A_\infty$-modules to induce a morphism of their minimal models.

papers.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
papers.abstract: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.

papers.title: Delay-induced multirhythmicity in a 3-cell inhibitory network
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of a delayed three-cell central pattern generator network using return-map analysis and a phase-reduced description derived from generalized FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators. The phase model captures the emergence and stability of synchronous, pacemaker, and traveling-wave rhythms and provides a systematic, computationally efficient framework for characterizing the network dynamics beyond direct return-map calculations. We conduct extensive two-parameter analyses of both the full and phase-reduced models, revealing rich multi-rhythmic dynamics and transitions among coexisting rhythmic states. The close agreement between the two descriptions establishes phase reduction as an efficient and reliable framework for characterizing the dynamical organization of delayed neural oscillator networks.

papers.title: Independent Backward Preimages and Algebraic Radial Decompositions of Operators
papers.abstract: Let $T\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, where $X$ is a complex Banach space. We introduce the spaces $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$, defined by independently chosen preimages under the powers of $T$ with exponential growth bounds, and study algebraic radial decompositions involving $\mathcal{H}_r(T)$, $\mathcal{K}_s(T)$, and $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$. We prove that every algebraic decomposition $X=\mathcal{H}_r(T)\oplus\mathcal{I}_s(T)$ is topological and that $\mathcal{I}_s(T)=\mathcal{K}_s(T)$. This removes the closedness assumption in the radial decomposition theorem of Koliha and Poon. We also prove that, for $0\leq a\leq b$, the closedness of $\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ and $\mathcal{H}_a(T)+\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ implies $\mathcal{I}_b(T)=\mathcal{K}_b(T)$. We establish finite-defect and circular spectral criteria and characterize the Cantor--Bendixson derivatives of the spectrum, Browder spectrum, and Drazin spectrum in terms of radial decompositions and quotient restrictions. As applications, we obtain new characterizations of generalized Drazin, generalized Drazin--Riesz, generalized Drazin--meromorphic, and $g_z$-invertible operators in terms of radial subspaces.

papers.title: Spectral and mapping properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator
papers.abstract: We investigate the spectral and boundedness properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$ and its associated semigroup in $L^p$ spaces with respect to the inverse Gaussian measure. We establish strong continuity and contractivity of this semigroup in $L^p$ for $p \in [1, \infty)$, and obtain a complete characterization of the spectrum of $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$. For $p \in (1, \infty)$, the spectrum is independent of $p$, consists entirely of eigenvalues and exhibits a spectral gap. For $p=1$, the spectrum is instead the left half-plane. Furthermore, we discuss ultracontractivity and hypercontractivity properties of the semigroup.

papers.title: Optimal Holding Times for Entanglement Swapping
papers.abstract: We revisit the optimization of entanglement holding times in memory-based quantum repeaters for maximizing entanglement swapping throughput under different fidelity constraints - strict, probabilistic, and mean. We consider two heterogeneous quantum links that are equipped with single or multiple memories and differ in decoherence rates, memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates and success probabilities, as well as classical communication latencies. Efficient models are developed to estimate the expected entanglement throughput and the probability density functions of the conditional wait time to swap. The models are then used to satisfy different fidelity requirements by optimizing the maximum holding times for the two links. Finally, our proposed model and approach are validated with a discrete-event quantum network simulator.

papers.title: On isospectral potentials on periodic discrete graphs
papers.abstract: We consider discrete Schrödinger operators with periodic (possibly complex valued) potentials $Q$ on periodic graphs. Using a system of spectral invariants obtained in \cite{S26}, we investigate the sets of isospectral potentials on periodic graphs. In particular, we show that the Floquet spectrum of the Schrödinger operators on the hexagonal lattice and on the Kagome lattice generically (with respect to perturbations of $Q$) determines the potential $Q$ uniquely up to the obvious symmetries (translations and rotations) in the periodic graph.

papers.title: Boxicity of Power Graphs of Finite Nilpotent Groups
papers.abstract: The \textit{boxicity} of an undirected graph $Γ$, denoted as $\operatorname{box}(Γ)$, is the smallest non-negative integer $d$ such that $Γ$ can be represented as the intersection graph of axis-parallel rectangular boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The \emph{power graph} of a group $G$, denoted as $\operatorname{Pow}(G)$, is an undirected graph whose vertex set is the group itself, with two elements being adjacent if one is a power of the other. We determine the exact boxicity of power graphs of finite nilpotent groups. For a cyclic group of order $n=\prod_{i=1}^{r}p_i^{e_i}>1$, where the $p_i$ are distinct primes, we prove that its power graph has boxicity $\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i-\max_i e_i$. For a finite nilpotent group $G$, let the number of noncyclic odd Sylow subgroups be denoted by $t(G)$. If $G$ has odd order or if $G$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, then $\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(G))=\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(\mathbb{Z}_{\operatorname{exp}(G)}))+t(G)$, where $\operatorname{exp}(G)$ denotes the \emph{exponent} of a group $G$. When the Sylow $2$-subgroup is noncyclic, and the odd part is nontrivial, the boxicity equals this value or one more, and we characterise precisely when each of these values is attained. The boxicity of power graphs of arbitrary finite groups and the exact boxicity of the comparability graph of the Boolean lattice were posed as open questions in Discrete Mathematics, 349(7):115017, 2026. As a consequence of our results, we answer the latter question completely and the former question partially, by computing the exact boxicity of the power graphs of nilpotent groups.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flows from singular initial data
papers.abstract: We establish uniqueness of Ricci flows with non-negative sectional curvatures and scaling invariant curvature bounds, assuming that the induced distance functions converge to the same initial distance function up to isometry. In the compact case, restricting the size of the initial singular set, we also establish uniqueness under suitable weaker conditions.

papers.title: Monadically Dependent Graph Classes Have Almost Bounded Merge-Width
papers.abstract: A graph class $\mathcal{C}$ is monadically dependent if one cannot interpret all graphs in vertex-colored graphs from $\mathcal{C}$ using a fixed formula of first-order logic. We prove that every monadically dependent graph class has almost bounded merge-width, thereby confirming a conjecture of the first and the last author [STOC '25]. Our proof is algorithmic and the witnessing decompositions in the form of merge sequences can be computed in nearly-cubic time. This is a step towards the proof of fixed-parameter tractability of model checking first-order logic on monadically dependent graph classes, which is achieved in a companion paper.

papers.title: Uniqueness and full coverage in $k$-neighbor graphs
papers.abstract: We study the number of infinite clusters in the $2dp$-neighbor graph on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, in which every vertex independently selects $\lfloor 2dp\rfloor$ of its nearest neighbors uniformly at random, and one more with probability $2dp-\lfloor 2dp\rfloor$. The model has negatively correlated edges and, for $1\le2dp\le2d-1$, neither finite energy nor insertion or deletion tolerance. We prove that the undirected graph has at most one infinite cluster for every $p\in [0,1]$, and that in the planar case the same holds for forward and strong forward clusters of the directed graph when $p\in[1/2,1]$. We further exhibit a second phase transition: for $p\ge(d+1)/(2d)$ the open cluster of the origin is almost surely the whole lattice, and for $p>(d+1)/(2d)$ any two vertices of a box are connected inside the box of twice the size with probability exponentially close to one. In particular, the percolation function is continuous but not analytic on the supercritical interval $(p_c,1]$. Finally, we prove that the full-coverage phase transition at $p_f = (d+1)/2d$ is of order $2^d$.

papers.title: Unit fraction representations using shifted Golomb primes
papers.abstract: We prove that every positive rational number is a sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators of the form $g-h$, where $g$ is a Golomb prime and $h$ is a fixed nonzero integer, as long as the necessary congruence conditions are satisfied. Golomb primes, introduced by Golomb in 1955, are a natural analogue of the primes. Erdős showed that the relative density of Golomb primes among the primes up to $N$ is about $1/\log\log N$, so they form a sparse subset of the primes. Our result is an analogue of Bloom's result on unit fraction representations using shifted primes, for this sparse subset of the primes. A key ingredient in our proof is a Siegel--Walfisz-type theorem for Golomb primes in arithmetic progressions, which we also prove here.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Coherent Imaging in The Presence of Atmospheric Turbulence
papers.abstract: We study the fundamental limits of jointly estimating the signal amplitude and the atmospheric phase distortion in complex-valued multi-look coherent imaging, where the measurements are corrupted by multiplicative speckle and additive Gaussian noise, all looks share a known Gaussian sensing matrix, and both parameters belong to structured classes. By analyzing a constrained maximum likelihood estimator, we establish an upper bound on the joint minimax risk that holds uniformly over the admissible parameter classes, while oracle reductions and Fano-type arguments yield worst-case lower bounds over the admissible parameter classes. These results quantify the effects of structural complexity, signal and measurement dimensions, the number of looks, and the noise level, and establish matching minimax rates in several settings, with a remaining gap for phase estimation at low noise when the measurement dimension exceeds the signal dimension. We also construct a two-stage estimator for signal recovery under arbitrary diagonal sign distortions in the real-valued analogue. Under additional conditions, it recovers the signs up to a global sign with high probability and yields a uniform signal risk bound without a distortion-complexity term. Numerical experiments illustrate the dependence of the joint, signal, and phase errors on the model parameters and provide further support for the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Regularization vs. Convolution in Kernel-Based Hypothesis Testing
papers.abstract: The maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) test is a popular nonparametric test on general domains. Two lines of work have studied its optimality through structurally different approaches. The first, a convolution approach on $\mathbb{R}^d$, uses translation-invariant kernels with a shrinking bandwidth and is minimax optimal over Sobolev balls under $L^2$-separation; the second, a regularization approach on general measurable spaces, uses spectral regularization of the kernel covariance operator and is minimax optimal over Hellinger- and $χ^2$-separated alternatives. In this paper, we study the regularization approach over Sobolev balls under $L^2$-separation, which reveals the connection between the two approaches. We show that, with a translation-invariant kernel on $\mathbb{R}^d$, both are ways of meeting a single condition on the kernel's spectral density: the spectral regularized discrepancy captures the $L^2$-separation $Δ$ of a Sobolev alternative of smoothness $s$ as soon as the regularization parameter $λ$ is below the spectral density on frequencies up to $Δ^{-1/(2s)}$. A kernel with a shrinking bandwidth $h$ meets this condition with $λ\asymp h^d$, and under this coupling the constant regularizer, which gives the MMD test itself, attains the Sobolev minimax rate. This explains, from a spectral perspective, the need for a shrinking bandwidth in the convolution approach. With a non-constant spectral regularizer, our analysis requires the bandwidth to shrink only when the spectral density decays faster than any polynomial, as for the Gaussian kernel. Thus, for Matérn and Laplace kernels, a fixed bandwidth with $λ\to 0$ attains the Sobolev minimax rate. Finally, an adaptive test over a grid of bandwidths and regularization parameters is minimax optimal, up to a $\log\log$ factor, over both classes without prior knowledge of the smoothness.

papers.title: Finding full immersions is fixed-parameter tractable in labeled tour graphs
papers.abstract: We give an $O_H(n^5)$-time algorithm to test whether an $n$-vertex labeled tour graph has a full immersion isomorphic to a labeled tour graph $H$. A labeled tour graph is a connected $4$-regular graph whose edges are labeled by binary vectors of fixed length. To obtain a full immersion, a vertex may be removed only by pairing up its four incident edges and "splitting off" both pairs, summing the labels within each pair. Even for one-bit labels, no polynomial-time algorithm was previously known for arbitrary fixed $H$. Our main tool is of independent interest: we give an algorithmic min-max theorem that, in particular, characterizes the maximum number of odd-length circuits in a rooted circuit decomposition of an Eulerian graph. Our results have implications for vertex-minors, whose study is motivated by applications in quantum networking, connections with graph minor theory, and the goal of developing an irrelevant vertex technique for dense graphs. For vertex-minors, circle graphs play the same role as planar graphs do for graph minors. As a corollary of our main theorem, we obtain a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm for apex-vertex-minor testing in $k$-apex circle graphs. We also prove an irrelevant vertex theorem for such graphs of large rank-width. More broadly, our results are essential to forthcoming work of three of the authors proving a structure theorem for graphs with a forbidden vertex-minor. There, our min-max theorem plays the role of both the algorithmic $A$-paths and Two Paths Theorems.

papers.title: An Explicit Construction of Commuting Quantum KdV Hamiltonians in the Universal Virasoro Vertex Algebra
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula for elements $H_{2k}$ of conformal weight $2k$, $k\ge1$, in the universal Virasoro vertex operator algebra $V$ at every central charge, such that $H_{2k}(0)H_{2l}\in TV$ for all $k,l\ge1$. Modulo translation, the kernel of $H_4(0)$ is generated by $[H_{2k}]$ in each positive even weight and is zero in positive odd weights. The formula uses a realization on differential polynomials by possibly infinite-order differential operators in a completion of the Weyl algebra, together with the inverse of the identity plus a nilpotent operator on each weight space. A Koszul-type exactness argument for the classical KdV flows proves conservation; uniqueness and the Jacobi identity give commutativity. The classical limit recovers the normalized Gelfand--Dickey densities. Explicit low-weight elements and exact symbolic verifications illustrate the construction.

papers.title: Generalised Killing Spinors and Euclidean Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study when the number of spinors satisfying the same generalised Killing equation for a symmetric endomorphism field $W$ forces local realisation as a Euclidean hypersurface. Let $N=2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ be the rank of the complex spinor bundle. We show that in dimension $n\geq4$, if the complex dimension of the solution space exceeds $N/2$, then the metric and $W$ satisfy the Gauss--Codazzi equations. This is proved in the smooth category by combining the curvature defects into a single bivector and bounding the dimension of its kernel on spinors, using algebraic curvature symmetries to handle exceptional cases. Examples obtained from non-flat four-dimensional hyperkähler manifolds show that this threshold is sharp for every $n\geq4$. In dimension three, the Heisenberg group carries the maximal number of common solutions while failing the Euclidean Gauss equation. Further, in the real analytic category, we use existing extension theorems for Einstein metrics and parallel spinors to extend all common solutions to parallel spinors on a single local Ricci-flat ambient manifold. Using Wang's counts of parallel spinors, we obtain an independent proof of the sharp threshold for real analytic data.

papers.title: Bass martingales need not stretch
papers.abstract: In classical optimal transport, the equivalence of optimality, convex gradient structure, and cyclical monotonicity is a central paradigm. Known counterexamples to this equivalence rely on carefully constructed costs. In contrast, we show that this equivalence can fail in martingale transport in dimension ${d \ge 2}$: already for the canonical martingale Benamou-Brenier problem and irreducible marginals we have the strict inclusions \[ \text{optimality} \;\subsetneq \; \text{(Bass) convex gradient structure} \;\subsetneq\; \text{martingale cyclical monotonicity}\, . \] However, under the stronger assumption of strict irreducibility, we establish that these three notions coincide. Understanding when the gradient structure guarantees optimality is also of practical relevance, since algorithms based on the Bass gradient representation are used in financial model calibration. All our counterexamples are based on the following phenomenon: for $d\ge2$, there exist two one-step martingales $X,Y$ with the same initial and terminal laws, and a convex function $ψ$ such that \[ 0=\mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[ψ(Y_1)\mid Y_0]-ψ(Y_0)\big] < \mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[ψ(X_1)\mid X_0]-ψ(X_0)\big] <\infty. \]

papers.title: Proof of two conjectures on the log-concavity of partition ranks and cranks
papers.abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang proved that the crank sequence $(M(m,n))_{|m|\le n-1}$ is unimodal for every $n\ge44$. Bringmann, Man, and Rolen subsequently established the unimodality of the rank sequence $(N(m,n))_{|m|\le n-2}$ for every $n\ge39$. Ji and Zang also conjectured that $(M(m,n))_{|m|\le n-71}$ is log-concave for every $n\ge72$, and that $(N(m,n))_{|m|\le n-72}$ is log-concave for every $n\ge73$. In this paper, we prove both conjectures.

papers.title: The Exact Number of Pentagons in Book-Free Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $B_k$ denote the book consisting of $k$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove that there exist absolute constants $ρ>0$ and $N$ such that, for every pair of integers $n,k$ with $n\ge N$ and $2\le k\le ρn$, writing $n=5q+r$ with $0\le r<5$, \[ \operatorname{ex}(n,C_5,B_k)=q^{\,5-r}(q+1)^r, \] with the balanced complete $C_5$-blow-ups as the only extremal graphs. The linear order of this range is best possible since for all sufficiently large $n$, the formula fails whenever $k\ge0.14n$.

papers.title: Fixed-Radius Neighbourhoods in Three-Dimensional Unit-Cube Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Conjecture 4 of Chan, Chang, Gao, Kisfaludi-Bak, Le, and Zheng (SoCG 2026): for every fixed integer $r\ge0$, the radius-$r$ neighbourhoods of a unit-cube graph in $\mathbb{R}^3$ have bounded VC-dimension. Our bound is $2^{2^{O(r)}}$, independent of the number of vertices. The main ingredient is a VC-dimension bound for reachability through arbitrary fixed-length sequences of three-dimensional generalized dominance relations. Its proof uses groups ordered in two coordinates, with neighbouring groups acting as barriers that preserve this invariant when one layer is removed. Combining these bounds with the existing interval-representation framework, we obtain a Las Vegas algorithm that, for every fixed integer $Δ\ge1$, decides whether a graph given by $n$ cube centres has diameter at most $Δ$ in expected $O_Δ(n^{2-\varepsilon_Δ})$ time, for an explicit constant $\varepsilon_Δ>0$. Finally, for every integer $r\ge7$, we construct unit-cube graphs with rational centres whose radius-$r$ neighbourhoods have VC-dimension $Ω(r^3)$.

papers.title: Arthur packets for $\mathrm{G}_2$ over $p$-adic fields
papers.abstract: We describe Arthur packets for the split reductive group $\mathrm{G}_2$ over a $p$-adic field and compute their stable and endoscopic character distributions. The construction uses the twisted Aubert duality recently studied by Cheng--Kaletha. We identify the corresponding Xu packets on $\mathrm{PGSO}_8$ and their triality-twisted characters. We also extend the result to long-root and short-root Arthur packets corresponding to unitary generic representations of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$.

papers.title: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. The problem is posed in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d$ denotes the dimension; constraints are specified either by a closed feasible set or by a single explicit inequality. For closed feasible sets that are star-shaped with respect to an interior ball, including all convex bodies, we use a resisting-oracle construction to show that every deterministic algorithm needs $Ω(ε^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsimε^{-2}$ and $δ\lesssimε$. For explicit inequalities satisfying uniform Goldstein constraint qualification and strict feasibility, finding Goldstein KKT stationary points requires exponentially many oracle calls in $d$ in the worst case, even at fixed stationarity accuracy. This exponential dependence holds under dimension-independent constraint regularity and strict-feasibility bounds, with a sufficiently small neighborhood radius and complementary slackness error. The result covers common constraints such as ball and box constraints and also allows nonconvex feasible regions. For convex coercive constraints with a Slater point, the resisting-oracle argument also gives an $Ω(ε^{-2})$ oracle-call bound in the same dimension and radius regime while allowing a larger complementary slackness error. These results hold for all deterministic algorithms using a local oracle, whether or not the returned point was queried. Each constructed objective has a strictly feasible global minimizer; the lower bounds therefore concern the information required to find stationary points, not their existence.

papers.title: Universality of smallest singular values of random row submatrices and phase retrieval problems
papers.abstract: We establish universal logarithmic laws for extreme least singular values of random row submatrices and for the global stability of real phase retrieval near its injectivity threshold. Let $A_m\in\mathbb{R}^{N_m\times m}$ have i.i.d. entries distributed as a centered, variance-one real subgaussian random variable with a bounded Lebesgue density, and suppose $N_m/m\toγ>1$. For integers $0\le r_m\le N_m-m$, let $M_{m,r_m}(A_m)$ be the minimum least singular value over all row submatrices of $A_m$ with $m+r_m$ rows. Writing $k_m=r_m+1$, we prove that whenever $k_m\log m=o(m)$, $(k_m/m)\log M_{m,r_m}(A_m)$ converges in probability to $-h(γ)$, where $h(γ)=γ\logγ-(γ-1)\log(γ-1)$. This covers both fixed and moderately growing surplus. The limiting rate is universal within the stated class of entry distributions. For real phase retrieval from $N_m=2m-1+r_m$ amplitude measurements, let $L_{A_m}$ denote the optimal lower Lipschitz constant of the map $x\mapsto|A_mx|$, with signals identified up to sign, and let $κ_{\mathrm{ph}}(A_m)=\|A_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}/L_{A_m}$ be its scale-invariant global condition number. In the same surplus regime, $(k_m/m)\log L_{A_m}$ and $(k_m/m)\logκ_{\mathrm{ph}}(A_m)$ converge in probability to $-\log 4$ and $\log 4$, respectively. Although these measurements determine every signal up to sign almost surely, the condition number grows exponentially in dimension for fixed surplus and exceeds every fixed power of $m$ throughout the stated regime, with probability tending to one. These conclusions quantify the distinction between uniqueness and uniform stability under measurement noise. All stated limits also hold almost surely on any common probability space, without requiring independence across dimensions.

papers.title: Evolution Dynamics and Cauchy Problems with Quaternionic Variables and Lifting to Banach Bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a theory of evolution dynamics in a Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-algebra and establish a well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem of evolution equations with quaternionic variables. First, we study the geometric properties of slice structures of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules. By employing different slice structures, we construct some noncommutative Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-subalgebras which are compatible with the slice regularity of the functions involved. Moreover, through the quaternionic sliced geometric path integral over Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-module, an integral representation of the solution to the homogeneous Cauchy problem with quaternionic variables is obtained in a quaternionic $σ$-ball, and for the first time, a local existence and uniqueness theorem is established for $σ$-analytic solutions. Then the local $σ$-analytic solution is extended to the entire quaternionic spherical sectorial region, thereby proving a global existence and uniqueness theorem for the Cauchy problem. Based on it, the notion of an evolution system in a quaternionic $\mathbb{H}$-algebra is introduced and its core properties are established. In addition, the global existence and uniqueness theorems are obtained under hyperbolic-like and parabolic-like conditions. Finally, the structure of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules and $\mathbb{H}$-algebras is lifted to Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-modules and $\mathbb{A}$-algebras, and a well-posedness theory for evolution equations in this setting is developed. This reveals, from a new perspective, the universality of well-posedness for the Cauchy problem under the generic noncommutative $\mathbb{A}$-algebraic structures.

papers.title: Multi-Step Performance Estimation for Gradient Descent under the Polyak Lojasiewicz Condition
papers.abstract: Gradient descent is a fundamental algorithm in machine learning and statistical inference. Performance estimation provides a systematic framework for obtaining sharp convergence bounds through semidefinite programming. We study the worst-case performance of constant-stepsize gradient descent over the class of $L$-smooth functions satisfying the $μ$-Polyak--Łojasiewicz (PŁ) inequality. We formulate the $N$-step objective-gap analysis as a semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation based on pairwise smoothness constraints and pointwise PŁ inequalities. Since an exact interpolation condition for smooth PŁ functions is not currently available, the resulting SDP provides a valid upper bound on the true worst-case performance. We solve a reduced SDP retaining only consecutive-pair smoothness constraints analytically for every horizon $N$ and every stepsize $t\in(0,2/L)$. The solution exhibits three stepsize regimes. For $0<t\leq 1/L$ and $1/L<t\leq \sqrt{3}/L$, the reduced and full pairwise SDPs have the same optimal value, and the one-step SDP contraction factor tensorizes to a geometric $N$-step rate. For $\sqrt{3}/L<t<2/L$, the reduced-SDP value is nongeometric in the horizon: an initial transient phase is followed by eventual geometric decay. The resulting asymptotic contraction factor is tight for the full pairwise SDP and strictly improves the bound obtained by recursively applying the one-step estimate. Explicit primal and dual feasible solutions certify the results, with numerical SDP experiments guiding their construction. Our results show that analyzing several iterations together can give a better convergence bound than repeatedly applying the sharp one-step SDP bound in the Regime III.

papers.title: 3-manifold decision problems and Riemann hypotheses
papers.abstract: Beginning with Kuperberg's work on unknot recognition, several fundamental decision problems in 3-manifold topology have been shown to be in coNP assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis. In this note, we explain how recent developments around the quasi-Riemann hypothesis yield unconditional versions of these results, leading for example to the first unconditional proof that 3-sphere recognition is in coNP.

papers.title: Counting graphs admitting a strictly matched involution
papers.abstract: We study graphs admitting a strictly matched involution, i.e., graphs for which a strictly matched involution exists. A strictly matched involution of a graph $G$ is a self-inverse graph automorphism $f$ with the properties that the fixed point set of $f$ induces a complete subgraph in $G$ and, for the vertices that are no fixed points, every vertex is connected to its image under $f$ by an edge. Andres, Huggan, Mc Inerney, and Nowakowski (2019) determined upper and lower bounds for the number $A(n)$ of graphs admitting a strictly matched involution on $n$ vertices. We improve the upper bound and we compute the exact values for the number $A(n)$ for all $n\leq11$. Furthermore, we use combinatorial enumeration techniques and a decomposition lemma to determine the number $C(n,m)$ of graphs admitting a strictly matched involution with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges for several infinite classes of pairs $(n,m)$.

papers.title: Polylogarithmic bound for the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture
papers.abstract: The classical Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture asserts that for any fixed forest $F$, any graph $G$ not containing $F$ as an induced subgraph, with bounded clique number $ω(G)$, has bounded chromatic number $χ(G)$. Recently, Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour proved that every such graph has chromatic number at most $|G|^{o(1)}$. We improve this bound to a polylogarithmic one $(\log |G|)^{O(1)}$.

papers.title: On the geometry of real polynomials of the 7-th degree with simple complex critical points
papers.abstract: We consider real monic polynomials with simple complex critical points. Critical values of such polynomial $p$ can be considered as vertices of the uniquely defined polygon, symmetric with respect to the $x$-axis. The inverse image of this polygon is a tree-like system of ovals that touch each other externally in critical points. This system of ovals will be called the geometrical code of $p$. Let $a_1+i\cdot b_1,\ldots,a_n+i\cdot b_n$, $a_1<a_2<\ldots<a_n$ and $b_i>0$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, be the set of critical points of our polynomial $p$ in the upper halfplane, and $c_1+i\cdot d_1,\ldots,c_n+i\cdot d_n$ be their images. The order of numbers $c_k$ and the list of signs of numbers $d_k$ will be called the algebraic code of $p$. In our experimental work we study geometrical and algebraic codes of the 7-th degree polynomials and the relations between them.

papers.title: Unique continuation, nonexistence and bubbling for the critical $p$-Laplace equation II: the degenerate elliptic case and higher dimensions
papers.abstract:
For every $p>1$, we prove that a nontrivial solution of  egin{equation*} -Δ_pu=f(x,u,
abla u) \end{equation*} in a planar domain, with $|f(x,s,ξ)|\leq C(|s|^{p-1}+|ξ|^{p-1})$, vanishes neither on an open set nor to infinite order at a point. This allows us to prove unique continuation properties of axially symmetric solutions to $p$-Laplace equations in higher dimensions $N\geq3$, with axially symmetric $p$-harmonic functions as a particular case. Unlike in our previous work, the analysis is based here on the regularity and quasiconformal properties of the whole stress field $|
abla u|^{p-2}
abla u$ in the plane, taking into account the more delicate regularity theory for $p>2$. This allows us to prove Liouville-type and bubble profile decomposition results for critical problems in dimensions $N\geq3$ and in the whole range $1<p<N$, under some symmetry conditions.

papers.title: The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
papers.abstract: A $(d+1)$-state lattice is the smallest complete one-step approximation of a $d$-dimensional Brownian market. Its centered quadratic increments must lie in the span of the traded innovations. We study the resulting Gamma-to-Delta aliasing through the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)=\mathbb{E}[(ξ^\top Hξ-\operatorname{tr} H)ξ]$, $H\in\operatorname{Sym}_d$, for centered isotropic innovations $ξ$. For quadratic claims this operator is exactly the difference, scaled by $\sqrt{h}/2$, between the lattice's replicating exposure and its price-sensitivity Delta. Applying the lattice replication rule to a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)|^2/4$ relative to ordinary discrete Delta hedging. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete lattices is $\sqrt{d-1}$, uniquely attained by the equal-probability regular simplex. For positive-semidefinite and rank-one unit-Frobenius Gamma classes, the sharp minimax value is instead $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also describe the corresponding orthogonal quadratic residual in nonminimal markets and the leading implementation error for smooth claims.

papers.title: Logarithmic corrections for four-dimensional loop percolation
papers.abstract: We study the one-arm probability of the discrete random-walk loop soup on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ at small positive intensity. Using the small-loop crossing and macroscopic attachment estimates of Gao, we prove that the expected capacity of the origin cluster formed by loops contained in a box grows at most as the square of the logarithm of the box radius. Consequently, there are constants $α_0,c,C,β>0$ such that, for $0<α\leα_0$, \[ cαR^{-2}[\log(R+2)]^{βα} \le \mathbb{P}_α(0\leftrightarrow B_R^c) \le CαR^{-2}[\log(R+2)]^2. \] The interval $(0,α_0]$ is strictly subcritical. The upper bound rests on a simultaneous capacity estimate for neighborhoods of loop ranges, followed by an expansion over chains in which sufficiently small intermediate loops have been removed. A deterministic bound on the variation of the surviving scale sequences makes the expansion summable. The positive logarithmic-power lower bound is already known from work of Chang and Sapozhnikov; we give a proof using macroscopic attachments and a layer-cake argument, with constants uniform at small intensity. In particular, the one-arm exponent equals two, and the logarithm of its correction has order $\log\log R$, for every fixed intensity in this interval. We also derive polynomial tail exponent one for the cardinality and capacity of the full cluster, determine their positive moment thresholds, and give an application to random wires.

papers.title: A unified approach to fluctuations of LES of time-dependent generalized patterned random matrices
papers.abstract: A unified approach for studying the linear eigenvalue statistics (LES) of generalized patterned random matrices was developed in Kumar, Maurya, Saha (2026). In this paper, as a continuation, we develop a unified method for studying the time-dependent LES of generalized patterned random matrices with independent process entries such as Brownian motion and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We prove that if the limiting moment sequence of the LES of the generalized patterned random matrix with independent standard Gaussian entries is M-determinate, then under some minimal assumption on the link function, the time-dependent LES converges to a deterministic real-valued process.

papers.title: Perelman's entropy and Gromov-Hausdorff versus dynamical stability of round spheres
papers.abstract: We study the Gromov-Hausdorff stability of round spheres under perturbations of Perelman's nu-entropy. We show that in dimension two almost maximal entropy, together with an area normalisation, implies Gromov-Hausdorff closeness to the round two-sphere. In contrast, in dimensions at least three, we construct smooth metrics on the sphere whose entropies converge to that of the round sphere, but which remain a definite Gromov-Hausdorff distance away from it. These metrics can be chosen conformal and uniformly bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the round metric, with the same volume as the round sphere. Finally, in dimension three, we contrast this Gromov-Hausdorff instability with a dynamical stability result: metrics with nu-entropy above that of the round shrinking cylinder converge exponentially fast to round metrics under the volume-normalised Ricci flow.

papers.title: Concavity of Normalized Generalized Brézin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the generalized Brézin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.

papers.title: Robust Markov Decision Processes: An Introduction Using Convex Optimization and Game Theory
papers.abstract: The goal of these notes is to provide a unified and rigorous introduction to robust sequential decision-making. We offer a self-contained introduction to the main results in the field. After a concise introduction to MDPs we introduce robust MDPs with general uncertainty sets, before focusing on rectangular models of uncertainty. We make a significant effort to show connections between robust MDPs and several other popular models for sequential decision-making: MDPs with uncertain rewards, Multi-Objective MDPs and Pareto optimality, MDPs with time-varying uncertain parameters, non-rectangular robust MDPs, stochastic games, distributionally robust MDPs, and risk-averse MDPs. Having all these results in one place, within a single unifying formalism, will hopefully be useful for researchers who want to start working on this topic. The exposition combines operator and fixed point approaches, convex optimization (more specifically, duality in saddle-point problems), and game-theoretic arguments. The latter identifies robust MDPs with a certain type of two-player game; this helps build useful intuition, especially when constructing counterexamples.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Differentially Private Synthetic Graph Release with Nearly-Linear Additive Error
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time $(\varepsilon, δ)$-edge-differentially private algorithm that releases a synthetic graph approximately preserving all cut values of a nonnegative weighted input graph $G$. Our algorithm outputs a nonnegative weighted graph $H$ such that, with probability at least $1-β$, simultaneously for all $S\subseteq V$, \[ \left|w_G(S,V\setminus S)-w_H(S,V\setminus S)\right| \leq γw_G(S,V\setminus S) + O\left(\frac{n}{γ\varepsilon} \log^7 \frac{n}{δβγ\varepsilon}\right). \] For fixed $γ, \varepsilon$ and $δ= β= n^{-10}$, the additive error is $n \operatorname{polylog} n$, improving upon the previous efficient bound of $n^{13/12 + o(1)}$. Furthermore, we establish an $Ω(n/γ\varepsilon)$ lower bound for the relevant parameter regime, showing that our result is tight up to polylogarithmic factors. Our algorithm uses a log-det-regularized SDP to generate fractional queries for multiplicative-weights updates and certify accuracy for all cuts. The privacy analysis charges privacy loss only fractionally per mechanism call, based on the amount of mass on edge coordinates retired from subsequent iterations. Our synthetic graph release yields improved error bounds for several downstream tasks in private graph analysis including correlation clustering, Max-Cut, Max-$k$-Cut, constrained cut problems and hierarchical clustering. Most notably, for unweighted complete-graph correlation clustering, we achieve the optimal $\widetilde O(n)$ additive error while reducing the best previously known approximation ratio for this additive error from several thousand to $1.387$. We also provide a formalization of our results in Lean.

papers.title: To lift or not to lift: Operator inference for nonlinear PDEs with boundary control
papers.abstract: Operator inference (OpInf) provides a nonintrusive framework for learning projection-based reduced-order models directly from data, but its standard formulations do not explicitly account for the fact that boundary actuation changes the admissible solution space of a PDE. This paper develops and evaluates a boundary-consistent, lifting-based OpInf formulation for nonlinear PDEs with time-varying inhomogeneous boundary conditions. The proposed approach decomposes the state into a known lifting component that satisfies the prescribed boundary conditions and a homogeneous component represented in a POD basis.
